Openings on the hat and in front of the peach allow the vessel to be filled and poured, and the back has a handle with a small ring at the top. The surface is covered with a clear pale-green glaze and decorated with white slip dots; it was found in an orchard on the outskirts of Daegu in 1971.

1111101850000.title_en: Lotus Sutra in Silver Ink on Oak Paper
1111101850000.description: This is a 7-volume copy of the Lotus Sutra transcribed in silver ink in 1373, during the reign of King Gongmin of Goryeo. The record states that it was sponsored by Heo Chil-cheong, and later notes show that it had been kept at Dogapsa Temple in Yeongam, Jeollanam-do. It was taken out of Korea and later recovered.

1111101860000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Standing Buddha from Sinhwa-ri, Yangpyeong
1111101860000.description: This gilt-bronze standing Buddha was found in 1976 in Sinhwa-ri, Yangpyeong, and measures about 30 cm in height. Although the pedestal and halo are missing, much of the gilt surface remains, and the figure is thought to date to the Silla period based on its form and the style of the drapery.

1113701870000.title_en: Five-story Moulded Brick-and-stone Pagoda, Sanhae-ri, Yeongyang
1113701870000.description: This is a five-story pagoda built of stone cut to resemble bricks, standing in a field by the river in Sanhae-ri, Yeongyang. The first-story body has a niche for a Buddha image, and the pagoda is thought to date to Unified Silla on the basis of its base, stonework, and decorative details.

1113701880000.description: This Silla gold crown was discovered in Cheonmachong Tomb in Gyeongju, where it had been found on the buried person. It is 32.5 cm high and is decorated with tree-like uprights, deer-antler-shaped uprights, round gold plates, curved jade ornaments, and hanging leaf-shaped pendants.

1113701890000.description: This small gold cap was found in Cheonmachong Tomb in Gyeongju and appears to have been worn inside a gold crown. It is made by joining four gold plates of different shapes, with pierced decoration including cloud patterns and T-shaped motifs.

1113701900000.description: This Silla belt from Cheonmachong Tomb is a decorated belt with square metal plates attached to a textile band. It consists of 44 pierced plates and hanging ornaments, and was found in worn position inside the coffin.

1113701910000.title_en: Gold Crown from the North Mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb
1113701910000.description: This gold crown was found in the north mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb in Gyeongju and is considered a representative example of Silla gold crowns. It has three tiers of tree-shaped uprights in front, deer-antler-shaped uprights at the back, and many curved jade ornaments and gold pendants.

1113701920000.title_en: Gold Belt from the North Mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb
1113701920000.description: This gold belt and its hanging pendants were found in the north mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb in Gyeongju. Made of 28 plates with hinged pendants, it was excavated in a complete state and provides important evidence for Silla wearing practice and the arrangement of the pendants.

1111101770000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Mold-Impressed Chrysanthemum-Design Tae Jar
1111101770000.description: This buncheong ware jar was used to contain a royal placenta and was discovered in 1970 during construction on the Korea University campus. It consists of an inner jar and an outer jar, each with a lid. The outer jar is decorated with impressed swastika, lotus, and chrysanthemum bands, while the inner jar is densely covered with chrysanthemum motifs.

1111101780000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Incised Fish-Design Flat Bottle
1111101780000.description: This early Joseon-period buncheong ware flat bottle has a flattened body on both sides and is decorated with white slip, incised designs, and a pale blue transparent glaze. Fish motifs appear on the front, back, and sides, and the side panels also include peony and plantain motifs. The contrast between the white slip and the grayish clay body is especially clear.

1111101790000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Sgraffito Lotus and Fish-Design Flat Bottle
1111101790000.description: This early Joseon-period buncheong ware flat bottle has a round body flattened on both sides and a small mouth. It is decorated with white slip, a transparent light brown glaze, and lotus and fish motifs made by scraping away the background and adding incised lines. The front side shows lotus leaves and several lotus buds with a fish motif, a representative example of the sgraffito technique.

1111101800000.description: This hanging scroll was painted by Kim Jeonghui in 1844 while he was in exile on Jeju Island. In the inscription, he explains that it was painted in gratitude to his disciple Yi Sangjeok, who had obtained important books for him from Beijing. The composition is extremely restrained, with a house and trees set against broad empty space.

1113701810000.description: This document is the royal certificate issued in 1205 to Jang Yangsu for passing the state examination. Written on yellow paper, it is the oldest surviving diploma of its kind. Although the beginning is missing, the remaining text preserves information on officials involved in the examination and is an important source for the study of Goryeo examination制度.

1112201820000.description: This gilt-bronze standing Buddha was unearthed in 1976 together with two gilt-bronze standing Bodhisattvas. It has a rounded face, a body draped in closely fitted robes, and a right hand raised with the palm facing forward. The form and treatment of the robe folds suggest a late 7th- to early 8th-century work.

1112201830000.description: This gilt-bronze standing Bodhisattva was excavated in 1976 with a standing Buddha and another Bodhisattva from the same area. The figure stands naturally on a lotus-decorated pedestal, wearing a floral crown with a small Buddha image at the front and a slender body with thin, closely fitted robes. The pose, jewelry, and robe treatment indicate a mid-7th-century work.

1112201840000.description: This gilt-bronze standing Bodhisattva was excavated in 1976 with a standing Buddha and another Bodhisattva from the same area. The figure faces forward with a serious expression, wears an ornate floral crown and elaborate jewelry, and likely originally held a vase and lotus branch in the missing left hand. The dense ornamentation and formal style suggest an early 7th-century work.

1113701930000.title_en: Glass Bottle and Cup from the South Mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb
1113701930000.description: A glass bottle and cup were excavated from Hwangnamdaechong Tomb, a Silla tomb in the Micheu Royal Tombs area of Gyeongju. The set is thought to have been imported from West Asia, based on the quality of the glass and the form, color, and decoration of the vessels.

1113701940000.title_en: Gold Necklace from the South Mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb
1113701940000.description: This gold necklace, 33.2 cm long, was found inside the coffin in the South Mound of Hwangnamdaechong Tomb, apparently worn around the deceased person's neck. It is made by alternating four strands of twisted gold wire chains with three hollow gold beads, and ending in a gold ornament shaped like a bent jade pendant.

1113701950000.title_en: Long-necked Jar with Applied Clay Figurines
1113701950000.description: These are two long-necked jars decorated with applied clay figurines, excavated from tombs in Gyeongju. The vessels are decorated with figures such as frogs, birds, turtles, people, and scenes of daily life, and the figurines are interpreted as having meanings related to fertility, abundance, and warding off evil.

1111101960000.title_en: Manuscript of the Avatamsaka Sutra in Pure White Paper with Ink, Volumes 1–10, 44–50
1111101960000.description: This is the oldest surviving Buddhist manuscript copy in Korea, written on a scroll, and completed in 755 after being begun in 754 during the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla. It includes a record of the people who took part in the copying, the methods of production, and the ritual procedures, and it also preserves a frontispiece illustration in gold and a painted cover image.

1113301970000.title_en: Boeokguksa Stupa at Cheongnyongsa Temple Site, Chungju
1113301970000.description: This octagonal stupa was built to enshrine the relics of Boeokguksa, a late Goryeo monk who died in 1392, and was completed in 1394. Its base, body, and roof are elaborately carved with Buddhist guardian figures, lions, dragons, and lotus motifs, and the form reflects wooden architectural elements.

1113301980000.description: This Silla stele was erected after Silla occupied Jeokseong, a former Goguryeo area, to help stabilize local sentiment. The inscription, preserved on a stone slab discovered in 1978, records the meritorious service of local people and is an important source for the study of Silla administration and law.

1113701990000.title_en: Rock-Carved Buddhist Statues at Sinseonsa Temple Site on Dancheoksan Mountain, Gyeongju
1113701990000.description: This group of rock carvings at the mid-slope of Dancheoksan Mountain consists of 10 Buddha and bodhisattva figures carved on the surfaces of a large rock shelter. The carvings include a standing Buddha, a bodhisattva holding a vase, triads, attendant figures, and an inscription stating that one Maitreya Buddha statue and two Three-Layer Bodhisattva statues were carved at Sinseonsa.

1112102000000.description: This standing gilt-bronze bodhisattva, now in the Busan Museum, survives relatively well even though the pedestal and halo are missing. It has a high topknot, a serene face, a full chest narrowing to a slim waist, and a simple robe, and its hand gesture suggests that it once held a flask.

1111102250000.title_en: Heungnyemun Gate Hall, Changdeokgung Palace, Seoul
1111102250000.description: Injeongjeon is the main state hall of Changdeokgung Palace, used for royal enthronement ceremonies, weddings, crown prince investiture, and official court rites. The present building was rebuilt after a fire in 1803 during King Sunjo's reign and later repaired in 1857.

1111102260000.description: Myeongjeongjeon is the main hall of Changgyeonggung Palace, where officials presented New Year greetings to the king, major state ceremonies were held, and foreign envoys were received. Originally built in 1484, it was burned during the Japanese invasions and rebuilt in 1616.

1111102270000.description: Jeongjeon is the main hall of Jongmyo Shrine, the royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon dynasty, where memorial tablets of kings and queens are enshrined and ancestral rites are performed. The hall extends in a long, simple row of 19 rooms and represents the highest ritual formality combined with restraint.

1111102280000.description: This engraved stone astronomical chart was ordered by King Taejo of Joseon and made by eleven astronomers including Gwon Geun and Yu Bang-taek. It records constellations, the ecliptic, the celestial equator, and 1,467 stars based on a corrected model of a Goguryeo star chart.

1111102290000.title_en: Jagyeokru Water Clock Vessel, Changgyeonggung Palace, Seoul
1111102290000.description: This is a surviving part of the water clock Jagyeokru, which measured time by the rising and falling of water and automatically struck bells, gongs, and drums. The remaining pieces are the water containers, and the mechanism that moved metal balls and triggered the signals has been lost.

1111102300000.description: This astronomical clock was made in 1669 by Song I-yeong and used at Hongmungwan for timekeeping and astronomy instruction. It combines a gear-driven clock mechanism with an armillary sphere and is the only surviving astronomical clock made in the Joseon period.

1111102310000.title_en: Molds from Yeongam, a Set of Bronze Casting Molds
1111102310000.description: This set consists of talc stone molds used for casting bronze tools and weapons. The pieces include molds for slender bronze daggers, bronze halberds, axes, chisels, needles, and fishing hooks, and are dated to the late Bronze Age.

1113502320000.title_en: Lee Hwa's Certificate of Meritorious Retainer at the Founding of the State
1113502320000.description: This royal certificate was issued to Lee Hwa, who contributed to the founding of Joseon, in the first year of King Taejo's reign. It records his meritorious service and related honors and privileges in a long paper scroll with silk reinforcements.

1111102170000.title_en: Geumgangjeondo (General View of Mount Geumgang) by Jeong Seon
1111102170000.description: This landscape painting was made by Jeong Seon in 1734, during the reign of King Yeongjo of Joseon. It depicts the inner Geumgang area in true-view landscape style, using ink and light color to show a bird’s-eye view of snow-covered peaks, the Manpokdong Valley, and surrounding forests.
1111102170000.material: Ink and light color on paper

1111102180000.description: This Buddhist painting from the Goryeo period shows Amitabha Buddha as the main figure, flanked by Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. It is notable for replacing the usual Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva with Ksitigarbha and for its use of gold powder and refined facial expression.
1111102180000.material: Ink and color with gold powder on silk

1111102190000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Underglaze Cobalt Blue Plum and Bamboo Design
1111102190000.description: This white porcelain jar was made in the early Joseon period, probably in the mid-15th century, and is decorated with plum and bamboo designs in underglaze cobalt blue. Its form and ornamentation show influence from Ming dynasty blue-and-white porcelain, and it is thought to have been made at the Gwangju official kiln in Gyeonggi Province.

1111102200000.title_en: Celadon Covered Bowl with Inlaid Dragon, Phoenix, and Peony Design with Stand
1111102200000.description: This Goryeo celadon set from the 13th century consists of a covered bowl, stand, and spoon made as a complete set. The surfaces are decorated with a wide range of inlaid motifs, including a squirrel-shaped finial, lotus, waves, phoenixes, dragons, cranes, clouds, and chrysanthemums.

1113202210000.title_en: Wooden Seated Child Manjusri, Sangwonsa Temple, Pyeongchang
1113202210000.description: This wooden seated figure of the Child Manjusri at Sangwonsa Temple was made in 1466, during the 12th year of King Sejo of Joseon. It is the only known Korean child statue made as an object of worship, and an inscription found inside the statue records that Princess Uisuk and her husband commissioned it.

1111102220000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Underglaze Cobalt Blue Plum and Bamboo Design with Lid
1111102220000.description: This lidded white porcelain jar was made in the early Joseon period, probably in the mid-15th century. It has a simplified plum and bamboo design in underglaze cobalt blue, with the decoration arranged to emphasize empty space, and it is believed to have been made at an official kiln.

1111102230000.description: Geunjeongjeon Hall is the main throne hall of Gyeongbokgung Palace, where royal ceremonies were held and foreign envoys received. The present building was rebuilt in 1867 after the original hall, first built in 1395, was destroyed during the Imjin War.

1111102240000.description: Gyeonghoeru Pavilion stands in the pond northwest of Geunjeongjeon Hall and was used for banquets on auspicious occasions or when foreign envoys visited. The present structure was rebuilt in 1867 after earlier versions were damaged and destroyed, and it is the largest pavilion in Korea on a single floor plan.

1113702010000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Buddha at Bukjiri, Bonghwa
1113702010000.description: This rock-carved seated Buddha is cut into a natural cliff face at Bukjiri, Bonghwa, where a large rectangular space was excavated to accommodate the image. The Buddha is about 4.3 meters high, with a broad face, powerful body, and a large halo carved with small seated Buddhas and a lotus design. It is generally dated to the late 7th century and is considered representative of the Buddhist sculpture style of the Yeongju-Bonghwa area in Unified Silla.

1111102020000.description: This volume is part of the 60-fascicle translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra by Buddhabhadra. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on mulberry paper, and a record at the end states that it was printed in 1098, the 3rd year of King Sukjong of Goryeo, through the donation of Yi Pil-seon. It is the oldest surviving printed edition of the Avatamsaka Sutra with a clearly recorded publication date.

1111102030000.description: This volume belongs to the 80-fascicle translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra by Śikṣānanda. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on mulberry paper, donated by Jeon Sun-mi of Damyang in Jeolla-do in prayer for her mother’s rebirth in Paradise. Although no publication record survives, it is thought to have been re-engraved and printed around the 12th century after comparing it with the text and carving of the Haeinsa edition.

1111102040000.description: This volume is part of the 80-fascicle translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra by Śikṣānanda. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on mulberry paper, and the opening section includes a detailed illustration summarizing the sutra’s content. It is considered to have been printed in the Goryeo period, and the frontispiece is regarded as one of the oldest known examples of its kind.

1113302050000.description: This is the only surviving Goguryeo stone stele in Korea. It is thought to have been erected by King Jangsu after Goguryeo’s campaigns in the Han River basin, and it was discovered in 1979 at the entrance to Ipseok Village. The inscription is heavily worn, but surviving characters identify Goguryeo offices and place names, making the stele an important source for the relations among Goguryeo, Silla, and Baekje.

1113802060000.title_en: Goryeo Woodblocks in Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1113802060000.description: These are woodblocks carved during the Goryeo period and preserved at Haeinsa Temple in Hapcheon. Unlike the Tripitaka Koreana blocks carved by the state agency, these were carved by local offices or temples and include Buddhist scriptures, writings of eminent monks, and literary collections. They are important sources for studying Goryeo woodblock printing, Buddhist culture, and the transmission of texts.

1111102070000.title_en: Cheonmado from the Jangni of Cheonmachong Tomb, Gyeongju
1111102070000.description: This horse painting was discovered in 1973 in Tomb No. 155 at Hwangnam-dong, Gyeongju, known as Cheonmachong. It was painted on a horse saddle flap made of layered birch bark, with a white heavenly horse in the center and vine patterns around the border. The work is dated to the 5th or 6th century and is one of the very few surviving paintings from Silla.
1111102070000.material: Ink and color on birch bark and leather

1113702080000.description: This hexagonal reliquary was found inside the bell-shaped stupa of the Sejonsari Pagoda at Dorisa Temple in Seonsan. It has a gilt surface, a base, body, and roof, with relief designs of the Four Heavenly Kings and Buddhist guardian figures, as well as decorative finials and lotus ornamentation. Based on its decoration, it is thought to have been made in the late 8th to 9th century of Unified Silla, when octagonal forms were more common.

1111102090000.title_en: Stone Pagoda for the Dharani Sutra of the Victorious Buddha Crown
1111102090000.description: This stone pagoda is a rare Korean example of a pagoda type that originated in the Western Xia and Wu-Yue traditions, named for the Dharani Sutra of the Victorious Buddha Crown enshrined inside. The original structure was found in ruins at a temple site in Daepyeong-ri, Buk-myeon, Cheonan, and the pagoda now preserved at the Dongguk University Museum has been partly restored from five surviving stones. It is thought to date to the Goryeo period.

1111102100000.title_en: Dharani Sutra of the Unfailing Snare of Cundī, Volume 13
1111102100000.description: This is a transcript of Buddhist scripture copied in silver powder on dark-blue paper and preserved in scroll form. It is volume 13 of a 30-volume set, and the end record states that it was made in 1275 under King Chungnyeol and copied by the monk Angche. It includes a frontispiece with protective deities drawn in fine gold lines.
1111102100000.material: Dark-blue paper with silver powder and gold pigment

1111102110000.title_en: White Paper Copy of the Lotus Sutra
1111102110000.description: This is a seven-volume manuscript copy of the Lotus Sutra transcribed on white mulberry paper in black ink by Ha Deok-ran in 1377, in prayer for her deceased mother and her father's longevity. Each volume is folded like a screen and has elaborate floral decoration and a gold-painted frontispiece showing the sutra's contents. A later record shows that it was taken to Japan in 1443 and was later held at Gwangdaewon in 1605.
1111102110000.material: Paper and ink with gold and silver pigment

1111102120000.title_en: Commentary on the Śūraṅgama Sutra in Korean, Published by the Gangyeongdogam
1111102120000.description: This 10-volume, 10-book edition of the Śūraṅgama Sutra was printed in 1462 under King Sejo, based on the Chinese translation by Ban Cimi and commentary by Gyehwan. It was produced by the Gangyeongdogam, the office established to publish Buddhist scriptures with Korean explanations, and is the only surviving complete set of the original printed edition. It is also valued as the earliest vernacular Buddhist scripture published by that office.

1111102130000.description: This large gilt-bronze pagoda is thought to have been made in the early Goryeo period as a ritual pagoda to enshrine relics inside a Buddhist hall. It survives only in part, but its five remaining stories show a structure modeled on stone pagodas and wooden architecture, with pillars, railings, door openings, and roof tiles. Floral and Buddha motifs are engraved on the surfaces, and small bells once hung from the eaves.

1111102140000.title_en: Bronze Incense Burner with Silver Inlay from Heunggwangsa Temple
1111102140000.description: This incense burner, called an 'hwan' in the Goryeo period, has a flaring, trumpet-shaped foot and is 40.1 cm tall. Its body and foot are decorated with silver inlay of dragons, phoenixes, reeds, lotus flowers, geese, and ducks, and an inscription around the base records that it was made in 1289 for Heunggwangsa Temple in Gaepung-gun. The workmanship is refined and the date of production is known.

1111102150000.description: This is a manuscript copy of volume 31 of the 40-volume Jeongwon edition of the Avataṃsaka Sutra, transcribed in silver powder on dark-blue paper. It was made in 1337 by Choe An-do and his wife, with the help of the monk Gyoyeon, to pray for blessings, removal of misfortune, and rebirth in the Pure Land. The scroll has a painted floral cover, a record of its making, and a detailed frontispiece.
1111102150000.material: Dark-blue paper with silver powder and gold pigment

1111102160000.title_en: Inwang Jesaekdo (Clearing after the Rain on Mount Inwang), by Jeong Seon
1111102160000.description: This landscape painting was painted in 1751 by the Joseon-period artist Jeong Seon, also known as Gyeomjae, and depicts Mount Inwang after rain. It captures the mist rising after rainfall by combining a view from below with a view looking up at the mountain, using bold brushwork for the wet rock face and finer strokes for the nearby ridges and trees. It is considered a representative work of true-view landscape painting.

1113602400000.description: A self-portrait painted by Yun Du-seo in light color on paper, measuring 20.5 cm by 38.5 cm. Yun is shown wearing a tanggeon hat with the top omitted, facing forward with detailed beard hairs and a face placed high in the composition. It is regarded as an outstanding work for its unusual style and technique among Korean self-portraits.

1113102410000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra, Volume 249, Early Tripitaka Edition
1113102410000.description: This is volume 249 of the Great Prajnaparamita Sutra from the early Goryeo Tripitaka, carved and printed in the reign of King Hyeonjong. Printed on paper in scroll form, it consists of 23 pasted sheets. It is considered the earliest surviving early Tripitaka Prajnaparamita volume in Korea.

1113702420000.description: This is a Silla stele believed to have been erected in 524, the 11th year of King Beopheung. Carved on one face of a natural stone, it records an event related to the incorporation of the Uljin area into Silla and the suppression of local resistance. It is an important source for studying Silla law, the six-bu system, and royal authority.

1111102430000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the Exposition of the Sacred Teachings, Volume 11, Early Tripitaka Edition
1111102430000.description: This is volume 11 of the Exposition of the Sacred Teachings, one of the early Goryeo Tripitaka texts printed in the 11th century. It was translated by Xuanzang from a work by Asanga and belongs to the Yogacara tradition. The surviving sheet shows the characteristics of the first carving and is preserved in fairly good condition.

1113102440000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the Treatise on the Stages of Yogacara Practice, Volume 17, Early Tripitaka Edition
1113102440000.description: This is volume 17 of the Treatise on the Stages of Yogacara Practice, an early Goryeo Tripitaka text printed in the 11th century. The surviving scroll is on mulberry paper and preserves features of the first carving, which differs from later recarved editions in layout and printing record. Its carving technique is considered superior to the later edition.

1111102450000.title_en: Woodblock Print of Newly Compiled Catalog of the Buddhist Canon, Volume 20, Early Tripitaka Edition
1111102450000.description: This is volume 20 of Newly Compiled Catalog of the Buddhist Canon, compiled by Zongfan based on the Zhengyuan shijiao dazanglu. It records the names of scriptures, translators, total page counts, and the order of the texts, and is a very rare source found only in the early Tripitaka edition.

1111102460000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the Maharatnakuta Sutra, Volume 59, Early Tripitaka Edition
1111102460000.description: This is volume 59 of the Maharatnakuta Sutra from the early Goryeo Tripitaka, made in the reign of King Hyeonjong. It was printed on paper in scroll form and shows early Tripitaka features such as the use of the character jang and omitted strokes in some characters. Based on the paper and printing condition, it is thought to date to the 11th century.

1113402470000.description: This standing bodhisattva was excavated in 1974 from a temple site in Songjeong-ri, Uidang-myeon, Gongju, and is now in the National Gongju Museum. The figure wears a three-faced jeweled crown with a small Buddha at the center, making it identifiable as Avalokitesvara, and holds a flower bud and a vase. It is attributed to the early 7th century Baekje period based on its form and ornament.

1113802330100.title_en: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha, Seoknamamsa Temple Site, Sancheong
1113802330100.description: This stone seated Vairocana Buddha was found at the Seoknamamsa Temple Site in Sancheong, along with a steatite reliquary inscribed with a record of its consecration. The inscription states that it was made in 766 by the monks Beobseung and Beopyeon to pray for the deceased Duonaerang and enshrined at Gwaneumam.

1112102330000.title_en: Stone Sarira Jar, Seoknamamsa Temple Site, Sancheong
1112102330000.description: This dark stone jar was discovered inside the central base stone of the pedestal where the Buddha image was missing at the Seoknamamsa Temple Site in Sancheong. An inscription on its surface records the making of the Vairocana Buddha image in the year 766, making it an important source for the dating of Silla Buddhist sculpture and the practice of enshrining relics in Buddhist images.

1111102340000.title_en: The Lotus Sutra in Dark Blue Paper and Silver Ink
1111102340000.description: This manuscript of the Lotus Sutra was copied by I Shin-gi in 1330 during the reign of King Chungsuk of Goryeo. It is written in silver ink on dark blue paper and consists of seven accordion-folded volumes, with decorative covers and titles in gold.

1111102350000.title_en: The Avatamsaka Sutra, Chapter on the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra, in Dark Blue Paper and Gold Ink
1111102350000.description: This manuscript is one section of the Avatamsaka Sutra copied in gold ink on dark blue paper. It was likely produced in the late Goryeo period, probably between 1341 and 1367, and includes a finely painted frontispiece and a record identifying the painter of the frontispiece.

1113702360000.title_en: West Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Janghang-ri, Gyeongju
1113702360000.description: This stone pagoda stands at the Janghang-ri Temple Site in Gyeongju and was restored in 1932 after damage in 1923. It has a two-tiered base and five stories, and the first-story body is carved on all four sides with paired guardian figures.

1111102370000.title_en: Landscape Screen of Gosan Nine-Bend Poems and Paintings
1111102370000.description: This 12-panel folding screen was compiled in 1803 from paintings and poems created by court and literati painters. It depicts the nine scenic spots of Gosan associated with Yi I, with poems and inscriptions added by later writers.
1111102370000.material: Ink and light colors on paper

1111102380000.description: This calligraphy work was written by Prince Anpyeong, the third son of King Sejong of Joseon. Written in running script on silk, it survives as one of the very few extant authentic works associated with him.

1111102390000.description: This portrait depicts Song Siyeol, a leading Neo-Confucian scholar of the mid-Joseon period. It is a half-length seated portrait on silk, and the inscription suggests a connection with 1651, although the exact date of production remains uncertain.

1113102480000.description: This is a map of Korea made in the early Joseon period. It shows the eight provinces, local prefectures, naval bases, and military garrisons, and also depicts mountains and rivers in detail. The map includes Manchuria to the north and Jeju Island and Tsushima to the south, reflecting the territorial awareness of the early Joseon period.

1111102490000.description: This palace painting depicts Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung, the two palaces east of Gyeongbokgung. It is a 16-panel folding screen that shows the palace buildings, bridges, walls, and landscaping in detailed and realistic form from an elevated diagonal viewpoint. Based on the condition of the buildings shown, it is estimated to have been painted by court painters before 1830.

1112102490200.description: This palace painting depicts Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung, the two palaces east of Gyeongbokgung. It is a 16-panel folding screen that shows the palace buildings, bridges, walls, and landscaping in detailed and realistic form from an elevated diagonal viewpoint. Based on the condition of the buildings shown, it is estimated to have been painted by court painters before 1830.

1111102500000.title_en: Record of Merit for Lee Won-gil, Founder-Crucial Meritorious Subject
1111102500000.description: This meritorious deed certificate was issued in 1395 to Lee Won-gil for his contribution to the founding of Joseon. It is a Joseon early-period document printed partly with woodblocks and partly with movable type. The document is important for studying the treatment of founding meritorious subjects and the form of meritorious registers in early Joseon.

1111102510000.title_en: Initial Printed Copy of the Mahayana Abhidharma-samucchaya, Volume 14
1111102510000.description: This is volume 14 of the early Tripitaka Koreana printed during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. It is a Buddhist doctrinal text translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty and consists of 27 leaves, folded like a screen. Its paper, carving style, ink color, and notation of leaf numbers show the characteristics of the first edition of the Tripitaka Koreana.

1111102520000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Incised Lotus Design and 'Hyo-mun' Inscription
1111102520000.description: This Goryeo celadon meiping vase measures 27.7 cm in height and has a small mouth and a broad shoulder. It is decorated with finely incised lotus and vine patterns, and the name 'Hyo-mun' is written on one side of the base. The vase is identified as being made at the Yucheon-ri kiln site in Buan, and it represents the peak of 12th-century jade-green celadon.

1111102530000.title_en: Celadon Bowl with Raised Lotus and Arabesque Design and Inlaid Peony Design with Silver Rim
1111102530000.description: This Goryeo celadon bowl has a silver rim around the mouth. The interior is decorated with raised lotus-and-vine motifs, while the exterior is decorated with inlaid peony designs using a different technique. It combines methods associated with plain celadon and inlaid celadon, and is valued as a unique surviving example of this mixed decorative style.

1111102540000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Incised Lotus Design and Lid
1111102540000.description: This Goryeo celadon meiping vase with a lid measures 43.0 cm in height and is a representative form of the mid-Goryeo period. The glaze is light green and relatively transparent, with fine crackles, and the body and lid are decorated with simple incised lotus motifs. It is the only extant meiping vase preserved with both lid and body as a complete set.

1111102550000.description: This set of prehistoric bronze bells was excavated from a hill near the grave of Heungseon Daewongun’s father in Yesan, Chungcheongnam-do. It includes one pair each of pahjuryeong, ssangduryeong, ganduryeong, and a combined X-shaped ssangduryeong, and is thought to have been used by ritual specialists in the late Bronze Age.

1113102560000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Volume 1
1113102560000.description: This is Volume 1 of the 80-volume translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra by Shikshananda, printed as part of the first edition of the Tripitaka made during King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on paper, and its textual features show the characteristics of the early Tripitaka edition.

1113302570000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Volume 29
1113302570000.description: This is Volume 29 of the 80-volume translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra by Shikshananda, printed as part of the first edition of the Tripitaka made during King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on paper, and its textual features indicate that it belongs to the early Tripitaka edition.

1111102580000.title_en: White Porcelain Faceted Vase with Blue Bamboo Design
1111102580000.description: This Joseon-period white porcelain vase has an octagonal body formed by cutting facets into the clay. It is decorated with a simple blue-and-white bamboo design and was likely made in the first half of the 18th century.

1111102590000.title_en: Buncheong Jar with Inlaid Cloud-and-Dragon Design
1111102590000.description: This Joseon-period buncheong ware jar has a slightly everted mouth and a thick, heavy body that narrows gradually downward. Its surface is decorated with stamped and inlaid chrysanthemum, vine, cloud-and-dragon, wave, and lotus motifs, and it is considered a representative jar of the first half of the 15th century.

1111102600000.title_en: Buncheong Flattened Bottle with Sgraffito and Iron-painted Peony Design
1111102600000.description: This Joseon-period buncheong ware bottle, shaped like a turtle shell, was used for carrying liquor or water outdoors. It is decorated with peonies in sgraffito and iron pigment, creating a strong black-and-white contrast that is characteristic of buncheong ware.

1111102610000.description: This set consists of two Joseon-period white porcelain jars, one large and one small. Their form, glaze, clay, and firing method suggest that they were made at a government kiln in Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do, in the early Joseon period.

1111102620000.description: This large Joseon-period white porcelain jar was made by joining the upper and lower halves separately, a common method for vessels of this size. It has a broad, rounded body, pale bluish glaze, and a plain, elegant form that is representative of late 17th- to mid-18th-century white porcelain.

1111102710000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the 12th Fascicle of Hyeonyangseonggyoron (Initial Edition)
1111102710000.description: This is the 12th fascicle of Hyeonyangseonggyoron, a Buddhist treatise translated by Xuanzang from a text attributed to Asanga. It is one of the earliest prints of the Goryeo Tripitaka, and the page layout, paper quality, and printing suggest it was produced in the 11th century. It preserves features of the original initial edition and is an important source for studying the original form of the first carving of the Tripitaka.

1111102720000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the 32nd Fascicle of Yugasa-jiron (Initial Edition)
1111102720000.description: This is the 32nd fascicle of Yugasa-jiron, a 100-fascicle Buddhist text translated by Xuanzang from a work attributed to Maitreya. It is an initial-edition print of the Goryeo Tripitaka produced in the 11th century. Compared with the later Tripitaka woodblocks kept at Haeinsa, it differs in the placement of chapter, fascicle, and case marks.

1111102730000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the 15th Fascicle of Yugasa-jiron (Initial Edition)
1111102730000.description: This is the 15th fascicle of Yugasa-jiron, a 100-fascicle Buddhist text translated by Xuanzang from a work attributed to Maitreya. It is an initial-edition print of the Goryeo Tripitaka from the 11th century. It differs from the later Haeinsa Tripitaka edition in the placement of chapter, fascicle, and case marks.

1113702750000.description: This pottery object depicts a mounted warrior and is thought to date to the Three Kingdoms period. A warrior in armor sits on a horse placed on a flared pedestal, and a double-horn cup is set behind him. The piece is valuable for studying Gaya horse gear and weapons.

1112302760000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the 53rd Fascicle of Yugasa-jiron (Initial Edition)
1112302760000.description: This is the 53rd fascicle of Yugasa-jiron, a 100-fascicle Buddhist text translated by Xuanzang from a work attributed to Maitreya. It is an initial-edition print of the Goryeo Tripitaka. The paper and printing characteristics indicate that it was produced in the 11th century.

1111102770000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the 36th Fascicle of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Twenty-Fascicle Version (Initial Edition)
1111102770000.description: This is the 36th fascicle of the Avatamsaka Sutra, a fundamental scripture of the Huayan school and an important Buddhist text in Korean Buddhist history. It is an initial-edition print of the Goryeo Tripitaka, produced in the 11th to 12th century during King Hyeonjong's reign. The work shows characteristics such as the use of different chapter marks from the later Haeinsa Tripitaka edition and omitted strokes in some characters.

1113302790000.title_en: Woodblock Print of the 74th Fascicle of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Twenty-Fascicle Version (Initial Edition)
1113302790000.description: This is the 74th fascicle of the Avatamsaka Sutra, a key scripture of the Huayan school, and one of the initial prints of the Goryeo Tripitaka made during King Hyeonjong's reign. It is a woodblock print on paper made in scroll form for storage. The text and layout show features of the initial edition, including the use of different volume marks and omitted strokes in some characters.

1111102800000.title_en: Bronze Bell of Cheonheungsa Temple, Seonggeosan Mountain
1111102800000.description: This is the largest surviving bell from the Goryeo period in Korea, made in 1010, the first year of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. The bell has a dragon-shaped knob, lotus and bead motifs, and two dancing apsaras between the sounding pads. Its inscription shows that it was made for Cheonheungsa Temple on Seonggeosan Mountain.

1111102630000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Underglaze Cobalt Blue Landscape, Flower and Bird Design
1111102630000.description: This white porcelain jar was made in the late Joseon period and stands 54.8 cm high. Blue cobalt pigment was used to paint large diamond-shaped flower panels with landscape and flower-and-bird designs, along with stylized characters for good fortune and longevity.

1113702640000.description: This stele was discovered in 1989 and served as a document confirming property distribution. Its inscription records the handling of a property ownership and inheritance dispute involving local nobles, and it is thought to have been erected in 503 during the reign of King Jijeung.

1111102650000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Zhou Version, Volume 13
1111102650000.description: This volume is part of the early woodblock-printed Tripiṭaka produced in Goryeo under King Hyeonjong to overcome the Khitan invasion. It is a scroll-format impression on mulberry paper of volume 13 of the 80-volume Chinese translation by Śikṣānanda, and is dated to the 11th century.

1111102660000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Zhou Version, Volumes 2 and 75
1111102660000.description: These are volumes 2 and 75 of the 80-volume Chinese translation of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra. They are scroll-format woodblock prints on mulberry paper and are considered to have been printed in the 12th century as part of the early Goryeo Tripiṭaka.

1111102670000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Abhidharma-sarira-jnana-sastra, Volume 12
1111102670000.description: This is volume 12 of the 16-volume Abhidharma-sarira-jnana-sastra translated by Xuanzang and included in the early Goryeo Tripiṭaka. It is a scroll-format woodblock print on mulberry paper, and is estimated to have been printed in the 12th century.

1111102680000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Abhidharma-vibhasa-sastra, Volumes 11 and 17
1111102680000.description: These are volumes 11 and 17 of the 60-volume Abhidharma-vibhasa-sastra translated by Buddhavarman and Dao Tai. They are scroll-format woodblock prints on mulberry paper and are thought to be 12th-century impressions from the early Goryeo Tripiṭaka.

1111102690000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Buddhapravacana-sarvottama-mahāsukha-vajra-asamaya-mahākalparāja Sūtra, Volume 6
1111102690000.description: This is volume 6 of the seven-volume sutra translated by Faxian. It is a scroll-format woodblock print on mulberry paper and is identified as an early Goryeo Tripiṭaka edition printed in the 12th century.

1111102700000.description: This Goryeo celadon water dropper is shaped as a mother monkey with her young, with separate openings for filling and pouring water. The fingers and toes are carefully modeled, and the transparent glaze gives the surface a soft jade-green color. It is thought to date to the first half of the 12th century.

1111102810000.description: This white porcelain ewer from the Joseon period has a bottle-like form with a lid topped by a lotus-bud knob and a small ring. The handle and mouth were made with different clay and glaze from the body, and the vessel is thought to have been produced in a government kiln in Gwangju, Gyeonggi Province, for royal use. Its materials and techniques suggest a date in the late 15th to early 16th century.

1113702820000.title_en: Wooden Seated Amitābha Buddha from Heukseoksa Temple, Yeongju, and Reliquary Objects
1113702820000.description: The main statue is a wooden seated Amitābha Buddha made in 1458, the fourth year of King Sejo, as the principal image of a triad at Beopheonsa Temple. Inside the statue were found reliquary contents including scriptures, fabrics, incense, grain, and other items that match the contents described in Buddhist consecration texts. These finds are important sources for the study of Buddhist bibliography and textiles.

1113702830000.description: This is a 24-volume, 6-volume-set printed edition of a historical work covering events from ancient China through 1279. According to the colophon, it was printed in 1422, the fourth year of King Sejong, using newly cast movable type made in 1420. It is an important source for the study of bibliography and the history of early printing technology.

1111102840000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Daebanggyeong, Vols. 162, 170, and 463
1111102840000.description: These are three scrolls from the early printed Tripitaka edition known as the Daebanggyeong, specifically volumes 162, 170, and 463. Volume 162 contains a record showing that it was printed in 1046 for prayers for national peace, the emperor's mother, and the repose of the owner's deceased father. The three volumes are valuable for studying the printing date and characteristics of the early Goryeo Tripitaka.

1112602850000.title_en: Petroglyphs at Bangudae Terrace, Daegok-ri, Ulsan
1112602850000.description: These petroglyphs are carved on a cliff face shaped like a bent "L" and depict more than 200 images, including land animals, sea creatures, and hunting scenes. The carvings show tigers, boars, deer, whales, shamans, hunters, fishers, nets, and boats, using pecking and grinding techniques. They are generally dated to the late Neolithic to the Bronze Age.

1111102860000.title_en: White Porcelain Bowls Inscribed with the Characters for Heaven, Earth, Dark, and Yellow
1111102860000.description: These four white porcelain bowls were made in the early Joseon period. Each bowl has a character incised under the foot, reading "cheon," "ji," "hyeon," or "hwang," which may have been used to distinguish vessels stored in the royal ware warehouses near Geunjeongjeon Hall. They are important materials for understanding the lineage of early Joseon white porcelain.

1113402870000.description: This large incense burner was discovered in a pit near the temple site west of the tombs at Neungsan-ri in Buyeo, along with more than 450 other artifacts. It consists of a body, lid, phoenix finial, and stand, with detailed scenes of mountains, animals, musicians, hunters, and landscape elements on the lid and body. It is regarded as a masterpiece of Baekje metalwork and a key work for understanding the religious and artistic culture of the period.

1113402880000.title_en: Stone Reliquary from the Neungsan-ri Temple Site, Buyeo
1113402880000.description: This stone reliquary for Buddhist relics was found beneath the former site of the wooden pagoda at the center of the Neungsan-ri temple site. An inscription on both sides states that it was made in 567, the 14th year of King Wideok, and indicates that a princess dedicated the relics. It is an important inscribed Baekje artifact and a key source for the study of cultural exchange with China.

1113502890000.description: This stone pagoda stands on a hill about 2 kilometers south of Wanggung-myeon, Iksan, in an area known as the former capital of the Mahan period. It has a single-tier base with five stories above it, and its original form was revealed when the buried base was dismantled and repaired in 1965. The structure retains some features of Baekje-style stone pagodas, while also showing elements associated with later Silla and early Goryeo forms.

1113802900000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall and Geumgang Gyedan of Tongdosa Temple, Yangsan
1113802900000.description: Tongdosa Temple was founded in 646 by the monk Jajang and is regarded as one of Korea’s three major Buddhist temples. The present Daeungjeon Hall was rebuilt in 1645 after being burned during the Japanese invasions, and it houses a Geumgang Gyedan behind the building instead of a Buddha image. The hall is a mid-Joseon building, and the Geumgang Gyedan is a traditional ordination platform that has been repaired several times over the Goryeo and Joseon periods.

1111102910000.description: This is a dictionary of Chinese characters compiled by the monk Hyeongyun in 997 during the Liao dynasty. The Korean printed edition was published in Naju under the supervision of Gwon Deuk-ryeong, and the extant volumes are believed to be a Goryeo re-carved edition. As the only surviving form of the original in the world, it is an especially important source for the study of Liao-period pronunciation and lexicography.

1113202920000.description: This document was written in 1464 by Hyegeukjonja Shinmi and others during the renovation of Sangwonsa Temple, as they prayed for King Sejo’s longevity. It survives in two booklets, with the original Chinese text and a Korean translation, and includes signatures and seals from King Sejo and members of the royal family. The Korean translation is noted as the oldest surviving manuscript of its kind.

1111102930000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Standing Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva from Gwiam-ri, Buyeo
1111102930000.description: This standing bodhisattva image was discovered in 1907 inside an iron cauldron buried at a temple site in Gwiam-myeon, Buyeo, together with another Avalokitesvara statue. The figure wears a crown with a small seated Buddha, has a gentle smile, and stands on a simple double-lotus pedestal. Its natural expression and balanced proportions show the style of early 7th-century Baekje sculpture.

1111102940000.title_en: White Porcelain Vase with Underglaze Cobalt, Iron, and Copper-Red Floral and Insect Design
1111102940000.description: This large white porcelain vase is decorated unusually with cobalt blue, iron brown, and copper-red pigments on a single vessel. The front and back are painted with chrysanthemums, orchids, bees, and butterflies in underglaze relief and colored decoration. It is thought to have been made in Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do, in the first half of the 18th century.
1111102940000.material: White porcelain with underglaze cobalt, iron, and copper-red pigments

1111102950000.description: This gilt-bronze crown, 25.5 centimeters high, was found in Tomb No. 9 at Sinchon-ri, Bannam-myeon, Naju. It consists of an outer crown and an inner cap, and its branch-like ornament differs in style from the mountain-shaped motifs seen on Silla crowns. Similar inner caps have also been found in Iksan and Japan, making the crown an important source for studying cultural exchange between Baekje and Japan.

1113102960000.title_en: Five Buddhas Assembly Banner of Chiljangsa Temple
1113102960000.description: This large Buddhist hanging banner was painted by Beophyeong in 1628 for use in major temple rites and worship. The composition is divided into three horizontal sections with clouds, showing the Three Body Buddhas, the Three Times Buddhas, and, at the bottom, seated Avalokitesvara and Ksitigarbha bodhisattvas. Its balanced composition and refined brushwork make it an important work for the study of early Joseon Buddhist painting.

1113302970000.title_en: Buddhist Hanging Scroll of the Vulture Peak Assembly at Ansimsa Temple
1113302970000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts Śākyamuni Buddha preaching on Vulture Peak. Śākyamuni is shown in the center with Manjusri and Samantabhadra bodhisattvas, the Four Heavenly Kings, and assembled attendants arranged symmetrically around him. It was made in 1652 during the reign of King Hyojong of Joseon.

1113402980000.title_en: Buddhist Hanging Scroll of the Three Bodies Buddha at Gapsa Temple
1113402980000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts the Three Bodies Buddhas preaching the Dharma, centered on Vairocana Buddha. Vairocana, Rocana, and Śākyamuni are shown with a large group of bodhisattvas, disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings arranged in tiers. It was made in 1650 during the reign of King Hyojong of Joseon.

1113402990000.title_en: Buddhist Hanging Scroll of Rocana Buddha at Sinwonsa Temple
1113402990000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts Rocana Buddha preaching the Dharma in the Vulture Peak Assembly. Rocana Buddha is shown alone in the center, with the Ten Great Bodhisattvas, the Ten Great Disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings placed to either side. It was made in 1664 during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Joseon.

1113403000000.title_en: Buddhist Hanging Scroll of Maitreya Buddha at Janggoksa Temple
1113403000000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts Maitreya Buddha holding a nyugwasa branch, with many other figures filling the composition. Maitreya is shown in the center with the Six Buddhas, Six Bodhisattvas, disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings arranged around him. It was made in 1673 during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Joseon.

1113603010000.title_en: Buddhist Hanging Scroll of the Vulture Peak Assembly at Hwaeomsa Temple
1113603010000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts Śākyamuni Buddha preaching on Vulture Peak. Śākyamuni is seated on a high lotus pedestal at the center, with Manjusri and Samantabhadra bodhisattvas and the Four Heavenly Kings around him. It was made in 1653 during the reign of King Hyojong of Joseon.

1113803020000.title_en: Buddhist Hanging Scroll of the Vulture Peak Assembly at Cheonggoksa Temple
1113803020000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts Śākyamuni Buddha preaching in the Vulture Peak Assembly. Śākyamuni fills the center of the composition, with Manjusri and Samantabhadra bodhisattvas to either side and figures such as Ānanda and Kāśyapa above them. It was made in 1722 during the reign of King Gyeongjong of Joseon.

1111103030000.title_en: Seungjeongwon Ilgi (Diaries of the Royal Secretariat)
1111103030000.description: This diary records matters handled by Seungjeongwon, the royal secretariat of Joseon, including the transmission of royal orders, administrative affairs, and court rites. It was written in chronological form, and the surviving portion covers the years from 1623 to 1910. The work was inscribed on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register in 2001.

1113603040000.description: Jinnamgwan Hall was built in 1599 as the guesthouse of the left naval headquarters of Jeolla Province. It retains the historical significance of the naval base that led victories in the Imjin War and the Jeongyu War, and it was rebuilt in 1718. The building is the largest surviving provincial government office structure in Korea.

1113803050000.description: Sejeongwan Hall is the main building of the former Tongjeyeong naval headquarters. According to a record found during repairs in 1963, it was begun in 1605 and raised that July, and it later served as the command center for the naval forces of Gyeongsang, Jeolla, and Chungcheong provinces for about 290 years.

1113103060000.description: This is a woodblock-printed volume of the early extant edition of Samguk yusa, a historical work compiled by the monk Iryeon in 1281. It binds volumes 3 through 5 into one book, and its text and paper repairs make it an important source for early Joseon bibliography and for correcting later printed editions.

1111103060200.description: Samguk yusa is a historical work compiled by the monk Iryeon in 1281. This edition is the Jeongdeok edition printed in Gyeongju in 1512 during King Jungjong's reign, and it is the oldest surviving complete woodblock-printed edition.

1111103060300.description: This is an early Joseon woodblock-printed copy of Samguk yusa, a historical work compiled by the monk Iryeon in 1281. Although only volumes 1 and 2 survive, it is a complete impression without missing leaves and is valuable for studying the text and comparing it with the 1512 edition.

1112103060400.description: This surviving copy of Samguk yusa contains only volumes 4 and 5. Printed in the early Joseon period from woodblocks first carved in 1394, it is an important source for textual comparison and for checking omissions and errors in later editions.

1113403070000.title_en: Rock-carved Triad Buddha Standing Image, Taean Dongmun-ri
1113403070000.description: This is an early Korean rock-carved Buddhist triad, formed on a fan-shaped cliff face with a square niche. Unlike the usual triad layout, it has two standing Buddhas and one standing bodhisattva, and it is regarded as an early Baekje example showing influence from Northern Qi Buddhist sculpture.

1113603080000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Tathagata, Bukmireukam Hermitage, Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1113603080000.description: This large high-relief rock-carved seated Buddha is shown with a donor figure and in the earth-touching gesture. The figure has a rounded, dignified face, a thick body, and a lotus pedestal and halo arrangement that reflect the transition from late Unified Silla to Goryeo styles.

1111103090000.description: A moon jar is a large white porcelain jar with a rounded, milky-white body that resembles the full moon. This example was made in Joseon dynasty official kilns in the late 17th to early 18th century, likely at the Gwangju Bunwon kilns, and was formed by joining upper and lower halves.

1113403230000.title_en: Stone Standing Maitreya Bodhisattva of Gwanchoksa Temple, Nonsan
1113403230000.description: This large stone Buddhist statue at Gwanchoksa Temple in Nonsan is said to have been made around 968 by the monk-sculptor Hye-myeong at the command of King Gwangjong of Goryeo. It is the largest stone Buddha statue in Korea and is noted for its distinctive, uncompromising form and monumental scale.

1113803240000.title_en: Royal Edict of Merit for I Je, Founder of the Joseon Dynasty
1113803240000.description: This royal edict was issued by King Taejo in 1392 to I Je, who was recognized as a first-rank founding meritorious subject for helping establish Joseon. The document records his contributions and the rewards granted to his family and relatives, and it bears the seal of the former Goryeo king, showing that the old royal seal continued to be used in the early Joseon period.

1111103250000.title_en: Gisa Gyecheop, the Gye Album of the Year of the Pig
1111103250000.description: This album records the events held when King Sukjong entered the Giroso at age 59 in 1719, following the precedent of King Taejo. It contains a preface, the king's verse, an afterword, participant lists, event paintings, portraits of the senior officials, congratulatory poems, and the names of the production staff.

1111103260000.description: This jar is one of the most important dated examples from the early period when celadon was first made in Korea. The inscription on the base states that it was made in 993 and that it was ritual ware for the first chamber of the royal ancestral shrine, with Choe Gil-hui recorded as the maker or supervisor.

1113403270000.title_en: Reliquary from the Site of Wangheungsa Temple, Buyeo
1113403270000.description: This reliquary set was excavated in 2007 from the site of Wangheungsa Temple in Buyeo and is the oldest known reliquary in Korea. An inscription on the bronze reliquary confirms that it was made in 577, providing an exact date and valuable evidence for Baekje Buddhist material culture.

1113703280000.title_en: Daejangjeon Hall and Yunjangdae of Yongmunsa Temple, Yecheon
1113703280000.description: Daejangjeon Hall and the two Yunjangdae were founded in connection with the recovery from the 1173 crisis during the reign of King Myeongjong of Goryeo. Daejangjeon is a rare Buddhist scripture hall that houses Yunjangdae, and the paired revolving scripture stands are unique in Korea.

1111103290000.title_en: Rain Gauge of the Chungcheong Provincial Office, Gongju
1111103290000.description: This rain gauge was made in 1837 and was once installed at the provincial office in Gongju. It is the only surviving example of the rain gauges distributed by the central government to provincial offices during the Joseon period.

1111103300000.title_en: Rain Gauge Stand of the Gyeongsang Provincial Office, Daegu
1111103300000.description: This granite rain gauge stand was made in 1770 and originally installed at the Daegu provincial office. Its inscription records the date of manufacture, and it is an important source for the history of Korea's systematic measurement of rainfall in the late Joseon period.

1113703180000.description: This granite stele was discovered in 2009 in Jungseong-ri, Heunghae-eup, Buk-gu, Pohang, and is the oldest extant Silla stele. Its inscription, cut on one face in 12 lines and 203 characters, is largely legible despite damage to the upper and right edges. The text provides important information on Silla's official ranks, the internal structure of the six bu, local administration, dispute settlement, and measures to prevent recurrence, and its script is classified as an early clerical script.

1111103190100.description: Compiled by Heo Jun and first printed in 1613, this is a major Korean medical classic. The National Library of Korea copy is a complete 25-volume set from Odaesan Sago, and it preserves an inner gift inscription, a preface by Yi Jeong-gwi dated 1611, and a publication record dated 1613. It is well preserved.

1113103190200.description: Compiled by Heo Jun and first printed in 1613, this is a major Korean medical classic. The Korea Institute of Korean Culture copy belongs to the Jaksangsan Sago edition and can be identified by its seals, although the inner gift inscription is missing. It is a complete 25-volume set and is well preserved.

1111103190300.description: Compiled by Heo Jun and first printed in 1613, this is a major Korean medical classic. The copy held by the Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies at Seoul National University exists in two related sets: a 24-volume Taebaeksan Sago copy and a 17-volume copy without an inner gift inscription. The 17-volume copy preserves volume 6 of the Miscellaneous Diseases section and helps supplement the incomplete Taebaeksan Sago copy.

1113103200000.description: This Buddhist hymn was composed by King Sejong in praise of Queen Soheon and printed in movable type soon after the creation of Hangul. Only about one third of the original survives, but it is an important source for early Korean language studies and the history of printing in the early Hangul period.

1113703210000.title_en: Woodblock Amitabha Buddha Sermon Scene, Daeseungsa Temple, Mungyeong
1113703210000.description: This woodblock work presents an image of the Pure Land assembly in the form of a hanging painting, assembled from 10 carved panels. At the center is Amitabha Buddha, with bodhisattvas, disciples, and guardian deities arranged symmetrically around him, for a total of 24 figures. Made in 1675, it is the oldest extant Joseon-period example of this type.

1113703220100.description: Samguk Sagi, compiled by Kim Busik in 1145, is a foundational historical source for the Three Kingdoms period. This National Treasure copy was printed in Gyeongju-bu in 1573 and sent to Oksanseowon, and it contains three kinds of woodblocks mixed together: the original Goryeo woodblocks, blocks recut in the early Joseon dynasty, and blocks recut again in the reign of King Jungjong. It survives as a complete nine-volume set in good condition.

1111103220200.description: Samguk Sagi, compiled by Kim Busik in 1145, is a foundational historical source for the Three Kingdoms period. This copy was printed from revised woodblocks supplemented up to 1512, and it largely preserves its original form. It is a complete nine-volume set without missing leaves, and it includes both Goryeo and Joseon-period woodblock material.

1111103100000.description: This large white porcelain jar, usually over 40 cm in height, has a round, milky-white form that resembles the full moon. It was made at the Bunwon kilns of the Bureau of Royal Cuisine in Gwangju during the late 17th to early 18th century Joseon period, probably mainly at the Gumsari kiln. Because it was made by joining separately formed upper and lower parts, it was technically difficult to shape and fire.

1113703110000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Bongjeongsa Temple, Andong
1113703110000.description: Daeungjeon is the main Buddhist hall of Bongjeongsa Temple, where the Seokgamoni Triad is enshrined. Based on records found during dismantling and repair in 1962, the building is thought to date to the early Joseon period. It is a three-bay by three-bay hall with a hipped-and-gabled roof and multi-bracket structure.

1113703120000.title_en: Rock-carved Buddha Images at Chilbulam Hermitage, Namsan Mountain, Gyeongju
1113703120000.description: Seven Buddha images are carved on a rocky cliff at Chilbulam Hermitage, with a four-direction Buddha arrangement on one side and a Buddha triad on the back rock face. The main Buddha sits on a lotus throne, flanked by standing bodhisattvas, and the figures are rendered with full, rounded forms and refined carving. They are generally dated to the 8th century of the Unified Silla period.

1113603130000.title_en: Amitabha Triad Wall Painting of Geungnakjeon Hall, Muwisa Temple, Gangjin
1113603130000.description: This wall painting on the front of the rear altar wall in Geungnakjeon Hall depicts Amitabha Buddha seated at the center, with Avalokiteshvara on the left and Ksitigarbha on the right. Along the top are six arhats arranged in pairs, with small Buddha figures above them. It is believed to have been made in 1476 during the reign of King Seongjong of Joseon.

1113603140000.title_en: Illustrated Avatamsaka Sutra Transformation Painting of Songgwangsa Temple, Suncheon
1113603140000.description: This hanging scroll is an illustrated transformation painting of the Avatamsaka Sutra, showing the sermons of the sutra’s seven places and nine assemblies. It was painted on silk with colors and uses a balanced composition with bright red, green, and gold. An inscription records that it was made in 1770 by a group of 12 monk-painters at Ansimsa Temple on Mudeungsan Mountain and later moved to Songgwangsa Temple.

1113703150000.title_en: Stupa Stele of Jijeung Daesa, Bongamsa Temple, Mungyeong
1113703150000.description: This stupa stele commemorates Dosun, also known as Jijeung Daesa, the founder of the Heiyang Seon school branch of the Gosan Seon line. Its scale and the carving of the turtle base and stele crown represent a typical late Unified Silla style, and the inscription, written by Choe Chi-won, is an important source for the history of Buddhism and Seon Buddhism in Silla. The stele was erected in 924 and preserves valuable information on names, places, institutions, and temple administration in late Silla.

1113503160000.title_en: Geungnakjeon Hall of Hwaamsa Temple, Wanju
1113503160000.description: Geungnakjeon is the hall symbolizing the Pure Land of Amitabha Buddha at Hwaamsa Temple. According to records found during repair work in 1981, it was built in 1605 during the reign of King Seonjo of Joseon. The hall is notable for its unique hwangang-style wooden structure, which is the only surviving example in Korea.

1113503170000.title_en: Portrait of King Taejo of Joseon
1113503170000.description: This portrait of Taejo Yi Seong-gye, the founder of Joseon, shows him seated frontally on a throne wearing an ikseon crown and royal dragon robe. The present hanging scroll was recopied in 1872 from an older original, and it is the only surviving Taejo portrait among the many that once existed. It is an important source for the study of early Joseon portrait painting.

1111103310000.description: This stone rain gauge stand was installed in front of Imunwon, an annex of Gyujanggak at Changdeokgung Palace, by royal order of King Jeongjo in 1782. It is made of marble and bears finely carved inscriptions, showing the work of a skilled court artisan. It was moved from its original site in the early 20th century and is now kept at the National Palace Museum of Korea.

1113203320000.description: This is a fully preserved moldered-stone pagoda built of limestone in the Goryeo period. It was erected on a high cliff in connection with the idea of sancheon bibo, or strengthening the energy of the land, and with the cult of enshrined relics. Records on the stele and related materials preserve its repair history and chronology.

1113803330000.title_en: Dry-lacquer Seated Statue of Huirang Daesa, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1113803330000.description: This statue depicts Huirang Daesa, a monk active from the end of Silla into the early Goryeo period, and is the only surviving Korean portrait sculpture of a monk. It is thought to have been made in the first half of the 10th century. The front of the figure was made with dry-lacquer technique, while the back and base combine wood, preserving important evidence of early sculptural technique.

1113403340000.title_en: Album of the Gisa Association and Box
1113403340000.description: This royal court album records the ceremony held in 1719 to mark King Sukjong's entry into the Giseoro, along with portraits of senior officials, documentary texts, and related lists and poems. The set also preserves the inner box, protective wrapper, and outer chest, which are rare examples of the original mounting and storage system. Together they provide important evidence for court painting, royal protocol, and craft techniques of the Joseon period.
1113403340000.material: Ink and color on silk; wood, textile, paper

1113103350000.title_en: Twenty Meritorious Subjects' Alliance Scroll - After the Recording of Bosa Meritorious Subjects
1113103350000.description: This alliance scroll was made in 1694 after a ritual gathering of meritorious subjects and their descendants. It records the text of the oath ceremony, the names of 20 categories of meritorious subjects and a total of 489 direct male-line descendants, and the ritual text for the royal ancestral shrine. It is a valuable historical record for studying the conferral, stripping, and restoration of meritorious titles under King Sukjong.

1113603360000.title_en: Wooden Seated Vairocana Buddha Triad, Hwaeomsa Temple, Gurye
1113603360000.description: This set of three wooden Buddha statues was made in 1635 by the Joseon-period master sculptors Cheongheon, Eungwon, and Ingyun, with their disciples. It represents the Three Bodies Buddha—Vairocana, Rocana, and Shakyamuni—and is the only surviving sculptural example of this iconography in Korea. The set was produced for Daeungjeon during the rebuilding of Hwaeomsa after the Japanese invasions.

1113403370000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Seated Medicine Buddha and Relics, Janggoksa Temple, Cheongyang
1113403370000.description: This gilt-bronze Medicine Buddha statue was made in 1346, as confirmed by a votive inscription found among the inner reliquary objects. It is the only surviving Goryeo-period gilt-bronze Medicine Buddha image and preserves the typical style of 14th-century Buddhist sculpture. The reliquary contents, including a large number of donor names, are also valuable historical sources.

1113803380000.title_en: Wooden Seated Vairocana Buddha and Relics, Beopbojeon Hall, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1113803380000.description: This wooden Vairocana Buddha statue and its inner reliquary objects are thought to date to the late 9th century of Unified Silla, based on style, iconography, and scientific analysis. It is regarded as the oldest surviving wooden Buddha statue in Korea and shows high sculptural quality with features related to ninth-century Seokguram style. The reliquary materials are also important sources for the study of Korean Buddhist history and art history.
1113803380000.material: Wood, with reliquary contents including textiles and scriptures

1112607010001.description: Gwanghallu Pavilion originated from Gwangtongnu Pavilion, reportedly built by the Joseon statesman Hwang Hui during his exile in Namwon. The present complex was rebuilt in 1626 after being destroyed in 1597, and includes the main pavilion, auxiliary pavilion, and moon veranda set around the pond and three islets in Gwanghallu Garden. It is also historically associated with the literary culture of Joseon officials and with the setting of the classic novel Chunhyangjeon.

1121100010000.description: Heunginjimun Gate is the eastern gate of the Seoul City Wall, also known as Dongdaemun Gate. The original gate was built in 1396, rebuilt in 1453, and the present structure was newly built in 1869. It is a two-story gatehouse with an ongseong outer wall, and is the only one of the eight city gates to have such a feature.

1121100020000.description: This bronze bell was cast in 1468 during the reign of King Sejo of Joseon and was used for the New Year’s Eve bell-ringing ceremony at Bosingak until 1985. It was originally kept at Jingnyeongsa Temple, later moved to Wongaksa Temple, and then stored in the bell pavilion after the Imjin War. The bell has inscriptions that record its casting date and is an important example of a Joseon royal bell.

1121100030000.title_en: Great Wonaksa Stele, Site of Wongaksa Temple, Seoul
1121100030000.description: This stele was erected in 1471 to record the founding of Wongaksa Temple. The stele is mounted on a turtle-shaped base and has a dragon carving at the top, showing a revival of earlier monumental forms. Its inscription was written by leading scholars of the time, including Kim Su-on, Seong Im, Seo Geo-jeong, and Jeong Nan-jeong.

1123100040000.title_en: Dangganjiju from the Site of Jungchosa Temple, Anyang
1123100040000.description: This pair of stone pillars supported the flagpole used for hanging a Buddhist banner at a temple entrance. The two pillars stand 85 cm apart, and an inscription on the western pillar records that the stones were selected in 826 and the structure was completed in 827. It is the only known dangganjiju in Korea with an inscription that clearly identifies its date of construction.

1123100060000.title_en: Stupa Stele for State Preceptor Wonjong at the Site of Godalsa Temple, Yeoju
1123100060000.description: This stupa stele commemorates State Preceptor Wonjong, whose secular name was Chanyeu and who died in 958. The stele was erected in 975 and completed in 977 to record his life and achievements. The turtle base and capstone are large and richly carved with dragons, clouds, lotus motifs, and other decorative details.

1123100070000.title_en: Stupa for State Preceptor Wonjong at the Site of Godalsa Temple, Yeoju
1123100070000.description: This stone stupa stands with its stele in the ruins of Godalsa Temple and is one of the best-preserved Buddhist stupas from early Goryeo. It is built on a three-tiered base with an octagonal plan, and the body is carved with door motifs and standing Four Heavenly Kings on four sides. The stele inscription indicates that the stupa was built before 977.

1123100080000.title_en: Stone Buddhist Pedestal from the Site of Godalsa Temple, Yeoju
1123100080000.description: This stone pedestal remains at the temple site after the Buddha image that once stood on it has disappeared. It is a large square pedestal composed of three tiers, with lotus petal carving on the upper and lower sections. Its refined carving style is considered a representative work of Goryeo Buddhist sculpture and is thought to date to the late 10th century.

1113803390000.title_en: Wood Seated Vairocana Buddha and Reliquaries of Daejeokgwangjeon Hall, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1113803390000.description: This is a single wooden seated Vairocana Buddha image now enshrined in Daejeokgwangjeon Hall at Haeinsa Temple, together with 53 reliquary objects placed inside the statue. Based on its style, techniques, and scientific analysis, it is believed to date to the late 9th century and is regarded as the oldest surviving wooden Buddha statue in Korea. The reliquary contents were added over a long period from Goryeo to the early Joseon period and include important scriptures and textiles.

1113503400000.title_en: Reliquaries Excavated from the West Pagoda Site of Mireuksa Temple, Iksan
1113503400000.description: These reliquaries were excavated in 2009 from the sarira chamber of the central pillar stone of the west pagoda site at Mireuksa Temple. They include a gold reliquary inscription dated to 639, a gilt-bronze outer casket, a gold inner casket, and six bronze containers holding beads and offering items. The inscription records the temple’s foundation and the enshrinement of relics under royal patronage in Baekje.

1113403410000.title_en: Long Swords of Admiral Yi Sun-sin
1113403410000.description: This pair of long swords, each with a scabbard, was made in 1594 and belongs to the group of relics associated with Yi Sun-sin. The blades bear inscriptions of verses attributed to Yi Sun-sin, and the tangs are engraved with the makers’ names, Taegwiryun and Lee Museung. They are important for studying Joseon military swords and the combination of Korean and Japanese sword-making techniques.

1113503420000.title_en: Bronze Bell of Naesosa Temple, Buan
1113503420000.description: This bronze bell was cast in 1222 under the supervision of the laymen Heo Baek and Jong Ik, with the artisan Han Chungseo as the maker. The bell’s inscription provides its date, patrons, and casting history, making it a key example of 13th-century Korean bells. Its decoration and form also show both continuity with Unified Silla bell traditions and the distinctive features of Goryeo-period bells.

1115103430000.description: Jukseoru is a pavilion that was originally built at least by the 12th century and was rebuilt in 1403, after which it underwent later additions and repairs. The present structure stands on natural bedrock and combines a central Joseon-period core with later extensions on both sides. It is noted for its open plan, exposed rafters, and long literary and pictorial associations.

1113803440000.description: Yeongnamnu developed from a small pavilion associated with Yeongnamsa Temple and was rebuilt as a government pavilion in 1365. The present complex took shape in 1844, when the main pavilion was enlarged and subsidiary buildings such as Nungpagak, Chimhyu-gak, and Yeosu-gak were arranged around it. It is a large wooden pavilion complex known for its scenic integration with the surrounding landscape.

1113603450000.title_en: Yeongsanhoesangdo and Eight Scenes of the Buddha’s Life from Songgwangsa Temple, Suncheon
1113603450000.description: This set consists of one Yeongsanhoesangdo and eight paintings of the Buddha’s life made together for enshrinement in Yeongsanjeon Hall at Songgwangsa Temple. The colophon records the date as 1725 and names the monk-painters, including Uigyeom. It is an early and important example of a unified set that combines a Yeongsanhoesangdo with an Eight Scenes cycle using the iconography of Seokssi wonryu eunghwasajeok.

1112412260001.description: This Buddhist painting was made in 1729, and its colophon names the monk-painter Uigyeom along with several other painters. It depicts Śākyamuni preaching on Vulture Peak, with the central Buddha emphasized and the surrounding figures arranged to create a sense of upward movement. Gold lines and fine detailing were used extensively in the robes and figures.

1123100090000.title_en: Hyeono Guksa Stele at Seobongsa Temple Site, Yongin
1123100090000.description: This stele was erected in 1185 to commemorate the life of Hyeono Guksa. Only the stele remains at the former temple site; no trace of the associated stupa has been found. It has a simple form with a granite base and a slate stele body, and is considered to show a new late Goryeo style of stone stele.

1122300100000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Jangjeong-ri, Ganghwa
1122300100000.description: This stone pagoda was collapsed and restored in 1960.
