It is believed to have been built during the reign of King Yejong in the early Joseon period. The building is a small but well-balanced structure with a hipped-and-gabled roof and the multi-bracket style.

1123401810000.title_en: Lower Daeungjeon Hall of Janggoksa Temple, Cheongyang
1123401810000.description: Janggoksa Temple has a distinctive layout with upper and lower Daeungjeon halls placed on different levels along the slope of the mountain. The Lower Daeungjeon Hall is thought to have been built in the mid-Joseon period and combines a simple gabled roof with the ornate multi-bracket style. Inside, the floor is boarded and the altar enshrines a gilt-bronze seated Buddha from the late Goryeo period.

1123701820000.description: Imcheonggak was built in 1519 by Lee Myeong, a former junior official in the Ministry of Justice, and later served as the house of Lee Sang-ryong, the first prime minister of the Provisional Government of Korea in Shanghai. Although part of the complex was removed during the construction of the Central Line railway, the surviving house remains an important example of a large aristocratic residence. The separately designated Gunjajeong pavilion is a mid-Joseon annex with an L-shaped plan and hipped-and-gabled roof.

1122502090000.description: This detached house belonged to Song Jun-gil (1606–1672), a Joseon scholar-official who served as Daesaheon, Ijo Panseo, and Bypjo Panseo. It is a modestly sized detached building of the Joseon period, with a main hall and ondol rooms arranged around an open wooden floor, and it has no visible chimney; an inscription on the building records repairs and rebuilding in the 17th and early 18th centuries.

1123702100000.description: Jeonggyodang Hall is the lecture hall of Dosan Seowon, a private Neo-Confucian academy founded to honor the learning and virtue of Toegye Yi Hwang (1501–1570). The hall was originally built in 1574 and repaired in 1969, and it consists of a wooden floor hall and ondol room under a hipped-and-gabled roof.

1123702110000.title_en: Sangdeoksa Shrine and Sammun Gate, Dosan Seowon, Andong
1123702110000.description: Sangdeoksa is the shrine at the rear of Dosan Seowon that enshrines the spirit tablet of Toegye Yi Hwang. It was first built in 1574 and later repaired in 1969, and the complex includes the main shrine and a three-bay gate built in a simpler gabled style.

1123802120000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Guryongsa Temple, Changnyeong
1123802120000.description: This hall at Guryongsa Temple houses three Buddha images: Bhaisajyaguru, Shakyamuni, and Amitabha, which is unusual for a main Buddha hall. A record found during repairs indicates that the building was first built in 1401, destroyed in the Japanese invasions, and rebuilt in 1617.

1123202140000.description: Daeseongjeon is the main shrine of Gangneung Hyanggyo, where Confucius and other Chinese sages are worshipped. The shrine was built in 1413, and it is a five-bay wooden building with a gabled roof, a column-top bracket system, a stone-paved floor, and an exposed-rafter ceiling.

1121102150000.title_en: Seated Rock-carved Buddha in Gugidong, Bukhansan, Seoul
1121102150000.description: This rock-cut Buddha is carved in relief on a large cliff face, with a separately inserted octagonal head cover protecting the face. It is considered a representative early Goryeo rock-carved seated Buddha, combining a firm face and flat body form with some abstract treatment in the drapery.

1123302160000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Buddha in Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123302160000.description: This large rock-carved Buddha at Beopjusa Temple is shown seated on a chair-like seat, together with a nearby relief of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva. It is a representative Goryeo-period Maitreya image, with a rounded face, long ears, and a distinctive pose with one hand raised and the other held forward.

1123402170000.title_en: Stone Standing Maitreya Bodhisattva, Daejosa Temple, Buyeo
1123402170000.description: This is a large stone standing Maitreya Bodhisattva from the Goryeo period, comparable in scale and style to the famous stone Maitreya Bodhisattva at Gwanchoksa Temple in Nonsan. It stands about 10 meters tall, wears a square crown with twin canopies and small bells, and has a broad, flat face with massive, heavy drapery.

1123702010000.title_en: Rock-Carved Buddhist Images at Tapgok Valley, Namsan Mountain, Gyeongju
1123702010000.description: This group of rock-carved Buddhist images was made at the site of a temple called Sininsa during Unified Silla. On the large square boulder, various figures such as a triad, separate bodhisattvas, Buddhas, monks, and flying apsaras are arranged on different faces along with two bodhi trees and a tathāgata figure.

1123702020000.description: These are two surviving stone lions from the four lion figures once placed on the upper surface of the base of the Three-Story Stone Pagoda in Gwandok-ri, Uiseong. The pair was likely made in the early 9th century, and one rare detail is a cub nursing beneath the female lion.

1123702030000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha Statue from Bakgok-ri, Cheongdo
1123702030000.description: This seated image of Shakyamuni Buddha was damaged in a major fire in 1928, including the halo, pedestal, and much of the body. Despite the damage, it is considered a refined stone Buddha statue of the late Unified Silla period, with a style similar to the main Buddha of Seokguram Grotto.

1123602040000.title_en: Samhyeon Wonchan Gwamun on the Universal Gate Chapter of the Lotus Sutra
1123602040000.description: This woodblock-printed book is a commentary on Chapter 25, the Universal Gate Chapter, of the Lotus Sutra, explaining the text in an easy-to-read format. Although the colophon states that it was made in 1099 during King Sukjong's reign, it was reprinted in the Joseon period by the Gamgyeongdogam using an earlier text as the original.

1123602050000.description: This is a woodblock-printed Buddhist text consisting of volumes 13 and 14 of a commentary on the Abhidharma-samuccaya-śāstra. The extant copy was re-engraved and printed in the Joseon period from a Goryeo-era text, and its colophon records the year 1093.

1123602060000.description: This woodblock-printed book contains volumes 1 and 2 of Hyejeong's commentary on the Lotus Sutra. It was originally published in 1095 and the surviving copy was reprinted in the Joseon period by the Gamgyeongdogam from an earlier Goryeo text.

1123602070000.description: This is a woodblock-printed book containing volumes 4 and 5 of a commentary and notes on the Diamond Sutra. It was reprinted in the Joseon period by the Gamgyeongdogam from a Goryeo collection, and the surviving colophon preserves the record of the original 1098 publication.

1123702080000.title_en: Copper Jar from Unmunsa Temple, Cheongdo
1123702080000.description: This dark-colored copper jar is thought to have been used as a Buddhist vessel at a temple, possibly as a nectar jar. An inscription records a repair in 1067, so the object is believed to have been made earlier, probably in the late Silla or early Goryeo period.

1123402190000.title_en: Stone Standing Triad of the Buddha at Gaetaesa Temple Site, Nonsan
1123402190000.description: This stone triad is thought to have been made when Gaetaesa Temple was founded in 936 to commemorate King Taejo of Goryeo's victory over Later Baekje. The central Buddha has a broad face and heavy proportions, while the two bodhisattvas are more elaborately carved. It is regarded as a notable early Goryeo local stone Buddhist sculpture that reflects a new style after Unified Silla.

1123702200000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha at Bukjiri, Yeongju (1963-1)
1123702200000.description: This seated Buddha was originally located at a temple site beyond the eastern side of Buseoksa Temple and was later moved to its present site. It is believed to have been made by the same sculptor as the other statue in the pair, and shows the calm, human-like style and fine parallel robe folds characteristic of late 9th-century Unified Silla Vairocana images. The octagonal pedestal is carved with offering bodhisattvas on each side.

1123702200200.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha at Bukjiri, Yeongju (1963-2)
1123702200200.description: This seated Buddha was originally located at a temple site beyond the eastern side of Buseoksa Temple and was later moved to its present site. It is believed to have been made by the same sculptor as the other statue in the pair, and shows the calm, human-like style and fine parallel robe folds characteristic of late 9th-century Unified Silla Vairocana images. The octagonal pedestal is carved with offering bodhisattvas on each side.

1123702210000.title_en: Rock-carved Triad of the Buddha and Seated Buddha at Gahung-dong, Yeongju
1123702210000.description: This rock-carved image consists of a main Buddha flanked by two standing bodhisattvas carved on a cliff face. The main Buddha has a large body, a round face, and a dignified expression, with a mandorla and lotus pedestal carved in relief from the natural rock. The work is considered a representative realist Buddhist carving of Unified Silla.

1123802220000.title_en: Rock-carved Standing Buddha at Chiin-ri, Hapcheon
1123802220000.description: This large rock-carved Buddha image is engraved on the side of a boulder along the road to the summit of Gayasan, behind Haeinsa Temple. The Buddha has a large high topknot, a square face, long ears, and a strong, upright posture, with the robe and hand gestures carved in a simplified but forceful manner. It is estimated to date to around the 9th century.

1123202230000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Dopiansa Temple, Cheorwon
1123202230000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands in front of the main hall of Dopiansa Temple. It has an unusual two-tiered base made with octagonal stones, and the roof stones have stepped supports that reflect features seen in late 9th-century Unified Silla pagodas. It is thought to have been built around 865, when the temple was founded.

1123402240000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Seongbok-ri, Seocheon
1123402240000.description: This Goryeo-period pagoda closely follows the style of the five-story stone pagoda at Jeongnimsa Temple Site in Buyeo, the Baekje model it most faithfully imitates. The base and body stones are arranged like the posts and walls of a wooden building, and the broad roof stones and finial show the spread of Baekje-style pagoda traditions in the region. Although the proportions are uneven, it is important for understanding the local transmission of this style.

1123102250000.title_en: Multistory Stone Pagoda of Silleuksa Temple, Yeoju
1123102250000.description: This pagoda stands in front of Geungnakbojeon Hall at Silleuksa Temple and is built with a two-tiered base and multiple stories above it. It follows the general stone-pagoda tradition of Unified Silla and Goryeo, but each part is made from single slabs of stone and shows distinctive carving in the base and roof stones. It is believed to have been erected in 1472 during a major renovation of the temple.

1123102260000.title_en: Multi-story Brick Pagoda of Silleuksa Temple, Yeoju
1123102260000.description: This brick pagoda stands on a scenic rock overlooking the lower reaches of the Han River. It is built on a two-tier stone base with three stepped platforms and a six-story brick body, though an added upper body gives it the appearance of seven stories. The pagoda has been repaired several times, and the surviving brick patterns suggest an early Goryeo date.

1123802270000.title_en: Inscribed Stele for the Construction of Inyangsa Temple, Changnyeong
1123802270000.description: This stele records the dates of construction for the bell, pagoda, main hall, and other buildings of Inyangsa Temple and related temples, along with the quantities of grain used. The back of the stele is carved with a monk figure, and the inscription shows varied script forms beyond the usual standard cursive style of the time. It is a valuable record of temple construction in the height of Unified Silla.

1123102280000.title_en: Stone Stupa of Bojejonja at Silleuksa Temple, Yeoju
1123102280000.description: This stone stupa enshrines the relics of Naong, also known as Bojejonja, behind Silleuksa Temple. It sits on a broad single-tier base with two supporting layers and a bell-shaped body topped by a large jewel ornament. It was erected in 1379 and is a representative example of late Goryeo stone stupa style.

1123102290000.title_en: Stele for Bojejonja at Silleuksa Temple, Yeoju
1123102290000.description: This is the funerary stele for Naong, known as Bojejonja, enshrined at Silleuksa Temple. It consists of a base with three tiers, a stele body, and a roof stone, with lotus designs carved on the upper surface of the base and stone pillars supporting the sides of the body. The inscription was composed by Yi Saek and written by Han Su in 1379.

1123102300000.title_en: Stone Stela for the Daejanggak Repository of Silleuksa Temple, Yeoju
1123102300000.description: This stele records the construction of Daejanggak, a repository for Buddhist scriptures that once stood west of Geungnakjeon Hall at Silleuksa Temple. The stele has a long rectangular base, a body supported by side pillars, and a roof stone, and its simplified form reflects late Goryeo stele style. It was erected in 1383.

1123102310000.title_en: Stone Lantern in Front of the Stone Stupa of Bojejonja at Silleuksa Temple, Yeoju
1123102310000.description: This octagonal stone lantern stands on a hillside northwest of Silleuksa Temple. It has a three-part base, a lantern chamber carved with flying celestial figures and dragons, and a roof stone with upturned corners. It was erected together with the stone stupa and stele in 1379.

1123402320000.title_en: Stone Lantern of Gwangchuksa Temple, Nonsan
1123402320000.description: This square stone lantern stands in front of the large stone Buddha at Gwangchuksa Temple. It has a three-part base, a two-story lantern chamber, and a roof stone topped with a flame-shaped finial, with large lotus designs carved on the base. It is believed to date to 968, during the reign of King Gwangjong of Goryeo.

1123402330000.title_en: Stone Lantern of Muryangsa Temple, Buyeo
1123402330000.description: This octagonal stone lantern stands in front of the main hall at Muryangsa Temple. It has a three-part base, a lantern chamber with openings on four of its eight sides, and a roof stone with gently upturned corners. It is thought to date to around the 10th century, late Unified Silla to early Goryeo.

1123502340000.description: This stone lantern was originally erected in the Wanju area and was moved to its present location during the Japanese colonial period. It has a three-tiered base, a shaft carved with dragon motifs in clouds, an octagonal light chamber with alternating window openings and Four Heavenly Kings reliefs, and an octagonal roof slab; the top finial is missing. It is thought to have been made around the 10th century in the early Goryeo period, while retaining features of late Unified Silla style.

1121102350000.title_en: Banner Pole Supports at Janguisaji Temple Site, Seoul
1121102350000.description: These are the two stone supports for a banner pole once standing at the entrance of a temple site now occupied by Segeomjeong Elementary School. The supports are plain and sturdy, with slightly chamfered outer edges and round holes on the inner faces for fastening the banner pole. Their exact date is unknown, but they are believed to be a Unified Silla-period work.

1123502360000.title_en: Banner Pole Supports at Mireuksa Temple Site, Iksan
1123502360000.description: Two stone supports for a banner pole stand about 90 meters apart on the south side of the Mireuksa Temple site, and they are considered to have been erected at the same time because their size, style, and construction method are identical. The bases are largely destroyed and buried, while the surviving supports are plain, with banded decoration on the outer faces and three holes on the inner faces for fixing the pole. They are thought to date to after the middle Unified Silla period.

1121102380000.title_en: White Porcelain Incense Burner with Baksan-shaped Lid
1121102380000.description: This white porcelain incense burner, said to have been excavated from a Goryeo tomb near Gaeseong, is 8.5 cm high and 8.1 cm in diameter. It has a rounded body, three curved rabbit-tail-shaped legs, and a hemispherical lid modeled after layered mountains, with one large opening at the top and seven smaller openings below for the smoke to escape. It is believed to have been made in the 12th century and reflects both Goryeo white porcelain and early Southern Song celadon characteristics.

1123702390000.title_en: Buncheong Jar with Inlaid Peony Design
1123702390000.description: This early Joseon buncheong ware bottle is 28 cm high, with a mouth diameter of 5.8 cm and a base diameter of 17 cm. It is decorated with an openwork-style inlay technique, with white peony scrolls inlaid across the body and black inlay added between the petals and vines to heighten the contrast. The form shows the transition from the more upright and compact maebyeong style of Goryeo to the more curved early Joseon style.

1121102400000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Underglaze Cobalt and Openwork Peony and Scroll Design
1121102400000.description: This Joseon-period white porcelain jar is 26.7 cm high, with an opening diameter of 14.25 cm, and has a hollowed, openwork outer body surrounding an inner vessel. The outer surface is decorated with openwork peony blossoms, stems, and leaves, while the shoulder has cobalt-painted vine patterns and the lower body has a relief band of floral motifs. It is believed to have been made in the late 18th century, probably at a kiln in Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do.

1123702420000.title_en: Wontongjeon Hall of Gaemoksa Temple, Andong
1123702420000.description: Gaemoksa Temple was originally called Heungguksa and is said to have been founded by Uisang during the reign of King Sinmun of Silla. The Wontongjeon Hall, which enshrines Avalokiteshvara, is believed to have been built in 1457 because a record found during repairs in 1969 bore the date 'Tianshun first year' (天順元年). It is a three-bay-by-three-bay hall with a gabled roof, a dancheong-free interior ceiling with exposed members, and an ondol-heated main space, making it an unusual early Joseon example.

1122202430000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Buddha at Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122202430000.description: This Buddha image was carved into a rock face on the right side of the entrance to Donghwasa Temple. The figure is placed high on the cliff and gives the impression of descending through the clouds, with a full face, a short neck with three folds, a straight torso, a boat-shaped nimbus, and a cloud-shaped pedestal. Based on its rounded face, ornate pedestal, and halo treatment, it is considered a 9th-century work of the late Unified Silla period.

1123702520000.title_en: Stele for Wongjin Guksa at Bogyeongsa Temple, Pohang
1123702520000.description: This stele records the life and deeds of Wongjin Guksa, a mid-Goryeo Buddhist monk enshrined at Bogyeongsa Temple. The stele was completed in 1224, three years after his death, with the text composed by Yi Gong-ro and the calligraphy written by Kim Hyo-in.

1123802530000.title_en: Stone Lantern of Cheongnyangsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123802530000.description: This stone lantern stands beside the three-story stone pagoda inside Cheongnyangsa Temple. It is an octagonal lantern with a lantern chamber, roof stone, and finial, and is thought to date to the late 9th century based on its style.

1122202540000.description: These stone pillars supported the flagpole used for temple banners at the entrance of Donghwasa Temple. The pillars are undecorated except for simple surface treatment and are considered a late Silla work based on their style and on the temple’s founding date.

1123702550000.description: These two stone pillars supported the flagpole used for temple banners at the entrance of Buseoksa Temple. They are simply carved and are considered an early Unified Silla work on stylistic grounds.

1123402560000.title_en: Iron Flagpole at Gapsa Temple, Gongju
1123402560000.description: This is an iron flagpole supported by stone pillars, located on the southeast slope of Gapsa Temple. It is said to have been erected in 680, though the text notes that the exact basis is uncertain and that its style fits the middle Unified Silla period.

1123402570000.title_en: Monk’s Stupa at Gapsa Temple, Gongju
1123402570000.description: This octagonal monk’s stupa was moved in 1917 and re-erected in front of Daejeokjeon Hall at Gapsa Temple. It has a three-tiered base with carved animals, musicians, guardian figures, and roof stones, and is regarded as a fine example of Goryeo stupa carving.

1122202580000.title_en: Monk’s Stupa with Lion and Musician Decoration, Sangyeok-dong, Daegu
1122202580000.description: This octagonal monk’s stupa has a three-tiered base, a low main body, and a roof stone with carved lotus, incense burner, and flying celestial beings. It was moved from a private residence in Daegu to the Kyungpook National University Museum, and both the original site and the monk enshrined are unknown.

1123102590000.title_en: Reliquary Set from the Sarita Pagoda of Sujongsa Temple, Namyangju
1123102590000.description: These relic-related objects were found when the stone stupa at Sujongsa Temple was repaired and re-erected. The set includes a celadon covered jar, a gold nine-story pagoda, and a silver gilt reliquary, with the gold and silver containers originally placed inside the celadon jar.

1122202440000.title_en: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha of Biroam Hermitage, Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122202440000.description: This seated Vairocana Buddha statue, 1.29 meters high, is believed to have been made at the same time as the three-story stone pagoda at Biroam Hermitage. It has a round face, a restrained expression, a boat-shaped halo, and a traditional Vairocana hand gesture. The work is considered a representative example of 9th-century Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture.

1123702450000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha of Gahanggasa Temple Site, Gimcheon
1123702450000.description: This 1.22-meter-high seated Buddha at the site of Gahanggasa Temple is badly damaged in several places. The face is round with a mysterious smile, and the drapery closely follows the body in smooth folds. It is estimated to have been made around the time of the temple's three-story stone pagoda, in the reign of King Gyeongdeok in 758.

1123702460000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha of Gounsa Temple, Uiseong
1123702460000.description: This Buddha statue is almost completely preserved and retains its pedestal and halo. It has a square face, small facial features, a developed chest, and a slightly raised shoulder line, along with a boat-shaped halo decorated with lotus and vine designs. The statue shows the characteristic style of 9th-century Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture.

1122202470000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Biroam Hermitage, Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122202470000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands in front of Daejeokgwangjeon Hall at Biroam Hermitage and is built on a two-tiered base. The pagoda follows the later Unified Silla style, with neatly proportioned tiers, slightly upturned eaves, and finials including the lotus-bud ornament. An inscription on the reliquary indicates that it was erected in 863 to pray for the repose of King Minae.

1122202480000.title_en: East and West Three-Story Stone Pagodas of Geumdangam Hermitage, Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122202480000.description: These two pagodas stand side by side in front of Geungnakjeon Hall at Geumdangam Hermitage, each built on a two-tiered base with a three-story body. The east pagoda was later repaired in part, while the west pagoda retains its original form more clearly; both reflect the typical late Unified Silla pagoda style. Excavation during restoration in 1957 uncovered 99 small pagodas and a reliquary container.

1123702490000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Buseoksa Temple, Yeongju
1123702490000.description: This stone pagoda stands east of Muryangsujeon Hall at Buseoksa Temple and is built on a two-tiered base with a three-story body. It is said to have been made when the temple was founded in 676, during the reign of King Munmu. When dismantled and restored in 1956, fragments of a metal pagoda, Buddha statues, and beads were found inside.

1122102500000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Beomeosa Temple, Busan
1122102500000.description: This pagoda stands in front of Daeungjeon Hall at Beomeosa Temple and is built on a two-tiered base with a three-story body. Its base is decorated with large carved cushion patterns rather than corner pillars, and the later Unified Silla style is also seen in the thin, flat roof stones. It is recorded as having been erected during the reign of King Heungdeok of Silla.

1123702510000.title_en: Stele of State Preceptor Daegak at Seonbongsa Temple, Chilgok
1123702510000.description: This stele was erected to honor the achievements of State Preceptor Daegak, who established the Cheontae school and helped complete the Sokjanggyeong. The stele has a square base, a body stone, and a capstone, with lotus designs on the base and vine patterns on the capstone. It was erected in 1132, and the inscription was written by the monk In and composed by Imjon.

1122202680000.title_en: Buncheong Flattened Bottle with Inlaid Lotus Design
1122202680000.description: This flattened bottle is made of buncheong ware, a distinctive early Joseon ceramic tradition that developed after inlaid celadon declined. It is decorated with stamped motifs, white slip, and inlaid lotus, chrysanthemum, and vine designs on both the body and base.

1123402690000.title_en: Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma, Volume 1
1123402690000.description: This illuminated sutra was copied in silver lettering on dark blue paper and is folded in an accordion style. The cover has decorative patterns and the opening frontispiece illustration is finely executed. It is generally attributed to the Goryeo period on the basis of its calligraphic style.
1123402690000.material: Ink and silver on dark blue paper

1123402690200.title_en: Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma, Volumes 2, 4, 5, and 6
1123402690200.description: These four fascicles are part of a seven-volume illuminated Lotus Sutra copied in silver lettering on dark blue paper in 1422. They were made at the request of the monk Deokmyeong for the rebirth of his mother in paradise.
1123402690200.material: Ink and silver on dark blue paper

1122102690300.title_en: Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma, Volume 3
1122102690300.description: This volume is one of the seven fascicles of an illuminated Lotus Sutra copied in silver lettering on dark blue paper in 1422 at the request of the monk Deokmyeong for his mother's rebirth in paradise. The cover is decorated with four jeweled-flower motifs in gold and silver, and the opening frontispiece is painted in gold.
1122102690300.material: Ink and gold and silver on dark blue paper

1121102690400.title_en: Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma, Volume 7 (2007)
1121102690400.description: This volume is one of the seven fascicles of an illuminated Lotus Sutra copied in silver lettering on dark blue paper in 1422 at the request of the monk Deokmyeong for his mother's rebirth in paradise. The cover is decorated with jeweled-flower motifs, and the opening frontispiece is painted in gold.
1121102690400.material: Ink and gold and silver on dark blue paper

1123402700000.title_en: Sutra of the Lotus Flower of the Wonderful Dharma, Volume 6
1123402700000.description: This illuminated sutra was copied in gold lettering on dark blue paper and belongs to the sixth volume of the seven-volume Lotus Sutra. An inscription at the end records that it was made in 1388 through the patronage of No Yurin.
1123402700000.material: Ink and gold on dark blue paper

1122202710000.description: This is the tenth and final volume of the Lengyan Sutra, copied in silver lettering on white paper made from hemp. An inscription at the end states that it was made in 1356 by Yi Bang-han to pray for the repose of his mother.
1122202710000.material: Ink and silver on hemp paper

1123502720000.description: Jangsu Hyanggyo was established in 1407 as a state-run local educational institution and was later moved to its present site in 1686. Daeseongjeon Hall is the building where Confucius and other sages were enshrined and worshipped, and it preserves the form of an early Joseon hyanggyo hall.

1123602600000.title_en: Diary of Miam, by Yu Hee-chun, and Woodblocks of Miamjip
1123602600000.description: This designated group consists of the handwritten diary of Yu Hee-chun (1513–1577), a scholar-official of the Joseon period, and the woodblocks used to print his collected works, Miamjip. The surviving diary covers the 11 years from 1567 to 1577, with some gaps, and records both official affairs and his personal daily life in detail. It was later used as a basic source for the compilation of the Veritable Records of King Seonjo.

1123702610000.description: This is the autograph diary of Gwon Beol (1478–1548), a scholar-official of the Joseon period. It consists of six volumes: Haneon Ilgi, Danghu Ilgi, Seungseon-si Ilgi, and Shinchangnyeong Chudan Ilgi, recording his official life in the royal secretariat and related political affairs. The diaries were used as source material for the Veritable Records of King Jungjong.

1123702620000.description: Geunsarok is a Neo-Confucian primer compiled in Song China by Ye Cai, selecting key texts such as Zhou Dunyi's Taijitu Shuo and Zhang Zai's Xi Ming. This copy was presented in 1370 by the scholar Pak Sang-chung to Yi In-min when he was appointed magistrate of Jinju. It was re-carved from an older edition, and the volume was later highly valued in Joseon scholarship.

1123602630000.description: Hasadang is a monks' living quarters at Songgwangsa Temple, located on a higher terrace behind Daeungjeon Hall. The building has three bays in front and two bays on the side, with an ondol room, a porch, and a kitchen, and it has a simple gable roof. It is an important example of a Joseon-period monks' quarters building.

1123802640000.title_en: Stone Standing Buddha of Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123802640000.description: This stone standing Buddha, now enshrined at Haeinsa Temple, has lost its halo and pedestal, and its neck, shoulders, arms, and feet are damaged or missing. The Buddha shows the late Unified Silla style, with a slender body, a long oval face, and highly formalized drapery. The figure is a valuable example of late Silla Buddhist sculpture.

1123802650000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha of Cheongnyangsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123802650000.description: This statue is a complete stone Buddha with the body, pedestal, and halo all preserved. It has a small ushnisha, a full round face, broad shoulders, and a powerful, well-modeled body; the pedestal is decorated with bodhisattvas, lotus motifs, and guardian figures. It is considered an excellent 9th-century Buddhist sculpture of Unified Silla.

1123802660000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Cheongnyangsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123802660000.description: This is a Unified Silla stone pagoda standing in front of Daeungjeon Hall at Cheongnyangsa Temple. It has a two-tiered stylobate and three stories of body and roof stones, with elegant proportions and lively carving. The pagoda is regarded as a representative stone pagoda of the 9th century.

1123502670000.title_en: Stone Lantern of Jingusaji Temple Site, Imsil
1123502670000.description: This stone lantern was moved from its original location and consists of a lower base, a central post, a fire chamber, a roof stone, and a partial finial. The surfaces are decorated with large reliefs of lotus flowers, cloud patterns, and decorative motifs, showing skilled stone carving. It is a large and balanced Unified Silla stone lantern.

1123602740000.title_en: Stupa of Gwangjaseonsa, Taean Temple, Gokseong
1123602740000.description: This Goryeo-period stupa at the entrance of Taean Temple enshrines the relics of Gwangjaseonsa, also known as Yun Da. The octagonal stone stupa has a complete and balanced form, with elaborate carvings including lotus motifs, guardian figures, and a largely intact finial.

1123602750000.title_en: Stele for Stupa of Gwangjaseonsa, Taean Temple, Gokseong
1123602750000.description: This stele records the life of the Goryeo monk Gwangjaseonsa Yun Da, whose stupa stands at Taean Temple. The stele body is damaged and much of the inscription is difficult to read, but the remaining parts and the carved turtle base and capstone show refined sculpture of the early Goryeo period.

1123502760000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Balsan-ri, Gunsan
1123502760000.description: This stone pagoda was originally at the site of Bongnimsa Temple in Wanju and was later moved to its present location. It originally had five stories on a two-tiered base, but now only four stories remain, and the pagoda is noted for its balanced form and the simple beauty of Goryeo stone pagodas.

1123502780000.title_en: White Paper Ink Manuscript of the Lotus Sutra
1123502780000.description: This manuscript is a copy of the Lotus Sutra written in ink on white paper and divided into seven volumes. A record at the end of volume seven shows that it was made in 1415 by Lady Yi to pray for the repose of her husband, Yu Geun.

1123502790000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Seated Statue, Seonunsa Temple, Gochang
1123502790000.description: This gilt-bronze Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva statue is housed at Seonunsa Temple and is thought to date to the early Joseon period. The figure wears a hood, has a rounded face and heavy, formal drapery, and shows the restrained style seen in early Joseon Buddhist sculpture.

1123502800000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Seated Statue, Doseoram, Seonunsa Temple, Gochang
1123502800000.description: This gilt-bronze Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva statue is enshrined at Doseoram in Seonunsa Temple and reflects the style of late Goryeo Buddhist sculpture. The figure wears a hood, sits with the right foot placed on the left knee, and holds a small wheel-shaped object in the left hand.

1121102820000.title_en: Twin Lion Stone Lantern from Godalsaji Temple Site, Yeoju
1121102820000.description: This stone lantern from the Godalsaji Temple site was moved to Gyeongbokgung in 1959 and is now in the National Museum of Korea. Its square base is supported by two crouching lions, and the surviving parts suggest it was made in the early Goryeo period, around the 10th century.

1121102830000.description: Geumbo is a geomungo score compiled by An Sang and published in woodblock print in 1572. It is the oldest extant printed musical score of its kind and includes explanations of notation, diagrams, and scores for several pieces, including material on the only surviving source for dangbipa music.

1121102840000.description: This gilt-bronze standing Buddha is 38.2 cm high and is now in the National Museum of Korea. The serene face, with closed eyes and a faint smile, and the natural drapery and posture show the characteristics of Unified Silla sculpture influenced by earlier Northern Wei styles.

1121102850000.description: This gilt-bronze standing bodhisattva, now in the National Museum of Korea, is said to have been excavated in Geochang, Gyeongsangnam-do. Its long neck, cylindrical body, stylized drapery, and the way it holds a jewel with both hands suggest a date in the late 6th or early 7th century.

1121102860000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Inlaid Grapevine and Boy Design
1121102860000.description: This large Goryeo celadon meiping vase stands 41.5 cm high and is unusually large among surviving meiping vessels. The body is filled with white-inlaid grapevines, leaves, and fruit, with a broad floral band on the shoulder and thunder-pattern and lotus bands near the base.

1121102870000.title_en: Buncheong Bottle with Sgraffito and Iron-painted Flower Design
1121102870000.description: This early Joseon buncheong bottle is decorated by coating the surface with white slip, carving away the background, and then applying iron pigment to the carved areas. The resulting contrast between the dark green background and white design creates a free and lively floral composition.

1123102880000.title_en: Bronze Incense Burner with Silver Inlay
1123102880000.description: This incense burner, called an 'hangwan,' was used in Buddhist rituals and has a flared lower body and a round stand. An inscription inside the rim records that it was made in 1346, during the reign of King Chunggu of Goryeo, and that it was originally made for Yonggwangsa Temple at Geumgangsan.

1123502890000.description: Pihyangjeong is a pavilion built as a place of rest and enjoyment of nature, and it is considered one of the finest pavilions in the Honam region. The present structure was expanded in 1716 and shows the mid-Joseon wooden architectural style, with a hipped-and-gabled roof, open sides, and lattice railings around the perimeter.

1123502900000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Seonunsa Temple, Gochang
1123502900000.description: Daeungjeon Hall of Seonunsa Temple is a Buddhist main hall that was rebuilt in 1613 after the earlier hall was destroyed. It has a five-bay front, three bays on the side, a simple gable roof, bracket sets in the Daepo style, and an interior with a well-formed ceiling and painted decoration.

1123502910000.title_en: Daeungbojeon Hall of Naesosa Temple, Buan
1123502910000.description: Daeungbojeon Hall of Naesosa Temple was built in 1633 when the temple was repaired under Monk Cheongmin. The hall has a three-bay plan, a hipped-and-gabled roof, bracket sets in the Daepo style, carved floral door panels, and a large painting of Avalokiteśvara on the rear wall.

1123603010000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda at Bukmireukam Hermitage, Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1123603010000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands at Bukmireukam Hermitage near the summit of Duryunsan Mountain. It has a two-tiered base, with the body stones and roof stones of each story made from single blocks, and surviving finial elements including the finial base and an upward-facing lotus ornament. The pagoda is thought to date to the early Goryeo period.

1123603020000.description: Yaksa-jeon Hall is a Buddhist hall enshrining Yaksa Buddha, the Buddha of healing, at Songgwangsa Temple in Joryeosan Mountain. It is a small building with one bay on each side and a hipped-and-gabled roof. Based on its details, it is believed to date to around the 17th century in the mid-Joseon period.

1123603030000.description: According to temple records, this hall was built in 1639 and repaired in 1736; the present building was restored in 1973. It enshrines a seated statue of Buddha and contains paintings of the Eight Scenes from the Buddha’s life and the Yeongsan Daehwe scene of Buddha’s sermon. The building has three bays in front, two bays on the side, a hipped-and-gabled roof, and a dapo bracket system.

1123603040000.description: This stone rainbow bridge is one of the largest surviving bridges of its kind and is still used by local residents. It was first made in stone in 1729 and rebuilt in 1737 as a three-arch bridge. The bridge has carved dragon heads at the center of the arches, reflecting folk beliefs associated with water and dragons.

1123703050000.description: This stone ice storage was built in 1737 to keep ice for presenting sweetfish from the Nakdonggang River to the king. It is laid out lengthwise north–south, with a northern side entrance, an inclined floor, a central drain, and four arched stone vaults supporting the ceiling. Ventilation holes were built into the structure to regulate the internal temperature.

1123703060000.description: Yangjindang is the old family house of the Pungsan Ryu clan and was the home of Gyemam Ryu Un-ryong (1539–1601). The building has four bays in front, three on the side, a hipped-and-gabled roof, and a verandah-like arrangement around the outer sides, giving it the appearance of an upper-floor house. Its open ceiling exposes the roof framing, and it is regarded as one of the notable large annex residences of the Joseon period.

1123703070000.title_en: Seated Stone Vairocana Buddha at Sudosaam Hermitage, Cheongamsa Temple, Gimcheon
1123703070000.description: This seated stone Buddha image at Sudosaam Hermitage is a Unified Silla period sculpture of Vairocana Buddha, measuring 2.51 m in height. The face is square and full, the drapery is rendered in a restrained and formal manner, and the hands form a distinctive mudra with the left index finger enclosed by the right hand. The pedestal is composed of three parts and includes lotus and animal motifs.

1123503080000.description: Pungnammun Gate was the southern gate of the old Jeonju Eupseong fortress. It was rebuilt in 1768 after earlier destruction, and the current gate was restored through major repair work begun in 1978. The structure has two stories, a hipped-and-gabled roof, and distinctive decorative carving, including dragon heads on the first-floor central pillars.

1123502920000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Gaeamsa Temple, Buan
1123502920000.description: This is the main Buddha hall of Gaeamsa Temple, rebuilt in 1636 and repaired in 1783 and 1913. It is a three-bay by three-bay hip-and-gable building in the Dapo style, with a two-tiered stone platform and elaborate carved bracket sets. The hall is noted for the rich carving on its bracket system and related members.

1123802940000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at the Site of Seungansaji Temple, Hamyang
1123802940000.description: This Goryeo-period pagoda stands at the site of Seungansa Temple and follows the basic form of Unified Silla stone pagodas. It has a two-tiered platform, three-story body, relief carvings of Buddhist figures on the upper platform, and figures of the Four Heavenly Kings on the first-story body. It was moved twice, and a relic container found in 1962 suggests it was first erected in 1494 after being relocated.

1123802950000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha at Yongseondae, Guryongsa Temple, Changnyeong
1123802950000.description: This stone seated Buddha is enshrined on Yongseondae near Guryongsa Temple and sits atop a high rock on a mountain peak. The halo is missing, and the figure shows a rounded face, tight-fitting robes with schematic parallel folds, and a well-proportioned pedestal with lotus motifs. Based on its style, it is thought to date to the late Unified Silla period, around the 9th century.

1123702960000.title_en: Stone Seated Bodhisattva at Sudamam Hermitage, Cheongamsa Temple, Gimcheon
1123702960000.description: This stone seated image is housed in Yakgwangjeon Hall at Sudamam Hermitage in Cheongamsan and is 1.54 meters tall. Although it wears a cylindrical crown and looks like a bodhisattva, the halo, pedestal, and bodily form suggest that it represents a Buddha. The schematic robe folds, formal halo, and pedestal indicate an early Goryeo date.

1123702970000.title_en: East and West Three-story Stone Pagodas at Sudamam Hermitage, Cheongamsa Temple, Gimcheon
1123702970000.description: These paired pagodas stand to the east and west of Daegwangjeon Hall, and a tradition says they were erected by Doseon in 859. The east pagoda has a single-tier base, a first-story body with niches containing seated Buddhas, and a narrow upper body, while the west pagoda has a two-tiered base and seated Buddha figures on the first-story body. Both show features characteristic of the middle to late Unified Silla period.

1123602980000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at the Site of Wonnamsa Temple, Gangjin
1123602980000.description: This three-story stone pagoda remains at the site of Wonnamsa Temple and is built on a single-tier base. Its first-story body is especially tall, while the upper stories become much smaller, and the roof stones are made in a style that recalls wooden pagodas. Because it stands in the former Baekje region and uses a number of Baekje-style features, it is regarded as an important pagoda of the early Goryeo period.

1123602990000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Hwaeomsa Temple, Gurye
1123602990000.description: Daeungjeon Hall is the main Buddha hall of Hwaeomsa Temple and was rebuilt in 1630 by Byeokam. The building has a five-bay by three-bay plan, a hip-and-gable roof, and Dapo bracket sets, and its interior has a coffered ceiling with an ornate canopy over the main Buddhist triad. It is considered an important example of mid-Joseon temple architecture.

1123603000000.title_en: Stone Lion Pagoda in Front of Wontongjeon Hall, Hwaeomsa Temple, Gurye
1123603000000.description: This unusual Unified Silla-period stone pagoda stands in front of Wontongjeon Hall at Hwaeomsa Temple and consists of four lions supporting a long rectangular stone. The upper platform is formed with lion figures, and the body stone has framed panels with carved guardian figures. Its sculptural style suggests a date in the 9th century.

1123503090000.title_en: Seven-Story Stone Pagoda at Cheonggoksa Temple Site, Jeongeup
1123503090000.description: This square-plan stone pagoda stands on the western slope of a hill in Mangje-dong, at the site locally known as Cheonggoksa. It has a low single-tier base and seven stories of the main body, with unusual base construction and lotus carvings on the undersides of the roof stones. It is considered a later Goryeo-period pagoda.

1123803100000.description: This stone ice storage is located beside a road in front of Myeongdeok Elementary School in Changnyeong. Built to store ice, it is oriented north-south with its entrance on the south side, and its interior has a sloped floor, drainage hole, ventilation holes, and a vaulted stone ceiling. An inscription records that it was built in 1742 by local magistrate Sin Seo during King Yeongjo's reign.

1122403110000.description: This diary records how the scholar No In, also known as Geumgye Noin, was captured during the Battle of Namwon Castle in the Imjin War, held in Japan for two years, and later escaped and returned to Korea via Beijing. It covers the period from February 22 to June 27, 1599, though the beginning and end of the text are damaged and missing. The diary also contains information on Korean education, civil service examinations, finance, military affairs, culture, and customs as explained to Chinese scholars.

1123803120000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Sotae-ri, Miryang
1123803120000.description: This stone pagoda stands on a single-tier base and has five stories. Its base and roof stones show distinctive forms, including carved roundels on the base, high first-story body stones, and small lotus ornaments on the corners of the roof stones. A record found in 1919 states that it was built in 1109 during the reign of King Yejong of Goryeo.

1123603130000.title_en: Stele for Jingak Guksa at Wollamsa Temple Site, Gangjin
1123603130000.description: This stele was erected at the site of Wollamsa Temple to honor Jingak Guksa, who founded the temple in the mid-Goryeo period. The stele consists of a tortoise-shaped base and a stele body, with a vivid and realistic carving of the tortoise. The inscription is said to have been composed by Yi Gyu-bo, and the stele is estimated to date to the reign of King Gojong of Goryeo.

1123703140000.title_en: The Lotus Sutra in Gold on Indigo Paper, Volume 3-4
1123703140000.description: This is a copy of the Lotus Sutra written in gold letters on indigo paper, with volumes 3 and 4 surviving. It is in a folding format, and the covers are decorated with floral patterns and the volume titles. The fine script and preserved gold lettering suggest a late Goryeo date.
1123703140000.material: Gold and ink on indigo paper

1123703150000.title_en: The Lotus Sutra in Black Ink on White Paper, Volume 1 and 3
1123703150000.description: This is a manuscript copy of the Lotus Sutra written in black ink on white paper, with volumes 1 and 3 surviving from the original set of seven. The covers have gold floral designs and titles, and volume 3 includes a painted illustration at the beginning. An inscription at the end states that it was made in 1389 by Jang’s wife, Myeou, for the repose of her deceased parents and all beings.

1123703160000.title_en: Stele for Won'eung Guksa at Unmunsa Temple, Cheongdo
1123703160000.description: This stele at Unmunsa Temple records the life and deeds of Won'eung Guksa, a Buddhist monk of the Goryeo period. The stele body survives in three broken sections, while the base and capstone are missing. The inscription says that after his death in 1144, the king bestowed the title of guksa and had the text composed by Yun Eon-i, so the stele is thought to date from after 1145.

1123703170000.title_en: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha, Unmunsa Temple, Cheongdo
1123703170000.description: This Goryeo-period stone seated Buddha is enshrined at Unmunsa Temple in Cheongdo and survives with its halo and pedestal intact. The figure is about 0.63 meters high, and although the surface has been heavily coated with white pigment, the details are relatively rough and plain. It is thought to have been made in the early 10th century, inheriting 9th-century Buddhist sculptural styles.

1123703180000.title_en: Stone Four Heavenly Kings, Unmunsa Temple, Cheongdo
1123703180000.description: These four stone pillars, now placed to the left and right of the Stone Seated Buddha at Unmunsa Temple, are believed to have originally stood on the four sides of the first story of a brick pagoda. Each figure wears armor, holds a weapon, and tramples an evil spirit while surrounded by a circular halo. They are generally dated to around 900, in the late Unified Silla period or the Later Three Kingdoms period.

1123703190000.title_en: Stone Seated Medicine Buddha, Jikjisa Temple, Gimcheon
1123703190000.description: This stone seated Buddha is enshrined at Jikjisa Temple, with the halo and the Buddha carved from a single stone. The left hand holds a medicine jar, identifying the image as the Medicine Buddha. Its restrained details and simplified halo ornament suggest a late Unified Silla style.

1123603200000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda, Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1123603200000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands in front of Eungjinjeon Hall at Daeheungsa Temple. It is a typical Unified Silla stone pagoda built on a two-tiered stylobate, with relief pillar forms carved on the base and each story of the body. Based on details such as the reduced central pillars of the base and the four-step underside of the roof stones, it is thought to date to the late Unified Silla period.

1121103210000.title_en: Bronze Incense Burner with Silver Inlay, Bongeunsa Temple
1121103210000.description: This large Goryeo-period incense burner is 37 cm high and 51 cm in diameter. Its entire surface is inlaid with fine silver threads, with lotus-vine and thunder patterns on the rim, Sanskrit letters and wish-granting jewel motifs on the body, and lotus and vine patterns on the foot. An inscription on the back of the rim records that it was made in 1344, the 5th year of King Chungmok of Goryeo.

1123903220000.description: Gwanddeokjeong is one of the oldest buildings in Jeju and is located in the center of Jeju City. According to historical records, it was first built in 1448 during the reign of King Sejong and later repaired several times; the present structure was repaired in 1969 and is believed to preserve construction methods from around the 17th century. It is a five-bay by four-bay open pavilion with a hipped-and-gabled roof.

1123703230000.description: This stone ice storage facility was dug into the ground to preserve ice. Only four half-arch vaults remain, and the roof has collapsed, but it is still one of the largest surviving ice storage structures in Korea after the one in Gyeongju. An inscription stone beside the entrance records construction details and suggests a date of 1713, in the 39th year of King Sukjong.

1122203250000.title_en: Sarira Reliquaries from the Five-story Brick Pagoda of Songnimsa Temple, Chilgok
1122203250000.description: These relics were discovered in 1959 during dismantling and repair of the Five-story Brick Pagoda at Songnimsa Temple. They include reliquary containers, glass vessels, jade and pearl ornaments, paper fragments, metal fittings, beads, and a celadon lidded box, showing that a variety of Unified Silla and Goryeo period objects had been placed inside the pagoda. Among them, the inlaid celadon round box is thought to be a fine work from the late 12th-century peak of Goryeo celadon.

1123403260000.title_en: A Set of Relics of Yi Sun-sin
1123403260000.description: This set comprises relics associated with Admiral Yi Sun-sin, kept at Hyeonchungsa in Asan, Chungcheongnam-do. It includes a jade ornament worn on a headgear, two waist belts and belt cases, and two sets of peach-shaped cups and stands. These objects are said to have been used during the Imjin War and are important materials for understanding the period and Yi Sun-sin's legacy.

1123703270000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Bingsansa Temple Site, Uiseong
1123703270000.description: This pagoda stands below Bingsan on a branch of Bohyeonsan in Uiseong. It is a stone pagoda made by dressing stones to the size of bricks, and it imitates the Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Tap-ri, Uiseong. It is estimated to have been built sometime between the late Unified Silla and early Goryeo periods.

1121103280000.description: This small gilt-bronze Buddha, 29 cm in height, is preserved at the National Museum of Korea. Although the halo and pedestal are missing, the statue is relatively well preserved, and the Medicine Buddha is identified by the medicine jar held in the left hand. It is thought to have been made around the 8th century.

1123403290000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha at Gunsuri, Buyeo
1123403290000.description: This Buddha statue was discovered in 1936 during an excavation of the Baekje temple site at Gunsuri, Buyeo. It is made of soapstone and seated on a tall square pedestal. The soft, gentle facial expression and the restrained drapery reflect the mature style of mid-6th-century Baekje Buddhist sculpture.

1123403300000.title_en: Gilt-Bronze Standing Bodhisattva at Gunsuri, Buyeo
1123403300000.description: This gilt-bronze bodhisattva was found in 1936 during the excavation of the Baekje temple site at Gunsuri, Buyeo. It wears an ornate crown, and its rounded face and warm smile are characteristic of Baekje sculpture. The form and hand gestures indicate a 6th-century Baekje work.

1121103310000.title_en: Gilt-Bronze Maitreya Bodhisattva in Half-Lotus Position (1963)
1121103310000.description: This Maitreya Bodhisattva statue is shown seated with the left leg lowered and the right hand raised to touch the cheek with two fingers in a contemplative pose. The form is slender and the drapery is simplified and stylized, while the lotus pedestal is unusually elaborate. It is believed to be a late Three Kingdoms period work.

1121103320000.title_en: Iron Seated Śākyamuni Buddha of Hasachang-dong, Hanam
1121103320000.description: This iron seated Buddha was found at a temple site in Hasachang-ri, Gwangju-gun, Gyeonggi-do, and is a Goryeo-period work. The rounded face, sharply defined eyes, and concise drapery show the characteristics of early Goryeo Buddhist sculpture. Its strong shoulders and prominent chest continue the style of the Seokguram main Buddha.

1121103330000.description: This small gilt-bronze standing bodhisattva is 15.1 cm tall and shows the characteristic features of bodhisattva statues from the Three Kingdoms period. The figure wears an unusual crown, and the face has a calm smile; the drapery crosses in an X-shape and flows outward. Although the halo and pedestal are missing, the statue is nearly complete.

1121103440000.title_en: Celadon Ewer with Molded Reed and Goose Design
1121103440000.description: This Goryeo celadon ewer was made in the 12th century and stands 34.2 cm high. One side of the body is decorated with reeds by the water and a pair of geese, and the other side with a pair of mandarin ducks resting under a weeping willow. It is modeled after the form of the famous bronze ewer with inlaid design, but made in celadon.

1121103450000.title_en: White Porcelain Meiping Vase with Inlaid Peony Design
1121103450000.description: This Goryeo white porcelain meiping vase was made in the 13th century and stands 29.2 cm high. Its form shows the influence of Northern Song Chinese wares, while the body is divided into six vertical panels and decorated with inlaid peonies, reeds, willows, water birds, and lotus motifs. It is a rare example that combines features of Goryeo celadon and white porcelain.

1121103460000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Inlaid and Copper-Decorated Peony Design
1121103460000.description: This Goryeo celadon meiping vase was made in the 13th century and stands 34.6 cm high. The main peony motifs were inlaid with red pigment, and the body is further decorated with black-and-white inlay, lotus petals, chrysanthemums, vines, and lightning patterns. The use of red pigment on the petal tips adds a vivid accent.

1121103470000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Meiping Vase with Inlaid Fish Design
1121103470000.description: This early Joseon buncheong ware meiping vase was made in the 15th century and stands 30.0 cm high. Although the form follows the earlier Goryeo meiping type, the complex decoration and motifs such as beads, transformed clouds, lotuses, cranes, and fish show a transition toward buncheong ware. The glaze also has a pale bluish celadon-like tone.

1121103480000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Lidded Food Container with Inlaid Peony Design
1121103480000.description: This early Joseon buncheong ware food container is 16 cm high and 16.8 cm in body diameter. It is decorated with peony petals and leaves using wide inlay, with small grass patterns in white inlay on the lid edge and a dynamic large stem carved between the peony motifs. The form is full-bodied, and the foot flares outward for stability.

1121103490000.title_en: Celadon Nested Cosmetic Box with Inlaid Chrysanthemum, Peony, and Lotus Design
1121103490000.description: This Goryeo celadon nested box, thought to have been used for cosmetics, consists of one outer box and five inner boxes. The lids and body are decorated with inlaid peonies, chrysanthemums, vines, lightning patterns, and lotus motifs, using both black-and-white inlay and white inlay. Similar fragments have been found at the Goryeo kiln site in Yuchon-ri, Buan.

1122203500000.title_en: Mungyeonggong Kim Goeng-pil Hall, Shrine, and Wall of Dodong Seowon, Dalseong
1122203500000.description: Dodong Seowon is a Joseon-period private Confucian academy founded to honor Kim Goeng-pil and later received royal patronage in 1607. The complex includes the lecture hall, the shrine housing Kim Goeng-pil's spirit tablet, and a surrounding tile-roofed wall. The main buildings are simple and restrained in design, reflecting the tradition of mid-Joseon seowon architecture.

1121103510000.title_en: Stupa of Great Master Daegyeong, Former Bojisa Temple Site, Yangpyeong
1121103510000.description: This octagonal Buddhist sarira stupa is believed to enshrine the relics of Great Master Daegyeong, who was active from the late Unified Silla to the early Goryeo period. The base, body, and roof stones are carved with figures such as lions, cloud patterns, lotus motifs, the Four Heavenly Kings, bodhisattvas, and flying celestial beings. It was moved to Seoul in 1913 from the former site of Bojisa Temple in Yangpyeong.

1123803340000.title_en: Bronze Incense Burner with Silver Inlay, Tongdosa Temple
1123803340000.description: This ritual incense burner was used at temples to burn incense or to be placed on an altar during ceremonies. It has a bowl-shaped body with a flaring lower part and a round pedestal, and the surface is densely decorated with silver-inlaid lotus, vine, phoenix, and cloud motifs.

1122203350000.description: This stone seated Buddha image shows the typical form of Vairocana Buddha popular in the late Unified Silla period. The figure has a large rounded face, a large boat-shaped halo with small seated Buddhas, and an octagonal pedestal with floral and animal designs.

1122403360000.description: This armor is a type of chain armor made by linking iron plates and iron rings together. It is said to have been worn by General Jeong Ji in battles against Japanese pirates and passed down by his descendants.

1121103380000.description: This is a small and simple Silla gold crown excavated from Geumnyeongchong Tomb. It is made only of gold, without jade ornaments, and has five upright tree-like branches with deer-antler-shaped side ornaments and hanging decorations.

1123703390000.description: This Silla gold crown was excavated from Seobongchong Tomb in Noseo-dong, Gyeongju. It has five upright branches, curved jade ornaments, deer-antler-shaped decorations, and large pendant earrings, with a distinctive internal framework unique to this crown.

1121103400000.title_en: Celadon Maebyeong with Iron-painted and White Slip Ginseng Leaf Design
1121103400000.description: This Goryeo maebyeong has a short neck, a squared mouth, and a slender body that descends almost in a straight line. The dark iron-painted surface is decorated with simple white ginseng leaf designs, a rare use of white slip over iron-painted celadon.

1121103420000.title_en: Celadon Covered Maebyeong with Incised Peony and Inlaid Brocade-cloth Design
1121103420000.description: This Goryeo maebyeong has a broad mouth, a full shoulder, and decorative motifs divided between the upper and lower parts of the vessel. It features incised peony and cloud designs, black-and-white inlaid chrysanthemum vines, and a brocade-cloth-like ornament draped over the shoulder.

1121103430000.title_en: Set of Decorative Bricks from Oe-ri, Buyeo
1121103430000.description: This set consists of eight decorated bricks excavated from an old temple site in Oe-ri, Buyeo. Each brick bears carved and fired designs such as landscapes, phoenixes, goblins, dragons, clouds, and lotus flowers, and they are believed to have been used to decorate floors or walls.

1121103520000.title_en: Ink on Dark Blue Paper with Silver Inscription of the Lotus Sutra, Volume 7 (1963)
1121103520000.description: This manuscript is the final volume, volume 7, of the Lotus Sutra copied on dark blue paper with silver powder. The colophon states that it was produced in 1386, during the 12th year of King U of Goryeo, through the donation of Kim of Juksan-gunbuin and others, under the direction of Gakseon and by Gakyeon.

1123803530000.title_en: Twin-Lion Stone Lantern at Hyeongamsa Temple Site, Hapcheon
1123803530000.description: This stone lantern from the Unified Silla period stands at the site of Yeongamsa Temple in Hapcheon. Its parts are mostly octagonal, and the middle support stone is carved with two lions facing each other; the lamp chamber also bears Four Heavenly Kings reliefs.

1123403540000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Cheoneungsa Temple Site, Cheonan
1123403540000.description: This large five-story stone pagoda stands at the site of Cheoneungsa Temple and dates to the early Goryeo period. It rests on a two-tier stylobate, with each story made from a single body stone and a single roof stone, and its proportions show the renewed enlargement of stone pagodas after the founding of Goryeo.

1123403550000.title_en: Rock-carved Standing Buddha in Singyeong-ri, Hongseong
1123403550000.description: This large standing Buddha was carved into a protruding rock face on Yongbongsan in Hongseong, with the figure measuring about 4 meters high. The face is broad and gentle, the robes are simplified into linear forms, and the halo is indicated only by faint incised lines on the rock surface.

1123403560000.title_en: Geumgangjeon Hall of Muryangsa Temple, Buyeo
1123403560000.description: This is the main hall of Muryangsa Temple and is a rare two-story Buddhist hall in Korea. Although it appears to have two floors, the interior is open as one space, and it houses an Amitabha Triad.

1121103570000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda at Jeongdosa Temple Site, Chilgok
1121103570000.description: This five-story stone pagoda was originally at the site of Jeongdosa Temple and was moved to Gyeongbokgung in 1924, then relocated again to the National Daegu Museum in 1994. An inscription on the upper stylobate records the date as the 11th year of Taepyeong, which corresponds to 1031, and a reliquary container was found inside when it was moved.

1121103580000.title_en: Stupa of Boje Jonja at Yeongjeonsa Temple Site, Wonju
1121103580000.description: These two stone stupas are reliquaries for Boje Jonja, the late Goryeo monk known as Naong Hwagang. They are unusual in that they take the form of stone pagodas rather than the more typical monk’s stupa, and they were erected in 1388.

1121103590000.title_en: Stele for Hongbeop Guksa at Jeongtosa Temple Site, Chungju
1121103590000.description: This stele commemorates Hongbeop Guksa and was erected in 1017, the 8th year of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. The tortoise pedestal has a dragon head, the headstone is carved with dragons, and the inscription records the monk’s life and the names of his disciples.

1121103600000.title_en: Stupa Stele of Buddhist Monk Wonrang from Wolgwangsa Temple Site, Jecheon
1121103600000.description: This stupa stele records the life and deeds of Wonrang Seonsa, a late Unified Silla Buddhist monk. It was originally at the Wolgwangsa Temple site in Jecheon, moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1922, and is now in the National Museum of Korea. The stele was erected in 890, after Wonrang’s death.

1121103610000.title_en: Stupa Stele of State Preceptor Daegyeong from Borisa Temple Site, Yangpyeong
1121103610000.description: This stupa stele records the life of Daegyeong Daesa, a monk active from the late Unified Silla to early Goryeo period. It was found at the Borisa Temple site and later moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace, and is now in the National Museum of Korea. The stele was erected in 939.

1121103620000.title_en: Stupa of State Preceptor Jinggyeong from Bongnimsa Temple Site, Changwon
1121103620000.description: This stone stupa is the reliquary stupa of Jinggyeong Daesa, a late Unified Silla monk. It was originally at the Bongnimsa Temple site and was moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1919; it is now in the National Museum of Korea. It is believed to have been made in 923, the year of the monk’s death.

1121103630000.title_en: Stupa Stele of State Preceptor Jinggyeong from Bongnimsa Temple Site, Changwon
1121103630000.description: This stupa stele is for Simhui, a late Unified Silla monk who was posthumously honored as Jinggyeong Daesa. It was originally at the Bongnimsa Temple site in Changwon, moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1919, and is now in the National Museum of Korea. The stele was erected in 924.

1121103640000.title_en: Stone Lantern from West Gate of Seoseongmun, Naju
1121103640000.description: This stone lantern originally stood near the west gate area in Naju and was moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1929 before later being transferred to the National Museum of Korea. After dismantling and conservation treatment in 2017, it is now displayed at the National Naju Museum. An inscription shows that it was erected in 1093.

1121103650000.title_en: Stupa of State Preceptor Jingong and Stone Container from Heungbapsa Temple Site, Wonju
1121103650000.description: This set consists of the stupa that enshrined the relics of Jingong Daesa and a stone container placed beside it. It was originally at the Heungbapsa Temple site in Wonju, moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace in 1931, and is now in the National Museum of Korea. Based on records in the Goryeosa, it is thought to date to 940.

1121103660000.title_en: Reliquary from the West Three-Story Stone Pagoda at Gameunsa Temple Site
1121103660000.description: This relic container set was discovered inside the third story of the west three-story stone pagoda at the Gameunsa Temple site during dismantling and repair. It consists of a square bronze reliquary box and the inner reliquary vessel placed inside it. The set is dated to the late 7th century, during Unified Silla.

1123303670000.title_en: Amitabha Buddha Relief Stele Inscribed in the Year of Gichuk
1123303670000.description: This stone relief is one of three relief stelae formerly kept at Biamsa Temple. It is carved on one side of a boat-shaped stone, with an inscription on the back. The main image is Amitabha Buddha surrounded by bodhisattvas, arhats, yaksha figures, and guardian figures, and it is generally dated to 689.

1123303680000.description: This stone image is called a "statue stele" because its form resembles a pagoda stele. It is carved from a single stone, including the base, the central block, and the cover stone, and features a large half-seated Maitreya Bodhisattva on the front, attendant bodhisattvas on the sides, and a stupa on the back. It is generally dated to 673, based on its carving style and its relation to other sculptures found at Biamsa Temple site.

1122603690000.description: This octagonal stupa stands on a broad terrace on a hill northeast of Seongnamsa Temple and has long been regarded as the reliquary stupa of Doseuiguksa. It is made in an octagonal form with a base stone, platform, body, and roof stone, and its surfaces are decorated with lions, clouds, floral motifs, guardian figures, and door-like carvings. When dismantled and repaired in 1962, a cavity for relics was found in the middle platform, but no relic contents remained.

1122603700000.title_en: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha Statue at Ganjeolsa Temple Site, Ulju
1122603700000.description: This stone seated Buddha statue remains relatively well preserved despite minor damage. The rounded face, narrow shoulders, and thin robe with U-shaped folds show the characteristics of ninth-century Unified Silla sculpture. It is thought to represent the Medicine Buddha, based on the hand gesture and the medicine container held in the left hand.

1123803710000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha Statue at Sawol-ri, Sancheong
1123803710000.description: This Buddha statue was buried at the temple site in Sawol-ri, Sancheong, and moved to Geumseonam Hermitage in Jinju in 1957. The statue has a pedestal and halo, though many parts, including the knees, are broken, and the style shows the late Unified Silla tendency toward a long face, broad shoulders, and a narrow waist. The right hand hangs downward, while the left hand holds a medicine bowl, indicating that it is probably a Medicine Buddha image.

1123803720000.title_en: Monk’s Stupa at Yongamsa Temple Site, Jinju
1123803720000.description: This stupa once stood at the northwest side of the Yongamsa Temple site and was restored in 1962 after damage. Parts of the base, central platform, and body were rebuilt, but the original form is thought to date to the early Goryeo period. The octagonal structure is well proportioned and preserves decorative cloud and guardian motifs on the base, along with an unusual layered arrangement in the platform.

1123803730000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Bocheonsa Temple Site, Uiryeong
1123803730000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands at the site of Bocheonsa Temple, which is said to have been founded in the reign of King Gyeongdeok of Unified Silla. Although the temple later disappeared, the pagoda remains and is considered an early Goryeo work that continues the general Unified Silla style. Its two-tiered base, curved roof stones, and remaining square finial platform show a balanced and refined design.

1123803740000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Yulgoksa Temple, Sancheong
1123803740000.description: This is the main Buddha hall of Yulgoksa Temple, and an inscription found during dismantling confirmed that it was largely rebuilt in 1679, the fifth year of King Sukjong. The wooden building has a three-bay front, three-bay side plan, a paljak roof, and daepo-style bracket complexes, with a richly patterned lattice front and a coffered ceiling inside. It is a large mid-Joseon mountain temple hall with a simple yet imposing appearance.

1123803750000.title_en: Rock-carved Standing Buddha at Deokjeon-ri, Hamyang
1123803750000.description: This large rock-carved standing Buddha is 5.8 meters tall and was carved on the face of a large rock, with the body, pedestal, and halo all represented. The broad face, long ears, short neck with three neck folds, and massive body give it a powerful appearance, although the proportions are somewhat unbalanced. The inverted scarf-like collar and regular U-shaped drapery folds are features commonly seen in early Goryeo Buddhist sculpture.

1123803760000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha of Gyosan-ri, Hamyang
1123803760000.description: This is a stone seated Buddha from the Goryeo period now located inside Hamyang Middle School. It is a large figure over 4 meters high including the pedestal, though the halo is lost and parts of the face, right hand, knees, and pedestal are damaged or missing. The robe is worn over only the left shoulder, and the square pedestal is carved with lotus, sunken eye, and cloud motifs.

1123803770000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha of Yangpyeong-ri, Geochang
1123803770000.description: This large stone standing Buddha from the Unified Silla period is said to have stood at a temple site formerly called Geumyangsa or Nohyesa. It stands on a separately made lotus pedestal, and a modern canopy has been added above the head. The figure shows a rounded face, slender body, and calm drapery lines that reflect late Unified Silla style.

1123803780000.title_en: Stone Standing Bodhisattva of Sangnim-ri, Geochang
1123803780000.description: This is a large Goryeo-period bodhisattva statue made of granite and standing on an octagonal pedestal with carved lotus motifs. The figure has lost its crown, and the face, jewelry, and robe are treated in a formal, somewhat rigid manner. It is thought to depict Avalokiteshvara, holding a bottle in the right hand and a lotus flower in the left.

1123803790000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Myeoamsa Temple Site, Jinju
1123803790000.description: This is a Goryeo-period stone pagoda remaining at an old temple site. It stands on a two-tier stylobate, with one stone used for each body and roof stone on each story; the first-story body is especially tall, and the overall proportions are unbalanced. The style departs from the standard Unified Silla pagoda type and is thought to date from the middle Goryeo period or later.

1123803800000.title_en: Stupa of Simgam, Ssanggyesa Temple, Hadong
1123803800000.description: This stone stupa at Ssanggyesa Temple is identified as the stupa of the Seon master Jingam. It has a symmetric octagonal base, a plain octagonal body, a broad roof stone with upturned corners, and a finial of later restoration or loss. It is thought to have been made in the late 9th century and shows a gradual move toward simplified forms.

1123803810000.description: This stone lantern, restored after having collapsed, was found at a temple site said to be Baekamsa or Daedongsa. The lantern has a round lower support, an octagonal shaft, a lantern housing carved with four guardian kings on four sides, and a roof stone with raised corners. It is considered a fine example of mid-8th-century Unified Silla stone lantern design.

1122603820000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Cheongsongsa Temple Site, Ulju
1122603820000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands at the Cheongsongsa temple site below Namamsan. It has a two-tier base and a body stone and roof stone made from a single stone for each story, with the first-story body unusually large and the roof stones relatively small. A bronze reliquary and other relics were discovered during dismantling and repair in 1962.

1121103830000.description: Donhwamun Gate is the main gate of Changdeokgung Palace and is the oldest surviving wooden gate of a palace in Korea. It was originally built in 1412 and rebuilt in 1609 during the reign of King Gwanghaegun. The gate has five bays on the front, two on the side, and a three-gate arrangement with a central royal gate and side gates for officials.

1121103840000.description: Honghwamun Gate is the main gate of Changgyeonggung Palace. Originally built in 1484, it burned down during the Japanese invasions of 1592 and was rebuilt in 1616; the present building has been repaired several times since then. It is a two-story wooden gate with a hip-and-gable roof and multi-bracket style supporting structure, and is considered an important source for studying early 17th-century wooden architecture.

1121103850000.title_en: Myeongjeongmun Gate and Haenggak Corridors, Changgyeonggung Palace, Seoul
1121103850000.description: Myeongjeongmun Gate and the surrounding corridors were built when Changgyeonggung Palace was founded in 1484, then rebuilt in 1616 after being burned in the Japanese invasions of 1592. Parts of the south and north corridors were restored in 1986 after demolition during the Japanese colonial period. The gate is a representative mid-Joseon palace gate and preserves features of earlier Joseon architectural style.

1121103860000.description: Okcheongyo Bridge is a stone bridge inside Changgyeonggung Palace, crossing Okryucheon Stream just beyond Honghwamun Gate. It has two connected semicircular arches and decorative stone carvings, including goblin faces on the spandrels and animal figures at the bridge ends. The bridge is believed to have been built in 1483, around the time the palace was established.

1123103870000.title_en: Seon-gak Wangsa Stele, Hoeamsaji Temple Site, Yangju
1123103870000.description: This stele was erected at the site of Hoeamsa Temple to commemorate the late Goryeo monk Naong. The stele has a Chinese Tang-style revival form, with a turtle pedestal and a stele body topped by carved dragons rather than a separate capstone. The inscription was composed by Yi Saek and written by Gwon Junghwa, and the stele is valued for its text and calligraphy.

1123103880000.title_en: Muhak Dae-sa Stupa, Hoeamsaji Temple Site, Yangju
1123103880000.description: This stupa stands on the northern ridge of the former Hoeamsa Temple site together with the stupas of Jijang and Naong. It is the tomb stupa of the monk Muhak, who was active from the late Goryeo to early Joseon period and was closely associated with King Taejo Yi Seong-gye. The stupa was built in 1407 and shows an early Joseon style with an octagonal base, body, and roof stone.

1123103890000.title_en: Twin-Lion Stone Lantern in Front of Muhak Dae-sa Stupa, Hoeamsaji Temple Site, Yangju
1123103890000.description: This stone lantern stands on the eastern ridge of the Hoeamsa Temple site, south of the stupas of Jijang, Naong, and Muhak. It uses a twin-lion support, a form that follows earlier Silla tradition, while its square overall plan and thick roof stone reflect an early Joseon style. It is considered a work from the early Joseon period, likely made around the same time as the neighboring stupa.

1123403900000.title_en: Goryeo Hand-copied Lotus Sutra, Gwangdeoksa Temple, Cheonan
