They are important as Baekje-period granite Buddha statues from the southernmost part of Baekje territory and for showing the right-shoulder-draped style of dress. The larger right-hand Buddha is relatively complete except for damage to the halo and lower part of the pedestal.

1123309150000.title_en: Daeungbojeon Hall of Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123309150000.description: This hall at Beopjusa Temple stands at the foot of Songnisan Mountain and was rebuilt by Byeokam in 1624 after the temple burned during the Japanese invasions. It is a two-story building with seven bays on the front and four on the side, and it has a paljak roof with multicluster bracket arms. The main triad inside was made when the hall was rebuilt.

1123309160000.title_en: Wontongbojeon Hall of Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123309160000.description: This hall at Beopjusa Temple was rebuilt by Byeokam in 1624 after the temple burned during the Japanese invasions. It is a one-story square building with three bays on each side, a pyramidal roof, and a simple bracket system used only on the main columns. The hall houses a gilded wooden Avalokiteshvara statue about 2.8 meters tall.

1123709170000.description: These woodblocks were used to print Baejayeobunryak, a basic reference book for finding rhymes when composing poetry or verse. The set consists of 162 blocks, including 150 from the Kangxi edition and 12 from the Wanli edition, and was printed by Bak Dong-bu in 1679. The blocks are unusually complete, with all parts of the text preserved.

1123809250000.title_en: Assembly of the Spirit Vulture Peak, Palsangjeon Hall, Ssanggyesa Temple
1123809250000.description: This Buddhist painting depicts the sermon delivered by the Buddha on Mount Yeongchwi (Vulture Peak). The Buddha sits at the center, surrounded by the Four Heavenly Kings, bodhisattvas, and disciples, with a balanced composition and refined use of space and painting technique. It was painted in 1681, in the seventh year of King Sukjong of Joseon.

1121109260000.description: This Goryeo Buddhist painting shows Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva in a splendid Pure Land setting. The bodhisattva sits slightly to the left on a rock and looks toward Sudhana, with delicate features, elaborate ornaments, bamboo in the background, and flowers and corals below. It is a rare surviving example of Goryeo Buddhist painting from the 14th century.

1121109270000.description: This gilt-bronze sculpture represents Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, who symbolizes the Buddha's compassion. The figure wears a high jeweled crown with a small Buddha image on the front, holds a kundika flask in the left hand, and shows the characteristic three-bend posture of Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture. Its elegant body proportions and flowing drapery are key features of the work.

1121109280000.title_en: Sarira Stupa and Sarira Reliquaries from Budoram Hermitage Site, Boinsa Temple, Namyangju
1121109280000.description: This set consists of a sarira stupa built in the Joseon period and the reliquaries found inside it. The stupa was erected in the reign of King Gwanghae to pray for the longevity of the crown prince and the protection of the Buddha, and the reliquaries inside include gilt-bronze, silver, and crystal containers. Records show that the reliquaries were sealed in 1620.
1121109280000.material: Stone; gilt bronze, silver, and crystal

1123109300000.title_en: Ritual Chair and Staffs Awarded to Yi Gyeong-seok, and Album of the Banquet for the Bestowal of the Chair and Staffs
1123109300000.description: This set records the Joseon court practice of honoring elderly officials with a chair, staffs, and a ceremonial procession. It includes one folding chair, four staffs, and an album with three paintings showing the receiving of the gifts, the reading of the royal edict, and the court entertainers' performance. The items were bestowed on Yi Gyeong-seok in 1668, during the ninth year of King Hyeonjong.

1121109320000.description: This is a royal portrait of King Yeongjo of Joseon, shown at the age of 51. He wears the ikseon-gwan crown and a red dragon robe, and the work reflects late Joseon portrait conventions in its treatment of the face and clothing. The portrait was copied in 1900 from an earlier original painted in 1744.

1123109330000.title_en: The Sutra of the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva (1987)
1123109330000.description: This woodblock-printed royal edition consists of three volumes in one bound book. It is an edition of the Ksitigarbha Sutra printed on paper by the Joseon royal court to pray for the repose of Queen Wongyeong, the consort of King Taejong, and Queen Soheon, the consort of King Sejong. The colophon indicates that it was printed between 1447 and 1450.

1123109340000.title_en: Botongja's Secret on Cultivating the Mind and the Four Dharma Discourses (Annotated Korean Translation)
1123109340000.description: This woodblock-printed book is an edition of Mowuja Susimgyeol, annotated and translated into Korean at the court printing bureau in the reign of King Sejo. It includes four Dharma discourses appended after the main text, and the colophon names several calligraphers involved in the copying. It was printed in 1467.

1121109350000.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist text was compiled in 1459 by combining Worin cheon-gang jigok and Seokbo sangjeol. Volumes 11 and 12 are parts not included in the previously known 10 volumes in 8 books, and this set is considered the first edition. It is an important source for the study of Hunminjeongeum, early Joseon Buddhism, and bibliography.

1121109360000.description: This woodblock-printed book contains volumes 6 and 7 of the seven-volume Lotus Sutra, bound into one volume. The colophon and printed postscript indicate that the blocks were carved in 1470 and printed again in 1482 for royal Buddhist rites. Two versions of the same book survive, differing in their binding style.

1121109360200.description: This woodblock-printed book contains volumes 6 and 7 of the seven-volume Lotus Sutra, bound into one volume. The text and printed postscript indicate that the blocks were carved in 1470 and printed again in 1482 for royal Buddhist rites. Surviving examples differ from the other version in their binding style, and this one preserves traces of red ground and gold-script writing.

1121109370000.title_en: Corrected Edition of the Compassionate Repentance Ritual, Volume 10
1121109370000.description: This is the tenth and final volume of a woodblock-printed Buddhist ritual text used for repentance while reciting scriptures. The publication date is not recorded, but the omission of the final strokes in taboo characters indicates that the woodblocks were carved in the Goryeo period, and the surviving imprint suggests later reprinting in Joseon. The first page includes a painting of the Seven Buddhas of the Past and the future Buddha Maitreya.

1121109380000.title_en: Annotated Scripture on the Essentials of the Great and Broad Perfect Enlightenment, Volume 1, Part 2
1121109380000.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist text is an annotated explanation of the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra by Tang monk Zongmi. It was printed on handmade paper from woodblocks copied from a Song-dynasty edition, and its layout and typeface closely resemble the Song exemplar. Although the lower part of the volume is missing, it is valued as a Goryeo-period copy of a Song model.

1121109390000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Śūraṅgama Sutra combines the contents of volumes 4 to 7 and 8 to 10 into two bound books. It was published in 1372 by Kim Ho, Choe Clan of Yeongam County, and Yi Clan of Jeongsun Ongju during King Gongmin's reign, and the present impression is thought to have been printed in the early Joseon period. The book has dark blue covers with the title written in gold.

1121109400000.title_en: Avatamsaka Sutra of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Handwritten in Ink on White Paper
1121109400000.description: This manuscript of the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Original Vows Sutra was copied by Hae-yeon in 1440 from the Chinese translation by Tantang. It consists of three folded volumes and was made on white paper with black ink, with the covers decorated in blue and silver and the title written in gold on a red ground. A colophon at the end records the donors and their wishes for repayment of the kindness of heaven, earth, parents, and the state.

1123109410100.title_en: Secret Letters Sent by King Seonjo to Song Eon-sin and Portrait of Song Eon-sin - Secret Letters Sent by King Seonjo to Song Eon-sin
1123109410100.description: This item preserves seven confidential letters written by King Seonjo to Song Eon-sin, who served as Minister of Personnel and other high offices. Later, King Jeongjo read the letters, added an explanatory postscript, and ordered a copy to be made for the royal library while returning the original to Song's descendants. The set is an important historical source for studying royal administration, military affairs, diplomatic exchanges, gift-giving, family institutions, and Song Eon-sin's lineage.

1121109180000.description: This woodblock-printed booklet is the seventh volume of the Lotus Sutra translated by Kumārajīva. The end of the book records that it was printed from a block carved by the monk Jaesaek in 1288, during the reign of King Chungnyeol of Goryeo. The text includes notes attached to each section and connected to the main text by lines.

1121109190000.title_en: Brahma's Net Sutra and Diamond Sutra
1121109190000.description: This single volume binds together the Brahma's Net Sutra and the Diamond Sutra, both translated by Kumārajīva. It was woodblock printed on mulberry paper in 1387, and the Diamond Sutra includes a verse by Cheonro and a postscript describing the carving of the blocks at the request of Yu Hyeong and Gang In-bu. The two sutras appear to have been printed in the same period.

1121109200000.title_en: Sutra on the Great Kindness of Parents
1121109200000.description: This woodblock-printed scroll is a copy of the sutra that teaches the Buddha's instruction on the great kindness of parents. It was carved at Gwangbeopsa Temple on Daeseongsan in Pyeongyang in 1454, during the reign of King Danjong of Joseon, and later mounted in a folding format after first being made as a scroll. The text is illustrated with scenes and verses explaining the ten kinds of parental kindness and the results of repaying or failing to repay it.

1121109210000.description: This book is a collection of Buddhist texts compiled by Ye Myeohaeng of Song China, including inscriptions, poems, essential teachings, and other sayings and writings related to Zen. It was first printed in 1462 at the Gangyeongdogam, the government office that handled the printing of Buddhist scriptures during King Sejo's reign. The copy is noted for its refined woodblock carving and clear printing.

1122609210300.description: This Buddhist book is a rare surviving woodblock-printed edition of Jinsiljujip compiled by Ye Myeohaeng of Song China from Zen-related writings by various monks and literati. It was printed from Gangyeongdogam woodblocks carved in 1462 during the reign of King Sejo, and the edition is valued as an excellent text for the study of Buddhism, Buddhist scholarship, and bibliography. A matching edition of the same work is already designated as a Treasure.

1123709220000.title_en: Wood-Carved Amitabha Buddha Sermon Image, Bogeon Hall, Nanjangsa Temple, Sangju
1123709220000.description: This is a wooden relief Buddhist hanging image rather than a painted banner. It is used as the rear Buddha image for Bogeon Hall and shows the principal Buddha seated on a lotus pedestal, with ten great bodhisattvas, ten great disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings arranged in tiers around him. The composition and carving style reflect the characteristics of late Joseon Buddhist painting, although no inscription survives to give an exact date.

1123709230000.title_en: Wood-Carved Amitabha Buddha Sermon Image, Gwaneum Seonwon, Nanjangsa Temple, Sangju
1123709230000.description: This work is a wooden relief image carved behind the principal Avalokitesvara statue in Gwaneum Seonwon. Amitabha Buddha is placed at the center, with attendant bodhisattvas, the disciples Ananda and Kashyapa, and the Four Heavenly Kings arranged around him. The simplified forms and stiff drapery reflect a seventeenth-century style, and the piece demonstrates highly skilled woodcarving.

1123609240000.title_en: Amitabha Preaching Painting, Gwangjeon Hall, Cheoneunsa Temple
1123609240000.description: This hanging painting depicts Amitabha Buddha preaching in the Pure Land, where he is said to lead the dead to rebirth in Paradise. It was painted in 1776 by fourteen monk-painters led by Sinam, with Amitabha surrounded symmetrically by bodhisattvas, disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings. The inscription gives the date, title, and names of the figures, making it an important source for the study of Amitabha paintings.
1123609240000.material: Ink and color on hemp cloth

1123109480200.description: This is the third volume of a Korean vernacular translation and correction copy of the Śūraṃgama Sūtra, printed in 1461 at the request of Prince Hyoryeong. It was produced with metal type, and the Korean text includes phonetic marks that make it an important source for the study of Middle Korean. The text also preserves traces of proofreading in red ink.

1121109490000.title_en: Repentance Ritual of Amitābha at the Pure Land Dharma Hall
1121109490000.description: This is a woodblock-printed Buddhist text issued in 1474 during the reign of King Seongjong. It was compiled as two volumes in one set and records the names and offices of the monks, royal relatives, and others involved in the engraving and publication. The colophon shows that it was carried out as a royal project.

1121109500000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Lotus Sutra was produced in 1488, using blocks carved in 1470. It is bound as one volume containing volumes 5 through 7, and the colophon states that it was printed to pray for the repose of Princess Sunsuk. It is an important source for the study of royal Buddhist faith in early Joseon.

1123809510000.title_en: Korean Vernacular Edict of King Seonjo
1123809510000.description: This is a decree written in Korean and issued to the people in 1593 while King Seonjo was in Uiju during the Imjin War. It urged captured subjects to return and stated that those taken by force would not be punished. The text is also valuable for the study of Korean-language writing and the wartime situation.

1123409520000.title_en: Royal Edict Bestowing the Title of Seonmu Meritorious Subject on Yi Gwang-ak
1123409520000.description: This royal edict was issued in 1604 to reward Yi Gwang-ak for his service in defending Jinju Fortress during the Imjin War. It is written on silk and was originally a scroll, later cut and mounted with covers. The document records his merits and the special privileges granted to meritorious subjects.

1122109530000.title_en: Royal Appointment Document for Jo Sung
1122109530000.description: This royal appointment document from 1396 grants Jo Sung the office of dopyeonguisa hasa. It is written in cursive script on a single sheet and preserves the formal format of early Joseon appointment documents. It is useful for studying official titles and administrative practice in early Joseon.

1122109540000.title_en: Military Examination Certificate for Jo Seo-gyeong
1122109540000.description: This red certificate was issued in 1435 to record Jo Seo-gyeong's success in the military state examination. It is a single sheet written in cursive script and bears the royal seal impression. The document is useful for studying early Joseon institutions, the examination system, and the use of seals.

1123609550000.title_en: Reliquary from the Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123609550000.description: These three relic containers were discovered during the dismantling and repair of the Three-Story Stone Pagoda at Seonamsa Temple in Suncheon. They include a celadon jar, a white porcelain jar, and a gilt-bronze reliquary tower containing a relic. The objects provide important evidence for the study of late Goryeo relic containers and metal craft.
1123609550000.material: Celadon, white porcelain, gilt bronze, crystal

1123609560000.title_en: Large Buddhist Cymbals from Taeansa Temple, Gokseong
1123609560000.description: This pair of Buddhist cymbals, called bara, was used in temple rituals and dance. It measures 92 cm in diameter and is the largest surviving bara in Korea; an inscription says it was made by Prince Hyoryeong to pray for the well-being of King Sejong, the queen, and the crown prince.

1123709570000.description: This geomungo was used by the early Joseon scholar Takyoung Kim Il-son and measures 160 cm in length, 19 cm in width, and 10 cm in height. The name "Takyeonggeum" is engraved on the instrument, and a crane is painted on the head; it is designated as the only national heritage item among instruments once used as scholars' personal favorite objects.

1123709580000.title_en: Clay Seated Vairocana Buddha Triad at Girimsa Temple, Gyeongju
1123709580000.description: This triad, enshrined in the Daejeokgwangjeon Hall of Girimsa Temple, was made by building a frame of cypress wood and covering it with clay. Vairocana Buddha is placed in the center, with Bhaisajyaguru and Amitabha as attendants on the left and right, and the restrained form and drapery suggest an early 16th-century date.

1123709590000.title_en: Consecration Texts from the Clay Vairocana Buddha at Girimsa Temple, Gyeongju
1123709590000.description: These are 54 items in 71 volumes of consecration texts found inside the clay Vairocana Buddha at Girimsa Temple, including manuscript sutras and woodblock prints. They include works copied or printed from the Goryeo period through the early Joseon period and preserve diverse binding formats such as seonjang, cheopjang, hojaeopjang, and pobaejang.

1121109600000.description: This edition of the Lotus Sutra, also called the "Bunhwayeong" sutra, is the core scripture of the Tiantai school and one of the key texts that shaped Korean Buddhist thought. It was printed as two volumes from a version transcribed by the monk Jiseon in smaller script, and the colophon states that it was published in 1382 through the donations of Suyeongun and Wang Gyu.

1123809610000.description: This is the volume 4-7 book of the Lotus Sutra, a key Mahayana Buddhist scripture, printed from woodblocks made in 1405 at Ansimsa Temple on Dosolsan. The text was transcribed by brothers Seong Dal-saeng and Seong Gae to pray for their deceased father's rebirth, and the edition preserves the colophon explaining its publication.

1123809610200.description: This is the volume 4-7 book of the Lotus Sutra, printed from woodblocks carved in 1405 from a manuscript copied by the brothers Seong Dal-saeng and Seong Gae. The colophon records the publication circumstances, including a donor who commissioned the illustration and printing to pray for her deceased husband's rebirth in the Pure Land.

1122209610300.description: This is the volume 4-7 book of the Lotus Sutra, a major Mahayana Buddhist scripture, based on a manuscript copied in 1405 by the brothers Seong Dal-saeng and Seong Gae and carved into woodblocks. It includes a colophon by Gwon Geun recording the publication, making it an important source for the study of early Joseon Buddhist printing.

1123109410200.description: This full-length seated portrait shows Song Eon-sin wearing an official robe and a samo hat, with a round fan, chest badge, and black leather shoes. The costume details match the rank he held as state censor and minister of personnel in the early 17th century. The painting is considered a representative example of a meritorious-retainer portrait from early Joseon.

1123509420000.title_en: Ancient Documents of the Hwang Jin Family
1123509420000.description: This group consists of 14 types and 125 documents preserved in the family of General Hwang Jin, a military official of the Joseon period who died at the second Battle of Jinju. The materials have been handed down for more than 400 years and include documents related to Hwang Jin as well as records of his two sons. They are valuable historical sources for studying events of the Imjin War.

1123609430000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Ucheon-ri, Boseong
1123609430000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands in a field in Ucheon-ri, near the road between Beolgyo and Boseong. It was dismantled and restored in 1970, and its proportions and construction suggest a 9th-century date. The base, body stones, and roof stones are each made from single blocks of stone, and only the finial remains at the top.

1123609440000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Buddha of Yusin-ri, Boseong
1123609440000.description: This rock-carved seated Buddha is cut in relief on one side of a large granite outcrop at the northern foot of Jonejisan. The figure has a round face, broad shoulders, and both hands held before the chest in a preaching gesture. The halo and pedestal are also carved, and the work is regarded as an outstanding early Goryeo example.

1123609450000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Geumdun Temple Site, Suncheon
1123609450000.description: This pagoda stands at a ruined temple site on Geumjeonsan, about 2 km north of Nagan-myeon. It has a two-tiered base and three stories of stone body and roof blocks, and the first-story body stone is decorated with doors on the front and back and offerings on the sides. Its style is typical of Unified Silla pagodas from around the 9th century.

1123609460000.title_en: Stone Buddhist Stele at Geumdun Temple Site, Suncheon
1123609460000.description: This stone Buddhist image stands with the three-story pagoda at the Geumdun Temple site and is carved on one face of a flat rectangular stone. It has a canopy and pedestal, and the figure is shown with hands joined in a preaching gesture. The back appears to have had inscriptions and carved figures, though they are now badly worn.

1123609470000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Mihwangsa Temple, Haenam
1123609470000.description: This main Buddha hall of Mihwangsa Temple stands at the foot of Dalmasan, at the southernmost point of the Korean mainland. It is a three-by-three bay building with a paljak roof and a dapo bracket structure. The hall enshrines a seated statue of Sakyamuni Buddha, and the ceiling bears the Buddhist character "beom" in the center.

1121109480000.title_en: Śūraṅgama Sūtra in Korean Translation, Volume 3 (1988)
1121109480000.description: This volume is part of the ten-volume Korean translation of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, a Buddhist scripture widely used in monastic study. It was translated and revised by monks and scholars and printed in 1461 with metal type made in the Eulhae year. The volume is an important source for studying Joseon-period Buddhist publishing and the printing date of Eulhae-type editions.

1121109690000.description: This is Volume 64 of the Goryeo reprinted edition of the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra, a foundational treatise of the Yogācāra school translated by Xuanzang from a work attributed to Maitreya. It was printed in 1246 by the Daejang Dogam as part of the Goryeo Tripitaka. It is a woodblock print on dak paper made in scroll form, and the surviving printing, paper, and original cover are said to be unusually well preserved.

1121109700000.title_en: Annotated and Korean-Translated Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment
1121109700000.description: This is a woodblock-printed Korean translation and annotation of the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment, produced by the Gangyeong Dogam in 1465. Surviving portions include the preface and selected fascicles, and the book shows careful proofreading marks and records of corrections. It is regarded as an important early printed example among the sutras translated into Korean.

1121109710000.title_en: Volume 5 to 7 of the Lotus Sutra
1121109710000.description: This is a woodblock-printed edition of volumes 5 to 7 of the Lotus Sutra, copied in 1405 and printed from the manuscript by Sinmun. The first page includes a painted illustration summarizing the sutra’s contents. The printing is on dak paper and the volume is bound as one book.

1121109720000.description: This is Volume 55 of the Goryeo reprinted edition of the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra, a Buddhist treatise translated by Xuanzang. It was printed on dak paper in scroll form, with the colophon indicating that the woodblocks were carved in 1247. The paper quality, size, and printing are described as matching Volume 64.

1121109730000.description: This is a metal-movable-type edition of the Korean translation of the Shurangama Sutra, also called the Great Buddha's Crown All-Tathāgata Secret Cause Cultivation and Attainment of Complete Enlightenment Sutra. The translation was begun in 1449 under the order of King Sejong and completed in 1461 under King Sejo. It was printed with Eulhae-ja type, and the text includes red corrections.
1121109730000.material: Metal movable type print on paper

1121109740000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Diamond Sutra was produced in 1387 during the reign of King U of Goryeo. It was printed on dak paper and bound as one book. The colophon records the circumstances of its production, and the edition is noted for its generally good printing and preservation.

1121109750000.description: This is a folded, screen-like woodblock-printed devotional text that lists the names of thirty Buddhas and bodhisattvas. The colophon records that it was printed in 1339, with donation by Joseowoo and Jeong Gongyeon, writing by Nam Yeongsin, and engraving by Hyeil. It reflects contemporary practices of reciting divine names for merit.

1121109760000.title_en: Lotus Sutra, Volumes 5 to 6, in Silver Ink on Oak Paper
1121109760000.description: This is a handwritten copy of the Lotus Sutra, volumes 5 to 6, made in silver ink on brown paper. It is in a folded format and preserves the text and covers, though the front illustration and colophon are absent. Based on its style and decorative features, it is estimated to have been produced in the 14th century.

1121109620000.description: This is a woodblock-printed edition of the Lotus Sutra, translated into Chinese by Kumārajīva and simplified by Jiehuan of the Song dynasty. It was carved on woodblocks in 1240, by order of Choe I, during the Goryeo period. The two volumes are bound as one book, printed on mulberry paper, and the colophon shows that it was issued through donations by Kim and others.

1121109630000.title_en: Abridged Commentary on the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra, Volume Lower
1121109630000.description: This is the lower-volume part of a woodblock-printed edition of an abridged commentary on the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra, printed on mulberry paper. It has a stitched binding with the pages folded and covered with an outer wrapper. Although the exact date is unknown, it is believed to be a Goryeo-period reprinting based on Song-dynasty blocks.

1121109640000.title_en: Commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, Volume 41
1121109640000.description: This is Volume 41 of the Commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra by Jingyuan of the Song dynasty. It is a woodblock-printed book made of folded leaves that can be opened like a screen, and the record at the beginning shows that it was printed in 1372 using Song woodblocks brought to Goryeo by Uicheon. The first part of the volume also preserves an illustrated transformation scene of the Huayan Sutra.

1121109650100.title_en: Combined Edition of Six Buddhist Sutras (1988-1)
1121109650100.description: This book combines six sutras commonly circulated in the early Joseon period, including the Diamond Sutra, the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra, the Śūraṅgama Mantra, the Amitabha Sutra, the Universal Gate chapter of the Lotus Sutra, and the Ritual Text for Avalokiteshvara. It was printed from woodblocks in 1472, based on blocks carved at Yeongjeam in 1440. The colophon by Kim Su-on shows that it was one of the many books printed at the request of Queen Dowager Insu to pray for the longevity of the royal family.

1123109650200.title_en: Combined Edition of Six Buddhist Sutras (2006)
1123109650200.description: This book combines six Buddhist scriptures, including the Diamond Sutra, the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra, the Śūraṅgama Mantra, the Ritual Text for Avalokiteshvara, the Amitabha Sutra, and the Universal Gate chapter of the Lotus Sutra. It was printed in 1472 at the request of Queen Dowager Insu, using older woodblocks, including the Diamond Sutra block carved at Yeongjeam in 1440. A colophon by Kim Su-on at the end confirms that it belongs to the group of Buddhist books printed on a large scale for the royal family.

1121109660000.title_en: Scripture on the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva (1988)
1121109660000.description: This is a three-volume woodblock-printed edition of the Scripture on the Original Vows of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, printed in 1469 at the request of Princess Jeongui for the repose of her late husband, An Maeng-dam. The beginning of the book includes a transformation painting, an invocation tablet, and images of guardian deities. The colophon was written by Kim Su-on, and engravers including Gwon Don-il, Sa Bu-gwi, and Go Mal-jong participated in carving the blocks.

1121109670000.title_en: Detailed Explanations of the Great Compendium of Ancient Prose and Fine Writing, Volumes 7-8
1121109670000.description: This is a metal-movable-type edition of the Chinese anthology Detailed Explanations of the Great Compendium of Ancient Prose and Fine Writing, printed in the first year of King Munjong's reign in 1450. It was printed with Geongo type cast in bronze, using Anpyeong Daegun's handwriting as the base text. Because Geongo type was melted down soon after Prince Anpyeong's death, printed copies in this type are very rare.

1121109680000.description: This is Volume 3 of the Lotus Sutra, preserved as a folded leaf book and reportedly taken from inside a Buddhist statue. The original upper and lower covers were removed when it was placed inside the statue, but the preservation condition is good. The final volume with the publication record is missing, so the exact date is unknown, though it is thought to have been printed in the early Joseon period.

1121109770000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Lotus Sutra was printed on paper in the form of a folded accordion book. It is the last volume of the seven-volume set, based on the interpretation by Song-dynasty monk Jiehuan, and was published in 1240 by order of Choi Yi during the reign of Goryeo King Gojong.

1121109780000.title_en: Avatamsaka Sutra in Gold on White Paper, Volume 29
1121109780000.description: This manuscript copies Volume 29 of the 80-volume Buddhist scripture translated by Śikṣānanda of the Tang dynasty. It was written in gold ink on white paper in an accordion-fold format, and is estimated to have been made in the early Joseon period, around the 15th century.

1123409790000.title_en: Seated Stone Buddha from Seohyeolsa Temple Site, Gongju
1123409790000.description: This is one of three Buddha statues excavated from the site of Seohyeolsa Temple in Gongju. It shows the restrained, schematic style of Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture, with a seated figure, an elaborate lotus pedestal, and a subdued treatment of the robe folds.

1123109800000.title_en: Wooden Seated Amitabha Buddha from Bongnimsa Temple, Hwaseong
1123109800000.description: This wooden seated Amitabha Buddha was identified as having been made no later than 1362 through a record found when the statue was regilded in 1978. The figure has a solemn face, a solid body slightly leaning forward, and distinctive robe folds that make it a representative work of the late Goryeo period.

1123109810000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Bhaisajyaguru Buddha in Gyosan-dong, Hanam
1123109810000.description: This rock-carved seated Buddha represents Bhaisajyaguru, the Buddha who heals all beings from illness. An inscription records the date as 977, and the statue has a calm face, a one-shoulder robe, a medicine bowl in the left hand, and a flame-decorated halo.

1123109820000.title_en: Rock-carved Half-seated Bodhisattva in Jangam-ri, Icheon
1123109820000.description: This large rock-carved bodhisattva is shallowly relief-carved across the face of a granite cliff known locally as Mireukbawi. An inscription on the back indicates that it was made in 981, and the figure is generally identified as Avalokiteśvara because of the high crown and the lotus stem held in the hand.

1123109830000.title_en: Standing Stone Buddha from Bongeopsa Temple Site, Anseong
1123109830000.description: This standing stone Buddha was originally at the Bongeopsa Temple site and was later moved through several locations. The statue and halo are carved from a single stone, and its broad shoulders, U-shaped robe folds, and balanced proportions are considered characteristic of early Goryeo regional Buddhist sculpture.

1123309840000.title_en: Standing Stone Buddha Triad from Sinhang-ri, Yeongdong
1123309840000.description: This Unified Silla stone Buddha triad stands in a pavilion with only a tiled roof at the site of the former Seokeunsa Temple. The central Buddha is flanked by two standing bodhisattvas, and the rounded face, heavy robe, and compact but dignified body are seen as continuing seventh-century stone Buddha traditions into the late seventh or early eighth century.

1123309850000.title_en: Stone Buddhist Sculpture Group of Yonghwasa Temple, Cheongju
1123309850000.description: This group consists of five Buddha statues and two bodhisattva statues now enshrined in Mireukbojeon Hall at Yonghwasa Temple in Cheongju. The seven large stone figures, ranging from 1.4 m to 5.5 m in height, are thought to date to the Goryeo period based on their faces, drapery treatment, and hand gestures.

1123409860000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Seated Statue of Unjangam Hermitage, Cheongyang
1123409860000.description: This gilt-bronze seated Avalokiteshvara statue was once kept by the roadside in a valley in front of Unjangam Hermitage and was moved there when the hermitage was rebuilt around 1900. It has been dated to the late Goryeo to early Joseon period on the basis of its style and the inscriptional evidence found inside the statue.

1123409870000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Seated Buddha of Shinamsa Temple, Dangjin
1123409870000.description: This is a seated gilt-bronze Buddha statue preserved at Shinamsa Temple and considered a Goryeo-period work. Its overall form is comparable to the Buddha statues of Janggoksa Temple in Cheongyang, but it is more massive and volumetric, with a heavy-faced, faintly smiling expression.

1123709880000.title_en: Stone Seated Buddha of Daeyul-ri, Gunwi
1123709880000.description: This standing figure is enshrined in Yonghajeon Hall of Daeyulsa Temple and stands on a round pedestal at a height of 2.65 m. Its refined face, low broad ushnisha, and drapery with shallow U-shaped folds indicate the characteristic style of Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture.

1123709890000.title_en: Wooden Amitabha Buddha Triad Seated Statue of Yongmunsa Temple, Yecheon
1123709890000.description: This wooden seated triad was made in 1684, during the reign of King Sukjong, as shown by the inscription on the lower part. The main figure and attendant images are carved in the round in a style that is closely related to the wooden hanging painting of the same temple, and the work is an important example of late 17th-century sculpture.

1123709890200.title_en: Wooden Amitabha Buddha as Preached by the Buddha Painting of Yongmunsa Temple, Yecheon
1123709890200.description: This wooden carved hanging Buddha image was made in 1684 and is considered the earliest extant example of its kind. It shows Amitabha seated at the center with attendant figures arranged above and below, and the composition is decorated with cloud patterns and radiating light motifs.

1123709900000.title_en: Iron Seated Vairocana Buddha of Namjangsa Temple, Sangju
1123709900000.description: This iron seated Vairocana Buddha is enshrined in Bogwangjeon Hall at Namjangsa Temple in Sangju, and only the main body survives today. Its solemn face, long ears, simple drapery, and prominent body build indicate that it is an important early Joseon iron Buddha statue.

1123709910000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva Seated Statue of Daeseungsa Temple, Mungyeong
1123709910000.description: This gilt-bronze seated Avalokiteshvara statue is kept under a glass case at Daeseungsa Temple and is thought to date to the late 15th century. An Avalokiteshvara prayer text found inside the statue indicates that it was made before it was re-gilded in 1516.

1122209920000.title_en: Dry Lacquer Seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and Reliquary Objects, Pagyesa Temple, Daegu
1122209920000.description: This seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is enshrined alone in a glass case at Pagyesa Temple. An inscription found inside the statue states that it was remade in 1447, during the 29th year of King Sejong, though its origin may be earlier. The statue shows features associated with late Goryeo Buddhist sculpture, including elaborate ornament and a solemn expression.

1123709930000.title_en: Dry Lacquer Seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva, Jangryuksa Temple, Yeongdeok
1123709930000.description: This early Joseon dry lacquer seated bodhisattva was made in 1395 through the donation of local officials and villagers, and was regilded in 1407. An inscription found inside the statue records both dates. Its angular face, strong modeling, and ornate decoration make it an important example for studying the transition from late Goryeo to early Joseon Buddhist sculpture.

1122309940000.title_en: Iron Seated Amitabha Buddha, Baengnyeonsa Temple, Ganghwa
1122309940000.description: This iron seated Amitabha Buddha at Baengnyeonsa Temple follows the restrained style that became popular in late Goryeo Buddhist sculpture. The slender face, simple drapery, and balanced seated posture create a calm and solemn impression. Based on its style, it is thought to date to the late 14th century or early 15th century.

1123709950000.title_en: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha with Wooden Halo, Chukseosa Temple, Bonghwa
1123709950000.description: This seated Vairocana Buddha is enshrined at Chukseosa Temple, and its original place of installation is unknown. The statue has a calm face, broad body, and a 9th-century style of drapery with stepped parallel folds. An inscription on the pagoda records that it was made in the late 9th century, making it an important work for studying late Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture.

1123709960000.title_en: Stone Seated Amitabha Buddha, Birosa Temple, Yeongju
1123709960000.description: This stone seated Amitabha Buddha at Birosa Temple originally had both a halo and a pedestal, though the halo is now broken and discarded. The rounded face, broad shoulders, and realistic treatment of the body reflect the naturalistic style of late Unified Silla sculpture. It is thought to date to the late 9th century.

1123709960200.title_en: Stone Seated Vairocana Buddha, Birosa Temple, Yeongju
1123709960200.description: This stone seated Vairocana Buddha was found at Birosa Temple together with a seated Amitabha Buddha. It shows the same late 9th-century characteristics of calm expression, stable body form, and stepped drapery. Together, the two statues are valuable evidence for Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture and beliefs.

1122209970000.title_en: Stone Seated Pensive Bodhisattva, Bukjiri, Bonghwa
1122209970000.description: This stone seated pensive bodhisattva was moved to Kyungpook National University in 1966 from beside the rock-carved Buddha at Bukjiri. Only the lower body and a separate round lotus pedestal survive, but the surviving parts show highly skilled carving. The pose, drapery, and ornaments suggest a mid-7th-century work.

1123809980000.title_en: Stone Standing Amitabha Buddha, Mitaam Hermitage, Yangsan
1123809980000.description: This stone standing Amitabha Buddha is enshrined in the cave temple of Mitaam Hermitage, which is said to have been founded by the monk Wonhyo. Its large ushnisha, long ears, rounded shoulders, and upright posture follow the style of the Gamsansa Temple stone Amitabha Buddha of 719. The halo, pedestal, and drapery indicate a Unified Silla date, probably in the first half of the 8th century.

1121110000000.title_en: Stone Seated Portrait of Master Seungga, Seunggasa Temple, Seoul
1121110000000.description: This stone seated portrait enshrined at Seunggasa Temple depicts Seungga Daeja, an Indian Buddhist monk who came to Tang China and was later praised as a manifestation of Avalokitesvara. An inscription on the back of the halo states that the sculpture was carved in 1024 under the direction of Jigwang and others.

1123810010000.title_en: Old Documents of the Yangsan Yi Clan's Head Family
1123810010000.description: This collection consists of 16 documents in 6 types preserved by the head family of the Yangsan Yi clan. Most of them date to the early Joseon period and include royal documents such as appointments, grants, and certificates related to the clan's descendants.

1123710020000.title_en: Documents and Books of the Gwon Ju Clan's Head Family
1123710020000.description: This collection contains 14 items in 9 types preserved by the head family of Gwon Ju, a civil official active from the reign of King Seongjong to King Yeonsan. It includes early documents such as appointment records, royal grants, and property division records, as well as books and handwritten letters by Gwon Ju.

1123710030000.title_en: Jo Jeong's Records of the Imjin War
1123710030000.description: This set comprises seven volumes of diaries written by Jo Jeong about what he saw, heard, and experienced during the Imjin War. The entries cover about six years from 1592 to 1597 and provide detailed information on social conditions, troop deployments, and the activities of the volunteer armies.

1123710040000.title_en: Documents and Books of Jo Jeong's Head Family (1989)
1123710040000.description: This collection contains 62 items preserved by the head family of Jo Jeong, a civil official of the Joseon period. It includes property division records, royal appointment documents, and seven books printed in the early Joseon period.

1123710040200.title_en: Documents and Books of Jo Jeong's Head Family (1991)
1123710040200.description: These three documents were produced during the reign of King Seonjo and are among the materials preserved by Jo Jeong's head family. They include examination-related royal documents that are useful for studying the Joseon civil service examination system.

1123710050000.title_en: Old Documents of the Jang Malson Clan's Head Family
1123710050000.description: This collection contains 18 documents in 5 types preserved by the head family of Jang Malson, a civil official of the Joseon period. The materials include land and slave ownership records, a document dividing property among sisters, and royal appointment documents.

1123710060000.title_en: Certificate of Appointment for Yi Jongju and Military Examination Diploma for Yi Im
1123710060000.description: This set consists of two royal documents preserved by the head family of Yi Jongju. One is a 1399 appointment document issued to Yi Jongju, and the other is a 1435 military examination diploma issued to his grandson Yi Im.

1121110310000.title_en: Celadon Flower-shaped Dish with Relief Lotus Pond Fish Design
1121110310000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon dish measures 9.3 cm in height, 16.1 cm in mouth diameter, and 6.1 cm in base diameter. The interior is decorated with delicate relief designs of three fish on the flat base and lotus, reeds, and ducks on the sides, while the exterior is plain. The rim is lobed into six points, forming a flower-like shape.

1123110320000.title_en: Celadon Bowl with Incised Lotus and Scroll Design and Inlaid Chrysanthemum Design
1123110320000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon bowl measures 6.9 cm in height, 16.6 cm in mouth diameter, and 4.0 cm in base diameter. The interior combines incised and molded decoration, while the exterior has four chrysanthemum motifs executed in white and black inlay. It is a rare example showing incised, molded, and inlaid decoration together on one vessel.

1121110330000.title_en: Celadon Pear-shaped Ewer with Inlaid Cloud, Crane, and Chrysanthemum Design and Stand
1121110330000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon ewer and stand were made as a set, based on their similar glaze and decoration. The ewer is shaped like a gourd and decorated with stamped chrysanthemums and cloud-and-crane motifs, while the stand has bands of scroll, chrysanthemum, and lotus designs. It is considered a representative work of 13th-century celadon in its late phase.

1121110340000.title_en: Celadon Maebyeong Vase with Inlaid Lotus Petal Design
1121110340000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon maebyeong vase stands 31.1 cm high with a slightly flared short mouth and a slender profile. Lotus petal designs are inlaid around the shoulder, body, and lower section, using white clay and dark clay. The pale blue-green glaze is translucent and contains fine bubbles.

1121110350000.title_en: Celadon Bottle with Incised Cloud Design
1121110350000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon bottle is a refined wine bottle standing 29.0 cm high. The neck is long and flared, and the body is decorated with incised scrolls, floral bands, small cloud motifs, and lotus designs. The glaze is thin, transparent, and pale blue-green with fine bubbles.

1121110360000.title_en: Celadon Pear-shaped Ewer with Inlaid Parrot Design
1121110360000.description: This Goryeo-period pear-shaped celadon ewer measures 26 cm in height and was made with a lid. The lower body is decorated with an inlaid pair of parrots inside a circular frame, while the spout and handle area have lotus-leaf and willow-branch motifs. It is considered a rare 12th-century example with an unusual use of parrot decoration on the lower body.

1121110370000.title_en: Celadon Bowl with Incised Chrysanthemum and Scroll Design
1121110370000.description: This Goryeo celadon bowl was made around the 11th century and measures 5.9 cm in height and 17.5 cm in mouth diameter. It has a wide footed base and a pale green transparent glaze with prominent crackling. The interior is decorated with a band and incised chrysanthemum scrolls, while the exterior is plain.

1121110380000.title_en: Celadon Bottle with Iron-painted and Relief Lotus Petal Design
1121110380000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon bottle was made around the 13th century and measures 8.1 cm in height. The upper body is decorated with relief plant motifs and iron-painted accents, and the lower body bears lotus designs; the base also has an incised character. It is notable for its unusual form, decoration, and inscription.

1121110230000.title_en: Celadon Lidded Box with Incised Cloud-and-Dragon Design and Inscription of "Sangyakguk"
1121110230000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon box is 9.3 cm high, with an opening diameter of 7 cm and a base diameter of 5.5 cm. The inscription "Sangyakguk" suggests that it was used as a container for medicine. The lid has an incised cloud-and-dragon design and transparent celadon glaze with fine crackles over the surface.

1123110240000.title_en: Celadon Bowl with Incised Lotus and Scroll Design and Inlaid Cloud-and-Crane Design
1123110240000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon bowl is 5.0 cm high, with an opening diameter of 16.2 cm and a base diameter of 4.4 cm. The interior is decorated with shallow relief lotus and vine patterns, while the exterior has inlaid cloud-and-crane designs between bands of white inlaid lines. It shows both relief and inlay techniques on a single vessel, an uncommon combination for an early celadon piece.

1121110250000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon water dropper is modeled in the shape of a peach and measures 8.6 cm in height and 9.6 cm by 7.1 cm in width. The stem and leaves are attached to the body to create a realistic form, and the surface is incised to emphasize the peach's texture and leaf veins. It is the only extant peach-shaped celadon water dropper from the Goryeo period.

1123110260000.title_en: Celadon Square Incense Burner with Relief Taotie Design
1123110260000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon incense burner is modeled after a square bronze cauldron form from the Zhou dynasty in China. It has a trapezoidal body with two angular handles on top, and each corner is decorated with a sculpted cicada figure. The exterior is densely decorated with impressed and incised patterns, including thunder-pattern bands and paired taotie motifs.

1121110270000.title_en: Celadon Incense Burner with Tortoise-Dragon Lid
1121110270000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon incense burner has a wide flanged rim and a lid decorated with a tortoise-dragon figure. The tortoise-dragon has a turtle-shaped body and a dragon's head, and the surface is finely detailed with incised lines; the shell is inscribed with the character "wang" (王). The burner is made so that smoke rises through the open body and out through the lid figure.

1121110280000.title_en: Celadon Jar with Incised Lotus and Scroll Design
1121110280000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon jar is 24.4 cm high, with an opening and base diameter of 11.5 cm. It has a rounded body decorated with large lotus blossoms and dense vine scrolls, rendered with a half-relief technique and fine incised lines. The glaze is a clear jade-green color with little crackling.

1123110290000.title_en: Celadon Ewer with Inlaid Peony Design
1123110290000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon ewer is 19.2 cm high, with an opening diameter of 3.4 cm and a base diameter of 10.3 cm. It has a nearly spherical body, lid, handle, and spout, with inlaid peony designs on the front and back. The spout and handle are also decorated with inlay and relief details, making it a rare early example of inlaid celadon.

1123110300000.title_en: Celadon Flowerpot with Inlaid Cloud-and-Crane Design
1123110300000.description: This Goryeo-period celadon flowerpot is 23.0 cm high, with an opening diameter of 28.2 cm and a base diameter of 22.0 cm. It has a cylindrical body with a drainage hole at the center of the bottom, indicating its use as a planter. Clouds and cranes are arranged in alternating patterns on the upper section, with lotus-petal patterns below.

1121110390000.title_en: Celadon Inlaid Bowl and Dish with Peony Design
1121110390000.description: This set consists of three Goryeo-period Buddhist alms bowls and one dish, all made in matching form, glaze, and decoration. The bowls and dish are decorated with inlaid chrysanthemum and peony motifs, with white-inlaid floral scroll patterns on the exterior. The four pieces appear to have been made at the same time.

1123610400000.title_en: Hwaeom Stone Sutra of Hwaeomsa Temple, Gurye
1123610400000.description: This stone sutra consists of carved passages from the Avatamsaka Sutra engraved on thin light-blue stone slabs. It was placed at Hwaeomsa Temple in 677 under the orders of the monk Uisang, and about 9,000 fragments remain after later damage and fire. The inscription is a valuable example of late Silla Buddhist scripture carving.

1123810410000.title_en: Palsangdo Paintings of Yeongsanjeon Hall, Tongdosa Temple
1123810410000.description: This set of eight paintings depicts the eight scenes of the Buddha's life from birth to nirvana. It was painted on silk in 1775 during the reign of King Yeongjo and is preserved as eight framed panels. The set includes explanatory texts for each scene and is an important work for the study of Joseon Buddhist painting.

1123810420000.title_en: Painting of the Three Bodies of the Buddha, Daegwangmyeongjeon Hall, Tongdosa Temple
1123810420000.description: This three-panel Buddhist painting depicts Vairocana, Locana, and Shakyamuni Buddhas. It was painted in 1759 by Im Han and others, with Vairocana in the center, Locana to the left, and Shakyamuni to the right. It is a rare example in Joseon Buddhist painting because it represents the Three Bodies as Vairocana, Locana, and Shakyamuni rather than the more common triad.

1123610430000.title_en: Portraits of the Sixteen Patriarchs, Songgwangsa Temple, Suncheon
1123610430000.description: These portraits depict sixteen eminent monks associated with Songgwangsa Temple and active in the late Goryeo period, including Bojo Guksa Jinul. Although sixteen panels were originally designated, only three remain at the temple today and the others have not been located. The portraits were installed in 1780 and are important examples of Buddhist portrait painting from the Joseon period.

1123610440000.title_en: Portrait of State Preceptor Uicheon, Daegakguksa, Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123610440000.description: This portrait depicts the Goryeo monk Uicheon (1055–1101), who worked to integrate Buddhism through the founding of the Cheontae school. It shows him seated and facing right, holding a staff in his left hand and prayer beads on his wrist with his right hand on the chair arm. The painting was retouched and supplemented in 1805 by the monk painter Doil Bhikshu, and the inscription by Hyegeun adds to its value.

1121110450000.title_en: Painting of a Birthday Banquet for Men Born in the Year Sinhae
1121110450000.description: This painting depicts a birthday banquet for three men who were all born in the year Sinhae, during the 6th year of King Myeongjong (1551). The composition is divided into three horizontal sections, with the banquet scene in the middle and written records of the participants and event below. Painted in 1626, it is an important source for studying genre painting and the daily life of Joseon yangban.

1121110460000.title_en: Painting of the Old Residence at Hwagae-hyeon
1121110460000.description: This painting depicts the villa in Jirisan associated with the early Joseon scholar-official Jeong Yeo-chang (1450–1504). It was made in 1643 at the request of Jeong's family to preserve the appearance of the residence before it was damaged. The work is considered an important example of An Gyeon-style landscape painting and a valuable source for the study of Joseon Confucian culture.

1123410070000.description: This group consists of six types and seven items left by Jo Heon (1544–1592), who served as a righteous army commander during the Japanese invasions of 1592 and died fighting at Geumsan. It includes the diary Jocheon ilgi, appointment documents, decrees appointing him as righteous army commander, a decree for memorial services, two memorial addresses, and a bamboo quiver. The documents date from the Joseon period, from Jo Heon’s lifetime through later commemorations.

1123110080000.title_en: Books and Documents of the Jeongranggongpa Lineage of the Hamyang Bak Clan
1123110080000.description: This collection was kept by the Hamyang Bak clan, and only seven kinds and 46 items judged to be old, rare, or historically valuable were designated. It includes works such as Naamsurok, Dangsigochwi, Dangjo Chaeknim, Mangukjeondo, Jeosang Ilwol, Tonggam, and Jeosang Ilyong. The materials are important sources for research on Joseon-period society, economy, culture, and politics.

1121110090000.title_en: Exemption Edict for Ssangbongsa Temple, Neungseong
1121110090000.description: This royal edict, issued in August 1457 by King Sejo, ordered that Ssangbongsa Temple in Neungseong be exempted from corvée labor and granted land and slaves. It states that the provincial governor and local magistrates should protect the temple and reduce its burdens according to the earlier royal instruction. The document is a valuable example of an early Joseon saepae edict and shows Sejo’s support for Buddhism.

1121110100100.description: This woodblock-printed Korean translation of the Lotus Sutra was printed in 1463 by the Gangyeongdogam and offered to the king by officials including Yun Sa-ro. The text is based on the Chinese translation by Kumarajiva, with annotations by Gyehwan and collected notes by Iryeo, and the main text and Gyehwan’s explanations are rendered in easy-to-read Korean. It is an important Buddhist text and a significant source for the study of early Korean vernacular printing.

1123110100200.description: This Korean translation of the Lotus Sutra was printed from woodblocks in 1463 at the Gangyeongdogam under King Sejo. Based on the Chinese version translated by Kumarajiva, it was annotated by Gyehwan and compiled by Iryeo, then rendered in Korean by Yun Sa-ro and others. It is an important source for the study of Middle Korean and early Joseon Buddhist printing.

1121110110000.description: This Buddhist scripture, also called the Ksitigarbha Sutra, teaches the vow of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to guide sentient beings and save even those suffering in hell. It was produced at Hwaamsa Temple in Wanju in 1453, with the text written by Gongam and carved on woodblocks by the great monk Uimyeong. The volume is made up of three parts bound into one book and preserves evidence of early Joseon methods of indicating page or leaf counts.

1123110120000.title_en: Short Record of the Dharma Words of Monk Mongsan (Eonhae) (1989)
1123110120000.description: This book contains Dharma words, or Buddhist teachings, by the Yuan monk Mongsan Deok-i and one work by the Goryeo monk Naong Hyegeun. It was annotated and translated into Korean by the Joseon monk Haegakjonja Sinmi, then printed from woodblocks on mulberry paper in 1472. The colophon shows that it was one of the Buddhist books published under Queen Dowager Insu, and it is an important source for Buddhist history and early Hunminjeongeum studies.

1123310130000.title_en: Commentary on the Great Avatamsaka Sutra, Volume 68
1123310130000.description: This is volume 68 of a 120-volume commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, explaining the scripture as interpreted by Tang-dynasty Jingguan and annotated by Song-dynasty Jingyuan. It was printed from woodblocks on mulberry paper in a folding format and is believed to be a Goryeo-period edition made from blocks sent by Jingyuan to Uicheon. It is a valuable source for understanding exchanges between famous monks of Song China and Goryeo.

1123310140000.description: This woodblock-printed book is a collection compiled by the Song dynasty scholar Nie Miaoxing, gathering inscriptions, songs, essential teachings, sermons, poems, and prose by various Zen masters. It was printed in 1462 by the Gangyeongdogam, the government office established under King Sejo to publish Buddhist scriptures with Korean explanations. The colophon also records that Hwang O-sin wrote the text and that Yun Pil-sang, No Sa-sin, and Han Gye-hui proofread it.

1123310150000.description: This book contains a summary by the Song dynasty monk Zhizhao of the basic doctrines and founders of the five major Buddhist schools of his time. The extant edition was re-engraved at Haeinsa by Monk Muhak in 1395, based on an earlier edition printed in Yuan China in 1357. It is a woodblock print on hemp paper and is an important source for early Joseon Buddhist studies and bibliography.

1123310160000.description: This is the second book of Volume 1 of the commentary on the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment, a scripture known in Korean as the Won'gakgyeong. The text is a woodblock print on hemp paper, and it was reformatted from a scroll layout into a bound book with 10 lines printed per page. It is believed to be a Goryeo woodblock edition based on a Song dynasty version.

1123310170000.title_en: Daebanggwang Bulhwaeomgyeong, Jin Edition Volume 15; Zhou Edition Volume 38; and Zhengyuan Edition Volumes 2 and 38
1123310170000.description: This item consists of four bound fascicles from different editions of the Avataṃsaka Sutra: the Jin edition, Zhou edition, and Zhengyuan edition. All are woodblock prints on hemp paper made in a folding format, and the colophon of one section preserves the name Chungjeong. Based on the text forms and carving style, the prints are thought to date to the 12th or 13th century, with some parts probably copied from Goryeo carvings of King Sukjong's reign.

1123710180000.title_en: Historical Documents of the Yean Branch of the Gwangsan Kim Clan
1123710180000.description: This group consists of 429 selected documents from a larger corpus of more than 1,000 records preserved by the head family of the Yean branch of the Gwangsan Kim clan over about 600 years. The designated materials include royal decrees, certificates, petitions, adoption records, family division documents, deeds of sale, and wedding-related documents. They are valuable sources for studying politics, economy, society, and family systems from the late Goryeo period through the Korean Empire.

1123710190000.title_en: Collected Books of the Yean Branch of the Gwangsan Kim Clan
1123710190000.description: This collection includes 61 items in 13 kinds of books and autograph albums preserved in the head family of the Yean branch of the Gwangsan Kim clan. It includes major Confucian works and collected writings such as Seojeon, Songjomyungsin Eonhaengnok, Maewoldangjip, Jeompiljaejip, and Jingbirok, as well as autograph albums containing calligraphy by Toegye Yi Hwang. These materials were published in the Joseon period and are important historical sources for studying that era.

1123810200000.title_en: Kim Gwang-nyeo and His Siblings' Family Property Division Agreement
1123810200000.description: This document records the division of inherited property among three siblings of the Gwangsan Kim clan in 1480, after their parents had died. The property, including land and enslaved people, was divided by age order rather than by sex, beginning with the eldest brother Kim Gwang-nyeo, followed by Han Geon’s wife, and then Kim Gwang-beom. The document is an important source for studying Joseon society and family systems.

1121110220000.title_en: Celadon Bottle with Inlaid Copper-Decorated Lotus, Arabesque, and Dragon Design
1121110220000.description: This Goryeo celadon bottle dates to the mid-14th century and measures 38.3 cm in height. It has a long upright neck, a slightly flared mouth, and a rounded body decorated with inlaid designs. The surface combines white and black inlay with copper pigment accents, including lotus, chrysanthemum, cloud, crane, and dragon motifs.

1121110470000.description: This small gilt-bronze statue depicts Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva seated on a lotus pedestal. The crown is decorated with floral designs and jewels, and the figure holds a sutra in the right hand, identifying it as Mahasthamaprapta. Based on its style, it is estimated to date to the late 14th or early 15th century.

1121110480000.title_en: Painting of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and the Ten Kings
1121110480000.description: This Buddhist painting depicts Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and the Ten Kings, the judges of the underworld. Ksitigarbha is placed large at the center, while the Ten Kings, the Four Heavenly Kings, and Domyeong Beings are arranged smaller below on both sides. It is considered one of the extant Goryeo Buddhist paintings and is thought to date to the 14th century.

1123310490000.description: This is a Korean vernacular translation of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, a scripture widely studied in Buddhist training. It was originally translated from the Chinese by Banjamilje and explained in simpler terms by Guihan, then rendered into Korean. The book was printed in metal type on paper made from mulberry bark mixed with straw, and the newly found Volume 6 completes the set of ten volumes.

1123310500000.description: This is a one-volume edition of the Amitābha Sūtra published by the Gangyeongdogam in 1464. It is a Korean vernacular translation of the Chinese text by Kumārajīva and was printed from wooden blocks on paper. The book is important because very few copies of the first Gangyeongdogam edition survive.

1123110510000.title_en: Annotated Korean Translation of the Collected Poems of Du Fu, Volume 13
1123110510000.description: This book is a Korean translation of poems by the Tang poet Du Fu, compiled under royal command during the reign of King Seongjong. It was translated by scholars of the Hongmungwan and printed with metal type and Korean type. The volume is valued as an important source for Korean literature, Korean linguistics, and printing history.

1122210510200.title_en: Annotated Korean Translation of the Collected Poems of Du Fu, Volumes 11-12
1122210510200.description: This is a combined one-volume edition of volumes 11 and 12 of the Korean translation of Du Fu's poems. It preserves a rare metal-type printing from the reign of King Seongjong and includes Korean glosses with tonal marks. Although parts of the beginning and end are missing, it remains an important source for the study of Korean literature, linguistics, and bibliography.

1123310510300.title_en: Annotated Korean Translation of the Collected Poems of Du Fu, Volume 21
1123310510300.description: This volume is part of the first edition of the Korean translation of Du Fu's poems printed in 1481 with metal type and Korean type. The text presents the Chinese original, notes, and vernacular explanation in a carefully arranged format, and the Korean text preserves pre-Imjin War phonological features through tonal marks. It is an important source for the study of Korean language and literary translation.

1123110510400.title_en: Annotated Korean Translation of the Collected Poems of Du Fu, Volumes 17-19
1123110510400.description: This item is a one-volume set of volumes 17 to 19 from the Korean translation of Du Fu's poems, printed with metal type during the reign of King Seongjong. The text is organized by subject categories such as birds, beasts, insects, fish, flowers, grasses, bamboo, and trees. It is valued as an important source for the study of Joseon-era Korean language, poetry, and translation.

1121110510500.description: This is a Korean vernacular translation and classification of Du Fu’s poetry, compiled by court officials and monks under King Seongjong’s order and first published in 1481. It is important both for its use of early Hangul metal type and for preserving early Hangul orthography and grammar.

1123110520000.description: This woodblock-printed book is one volume from a two-volume edition of a work by the Goryeo monk Je-gwan that summarizes Tiantai Buddhist thought. According to the colophon, it was copied anew and printed by the Gibok Dogam in 1315.

1123110530000.description: This is a Hangul translation of Buddhist ritual texts, ordered by the court and printed in 1496 with wooden type. It was produced in 400 copies and is valued as an important source for the history of printing and early Korean language.

1121110540000.description: This early Joseon white porcelain bottle has a broad mouth, long neck, full body, and wide high foot. It is thought to have been made in Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do, in the late 15th to early 16th century.

1121110550000.description: This set of white porcelain childbirth jars was used at the royal court to hold the placenta of a prince or princess, together with a stone inscribed with the child’s name and birth date. The outer and inner jars are similar in form, and the set dates to the early Joseon period.

1121110560000.title_en: White Porcelain Blue-and-iron-Decorated Three-mountain Thunder-pattern Ritual Vessel
1121110560000.description: This is an early Joseon white porcelain ritual vessel modeled after a bronze ancestral rite vessel known as a sanroe. It is decorated with iron-painted thunder patterns and blue-painted three-mountain motifs, and is the only surviving white porcelain example of this type.
1121110560000.material: White porcelain with underglaze cobalt blue and iron underglaze

1121110570000.title_en: White Porcelain Blue-and-white “Mangudae” Inscribed Saucer with Floral and Insect Design
1121110570000.description: This shallow saucer has the inscription “Mangudae” at the center, with two chrysanthemums and a bee painted around it. It is thought to have been made in Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do, in the late 15th to early 16th century.
1121110570000.material: White porcelain with underglaze cobalt blue

1121110580000.title_en: White Porcelain Blue-and-white Seven-treasure and Orchid Bottle
1121110580000.description: This late Joseon bottle combines an eight-sided lower body with a long-necked upper section, creating a gourd-like form. It is decorated with seven-treasure motifs on the upper part and orchid motifs on the lower part, and is thought to date to the first half of the 18th century.
1121110580000.material: White porcelain with underglaze cobalt blue

1121110590000.title_en: White Porcelain Brush Holder with Underglaze Cobalt Floral Design
1121110590000.description: This Joseon Dynasty brush holder is a cylindrical white porcelain vessel used for storing paper, with a pale bluish-white glaze. Blue bands and freely painted orchid motifs are placed around the lower body, and it is thought to have been made in the first half of the 18th century at the Gwangju kiln site in Gimsari or a slightly later Bunwon-ri kiln.

1121110600000.title_en: White Porcelain Bottle with Iron-painted Hanging Cord Design
1121110600000.description: This Joseon Dynasty wine bottle has a flaring rim, a narrow neck, and a rounded body, with a dark iron-painted cord motif on the surface. The base interior bears a Korean inscription, and the piece is believed to date to the late 16th century, making it a rare early example of iron-painted white porcelain.

1121110610000.title_en: White Porcelain Horn Cup with Iron-painted Decoration
1121110610000.description: This horn-shaped cup is modeled after a cow horn, with the tip darkly painted to emphasize its realism. It is a Joseon Dynasty white porcelain piece, likely produced at the Buncheon-ri or Gwaneum-ri kilns in Gwangju, and is considered an important early Joseon example of this rare form.

1121110620000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Ewer with Iron-painted Scroll Design
1121110620000.description: This buncheong ware ewer, made in the first half of the 16th century, was used for holding water, liquor, soy sauce, or urine. Its surface is coated with white slip and decorated with freely brushed iron-oxide vine scrolls and a 十-shaped mark, showing characteristic buncheong techniques.

1121110630000.title_en: White Porcelain Octagonal Dish with Underglaze Cobalt Plum Blossom, Moon, and Ten Symbols of Longevity Design
1121110630000.description: This Joseon Dynasty white porcelain dish has an octagonal exterior and was made in the mid to late 18th century. The interior bears a plum blossom and moon motif, while the outside is decorated with the Ten Symbols of Longevity in underglaze cobalt blue.

1121110640000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Underglaze Cobalt Cloud-and-Dragon Design
1121110640000.description: This typical Joseon Dynasty jar has three large medallion-like panels on the body, each showing a dragon playing with a wish-fulfilling jewel among clouds. The blue decoration is somewhat pale, and the glossy, crackled glaze suggests a production date in the late 18th century at Gwangju, Gyeonggi-do.

1121110650000.title_en: White Porcelain Placenta Jar and Placenta Stone (1991)
1121110650000.description: This set consists of an outer placenta jar, an inner placenta jar, and a placenta stone used for royal children in the Joseon Dynasty. The placenta stone is inscribed with the production date, and the jars are thought to have been made before 1581, providing important evidence for late 16th-century royal porcelain.

1121110660000.title_en: White Porcelain Octagonal Cylindrical Bottle with Underglaze Cobalt Flower-and-Bird Design
1121110660000.description: This Joseon Dynasty bottle has an octagonal body, a flaring mouth, and a narrow cylindrical neck, making it a form used for pouring liquor. Large flower-and-bird motifs are painted in underglaze cobalt blue on the front and back, and the base bears a lightly incised 官 mark, suggesting a late 18th-century date.

1121110750000.title_en: Volume 16 of the First Tripitaka Koreana Edition of the Abhidharmamahāvibhāṣā-śāstra
1121110750000.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist text is Volume 16 of the First Tripitaka Koreana Edition compiled during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo (r. 1011–1031). It was printed on paper joined into a long scroll format, and is estimated to have been produced in the 12th century. The volume is part of the first carving of the Tripitaka made to overcome the Khitan invasions through the power of Buddhism.

1121110760000.title_en: Record of Meritorious Subject, Kim Cheolli, for Founding the State
1121110760000.description: This is a meritorious subject certificate issued in 1395 to Kim Cheolli by the Office for Meritorious Subjects for his contributions to the founding of Joseon by Yi Seong-gye. The document records 695 names and bears the seal of the Ministry of Personnel in 45 places. It also includes the names and signatures of officials involved in issuing the certificate.

1121110770100.title_en: Jeonsik Edition of the Neoseongnok, Volumes 1–3 and 9–14
1121110770100.description: This printed edition of the Neoseongnok was published in Jinyang in 1370, during the reign of King Gongmin of Goryeo, after Yi Nosuk obtained a copy through Park Sangchung. The volume endings state the place of publication and the year, and the text shows the Goryeo practice of omitting the character for the reign title 'Hongmu' (Hongwu). It is a woodblock-printed book.

1121110770200.description: This complete edition of the Neoseongnok was printed with moveable metal type called Choju Gapinja. A colophon written by Kim Mun at the end of volume 14, dated June 1436 in the 18th year of King Sejong, identifies the printing date. The book is well preserved and contains four seals.

1121110780000.title_en: Calligraphic Works by Han Ho - Seokbong Jeongjeokcheop
1121110780000.description: This calligraphy album contains three pieces written by Han Ho, also known as Seokbong, and presented at a gathering in 1596. The album includes excerpts from Wang Bo's 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng,' Han Wudi's 'Autumn Wind Song,' and Li Bai's 'Preface to a Spring Night Banquet at the Peach and Plum Garden.' It preserves both the calligrapher's writing and a record of the guests present at the banquet.

1121110780200.title_en: Calligraphic Works by Han Ho - Seokbong Jinjeokcheop
1121110780200.description: This album gathers late calligraphy by Han Ho, also known as Seokbong, written between 1602 and 1604, with one additional Daoist scripture copied at an unknown date. It includes pieces written in regular, running, and cursive scripts, and several dates and seals identify Han Ho as the writer. The mounting and seals show that it was later collected by Kim Gwangguk.

1121110780300.title_en: Calligraphic Works by Han Ho - Seokbong Han Ho Haeseocheop
1121110780300.description: This two-volume album contains 21 poems and prose pieces by Choi Rip copied in Han Ho's regular script, with one additional poem by Li Bai written in cursive script in the lower volume. A colophon dated September 1803 by Eom Gye-eung appears at the end of the lower volume. The work is important for showing Han Ho's characteristic style as a court calligrapher.

1121110790000.description: This is a book on rites compiled in Ming China under the Hongwu reign. It was used in Korea from the late Goryeo period through the early Joseon period, especially in the procedures of the Ministry of Rites, before being gradually replaced after the compilation of the Gukjo Oryeui. The book is an important source for studying diplomatic and ritual practices before King Seongjong's time.

1121110670000.title_en: Buncheong Bottle with Inlaid Lotus and Arabesque Design
1121110670000.description: This Joseon-period bottle is 31.7 cm high and has a stable, rounded profile that widens below the neck and narrows again toward the foot. The surface is decorated with white inlaid lines, arabesque scrolls, stylized lotus motifs, and dotted diaper patterns, with the lotus outlines done in white inlay and the interiors in black inlay. The glaze was applied over the whole vessel but is uneven, leaving a textured surface.

1121110680000.title_en: Buncheong Covered Jar with Inlaid Peony and Arabesque Design
1121110680000.description: This covered jar is a Joseon-period buncheong ware vessel, and its form and decoration show the transition from late inlaid celadon to buncheong ware. The body is divided into three sections by inlaid white lines, with black- and white-inlaid lotus petals, dense peony and scroll motifs, and lotus decoration around the lower body. The lid has a circular knob and peony leaves on the top surface; the vessel is thought to date to the 15th century.

1121110690000.title_en: Buncheong Flattened Bottle with Incised Tree and Bird Design
1121110690000.description: This Joseon-period bottle has a flattened oval body formed by beating the two sides of a rounded vessel, with a slightly narrow neck. Its surface is decorated with combed and incised designs on a light white slip, including abstract floral motifs on both sides and a tree with a bird on one face. The freer, semi-abstract treatment of the decoration suggests an early Joseon date.

1121110700000.title_en: Buncheong Jar with Scraped Peony Design
1121110700000.description: This large Joseon-period jar was used for storing liquids such as water, wine, soy sauce, or urine. It has an elongated oval body with one rounded side and one flattened side, and is decorated with combed and scraped designs over a white slip. The motifs include peonies, lotus petals, leaf patterns, and wave bands, and it is thought to date to the early Joseon period.

1121110710000.description: This is a Joseon-period celadon jar, 23.4 cm high, with a rounded rim, a wide shoulder, and a body that narrows toward the base. The lid has a lotus-bud-shaped knob, and the vessel is covered with celadon glaze that is unevenly applied and slightly mottled. Its form resembles early Joseon white porcelain jars.

1121110720000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Sutra on the Precepts of the Upāsaka
1121110720000.description: This scroll is one volume of the early printed Tripitaka edition produced in the reign of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo to pray for the defeat of the Khitan invasion. It is a woodblock print on dak paper, measuring 29 cm by 47.3 cm, and was printed from a text translated by Gunabhadra of the Liu Song dynasty. The record has no publication date and shows features characteristic of the early Goryeo Tripitaka.

1121110730000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Abhidharmakośa-śāstra, Volume 24
1121110730000.description: This is volume 24 of the early printed Tripitaka edition made during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on paper, consisting of 16 joined sheets, and was translated by Saṅghadeva and Zhu Fonian. The absence of a publication date and the use of early orthographic features indicate that it belongs to the first Goryeo Tripitaka, and it is thought to have been printed in the 12th century.

1121110740000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Abhidharma-Śarīra-śāstra, Volume 13
