1121110740000.description: This is volume 13 of the early printed Tripitaka edition made during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo. It is a woodblock-printed scroll on paper, translated by Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty, and originally consisted of 23 joined sheets, though the first three sheets are now missing. The absence of a publication date and the text’s features indicate that it belongs to the first Goryeo Tripitaka, and it is thought to have been printed in the 12th century.

1123310880200.description: This medical book records symptoms related to childbirth and prescriptions for treatment. It was translated into Korean by the royal physician Heo Jun in 1608 at the king’s command and printed at Naeuiwon using type from Hunryeondogam.

1121110890000.description: This is the surviving portion of a poetic anthology compiled by Choe Hae, a late Goryeo civil official, from outstanding Chinese-style verse by Korean scholars of the Goryeo period. The extant text consists of volumes 7 to 9 and is valued as an early source for literary history and for study of the poets and their works.

1121110900000.description: This printed book gathers the three imperial poems personally composed by Ming Taizu for Gwon Geun and 24 response poems written at the emperor’s command, with notes added by Gwon Lam. It was published in woodblock print in 1462, and the copy preserved from the Jinju Ha clan is noted for its fine printing and good condition.

1123810900200.description: This printed book gathers the three imperial poems personally composed by Ming Taizu for Gwon Geun and 24 response poems written at the emperor’s command, with notes added by Gwon Lam. It was published in woodblock print in 1462, and the copy preserved from the Jinju Ha clan is noted for its fine printing and good condition.

1121110910000.description: This is a woodblock-printed edition of Yi Seung-hyu’s historical verse work, originally composed in 1360. It presents Chinese history in seven-syllable verse in the first volume and Korean history in two sections in the second volume, and is an important source for comparing with Samguk sagi and Samguk yusa.

1121110910200.description: This woodblock edition was printed in the early Joseon period from printing blocks believed to have been carved around 1360 in the reign of King Gongmin of Goryeo. Yi Seung-hyu’s work recounts Chinese and Korean history in verse and is valued as a rare source for ancient history and literary studies.

1121110920000.description: This sutra teaches ways for beings to rely on Buddhist power and practice in order to eliminate sins and attain health and long life. The extant edition was re-carved and printed in 1416, based on older Goryeo-period printing blocks that had worn out.

1121110930000.description: This is a woodblock-printed edition of the Chan Buddhist classic commonly known as the Blue Cliff Record, printed with medium-sized metal type from the Eulyuja font. The text presents and explains around 100 sayings and verses selected by the monk Seoldo, and this copy is valued as the oldest surviving complete edition.

1121110800000.title_en: Great Expansive and Perfect Enlightenment Sutra with Brief Commentary and Annotation, Volume 1
1121110800000.description: This is a woodblock-printed Buddhist text of the Great Expansive and Perfect Enlightenment Sutra with brief commentary and annotation by Zongmi of the Tang dynasty. It includes a preface by Pei Xiu at the beginning. The book was re-carved in Goryeo based on a Song dynasty edition and is printed on traditional Korean paper.

1121110810000.description: This woodblock-printed edition was produced in 1399 and contains the Lotus Sutra translated by Kumarajiva with annotations by Gyehuan. The seven fascicles are bound in two volumes, and a record at the end states that it was published under the patronage of Hae-rin, Jeong Cheon-ik, and Lee Yang. It is considered an important source for the study of Buddhist history and bibliography.

1121110820000.title_en: Diamond Sutra with the Five Masters' Commentaries
1121110820000.description: This woodblock-printed book was made in 1415 and compiles five commentaries on the Diamond Sutra by Fu Dashi of the Liang dynasty, Huineng of the Tang dynasty, Zongjing of the Song dynasty, and Cheonno. The upper and lower fascicles are bound as one volume, and the first and last leaves are partly missing. It was printed by Seonggeo, with sponsorship from Haehye and Jou, and is a valuable Buddhist and bibliographic source.

1121110830000.description: This is the twentieth fascicle of the 40-volume Avatamsaka Sutra translated by the Tang dynasty translator Prājña. It is a folded, accordion-style woodblock print on Korean paper, with a dark blue cover and a title written in gold. The print is thought to be a later impression from a Goryeo-era edition carved in the reign of King Sukjong of Goryeo.

1121110860000.description: This medical book was compiled by Heo Jun in 1613 on royal command during a severe epidemic then called Tanghongyeok or Tangdokyeok. It records the causes of the disease, methods of diagnosis and treatment, preventive measures, and prescriptions. The same woodblock edition is preserved in three copies, each with a royal gift record indicating former storage at different government repositories.

1121110870100.title_en: Sinchan Byeokonbang (Newly Compiled Methods for Preventing Epidemics)
1121110870100.description: This medical text was compiled by Heo Jun in 1613 on royal command for the treatment of an epidemic disease. It discusses the cause of the illness, treatment methods, medicinal substances, and prohibitions, and includes a preface by Lee Jeong-gwi dated the second month of 1613. The designated copies were printed by the Royal Medical Office and bear royal gift marks on the covers.

1121110870200.title_en: Sinchan Byeokonbang (Newly Compiled Methods for Preventing Epidemics)
1121110870200.description: This manuscript copy of the medical text was compiled by Heo Jun in 1613 on royal command. It records the causes, pulse patterns, symptoms, medicine names, treatment methods, and prohibitions related to epidemic disease. The surviving copy is now held by the Huh Joon Museum and is valued as a source for the history of disease.

1123310880100.title_en: Eonhae Taesan Jibyo (Korean Translation of Essential Methods for Pregnancy and Childbirth)
1123310880100.description: This is a Korean translation of a medical text on symptoms and prescriptions related to pregnancy and childbirth, compiled by the royal physician Heo Jun in 1608 by order of the king. It begins with advice on conceiving a child and goes on to describe symptoms during pregnancy, prescriptions, and rules and taboos during delivery. The book contains a publication record at the end and a royal gift record on the back cover.

1121110940000.description: This woodblock-printed book contains a summary by the Song monk Jisao of the basic doctrines and founding figures of five Buddhist schools. The Korean edition was re-engraved at Hoeamsa Temple in 1395 based on a 1357 Yuan-dynasty edition by Gang Geumgang.

1123110950000.title_en: Collected Texts from the Buddha’s Belly, Wooden Amitabha Buddha Seated Statue, Bongnimsa Temple, Hwaseong
1123110950000.description: This collection consists of eight types and 17 items found in the inner reliquary of a wooden seated Amitabha Buddha statue at Bongnimsa Temple, Hwaseong. It includes manuscript and printed Buddhist texts such as a small-format Diamond Sutra and a section of a Goryeo-period Avatamsaka Sutra, reflecting late Goryeo faith in sutra copying and recitation.

1123110960000.description: This is a diary written by O Hui-mun during the Imjin War, recording events from 1591 to February 1601. The seven-volume set includes court documents, proclamations, appeals, and other writings that help explain the war, local conditions, and civilian life at the time.

1123610970000.description: This is a portrait of Yeom Je-sin (1304–1382), a late Goryeo civil official who served as chancellor. He is shown wearing a pyeongjeong-gwan and looking to the right, with delicate linework used for the face, hair, beard, and robe patterns.

1121110980000.title_en: Diamond Sutra and Two Other Sutras in Silver on Dark Blue Paper
1121110980000.description: This sutra manuscript contains the three basic scriptures of Maitreya faith: the Maitreya Bodhisattva’s Descent to Tusita Heaven Sutra, the Maitreya Descent Sutra, and the Maitreya Great Enlightenment Sutra. It was written in silver pigment on dark blue paper in 1315 by the monk Sinin as a prayer for peace in the country and the repose of deceased parents.
1121110980000.material: Dark blue paper and silver pigment

1121110990000.title_en: Maitreya Descent Sutra in Gold on Dark Blue Paper
1121110990000.description: This manuscript copies the Maitreya Descent Sutra, translated by Zhufahu of the Western Jin, in gold pigment on dark blue paper. Its format and layout suggest it was made in the middle to late Goryeo period, and it reflects the spread of Maitreya faith at that time.
1121110990000.material: Dark blue paper and gold pigment

1121111000000.title_en: Sutra of Precious Rain, Volume 2, in Silver on Mulberry Paper
1121111000000.description: This is volume 2 of the ten-volume Sutra of Precious Rain, translated by Dharmaruci, copied in silver pigment on brown mulberry paper. The volume is in accordion-fold format, and the character mark under the title indicates it was numbered according to the Thousand Character Classic order used in a larger Buddhist canon project.

1121111010000.title_en: Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra, Volume 305, in Silver on Mulberry Paper
1121111010000.description: This is volume 305 of the 600-volume Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra translated by Xuanzang, corresponding to the beginning of the Buddha-Mother chapter. It is copied in silver pigment on brown mulberry paper in accordion-fold format, with a decorated cover and a title written in gold.

1121111020000.description: This manuscript is a 14th-century copied Buddhist scripture in which the text was transcribed in silver ink on dark brown paper. It is volume 28 of the 100-volume translation by Kumarajiva and survives as 13 leaves, with the cover and the first six leaves missing. The end of the volume bears the mark “Geonpal,” showing that it was numbered within a major canon arranged by the Thousand Character Classic order.
1121111020000.material: Silver ink on dark brown paper

1121111030000.description: This manuscript is volume 13 of the 60-volume Jin-version translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra by Buddhabhadra. The text was copied on dark blue paper using gold and silver powder, and the cover is decorated with floral patterns and the sutra title written in gold. It is believed to have been written around 1330.
1121111030000.material: Gold and silver ink on dark blue paper

1121111040000.description: This woodblock-printed book is a later reprint of an edition first published in 1474 for Queen Dowager Jeonghui to pray for the repose of Queen Gonghye. It consists of three volumes bound into one book and was reprinted in 1485. The volume-end record indicates later reprinting from a restored woodblock.

1121111050000.title_en: Summary of the Ritual for the Water and Land Dharma Assembly
1121111050000.description: This book was printed in 1470 at Gyeonseongsa Temple at the request of Lady Shin, wife of Grand Prince Gwangpyeong, to pray for her husband's repose. It is the oldest extant edition of this ritual manual for a Water and Land rite. The text is important for understanding Buddhist belief in early Joseon.

1121111060000.title_en: Commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, Volumes 84, 100, and 117
1121111060000.description: These three volumes are part of Chengguan's commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, edited by the Song monk Jingyuan. They were printed from woodblocks sent from Song China and are preserved here as volumes 84, 100, and 117. The work is valued as evidence of Buddhist cultural exchange among Korea, China, and Japan.

1121111070000.description: This book consists of volumes 5, 6, and 7 of the Korean edition of the Lotus Sutra translated by Kumarajiva. It was printed in 1451 by Queen Consort Myeongbin Kim to pray for the repose of King Taejong, King Sejong, Queen Soheon, and her parents. The three volumes are bound together as one book.

1121111080000.description: This is a royal woodblock-printed edition of a dhāraṇī sutra that was widely circulated for the belief that reciting and keeping it could avert calamity. The colophon states that it was published in 1485 under the patronage of Queen Dowager Insu, based on a Tang-period model. The text is arranged in three sections and includes an illustrated opening section with a transformation image.

1123711090000.description: This designation covers ten kinds of books, totaling 25 volumes, preserved at Imgo Seowon. The collection includes works such as Sinpyeon Uimjeom Seongli Gunseo Guhye and Nono Eonhae, along with records and regulations related to the seowon. The materials document the history and operation of Imgo Seowon from its founding in 1553 through the late Joseon period.

1123711100000.description: This is a portrait of Jeong Mong-ju (1337–1392), a loyal retainer of the Goryeo dynasty, seated in a full-length frontal pose and wearing an official hat and light blue court robe. It was newly copied onto silk by Kim Sik in 1629, and is one of three surviving portraits of Jeong Mong-ju kept at Imgo Seowon.

1123111100200.description: This portrait of Jeong Mong-ju (1337–1392) is believed to have been copied in 1555, based on the inscription and references in Poeun-jip. It shows him seated in a full-length pose wearing an official hat and robe, and is one of several related copies made from the same original portrait tradition.

1123311110000.description: This book was printed in 1612, when Heo Jun revised the Chinese medical text Chando Maegyeol at the king's command. It discusses pulse diagnosis and related methods in 29 sections, and is an important source for studying the level of medicine in the Joseon period.

1123811120000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Daewonsa Temple Site, Sancheong
1123811120000.description: This stone pagoda stands in front of the Sarijeon at Daewonsa Temple and consists of a two-tiered base with an eight-story body. It was rebuilt in 1784 after the original pagoda was destroyed during the Imjin War, and is considered a rare surviving example of an early Joseon stone pagoda.

1123811130000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Deoksansa Temple Site, Sancheong
1123811130000.description: This pagoda stands in front of the main hall of Deoksansa Temple and has a two-tiered base with a three-story body. Its form indicates that it was built in the late Unified Silla period, and it is an important example for studying the stone pagoda style of that time.

1123811140000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Daepo-ri, Sancheong
1123811140000.description: This pagoda stands in Daepo-ri village in Samjang-myeon and consists of a two-tiered base with a three-story body. It was rebuilt after being dug up and collapsed, and is thought to date to the late Unified Silla period.

1123611150000.title_en: Five-story Stone Pagoda of Bongcheon-ri, Boseong
1123611150000.description: This pagoda stands at the site of Old Odongsa Temple and has a two-tiered base with a five-story body. A monk figure is carved in relief on the south side of the upper base, and the pagoda is considered an early Goryeo work.

1123611160000.title_en: Haeryeon Stupa of Yumasa Temple, Hwasun
1123611160000.description: This octagonal stupa enshrines the remains or relics of a Buddhist monk and was moved to its present location in 1981 after being damaged by tomb robbers. The structure has a high base, a body carved with door-shaped panels and the inscription 'Haeryeonjitab,' and a roof stone decorated with layered supports and floral ornament.

1123611170000.title_en: Stupa of Daegakam Hermitage, Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123611170000.description: This octagonal monk’s stupa stands on a three-part base and is surmounted by a body stone and finial. Its decorative details and roof stone form indicate a work of the early Goryeo period.

1123611180000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda of Seongpungsa Temple Site, Yeongam
1123611180000.description: This five-story stone pagoda stands at the site of Seongpungsa Temple and has a two-tiered base with each story carved from a single stone. An inscription found inside the pagoda shows that it was erected in 1009.

1121111190000.title_en: Eight-Pointed Seven-Story Stone Pagoda of Changgyeonggung Palace
1121111190000.description: This stone pagoda stands beside a pond inside Changgyeonggung Palace and has an octagonal plan with seven stories. An inscription on the first-story body stone records that it was erected in 1470.

1123811200000.title_en: Daegwangjeon Hall of Sinhungsa Temple, Yangsan
1123811200000.description: Daegwangjeon Hall is the main Dharma hall of Sinhungsa Temple and houses Vairocana Buddha. A record found during repair work indicates that the building was constructed in 1657, and wall paintings and surviving dancheong ornamentation remain inside.

1123711210000.title_en: Seated Stone Vairocana Buddha of Geumbong-ri, Seongju
1123711210000.description: This late Silla seated stone Vairocana Buddha has a pedestal and halo. The rounded face, calm proportions, and the hand gesture conform to the standard iconography of Vairocana Buddha.

1123711220000.title_en: Rock-carved Standing Buddha in Hwangsang-dong, Gumi
1123711220000.description: This large standing Buddha was carved on a flat surface of a great natural rock face. The refined facial features, long ears, and flowing robe folds are characteristic of a late Unified Silla work.

1123511230000.title_en: Group of Rock-Carved Buddhas at the Site of Gaeryeongam Hermitage, Namwon
1123511230000.description: This rock-carved group at the cliff behind the former site of Gaeryeongam Hermitage consists of 12 Buddha images of various sizes. The largest figure, about 4 meters high, is treated as the main Buddha, and inscriptions such as "Sejeon" and "Myeongwoljibul" are also preserved.

1121111240000.title_en: Commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, Volume 30
1121111240000.description: This is volume 30 of the 120-volume commentary by Jingyuan of the Song dynasty on the 80-volume text translated by Siksananda. Printed in 1087 from woodblocks sent from Song China, it was later transmitted from Goryeo to Japan.

1123111330000.title_en: Commission of Merit for Won Gyun
1123111330000.description: This royal certificate, issued in 1604, names Won Gyun as a meritorious subject for defeating Japanese forces and dying in battle during the Japanese invasions of Korea. It also records posthumous favors for his descendants, including 13 slaves, 150 gyeol of land, silver, cloth, and a horse. A separate memorial text attached to the document records a memorial rite for Won Gyun in 1605.

1123611340000.title_en: Wooden Boy Attendants of Manjusri and Samantabhadra, Dogapsa Temple, Yeongam
1123611340000.description: These two wooden boy attendant statues are housed inside the Haetalmun Gate at Dogapsa Temple. One rides a lion and the other rides an elephant, and they are thought to represent the incarnations of Manjusri and Samantabhadra, respectively. They were probably made when the gate was built in 1473.

1123111350000.title_en: Royal Decree Granting Fields to Jo On
1123111350000.description: This royal decree records the grant of merit fields to Jo On for his service during the First Prince's Rebellion in 1398. Jo On had already been recognized as a founder of the Joseon dynasty and later received further rewards for his military role in the Second Prince's Rebellion. The document lists the location and size of the 150 gyeol of fields granted to him.

1123111360000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of Iphak Doseol is a Neo-Confucian introductory text written by Gwon Geun in 1390 for beginners in study. It contains diagrams and explanations on major Neo-Confucian concepts such as the unity of Heaven, humanity, mind, and nature, and was first printed in 1425. The text is important for understanding the development of Neo-Confucian thought in Korea.

1123811360200.description: This edition of Iphak Doseol is a Neo-Confucian introductory text written by Gwon Geun in 1390. It explains key ideas from the Confucian classics and related diagrams, and the first edition was printed in 1397, while this version was printed in 1425. Additional diagrams and explanations were added to this edition, along with publication records at the end of the volume.

1121111370000.description: This is Volume 4 of the Jeongwon edition of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, written on mulberry paper with silver ink. The dark blue cover is decorated with floral designs and gold lettering, while the text is written on brown paper in silver ink. It is thought to date to the late Goryeo period.

1121111380000.description: This is the last volume of the Lotus Sutra, written on dark blue paper with gold powder. A record at the end says it was dedicated in 1366 at Bongjeongsa Temple for the repose of the donor's deceased parents and ancestors. Based on its format and style, it is believed to have been made in the late Goryeo period.
1121111380000.material: Dark blue paper and gold ink

1121111390000.description: This is the last volume of the Lotus Sutra, copied in black ink on white paper and mounted in a folding format. A record dated 1405 says that the Buddhist layman Sinun commissioned the sutra to help his deceased parents escape suffering and attain nirvana. It is an important source for the study of early Joseon Buddhist manuscript sutras.

1121111250000.title_en: Sutra on Profound Kindness of Parents, Preached by the Buddha
1121111250000.description: This woodblock-printed book was published in 1432 by Lady Myeongbin Kim, a concubine of King Taejong. It is an accordion-folded booklet printed on dak paper and includes illustrations of the ten kinds of kindness shown by parents, as well as the section known as the Sutra on Parents and the Burial of a Child's Bones.

1121111260000.title_en: Explanatory Commentary on the Chapter on the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra from the Flower Garland Sutra
1121111260000.description: This book is a commentary by Chengguan on the final chapter of the eighty-volume Chinese translation of the Flower Garland Sutra. It is a woodblock-printed accordion-folded book on dak paper, and the record at the end states that it was re-engraved in 1387 based on an earlier edition printed in 1256.

1121111270000.title_en: The Diamond Sutra, Explained by Cheonno
1121111270000.description: This is a printed edition of the Diamond Sutra with annotations and verse by Cheonno of Song China. According to the colophon, it was published in 1387 during the reign of King U of Goryeo, based on a Song dynasty edition.

1123111280000.title_en: Commentary on the Flower Garland Sutra, Vols. 21 and 24
1123111280000.description: This is a woodblock-printed edition of the commentary on the eighty-volume Flower Garland Sutra by Song dynasty monk Jingyuan. The record says it was printed from woodblocks brought from Song to Goryeo in 1087, and these volumes are accordion-folded booklets printed on dak paper.

1123111290000.description: This dhāraṇī is one of the most widely circulated in Korea and is presented here as an accordion-folded woodblock print on dak paper. It has no publication record, but the worn block-cut letters and printing style suggest that it was carved in the late Goryeo period and printed in the early Joseon period.

1123111300000.title_en: Medicine Buddha's Original Vows and Merits Sutra
1123111300000.description: Also known as the Medicine Buddha Sutra, this text was printed by the Gyojang Dogam established at Heungwangsa in 1086 for the printing of the continued Buddhist canon. The surviving copy is a woodblock print on dak paper, and it is believed to have been printed in the early Joseon period from a Goryeo-period block.

1123111310000.description: This book is the part of the Brahmā's Net Sutra that explains the ten grave and forty-eight light precepts for bodhisattvas. The end of the volume contains a text written in 1306 by the Yuan monk Sogyeong, and the surviving copy is a later Goryeo woodblock print on dak paper.

1123111320000.title_en: Selected Sayings from the Buddha and Patriarchs, Compiled by Buddhist Master Baegun
1123111320000.description: This book gathers important passages from the sayings, dialogues, and letters of Buddhas and earlier masters, with the central theme that a person who keeps the mind straight realizes that that mind is the Buddha's mind. It was compiled in 1378 by Baegun's disciples at Chwiamsa in Yeoju, based on a metal-type edition printed at Heungdeoksa in 1377.

1123411470200.description: This volume comprises volumes 1-2 of the seven-volume Lotus Sutra printed in April 1470 at the request of Queen Dowager Jeonghui, the widow of King Sejo, to pray for the repose of Sejo, King Yejong, and Prince Uigyeong. It was printed from woodblocks engraved by leading carvers of the time, and the text was carved in the original Chinese only for use in Buddhist rites for the dead.

1121111470300.description: This is a royal edition of the Lotus Sutra printed in 1470 at the request of Queen Dowager Jeonghui in the first year of King Seongjong. It is regarded as an important source for the history of Buddhism, printing, and royal editions in early Joseon because its production date and purpose are clear and surviving copies are extremely rare.

1123111480000.title_en: Beopjip Byeollok Jeolyo Byeong Ip Sagi
1123111480000.description: This book is an early Joseon woodblock edition printed in 1486. Written by the Goryeo monk Jinul, it presents guidance for practice based on Seon thought and is considered a major philosophical text and an important study in Buddhist doctrine and practice.

1123111490000.title_en: Newly Printed and Annotated Kongzi Jiayu
1123111490000.description: This is a woodblock edition printed at the Gangneung provincial office by Bak Eun after he learned that the book had not yet been published in Korea. It was produced by recarving an existing text, and is valued as material for the study of printing culture in early Joseon.

1123711510000.description: This pair of stirrups from the Unified Silla period is a rare example with black lacquer applied to both the inside and outside surfaces. The stirrups are decorated with floral, diagonal, flame, and fishbone patterns, and their form shows the development of stirrups from earlier round-hooped types.

1123711520000.title_en: A Set of Bronze Artifacts from Jukdong-ri, Gyeongju
1123711520000.description: This assemblage was excavated from Jukdong-ri, Gyeongju, and consists of 34 bronze objects dating to the Early Iron Age. The group includes bronzes such as bells, belt fittings, spears, dagger-axes, daggers, ornaments, and fittings, and is thought to date to the early first century BCE.

1121111530000.description: This woodblock-printed copy combines volumes 1-3 of the Lotus Sutra translated by Kumarajiva of the Later Qin. The opening pages include an illustration summarizing the scripture and a guardian figure, and the colophon records the names of the scribe and donors.

1122311540000.description: This is a woodblock-printed, accordion-fold copy of volume 31 of the Zhenyuan edition of the Avataṃsaka Sutra. It was printed from the Haeinsa Goryeo woodblocks made in the time of King Sukjong of Goryeo, and is estimated to date to the 13th or 14th century.

1122311550000.title_en: Revised Edition of Gyeongnyul Isang, Volume 1
1122311550000.description: A woodblock-printed volume of Gyeongnyul Isang, a reference work that collects key passages from the scriptures and vinaya by subject and lists sources for study. It was likely carved and bound at the Bunsa Daejanggam in Namhae and is believed to have been printed in the late Goryeo to early Joseon period. This is Volume 1 of the complete 50-volume work and is useful for studying the Goryeo Tripitaka.

1121111560000.title_en: Revised Edition of Gyeongnyul Isang, Volume 8
1121111560000.description: A woodblock-printed volume of Gyeongnyul Isang, a reference work that collects key passages from the scriptures and vinaya by subject and lists sources for study. The woodblocks were carved at the Bunsa Daejanggam in Namhae in 1243, and the book was printed in the late Goryeo to early Joseon period. This is Volume 8 of the complete 50-volume work and is useful for studying the Goryeo Tripitaka.

1121111570000.description: This book is an abridged four-volume compilation of the Seongnidaejeon made by Kim Jeong-guk in 1538. He revised and supplemented the wood movable type kept at the magistrate's office in Naju and used it to print 400 copies. It was valued as a reorganization of a standard Neo-Confucian text to fit Korean needs.

1123311570200.description: This four-volume, four-book edition is an abridged compilation of the Seongnidaejeon by the Joseon scholar-official Kim Jeong-guk. It was printed in the autumn of 1538 using the Geumseong wood movable type kept at Naju, with missing characters newly supplied. The colophon records the printing date, and the set is noted for its good preservation.

1121111580000.description: This is a woodblock-printed set of volumes 27 to 30 of Gogeum Unhoe Geuyo, a Chinese rhyme dictionary originally compiled by Huang Gongshao and supplemented by Taechung. It was printed in 1434 in Gyeongju and Milyang after Sin In-son requested its publication from King Sejong. The printing was carried out by both monks and lay artisans, and the text became an important basis for Dongguk Jeongun.

1121111590000.title_en: Annotated and Fully Explained Spring and Autumn Annals with Punctuation and Direct Commentary, Volumes 62–70
1121111590000.description: This is a woodblock-printed re-engraving of a Korean edition of the Zuo Zhuan that includes annotations and explanations for difficult characters and the full text. It was published in Jeolla Province in 1431 by provincial officials. The carving is described as careful and the printing as an early edition that preserves the characteristics of the original.

1121111600000.title_en: Certificate of Merit for Jin Chung-gwi, Founding Meritorious Subject of the First Rank
1121111600000.description: This is a royal certificate issued in 1395 by the Hall of Meritorious Subjects to Jin Chung-gwi, former magistrate of Uiju, recognizing him as a founding meritorious subject. It is written on traditional Korean paper as a handscroll with a wooden roller, and the document lists 106 meritorious subjects. The end of the scroll records the officials involved in issuing the certificate and their signatures.

1121111610000.title_en: Royal Appointment Document for Jin Chung-gwi
1121111610000.description: This royal order appoints Jin Chung-gwi as magistrate of Uiju in 1394. Jin later served in other posts and died in 1412, but records about him are otherwise scarce in the historical sources. The document is an important source for studying people active in the founding of Joseon.

1123311620000.title_en: The Lotus Sutra Samadhi Repentance Ritual, Volume 2
1123311620000.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist text is the surviving lower volume of a three-volume work based on the Lotus Sutra. It was printed on handmade paper in 1472 from blocks thought to date to the late Goryeo period, at the request of Queen Insu for the repose of the royal ancestors and the well-being of the king and queen.

1123111630000.title_en: Explanatory Commentary on the Song of Enlightenment, Volume 2
1123111630000.description: This woodblock-printed book is a Korean translation of the Song of Enlightenment, printed in 1495 from blocks carved in 1464 at the Buddhist scripture office. It was published at Wongaksa under the sponsorship of Queen Dowager Jeonghyeon, and the end of the volume includes a colophon printed with specially made wooden type.

1123311640000.description: This is a woodblock-printed edition of the Lotus Sutra, bound in one volume from volumes 3 and 4 of the seven-volume set. The blocks were carved in 1470 under the patronage of Grand Queen Dowager Yuni to pray for the repose of the souls of King Yejong, King Sejo, and King Deokjong.

1121111640200.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture is a later printing from the set carved during the reign of King Seongjong, with the original cover missing but the text otherwise complete. The volumes preserve evidence of skilled carving and high-quality printing, and they are considered important for studying royal Buddhist patronage in early Joseon.

1122511650000.title_en: Ritual for Repentance at the Amitabha Hall, Volumes 3–4 and 7–8
1122511650000.description: This woodblock-printed ritual manual for repentance and Pure Land practice was published in 1474 by Grand Queen Dowager Jeonghyeon for the repose of Queen Gonghye. The volumes are part of a larger ten-volume set and preserve detailed records of the monks, royal relatives, and craftsmen involved in carving and printing the edition.

1122111650200.title_en: Ritual for Repentance at the Amitabha Hall, Volumes 1–5
1122111650200.description: This royal woodblock edition of the Amitabha repentance ritual was re-engraved in 1474 at the office for printing Buddhist scriptures by order of Queen Jeonghye of Joseon. It is one of the oldest surviving editions of the text and contains records of royal patrons, monks, and craftsmen, as well as frontispiece images of the Buddhas of the Three Ages.

1121111660000.description: This bronze bell was accidentally discovered in 1967 in Sangp-ri, Gumsa-myeon, Yeoju-gun, Gyeonggi-do. An inscription on the bell states that it was made in 1058, during the Goryeo period.

1123311670000.title_en: Bronze Bell Excavated from Uncheon-dong, Cheongju
1123311670000.description: This bronze bell was excavated in Uncheon-dong, Cheongju, together with a gilt-bronze Buddha statue and a Goryeo-period bronze drum. Based on its form and decoration, it is estimated to date to the mid-9th century, late in the Unified Silla period.

1121111680000.title_en: Celadon Maebyeong with Inlaid Plum, Bamboo, and Crane Design
1121111680000.description: This Goryeo maebyeong vase is 33 cm high and was made in the late 12th century. It is decorated in white and black inlay with slender plum and bamboo branches and three cranes shown in lively poses, and it was excavated in Hadong, Gyeongsangnam-do.

1121111690000.description: This set consists of a white porcelain taehangari, used to bury the placenta of a royal prince or princess, and a taejiseok stone inscribed with the child’s name and birth details. The inscription shows that the set was made in 1643 for Prince Aji and buried with his placenta.

1121111710000.title_en: Daebanggwang Wollyeog Yaksoju-gyeong, Volume 2 of the Lower Fascicle
1121111710000.description: This is the second book of the lower fascicle of a Korean woodblock-printed edition of the commentary on the Yulgan Sutra by Zongmi. It was printed on handmade paper and bound in the butterfly binding style.

1123111740100.title_en: Appointment Certificate for Jeongsa Merit Subject Lee Jung-ro
1123111740100.description: This royal certificate was issued in 1625 after Lee Jung-ro had died, honoring him for his loyalty and service during the restoration of King Injo. It records posthumous promotions for Lee Jung-ro and his family, as well as grants of slaves, land, silver, cloth, and a horse.

1123111740200.description: This full-length seated portrait shows Lee Jung-ro wearing official attire and a military rank badge, indicating his rank as a second-grade military official. The painting reflects the portrait style of early 17th-century Joseon, with simplified forms and careful attention to facial expression and costume.

1123111750000.title_en: Certificate of Merit for Shim Dae, Hosing Merit Subject
1123111750000.description: This royal certificate was granted in 1604 to Shim Dae for escorting King Seonjo to Uiju during the Japanese invasions. It records his merits, posthumous honors, and rewards including slaves, land, silver, and silk.

1123111760000.description: This portrait depicts the Joseon official Yu Su seated and facing to the right, with an accompanying case preserved with the painting. It was painted in 1726 by the court painter Jin Jae-hae and is valuable as a dated example of early 18th-century portrait style.

1123111770000.title_en: Portrait of O Myeong-hang and Certificate of Yangmu Merit
1123111770000.description: This set consists of a portrait of the Joseon official O Myeong-hang, a royal certificate naming him a first-class merit subject, and the wooden case that held them. The portrait and certificate were made after his role in suppressing the rebellion led by Lee In-jwa in 1727.
1123111770000.material: Ink and color on silk; paper; wood

1121111400000.description: This printed book is the third volume of a Korean translation of the Lotus Sutra, in which only the main text and the commentary by Gyehwan were rendered into Hangeul in 1463. It was printed from woodblocks carved by the Gangyeongdogam, an office established by King Sejo to publish Buddhist scriptures in Hangeul. The book survives as two fascicles in excellent condition and is considered an early printed edition with evidence of collation marks.

1123711410000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Locks and Bronze Bell from Hancheonsa Temple, Yecheon
1123711410000.description: This group consists of three gilt-bronze locks and one bronze temple bell found during site maintenance at Hancheonsa Temple in 1989. The locks are rare Goryeo-period metal fittings with vine-scroll decoration and lotus-bud-shaped clasps, and the bell is a typical Buddhist ritual object used to summon the monastic community or announce urgent matters. The findspot is clear, making the group important for the study of Korean metalcraft.

1121111420000.title_en: Anthology of Chan Sayings from Three Masters, Volume 1
1121111420000.description: This woodblock-printed book is the first surviving volume of a six-volume compilation excerpted from Hyesim's Seonmun nyeomsongjip. It was reprinted by the Gangyeongdogam in 1464 based on a woodblock edition originally made in 1246, and the pages preserve the names of block carvers such as Jeongan, Sonchang, and Yuip. The surviving volume is printed on paper and has a later repaired cover.

1121111430000.title_en: Precisely Correct Edition of the Repentance Ritual for the Hall of Compassion, Volumes 4-6
1121111430000.description: This woodblock-printed book contains volumes 4 through 6 of the Buddhist repentance ritual text Jabi dorang chambeop. It was printed from woodblocks carved in 1352, but the paper quality, bookbinding style, and other features show that the surviving copy was printed again in the early Joseon period. The text is arranged in a book format adapted from a scroll layout, with punctuation marks added for easier reading.

1123111440000.title_en: Ritual of Repentance for Amitābha's Pure Land, Volumes 6-10 (1992)
1123111440000.description: This book contains volumes 6 through 10 of the ritual manual for repentance directed to Amitābha Buddha. It was published in 1474 by order of Queen Dowager Jeonghui to pray for the repose of Queen Gonghye and also for earlier kings and queens. The colophon records the officials and monks involved in the woodblock carving, making it an important source for the history of Joseon woodblock printing.

1123111450000.description: This is the first volume of the Lotus Sutra translated by Kumarajiva and printed from woodblocks on paper. The front of the book has a diagrammatic illustration summarizing the sutra, and the cover is dark blue with the title written in gold. The original colophon is missing, but the style of the text suggests it was made around the same time as a 1401 edition of the Surangama Sutra.

1123111460000.description: This is volume 24 of the Jeongwon edition of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, a woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture. The volume isolates the "Bohyeon haengwon pum" section, which explains ten methods for entering the world of enlightenment, and was printed in the accordion-fold format. The blocks are believed to have been carved in the 12th to 13th centuries, while the surviving printed copy is thought to date to around the 14th century.

1121111470000.description: This woodblock-printed book brings together volumes 3-4 and 5-7 of the Lotus Sutra in two bound books. It was published in 1470 at the request of Queen Jeonghui to pray for the repose of King Sejo, Crown Prince Deokjong, and King Yejong. The printing is neat and the preservation is good, reflecting the high level of the craftsmen involved.

1122311780000.description: This book is a medical text compiled in 1398 and printed in the following year under the supervision of Kim Huiseon at Gangwon Provincial Office. It was based mainly on earlier Korean medical works and records of local medicinal practice, and the extant copy is Volume 6 of the original 30-volume set. It is an important source for the development of Joseon-period Korean medicine and herbal treatment using native medicinal plants.

1122311790000.description: This is a specialized medical book on the treatment of diseases related to pregnancy, childbirth, and infant care. Compiled by the physician No Jungnye in 1434 by royal command, it is organized into two volumes and draws on 15 medical texts for practical use. It is a rare and valuable source for the history of medicine.

1122311800000.description: This is a specialized medical text on acupuncture and moxibustion, printed in 1474. The extant copy lacks the preface, which was supplemented by handwritten text, and damaged portions of the main text were repaired by inserting separate paper leaves. It was reprinted in 1643 by the Hunryeondogam type office and is an important source for bibliography and traditional Korean medicine.

1123511810000.description: These are documents related to the local compact (hyangyak) organized and maintained in Gohyeondong, Taein County, Jeolla-do, over roughly 400 years from the reign of King Seonjo through 1977. The collection consists of 29 volumes, including 24 volumes classified as hyangyak materials and 5 related volumes. It is one of the largest and most complete surviving sets of hyangyak documents and is valuable for research on local self-governance.

1123211820000.title_en: Wooden Seated Amitabha Buddha from Baekdamsa Temple, Inje, and Relic Deposits
1123211820000.description: This wooden seated Buddha enshrined as the main image in Geungnakbojeon Hall at Baekdamsa Temple depicts Amitabha Buddha and was made in 1748. It has a rounded face, prominent ushnisha, broad chest and shoulders, and thick robes with curved folds that retain some early Joseon features. The set includes the statue, four votive texts, one jacket, and other relics placed inside the image.

1123611830000.title_en: Nahan Hall of Myeonghwasa Temple, Haenam
1123611830000.description: This hall at Myeonghwasa Temple was rebuilt in 1751 after the original temple buildings were destroyed in the Imjin War. It is a three-bay by two-bay Buddhist hall with a hipped-and-gabled roof and multipurpose bracket system, and the interior walls are painted with the Sixteen Arhats. The building shows characteristic late Joseon architectural features.

1123611840000.title_en: North Stupa at Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123611840000.description: This stone stupa, which stands on a hillside north of the main precinct of Seonamsa Temple, is a tomb stupa for a monk and likely dates to the early Goryeo period. It is octagonal in plan and decorated with lion figures, cloud motifs, lotus petals, guardian figures, and floral ornaments. The form closely follows the octagonal stupa tradition inherited from Unified Silla.

1123611850000.title_en: East Stupa at Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123611850000.description: This octagonal stone stupa is one of the three Goryeo-period monastic stupas at Seonamsa Temple. Its base, body, and roof are decorated with cloud patterns, wave motifs, lotus designs, guardian figures, and door panels with metal fittings. It is considered to have been made in the early Goryeo period, following the octagonal stupa tradition of Unified Silla.

1121111930000.title_en: Detailed Edition of the Repentance Rite of Compassion and the Dharma Hall, Volumes 1–5
1121111930000.description: A woodblock-printed Buddhist ritual text in five volumes bound as one book. It is the first half of a revised edition of the repentance rite used for confessing sins while reciting scriptures, and this copy was printed in Joseon, likely from blocks carved in 1474 for a royal prayer for Queen Jeonghui and Queen Gonghye.

1123111930200.title_en: Detailed Edition of the Repentance Rite of Compassion and the Dharma Hall, Volumes 6–10
1123111930200.description: A woodblock-printed Buddhist ritual text in five volumes bound as one book. It is the second half of a Joseon reprint from blocks carved in the reign of King Seongjong, with a colophon and printing record showing both 1474 and a later reprint in 1488.

1122412240005.title_en: Detailed Edition of the Repentance Rite of Compassion and the Dharma Hall
1122412240005.description: This is a complete 10-volume royal edition of a Buddhist repentance text, woodblock-printed on paper. The blocks were carved in 1474 under Queen Jeonghui for prayers for deceased members of the royal family, and the extant printing was made in 1481 for Queen Ansun’s prayer for the salvation of a relative.

1123811940000.description: A woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture copied on paper in accordion-fold format. No publication record survives, but it is thought to have been printed in the early Joseon period because its calligraphy matches that of another related volume.

1123811950000.description: A woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture in two volumes, printed on paper. It was produced in 1401 by order of King Taejong from a text written and carved at court, and it belongs to the same edition as the complete 1–10 volume set.

1123811960000.description: A complete woodblock-printed edition of the Lotus Sutra in seven volumes. It was printed in 1456 by a lady of the court to pray for the repose of the spirit of Hong of the Hahwack family, the wife of Han Hwak.

1121111960200.description: A woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture consisting of volumes 4 through 7. It was printed from blocks carved around 1422, based on a manuscript written by the brothers Seong Dal-saeng and Seong Gae, and is considered an important early Joseon Buddhist printing.

1123511970000.title_en: Collection of Farewell Poems by Distinguished Scholars of the Gimyo Year
1123511970000.description: A manuscript album of farewell poems and writings presented to An Cheosun when he was appointed county magistrate of Gurye in 1518. The surviving album was compiled after his death in 1603 and rebound again in 1829, and it preserves the names, pen names, and offices of 24 scholars.

1123711860000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Gangnaksa Temple Site, Gumi
1123711860000.description: This stone pagoda was found collapsed at the old temple site said to have been Gangnaksa. It was moved to the courtyard in front of the Seonsan County office in 1968 and then moved again to its present location in October 1980. The pagoda has a one-tier stylobate with three stories of the tower body and a finial on top.

1123911870000.title_en: Five-story Stone Pagoda of Bultapsa Temple, Jeju
1123911870000.description: This stone pagoda stands at the old site of Wondangsa Temple, where Bultapsa later took its place. It has a one-tier stylobate, five stories of the tower body, and a finial, with a stone wall around it. Based on its form and details, it is thought to date to the late Goryeo period.

1123711880000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Cheonryongsa Temple Site, Namsan, Gyeongju
1123711880000.description: This pagoda stood collapsed at the former site of Cheonryongsa Temple and was restored in 1990 with missing parts supplemented. It has a one-tier stylobate and three stories of the tower body. Based on its stylistic details, it is thought to date to the 9th century of Unified Silla.

1123411890100.description: These are two portraits of Park Mun-su, a civil official of the Joseon period. The larger portrait shows him as a 38-year-old in a full-length seated pose, while the other shows him in a half-length pose wearing a red official robe. Both works are in good condition and are regarded as high-quality portraits.

1121111890200.description: This portrait depicts Park Mun-su, the well-known Joseon official and magistrate, as an elderly man. The text states that he received a merit subject portrait in 1728, but this half-length portrait was painted later in a different context. It is especially significant for the history of Joseon portraiture and merit subject portraits.

1121111900000.description: This portrait is believed to depict the Joseon military official O Jachi and shows him seated while facing to the right. He wears a black manggeon-style official hat and a dark blue official robe, with a tiger-patterned rank badge on his chest. It is considered to have been painted together with other merit subject portraits in 1476.

1121111910000.title_en: Volume 30 of the Annotated Avatamsaka Sutra, Early Printed Edition
1121111910000.description: This is Volume 30 of the eighty-volume Xuanzang translation of the Avatamsaka Sutra, bound as a single scroll-like book. It is a woodblock-printed book from the early Goryeo Tripitaka, the first Tripitaka carved in Korea. The text and printing features suggest a 11th-century publication.

1121111920000.title_en: Volume 38 of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Jin Version
1121111920000.description: This is Volume 38 of the 60-volume Jin version of the Avatamsaka Sutra translated by Buddhabhadra. It is a woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture in a foldable concertina format, with a blue cover marked in gold. It is thought to have been reprinted at Haeinsa Temple in the late Goryeo period from an earlier woodblock edition made in the reign of King Sukjong.

1123511980000.title_en: Collection of Letters from the Gimyosaheomun (Gimyujehyeon Sucheop)
1123511980000.description: This letter album was compiled from letters sent to An Cheoseon by friends and colleagues around the time of the Gimyosahwa. It contains 39 letters from 12 correspondents dating from 1517 to 1531, with a preface by Han Jun-gyeom and a postscript by Jo Seong-gyo.

1121111990000.title_en: Painting of Plum Blossoms by Yu Suk
1121111990000.description: This eight-panel folding screen was painted by Yu Suk in 1868. It is the artist’s only known plum blossom painting, and an inscription by the artist is written in the lower left. The work is noted for its large scale and for being a representative plum blossom painting of the 19th century.

1123512000000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Buddha, Dongbulam Hermitage Site, Seonunsa Temple, Gochang
1123512000000.description: This rock-carved seated Buddha is engraved on a cliff beside the path leading up to Dosoram at Seonunsa Temple. It is a large early Goryeo stone Buddha that shows the characteristic style of the period. The chest cavity reportedly yielded a hidden document during the Donghak Peasant War.

1123712010000.title_en: Daeungbojeon Hall of Buryeongsa Temple, Uljin
1123712010000.description: Daeungbojeon is the main Buddha hall of Buryeongsa Temple, and the present building is thought to have been built in 1725 based on a record in the hanging painting inside. It is a 3-bay by 3-bay building with a hipped-and-gabled roof and a multi-bracketing structure. Its interior materials, painted surfaces, and dancheong are especially well preserved and are considered valuable for studying late Joseon architecture.

1123712020000.title_en: Documents of the Nongam Yi Hyeon-bo Family
1123712020000.description: This collection consists of old documents, books, and one painting preserved by the descendants of Yi Hyeon-bo, a Joseon official and renowned sijo poet. It includes royal edicts, family records, literary manuscripts, and the painting "Eundae Gyehoedo," which is valuable for the study of Joseon-period administration, literature, and genealogy. The set also contains several works gathered in the family archive, including "Aildang Gu-gyeongcheop" and related volumes.

1123712030000.title_en: Documents of the O Un Family
1123712030000.description: This collection consists of old documents and books preserved by the descendants of O Un, a mid-Joseon official and scholar. The documents include division-of-property records, verification documents, household registers, royal edicts, and a memorial rite document, while the books include printed and manuscript works such as "Daehak Janggu Daejeon" and "Dongmunseon." They are important sources for studies of social and economic history, family and status systems, bibliography, and hyangyak.

1121112040000.title_en: Water-Moon Avalokitesvara Painting by Uigyeom and Others
1121112040000.description: This hanging scroll depicts Water-Moon Avalokitesvara seated before the pure land, with a vase holding a willow branch and a pair of bamboo stalks placed beside the rocks. It was painted by the monk-painter Uigyeom in 1730. The composition recalls Goryeo Buddhist paintings, but the frontal pose, colors, and rock forms show Joseon-period features.

1122312050000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Avatamsaka Sutra, Chapter Text, Volumes 67 and 77
1122312050000.description: These are two volumes of the early woodblock-printed edition of the Avatamsaka Sutra, printed on handmade paper in scroll form. They are part of the first Tripitaka carved in Korea during the reign of King Hyeonjong of Goryeo, and the text describes Sudhana's search for 53 spiritual masters. Although undated, they are considered to have been printed in the 11th century.

1122312060000.title_en: Early Woodblock Print of the Ten Stages Treatise, Volume 17
1122312060000.description: This is the final volume of the early Goryeo Tripitaka edition of the Ten Stages Treatise (Shizhu piposha lun), translated by Kumarajiva in the Later Qin period. It was printed from woodblocks on mulberry paper, assembled in a scroll format, and is estimated to have been produced in the 11th century.

1122312070000.description: This 4-volume, 1-volume edition is an expanded and edited version of Yang Yu's Essential Matters for Mountain Dwelling, revised by the Yuan scholar Wang Yumu. It classifies the practical knowledge a person living in a mountain village should know into four sections and 74 items, with examples, diagnoses, and prescriptions.

1122312080000.title_en: Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals with Left's Commentary, Volumes 60–70 (1994)
1122312080000.description: This is the surviving portion, volumes 60–70, of a woodblock-printed edition published in Cheongdo in 1431 under the supervision of Jo Chi and An Jil. The volume includes a colophon and publication record, and it is an important source for studying early Joseon printing and the transmission of the Zuo Zhuan.

1123812080200.title_en: Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals with Left's Commentary, Volumes 60–70 (2011)
1123812080200.description: This is the surviving portion, volumes 60–70, of the 1431 Cheongdo woodblock edition of the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals with Left's Commentary. The book preserves the colophon and publication record, including the names of the officials and craftsmen involved in printing.

1122312090000.description: This woodblock-printed book is an annotated and explained edition of Du Fu's seven-character regulated verse prepared by the Yuan scholar Yu Ji and printed in Cheongju in 1470. The colophon, preface, and publication record are preserved, making it a valuable bibliographic source.

1121112100000.description: This large Buddhist banner painting depicts Sakyamuni standing alone and was used as an object of worship during large outdoor Buddhist rites. Painted in 1725, it shows Sakyamuni dressed in ornate Bodhisattva-like regalia with a jeweled crown.

1123112110000.title_en: Brief Commentary on the Heart Sutra
1123112110000.description: This is a commentary on the Heart Sutra, translated by Xuanzang and annotated by Fazang, with Zhongxi's Xuanjing ji appended and republished. The book was printed from woodblocks on paper, and the colophon states that it was produced by order of King Sejo in 1464 at the Gangyeong Dogam.

1123712120000.title_en: Investiture Certificate for Meritorious Retainer Yi Yun-ryong and Related Documents
1123712120000.description: These are two Joseon-period documents: a royal certificate of merit and a military appointment document granted to Yi Yun-ryong for his service in the Imjin War. The certificate records his designation as a third-class meritorious retainer, and the appointment document names him as a military commander in the Gyeongsang Left Navy.

1121112290000.title_en: Buncheong Stoneware Flattened Flask with Incised Lotus Design
1121112290000.description: This fifteenth-century Joseon-period flattened flask is 20.5 cm high with a flat body, a mouth diameter of 5.0 cm, and a base diameter of 8.3 cm. The vessel was formed on a wheel and then beaten flat on both sides; lotus bands decorate the neck, lotus motifs appear on the front and back flattened faces, and grass designs are incised on both sides.

1123112300000.title_en: White Porcelain Bottle with Inlaid Lotus and Scroll Design
1123112300000.description: This Joseon-period soft white porcelain bottle is 29.9 cm high with a flared mouth and a rounded body that narrows toward the foot. Black inlay decorates the shoulder with vine motifs and horizontal lines, while lotus flowers and scroll patterns are inlaid on the body with evenly cut lines that give it a neat appearance.

1121112310000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Iron-painted Cloud and Bamboo Design
1121112310000.description: This mid-Joseon jar is 33.2 cm high and shows a joined mark at the swollen central part of the body. Cloud bands are painted around the mouth and lower body, and bamboo motifs are drawn on the middle of the vessel in iron pigment; the translucent glaze has a pale grayish-white tone.

1123812320000.title_en: Wooden Seated Figures of Jeseokcheon and Daebeomcheon, Cheonggoksa Temple, Jinju
1123812320000.description: These two wooden seated figures of Jeseokcheon and Daebeomcheon date to the eighteenth century and are the only known sculptural examples in Korea, where these deities were more commonly depicted in paintings. The figures follow late Joseon stylistic features and differ clearly from examples made in China and Japan.

1123812330000.description: This cannon is one of the four types of tube cannon named after characters from the Chinese cosmic sequence, with Hyeonja being the third in size. Recovered from the sea near Baekdo in 1992, it measures 75.8 cm in length and bears the maker's name, Yang Naeyodong, which suggests a date around 1555 in the reign of King Myeongjong.

1123312340000.description: This is Volume 201 of the 1477 metal-type edition of Uibang Yuchwi, a Joseon medical encyclopedia first compiled by royal order in 1445. It is the only known first edition discovered in Korea and is an important source for the study of the history of printing and medical texts.

1123312350000.description: This is a printed copy of volumes 4 and 5 of Hyangyak Jesaeng Jipseongbang, an early Joseon medical text first published in 1399. The surviving copy is incomplete, and the work is valued for its use of indigenous Korean medicinal herbs and for its role as a basis for later Joseon medical compilations.

1123312360100.description: This is volume 6 of a Korean-language medical handbook compiled in 1489 by order of King Seongjong and printed from woodblocks. It organizes treatments for 127 diseases and is an important source for the history of Korean medical printing and the Korean language.

1121112180000.description: This is a collected works of Dunchon Yi Jip (1314–1387), a late Goryeo scholar, printed in July 1410, the 10th year of King Taejong of Joseon. The preface by Ha Ryun explains the background of the publication and records the scholarly relations among leading men of the time. It is valued as an important source for philological research on an early Joseon printed book.

1121112190000.title_en: The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment, Volume 1, Parts 1–2 and Volume 2, Parts 1–2
1121112190000.description: This is a five-volume Buddhist scripture bound in two books and printed in the same format as texts produced by the Gyeonggyeongdogam, though with only the phonetic glosses added rather than a full vernacular translation. It was intended to be printed with copper type made from the calligraphy of Jeong Nan-jong in 1465, but the policy situation led to the text being printed only with glosses. The surviving impression is rare and is regarded as important for the study of Buddhist printing and metal type.

1123112190200.title_en: The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment, Volume 2, Part 2; Volume 3, Parts 1–2
1123112190200.description: This copper-type edition of the scripture was printed in 1465, the 11th year of King Sejo, using the Eulyu type. It was edited from a vernacular glossed version that Sejo had prepared from the commentary by Zongmi, and only the Korean phonetic glosses were selected for printing. The book is an important source for the study of 15th-century Korean language, bibliography, and metal type printing.

1122112190300.title_en: The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment (Eonhae), Volume 2, Parts 1–2
1122112190300.description: This is a metal-type printed edition of the vernacular glossed Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment produced by the Printing Office in 1465, the 11th year of King Sejo. It was printed with Eulyu type based on a vernacular edition derived from the commentary of Zongmi. Because few copies survive and the printing is clear, it is considered an important source for the study of Joseon-period Korean language and metal-type printing.

1121112190400.title_en: The Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment (Eonhae), Volume 1, Part 2
1121112190400.description: This edition was printed in 1465, the 11th year of King Sejo, with the Eulyu metal type based on a version of the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment annotated in Korean by Sejo. Surviving copies are few because the type was later melted down and reused when the Gapjin type was cast. It is regarded as a valuable source for the study of 15th-century Korean language, bibliography, and metal-type printing history.

1123212200000.description: This is a group of books, documents, and artifacts related to Princess Myeongan, the third daughter of King Hyeonjong of Joseon, and to Myeongan Palace where she lived. The set includes royal letters, document collections, and household goods sent to the princess from the palace. It provides important evidence for the study of palace life, calligraphy, and social and economic history in Joseon.

1123712210000.description: This portrait depicts the Joseon scholar Kim Jin (1500–?) and was painted in 1572, the 5th year of King Seonjo. He is shown seated in profile, wearing a green robe and a wide-brimmed official hat, with the hands folded inside the sleeves. The work is a valuable example of a scholar-official portrait from the Andong region.

1121112220000.description: This book was written by the Goryeo monk Jinul in 1209 and printed in 1486 at Gyubongam on Mt. Mudeung in Gwangju. It is regarded as a crystallization of Jinul's Seon thought and has long been used as a textbook for monastic study. The edition is valued as an important text in the history of Korean Buddhist philosophy.

1123812130000.title_en: Seated Vairocana Buddha Statue of Cheonhwangsa Temple, Miryang
1123812130000.description: This seated stone Buddha includes a newly made head added after damage. The elegant shoulders, broad chest, slim waist, and thin robe with stepped folds reflect features of late 8th-century sculpture, and the base is a unique lion throne with three sections. The lower part is carved with eleven lions in the round, making it the only seated stone Buddha in Korea with a lion throne.

1122212140000.title_en: Painted Hanging Scroll of the Vulture Peak Assembly at Pagyesa Temple
1122212140000.description: This hanging scroll depicts Śākyamuni preaching to his disciples on Vulture Peak. It was made in 1707 during the reign of King Sukjong and is painted in colors on silk, with bright green, red, and gold tones. The work is representative of early 18th-century Buddhist painting and has high documentary value.

1121112150000.title_en: Portrait of Yi Saek - Mogeun Yeongdang-bon
1121112150000.description: This is a portrait of Yi Saek (1328–1396), a late Goryeo scholar known as one of the Three Hermits. The original portrait is no longer extant, and the surviving versions are later copies made from an earlier model; this set includes a large and a small version. The paintings are valued as important materials for the study of portraiture in the Joseon period.

1121112150200.title_en: Portrait of Yi Saek - Yeongmo Yeongdang-bon
1121112150200.description: This is a portrait of Yi Saek (1328–1396), a late Goryeo scholar known as one of the Three Hermits. The original portrait is no longer extant, and the surviving versions are later copies made from an earlier model. As a copied portrait of an important historical figure, it is valued as a source for the history of Korean painting.

1121112150300.title_en: Portrait of Yi Saek - Nusan Yeongdang-bon
1121112150300.description: This portrait depicts Yi Saek (1328–1396), a late Goryeo scholar known as one of the Three Hermits. The surviving image is a copied version of an earlier original, and the Nusan Yeongdang-bon was reportedly recopied in 1654 by Huh Ui and Kim Myeong-guk. It preserves the figure in official dress and is regarded as highly important in the history of portrait painting.

1121112150400.title_en: Portrait of Yi Saek - Daejeon Yeongdang-bon
1121112150400.description: This portrait depicts Yi Saek (1328–1396), a late Goryeo scholar known as one of the Three Hermits. The Daejeon Yeongdang-bon was copied in 1844 and follows the same form and scale as the Nusan Yeongdang-bon. It is considered a well-executed portrait that preserves the style of older painting traditions.

1123712160000.description: This is a portrait of Son So (1433–1484), who received merit for suppressing the rebellion of Yi Si-ae and later served as magistrate in Andong and Jinju. It was painted in 1476, nine years after the event, and shows him seated in official robes and a samo hat. Despite damage and losses, the portrait remains an important example of early Joseon merit portraiture.

1121112170000.description: This is a metal movable-type edition of an arithmetic textbook first compiled in Yuan China by Zhu Shijie and printed in the early Joseon period with Eulhaeja type. It was used in the recruitment examinations for those studying practical mathematics, together with works such as Yanghui suanfa and Xiangming suanfa. The book is an important source for understanding Joseon-era systems of weights and measures.

1121112220200.title_en: Beopjip Byeolhaengnok Jeolyo Byeong Ip Sagi
1121112220200.description: This printed Buddhist text was published in 1486 at Gyubongam on Mudeungsan in Gwangju, Jeolla-do. It is a woodblock edition of Jigon’s abridgment of Zongmi’s "Record of the Separate Practice of the Dharma" with Jigon’s own notes inserted. The colophon records the reason for publication and the names of participants, making it an important source for the study of Buddhist scholarship and early Joseon-period Buddhist publishing.

1121112230000.title_en: Collected Commentaries on the Diamond Sutra, Volume 2
1121112230000.description: This is a woodblock-printed Buddhist scripture published in 1417, containing commentaries on the "Diamond Sutra" from the 15th through the 32nd sections of the text. The end of the volume includes a statement about the scripture’s purpose, a note identifying the source as a stone-engraved text from Yeonggyeongsa, and records on proofreading, a preface by the Sixth Patriarch, and the publication history. It is an important example of an early Joseon Buddhist printed book.

1121112240000.title_en: The Three Scriptures of the Buddha and Patriarchs
1121112240000.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist compilation was produced in Goryeo in 1384. It combines the "Sishier Zhang Jing," the "Foyijiao Jing," and the "Guishan Jingce," and includes a preface by Mongsan Deok-i and a colophon by Yi Saek stating that it was reprinted in the tenth year of King U of Goryeo. The book is valuable for the study of Goryeo Buddhist printing and surviving editions of these scriptures.

1122112240200.title_en: The Three Scriptures of the Buddha and Patriarchs
1122112240200.description: This is a woodblock-printed compilation of three Buddhist texts: the "Sishier Zhang Jing," the "Foyijiao Jing," and the "Guishan Jingce." It contains a preface by Mongsan Deok-i dated 1286 and a colophon by Yi Saek stating that it was reprinted in 1384 by Jigong, Jido, and Gakwon through the donation of a person surnamed Kim. The volume is considered a faithful reproduction of an Yuan-dynasty edition and is noteworthy for preserving an additional colophon not seen in other designated copies.

1123112250000.description: This is the latter half of volume 7 of the "Lotus Sutra," a woodblock-printed vernacular Korean edition produced by the Office for the Printing of Sutras. The main text and commentary by Gaehwan are rendered in Korean, and the end of the book includes a note by Kim Suon explaining the circumstances of publication. It was printed in 1472 from woodblocks carved in 1463 and is an important record of sutra publication under Queen Insu.

1121112260000.description: This royal decree was issued on a leap seventh month day in 1406 when King Taejong appointed the military official Jo Heup as Gaseondaebu, Jwagun Dosechongje-bu Dongjije Chongje. It is written vertically in cursive script over seven lines and bears the seal-inscription "Joseon Gukwang Jiin" above the date. The document is an important source for the study of early Joseon document forms, royal seals, and personnel administration.

1122312270000.description: This medical book on preventing illness through food was printed with movable metal type during the reigns of King Jungjong to King Myeongjong, based on an edition first published in 1526 with a preface by Ming scholar Yao Wenqing and others. It is organized into eight categories, including water, grains, vegetables, fruits, birds, beasts, fish, and flavors, with entries explaining taste, nature, benefits, and harmful effects. The work is rare and is regarded as an important source for bibliography and medical history.

1121112280000.title_en: Celadon Ewer with Incised Dragon Design
1121112280000.description: This Goryeo celadon ewer is 21.1 cm high and is shaped like a bottle with a handle and a wide mouth. Four coiled dragons are incised on the body, and thunder-pattern bands divide the vessel into three sections. Its form and decoration suggest that it was modeled on a metal ewer and that it was made in the first half of the 12th century, probably at the Gangjin kiln site in Jeolla-do.

1121112360200.description: This is a 16th-century printed vernacular edition of Gubeug ganibang, a medical text first compiled and published in 1489 during the reign of King Seongjong. The work is a collection of treatments for 127 illnesses and is an important source for Korean medicine and the study of the Korean language.

1123712370000.title_en: Historical Documents of the Samujeongpa Lineage of the Milyeong Park Clan
1123712370000.description: This set consists of documents preserved by the Samujeongpa lineage of the Milyeong Park clan, relating to Park Gyeongsin and his two sons, Ji-nam and Cheol-nam. It includes a Seonmu Wonjong Gongsin record, royal issuance documents, and related certificates granted in the Joseon period.

1121112380000.description: This Buddhist painting depicts Amitabha Buddha, who guides the souls of the dead toward rebirth in the Pure Land. Although undated, it is believed to be a Goryeo-period work based on its style, including the red robe, green undergarment, and gold halo.

1121112390000.description: This hanging scroll was made for rites praying that the dead would leave hell and attain rebirth in the Pure Land. Dated to 1681, it shows a three-tiered composition with the Buddha realm above, Buddhist ritual scenes in the middle, and the world of hell and hungry ghosts below.

1123812400000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Lotus Sutra preserves volumes 3 and 4 of a seven-volume set, bound as one book in a wrapped-back format. It was published in 1470 by Queen Dowager Jaseong to pray for the repose of King Yejong, King Sejo, and Crown Prince Deokjong.

1123712410000.description: This is a woodblock-printed Buddhist ritual text containing the procedures for repentance and prayers before Amitabha Buddha. It was originally published in 1474 under royal patronage, and this surviving set was reprinted at Haeinsa in 1503 from blocks closely following the original.

1123812420000.description: This stone pagoda stands by the road before the Iljumun Gate at Haeinsa Temple and is a representative late Unified Silla small pagoda. It has a two-tiered base and a three-story body, and the pagoda inscription records that it was built in 895 to honor monks who died protecting temple treasures.

1123512430000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Songgwangsa Temple, Wanju
1123512430000.description: This is the main hall of Songgwangsa Temple, said to have been built in 1622 and later completed through additional work in 1636 and 1857. It is a three-bay by five-bay wooden hall with a hip-and-gable roof and multi-bracket style, and enshrines Sakyamuni Buddha with Amitabha and Bhaisajyaguru on either side.

1123812530000.description: This bronze bell is housed inside Daejeokgwangjeon Hall at Haeinsa Temple. It was cast in 1491, the 22nd year of King Seongjong of Joseon, and its surface is richly decorated with lotus, floral, dragon, and hexagram motifs. The bell is considered an important source for the study of the development of Joseon-period bells and has high value as Buddhist ritual craft.

1123612540000.title_en: Wooden Four Guardian Kings of Borimsa Temple, Jangheung
1123612540000.description: These are four wooden statues of the Four Guardian Kings placed at Borimsa Temple. They were made in 1515, the 10th year of King Jungjong of Joseon, and are the oldest extant wooden Four Guardian Kings statues preserved in a temple gate. Each figure is shown in armor holding different ritual objects and trampling evil spirits, and the group is valued for its excellent carving and as an important model for Joseon-period guardian statues.

1123512550000.title_en: Clay Four Guardian Kings of Songgwangsa Temple, Wanju
1123512550000.description: These are four clay statues of the Four Guardian Kings at Songgwangsa Temple. They were made in 1649, the 27th year of King Injo of Joseon, and some records also note later repair and replacement of the pagoda held by one figure. The statues show the standard Joseon-period guardian kings with armored, wrathful expressions and are important as well-documented examples made after the Byeongja War.

1123112560000.title_en: Chiljangsa Temple Three Buddhas Assembly Hanging Scroll
1123112560000.description: This hanging scroll depicts the Vulture Peak assembly, showing Śākyamuni preaching with the lower section centered on him and the upper section featuring Nositana Buddha and Amitabha Buddha. Eight bodhisattvas, ten great disciples, Four Heavenly Kings, and heavenly beings are arranged around the main figures. Painted in 1710, it shows a simplified composition characteristic of late Joseon Buddhist painting.

1123112570000.title_en: Cheongnyongsa Temple Vulture Peak Assembly Hanging Scroll
1123112570000.description: This large Buddhist hanging scroll depicts Śākyamuni preaching on Vulture Peak. The central Buddha is surrounded by bodhisattvas, disciples, Indra, Brahma, and protective deities, with many small Buddha images painted at the top. It was painted in 1658 and is regarded as a representative example of mid-17th-century Vulture Peak assembly paintings.

1123312580000.title_en: Bosalsa Temple Vulture Peak Assembly Hanging Scroll
1123312580000.description: This large hanging scroll depicts Śākyamuni preaching and was painted on hemp cloth. It is dated to 1649, the 27th year of King Injo, and the surviving inscription identifies the painters Shin Gyeom, Deokhui, and Gyeongyun. The composition is crowded and symmetrical, with Śākyamuni at the center surrounded by bodhisattvas and disciples, and it is considered an important representative work of the period.

1123312590000.title_en: Beopjusa Temple Hanging Scroll of a Bodhisattva
1123312590000.description: This large outdoor Buddhist hanging scroll shows a single bodhisattva figure filling the entire surface. The figure stands holding flower branches with both hands and wears a decorated crown and richly patterned robes, with large halos around the head and body. Dated to 1766, it also preserves records related to the temple's foundation and the Buddhist thought of the time.

1123412600000.title_en: Magoksa Temple Hanging Scroll of Śākyamuni Buddha
1123412600000.description: This large hanging scroll is an outdoor Buddhist painting centered on Śākyamuni Buddha. Around the main Buddha are bodhisattvas, disciples, Indra and Brahma, the Four Heavenly Kings, heavenly beings, asuras, and dragon kings arranged symmetrically. Dated to 1687, it also includes the names of the main figures and records that it was used for Buddha's Birthday, water-and-land rites, and memorial services for the dead.

1123512440000.description: This bell pavilion at Songgwangsa Temple is a two-story pavilion in a ten-shaped plan. The lower story has mixed round and square columns, while the upper story uses round columns throughout; the center bay houses the bell, and the projecting bays store the wooden fish, drum, and cloud plate. It is valued as the only surviving two-story pavilion of this ten-shaped form from the Joseon period.

1121112450000.description: This is the autograph memoir of independence activist and politician Kim Gu, also known as Baekbeom. The first volume, written in 1929, recounts his life and independence activities in letter form to his sons, while the second volume continues the record of his struggle after the 1932 Shanghai incidents and contains the essay "My Desire." It is an important primary source for the history of the Korean independence movement.

1123412460000.title_en: Royal Edict Granting Tax Exemption to Gwangdeoksa Temple, Cheonan
1123412460000.description: This royal edict was issued by King Sejo on August 10, 1457, and granted relief from compulsory labor to Gwangdeoksa Temple and Gaechonsa Temple in Cheonan. It follows the form of early Joseon royal temple-grant documents and is useful for studying the Buddhist policy of King Sejo.

1123412470000.title_en: Joseon Buddhist Transcriptions, Gwangdeoksa Temple, Cheonan
