1123412470000.description: This set of Buddhist transcriptions preserved at Gwangdeoksa Temple includes the "Bumo Eunjung-gyeong" and "Jangsu Myeoljwe Hojedongja Daranigyeong." They were copied in black ink on white paper and decorated for folding display, and the remaining colophon indicates that Prince Hyoryeong, his wife, and his son donated them. They are valuable sources for the study of early Joseon Buddhism and book history.

1121112480000.title_en: Daebuljeong Yeorae Milin Susung Jobeop Simseunggyeong, Volumes 1-4
1121112480000.description: This is a printed edition of volumes 1 through 4 of the "Śūraṅgama Sūtra" commentary, produced at Muryangsa Temple in Hongsan during the reign of King Seongjong. It was printed from woodblocks carved by Park Gyeong, with contributions from the local magistrate and others, and the colophon preserves details of its publication. The book is also important for the study of Middle Korean because it includes Korean phonetic annotations in Hangul and Idu.

1122312490000.title_en: Simplified Prescriptions for Preventing Epidemic Diseases (Eonhae), 1578
1122312490000.description: This medical book was compiled in the Joseon period from prescriptions for treating epidemic diseases, and was translated into Korean for wider use. The extant copy is the 1578 reprint made with Eulhaeja metal type, and it is an important source for the study of 16th-century Korean and the history of medicine.

1122312500000.description: This is a surviving fragment of a medical book originally compiled in Yuan China by Wi Yeok-rim and reprinted in Joseon in 1425. The extant portion contains volumes 10 and 11, covering topics such as headaches, facial disorders, child health, and childbirth. It is a rare medical text in Korea and is important for both medical and bibliography studies.

1123612520000.title_en: Carefully Revised Jabi Doryang Chambeop, Volumes 9-10 (1997)
1123612520000.description: This woodblock-printed Buddhist ritual text contains volumes 9 and 10 of the "Jabi Doryang Chambeop." It is a revised reprint made by the Gyeongguk Dogam in 1462 from an earlier carving created in 1447 for prayers for the afterlife of King Taejong, Queen Wongyeong, Queen Soheon, and the donors' parents. It is a useful source for the study of early Joseon Buddhist ritual and the history of the Gyeongguk Dogam.

1123412610000.title_en: Gwangdeoksa Temple Hanging Painting of Rocana Buddha
1123412610000.description: This large Buddhist hanging painting was used for major Buddhist rites and depicts Rocana Buddha as the central figure. Around the main image are two great bodhisattvas, two great disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings, with red and green colors and cloud motifs adding to the ornate composition.

1123412620000.title_en: Yongbongsa Temple Hanging Painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly
1123412620000.description: This hanging painting depicts Sakyamuni Buddha preaching at Vulture Peak, with the Buddha shown at the center and surrounded by bodhisattvas, disciples, the Four Heavenly Kings, Indra, and Brahma. It was painted in 1690 by the monk-painter Jingan and later retouched in 1725, with red and green used as the main colors.

1123412630000.title_en: Sudeoksa Temple Hanging Painting of Rocana Buddha
1123412630000.description: This large Buddhist hanging painting centers on Rocana Buddha and is surrounded by twelve great bodhisattvas, ten great disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings. The halo inscription identifies the main figure as the Perfect Reward Body Rocana Buddha, and the composition uses strong red and green tones for a brilliant effect.

1123412640000.title_en: Gaesimsa Temple Hanging Painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly
1123412640000.description: This hanging painting shows Sakyamuni Buddha preaching at Vulture Peak, with the Buddha standing at the center and surrounded by multiple Buddha figures, bodhisattvas, and guardian deities. It was painted in 1772 to pray for the long life of the king, queen, and crown prince, and is characterized by elaborate patterns and vivid coloring.

1123512660000.description: This large hanging painting depicts a magnificently adorned standing Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva filling the entire screen. It was painted in 1692 by four painters including Myeongwon, and the halo, crown, robes, and patterns are all rendered in a richly decorative style.

1123512670000.title_en: Ankoksa Temple Hanging Painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly
1123512670000.description: This hanging painting depicts Sakyamuni Buddha preaching at Vulture Peak, with Dabo Tathagata, Manjusri, and Samantabhadra on one side and Amitabha Buddha, Avalokitesvara, and Mahasthamaprapta on the other. It is believed to have been made around 1730 by monk-painters including Uigyeom, and the large, powerful body of the main Buddha dominates the composition.

1123512680000.title_en: Naesosa Temple Hanging Painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly
1123512680000.description: This hanging painting shows Sakyamuni Buddha preaching at Vulture Peak, with Manjusri and Samantabhadra beside him and Dabo Tathagata, Amitabha Buddha, Avalokitesvara, and Mahasthamaprapta behind them. Painted in 1700, it is notable for its detailed line work, bright faces, and elegant use of red, green, and light colors.

1123512690000.title_en: Gaeamsa Temple Hanging Painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly and Preliminary Sketch
1123512690000.description: This set consists of a hanging painting of Sakyamuni preaching at Vulture Peak and its surviving preliminary sketch. The main painting, completed in 1749 with participation by the monk-painter Uigyeom, includes Sakyamuni, bodhisattvas, and multiple attendant Buddhas, and the sketch is noted as the only known example of its kind.

1121112890000.description: This royal order was issued by King Sejo on March 12, 1457, together with a sealed military token, to Yi Yun-son, then military commander of Pyeongan Province. It is the oldest surviving example of a yuseo and an important source for the form of royal orders issued in the early Joseon period.

1121112900000.description: This manuscript compiles the biographies, prefaces and postscripts, and poems of three generations of the Gang family: Gang Hui-maeng, his grandfather Gang Hoe-baek, his father Gang Seok-deok, and his elder brother Gang Hui-an. It also includes Gang Hui-an's Yanghwaseorok, and is regarded as the original text and the oldest surviving version known from the many extant copies.

1121112910000.description: This seven-volume, seven-book musical manuscript was compiled by Seo Myeong-eung in 1759 from music of the Joseon court, especially pieces associated with the reign of King Sejo. It preserves several important court and folk melodies, including early forms of repertory that developed from Goryeo through the late Joseon period.

1123212920000.title_en: Iron Seated Vairocana Buddha of Samhwasa Temple, Donghae
1123212920000.description: This iron seated Buddha enshrined in the Daeungjeon Hall of Samhwasa Temple was restored from a disassembled state and mounted on a concrete pedestal. An inscription discovered on the back records that the image was made in connection with the Avatamsaka Sutra for the benefit of the donor's parents, allowing it to be dated to the late Silla to early Goryeo period.

1123412930000.description: This is a Joseon-period shrine altar established to conduct state rites for the mountain deity of Gyeryongsan. The present complex was rebuilt in 1879 by order of Empress Myeongseong, and its main buildings are arranged symmetrically along a central axis with walls enclosing the precinct.

1123312950000.title_en: Stupa Stele for Buddhist Monk Tongil of Gakyeonsa Temple, Goesan
1123312950000.description: This stele records the life of Tongil, an early Goryeo monk who studied in China and later lectured on Buddhist doctrine at the royal court. Erected in 958, it remains in its original location and is notable for its stone turtle base, dragon-headed form, and four-dragon carving on the capstone.

1123312960000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Silleuksa Temple, Jecheon
1123312960000.description: This pagoda stands on a two-tier stylobate with three stories of body stones above it. It follows the stone pagoda style of Unified Silla while showing early Goryeo workmanship, and excavation during restoration in 1981 uncovered 108 small clay pagodas and fragments of a reliquary box inside the foundation.

1121112970000.description: This work was compiled by the Chan master Xuanke of the Tang dynasty as a summary of essential points of Seon practice. In Korea it was first obtained in the Goryeo period and printed again in 1472 as part of a Buddhist scripture project ordered by Queen Dowager Insu, and the surviving copy preserves both woodblock and movable-type printing.

1123612790000.title_en: Sakyamuni Hanging Painting of Jukrimsa Temple
1123612790000.description: This is a relatively small hanging painting depicting Sakyamuni alone. The Buddha is shown seated in full lotus position on a lotus pedestal, with a golden halo behind the head and floral patterns on the red-and-green robe. The right hand rests on the knee in a gesture of subduing demons, and the left hand forms the earth-touching mudra.

1123712800000.title_en: Bronze Bell of Oeosa Temple, Pohang
1123712800000.description: This is a Goryeo-period bronze bell that follows the form of Silla bells. It has a dragon-shaped suspension loop, a sound tube at the back, floral bands and lotus-bud decorations, and striking points placed on both the front and back. Inscriptions record that it was cast in 1216, hung at Oeosa Temple, and made by the master craftsman Seunggwang.

1121112810000.description: This printed book is a Chinese historical chronicle compiled by Sima Guang and revised under King Sejong's order. It was printed in 1436 and survives as an old edition with a record at the end of the complete copy indicating printing in the eighth month of that year. It is valued as a rare source for bibliography and the history of printing.

1121112810200.description: This is a surviving fragment of the Joseon period woodblock-style metal movable type edition of Zizhi Tongjian printed in 1436. The work was revised and annotated by court scholars under King Sejong and printed with the early gabinja type at the Hall of Government Deliberation in Gyeongbokgung Palace. Although incomplete, it is considered important for the study of early Joseon printing and bibliography.

1123112810300.description: This is a three-volume surviving fragment of the Zizhi Tongjian edition printed in 1436 under King Sejong. The text was edited by court scholars and printed with the early gabinja metal movable type. Its well-preserved condition makes it an important source for the study of early Joseon printing and publishing history.

1122612810400.description: This book is a surviving fragment from the 1436 gabinja movable-type edition of Zizhi Tongjian. It consists of one volume set from the original 100-book edition and is considered valuable for the study of early Joseon printing and bibliography. The surviving copy is rare and remains in good condition.

1122112810500.description: This is a surviving fragment of the 1436 gabinja movable-type edition of Zizhi Tongjian. It preserves one volume set from the original 100-book edition and is rare because complete copies no longer survive. It is an important source for the study of early Joseon printing and bibliography.

1122212810600.description: This is a 1436 printed edition of Zizhi Tongjian corresponding to volumes 129 through 132. Although it lacks a printing colophon, the text contains the phrase "Sujeongjeon hunui," indicating that it was edited at the Hall of Government Deliberation in Gyeongbokgung Palace, and its typography matches other known copies from the same edition. Volumes 129 and 130 provide important evidence for understanding the full extent of the 1463 printed Zizhi Tongjian.

1123112980000.description: This is a pair of portraits of Jo Yeong-bok (1672–1728), a Joseon civil official, depicting him in a white robe and in official attire. One portrait was painted by his younger brother Jo Yeong-seok in 1724, and the other was painted by the painter Jin Jae-hae in 1725. The two portraits show the same person in different formats and are valuable for comparing the characteristics of portraits of the period.

1123312990000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda of Boan Temple, Goesan
1123312990000.description: This stone pagoda stands beside the north wall of Boan Temple and has a one-tier base with a three-story body. A niche modeled after a Buddhist shrine is carved on the south face of the first story, a rare feature among stone pagodas found in the Chungcheongbuk-do area. It is considered to date to the later Goryeo period based on its simplified base and the form of the roof stones.

1123813000000.description: Hongjeam is a hermitage belonging to Haeinsa Temple, and it is where the monk-military commander Samyeong Daesa practiced meditation and died. It was built in 1614 to enshrine his portrait, and its name comes from the posthumous title "Jatong Hongje Jonja" bestowed on him by King Gwanghaegun. The building combines worship space and living quarters in an unusual layout centered on a main hall.

1123813010000.title_en: Stupa and Stele of Samyeong Daesa at Hongjeam Hermitage, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123813010000.description: This pair consists of the stupa and stele of Samyeong Daesa at Hongjeam Hermitage in Haeinsa Temple. The stele was erected in 1612 and records the life of the monk-military commander, with the inscription written by Heo Gyun. The stupa and stele were originally made as a set, continuing a tradition seen since the Silla period.

1123113020000.description: This Buddhist painting was made in 1692 to pray for the rebirth of ancestors in the Pure Land. The composition is divided into three sections, with the upper section showing Amitabha and other deities, the middle section showing a ritual offering scene, and the lower section depicting lively scenes of everyday life. It is also notable for the use of gold on the bodies of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas.

1123713030000.title_en: White Paper and Gold Ink Diamond Sutra and Universal Gate Vows
1123713030000.description: This illuminated manuscript was copied in 1371 through the donation of the Buddhist nuns Myoji and Myosu. It contains the Diamond Sutra, the Universal Gate chapter of the Lotus Sutra, and a prayer text by Yonggajeosa, with gold ink used in the illustrations at the beginning. The colophon at the end records the donor and date, making it an important example of late Goryeo Buddhist faith and manuscript practice.

1123613040000.title_en: Royal Certificate of Merit for Yu Mong-in
1123613040000.description: This is a royal certificate issued in March 1613 granting Yu Mong-in the third rank of the Wiseong Meritorious Retainer title for escorting Crown Prince Gwanghaegun during the Imjin War. The document sets out his service, the rewards granted to him and his family, and the oath of loyalty binding the meritorious retainers. It is an important source for the study of Joseon meritorious retainers and the Imjin War.

1123613050000.description: This full-length seated portrait shows Kim Wan wearing formal court dress with an official hat and sitting with his hands clasped. The rank badge and belt indicate that the sitter held the second rank, junior grade, and the portrait reflects the mid-Joseon style of meritorious-retainer portraits. The facial rendering and clothing folds are handled in a restrained, early 17th-century manner.

1123713060100.description: This seven-volume, two-volume-set woodblock edition of the Lotus Sutra was printed at Ansimsa Temple in Jeolla-do in 1405 under the supervision of monk Sinmun. It includes a frontispiece illustration, notes by Gupnam of Song, and Korean phonetic and explanatory markings throughout the text. The colophon by Gwon Geun and the records of donors are preserved, making it an important source for the publication history of the sutra.

1121113060200.description: This complete seven-volume, two-volume-set edition of the Lotus Sutra was printed at Ansimsa Temple in Jeolla-do in 1405, based on a version carefully copied by Seong Dal-saeng and Seong Gae. Volume 4 contains a six-page frontispiece illustration, and the text preserves gugyeol, headnotes, and Hangul phonetic glosses. It is valued for its completeness and for the evidence it provides on early Joseon Buddhist publishing and language use.

1123713060300.description: This seven-volume, two-volume-set Lotus Sutra was printed from woodblocks carved in 1405 at Ansimsa Temple in Unje-hyeon, Jeolla-do, and survives as a later printed edition. Except for one frontispiece page, it retains the form of a complete set, and all donation and publication information can be confirmed. The work is an important source for studying early Joseon Buddhist printing, frontispiece production, and the Buddhist thought of the late Goryeo and early Joseon periods.

1123613070000.title_en: Daewoongjeon Hall of Neunggasa Temple, Goheung
1123613070000.description: This Buddhist hall was rebuilt in the mid-18th century and has a front of five bays and a side of three bays. It uses a dapo bracket system and is decorated with carved details such as lotus buds and bracket ornaments, showing characteristic Buddhist architecture of the Honam region in the mid- to late Joseon period. It is considered important for architectural and art-historical study.

1123213080000.title_en: Royal Certificate Bestowing the Hosing Gongsin Title on Hong Jin
1123213080000.description: This royal certificate granted Hong Jin second rank among the Hosing Gongsin in recognition of his service during the Japanese invasions of Korea. It records the conferral details, the list of meritorious retainers by rank, and the date of issue in October 1604, with Seonjo's royal seal stamped on it. The document is valuable for studying the reward system for Hosing Gongsin officials.

1123613090000.title_en: Rock Inscription for the Burial of Incense at Eomgilli, Yeongam
1123613090000.description: This inscription is carved in intaglio on a natural rock face on Cheoram Mountain in Eomgilli, Yeongam, and contains 21 lines and 118 characters. It was made in 1344, making it the earliest extant burial-of-incense inscription in Korea. The inscription records the date, purpose, place, participants, donors, and carvers, and is an important source for the burial-of-incense custom of late Goryeo.

1123613100000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Bulhoesa Temple, Naju
1123613100000.description: This Daeungjeon Hall was rebuilt in 1799 and is a highly ornamental late Joseon Buddhist hall with a three-bay front and three-bay side. It stands on a natural stone foundation and uses a dapo bracket system, with carved decorations including dragon heads and lotus motifs in the interior. The building preserves the appearance of its original construction period and has historical and scholarly value.

1123613110000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123613110000.description: This Daeungjeon Hall was rebuilt in 1824 after earlier buildings were destroyed by fire in 1597 and again in 1766. The hall has a three-bay front and side, a hipped-and-gabled roof, and a dapo bracket structure with elaborate decorative details such as dragon-head ornamentation and lotus-bud carvings. It is an important example of the ornate Buddhist architecture of the late Joseon period.

1123712700000.title_en: Hangwae Buldang Hanging Scroll of Seated Buddha, Eunhaesa Temple
1123712700000.description: This large hanging Buddhist painting was made in 1750 and used for major temple rituals, to be displayed in the courtyard in front of the main hall. The Buddha is shown alone on a silk ground, with symmetrical decorative elements on both sides, and the composition uses mainly red and green against an ocher background.

1123712710000.title_en: Hanging Scroll of Rocana Buddha, Sudosa Temple
1123712710000.description: This large hanging Buddhist painting, made in 1704, depicts Rocana Buddha alone as the main image for ritual display. The Buddha wears a jeweled crown and holds a lotus branch, with seven small Buddha figures around the crown and multicolored rays rising behind the figure.

1123712720000.title_en: Vulture Peak Assembly Painting, Bulyeongsa Temple
1123712720000.description: This painting, made in 1733, depicts the scene of Sakyamuni Buddha preaching at Vulture Peak. It features Sakyamuni in the earth-touching gesture, surrounded by ten bodhisattvas, the Four Heavenly Kings, and ten chief disciples, with the larger central bodhisattva figures as a notable feature.

1123512740000.title_en: Three Seated Clay Statues of Sakyamuni Buddha with Reliquary Objects, Songgwangsa Temple, Wanju
1123512740000.description: This set consists of three large seated clay Buddha statues: Sakyamuni Buddha in the center, Amitabha Buddha on the right, and Medicine Buddha on the left. Relics discovered inside the main statue include dedicatory documents, Buddhist scriptures such as the Lotus Sutra, and several items related to the inner reliquary deposit, and the creation record shows that they were made in 1641.

1123212750000.title_en: South Three-Story Stone Pagoda at Hangaesaji Temple Site, Inje
1123212750000.description: This pagoda stands at the temple site of Hangaesa in Inje and is believed to have been built around the mid-9th century. It is a typical Unified Silla stone pagoda with a two-tiered stylobate and three-story body, and it was restored after being moved from its original location.

1123212760000.title_en: North Three-Story Stone Pagoda at Hangaesaji Temple Site, Inje
1123212760000.description: This pagoda stands on the hillside at the Hangaesa temple site in Inje and is believed to date to the mid-9th century. It is a typical Unified Silla stone pagoda with a two-tiered stylobate and three-story body, and it was restored in 1984 after having collapsed.

1123212770000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Samhwasa Temple, Donghae
1123212770000.description: This stone pagoda at Samhwasa Temple has a two-tiered base and a three-story body, with pillar-like decorations at the corners and centers of each side. It is believed to have been made in the late 9th century, and relics including small stone pagodas and a bronze Buddha pedestal fragment were found inside during restoration in 1997.

1123712780000.title_en: Hanging Scroll of the Vulture Peak Assembly, Bukjangsa Temple
1123712780000.description: This large hanging Buddhist painting, made in 1688, depicts the Vulture Peak assembly with Sakyamuni Buddha standing at the center and bodhisattvas surrounding him. It is known for its balanced figure composition, bright red and green colors, and detailed floral patterns.

1123613120000.title_en: Amitabha Buddha Triad, Muwiisa Temple, Gangjin
1123613120000.description:
This seated triad is enshrined on the altar of the Geuknakjeon Hall at Muwiisa Temple. It consists of Amitabha Buddha in the center, with Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva on the left and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva on the right.
The work was made in 1478, during the reign of King Seongjong of Joseon. It preserves the transitional style from late Goryeo Buddhist sculpture to early Joseon sculpture and is an important example for the study of early Joseon Buddhist images.

1123613140000.title_en: White-robed Avalokitesvara Mural, Geuknakjeon Hall, Muwiisa Temple
1123613140000.description:
This mural is painted on the rear wall behind the Amitabha mural in Geuknakjeon Hall. It depicts White-robed Avalokitesvara standing on a lotus leaf above rolling waves, with a bhiksu below and a bird perched on his shoulder.
It is believed to have been painted around 1476, in the early Joseon period. Together with the front Amitabha mural, it is an important source for the study of early Joseon Buddhist paintings in the Goryeo style.

1123613150000.title_en: Wall Paintings on the Interior Walls of Geuknakjeon Hall, Muwiisa Temple
1123613150000.description:
These are the wall paintings that once decorated the interior walls of Geuknakjeon Hall, now dismantled and preserved in a conservation building. The ensemble includes 29 pieces, among them triad paintings, Amitabha welcoming paintings, bodhisattva paintings, and decorative designs such as lotus-and-vine motifs and peony patterns.
Among them, several works, including the triad painting, the Amitabha welcoming painting, and some bodhisattva and pattern paintings, are especially important for the study of early Joseon Buddhist painting in the Goryeo style. Their creation spans the 15th to 19th centuries, but an exact single year cannot be determined.

1123813160000.description:
This large hanging scroll depicts a single bodhisattva-like figure filling the entire composition. The figure wears an elaborate crown with five small buddhas at the center and holds lotus stems with blossoms in both hands.
It was painted in 1684, during the reign of King Sukjong of Joseon. The painting is noted for its well-preserved condition, refined linework, balanced proportions, and detailed decorative patterns.

1123813170000.title_en: Banner Painting and Chest of Unheungsa Temple
1123813170000.description:
This set consists of a Yeongsan Assembly banner painting showing the seated Buddha with many attendant figures, and the chest used to store the banner. The painting was created in 1730 by monk-painters including Uigyeom, and the chest was made the following year, in 1731.
The banner is characterized by a large central Buddha, crowded patterns, and red Sanskrit characters placed on various parts of the figures. The chest also has openwork metal fittings with auspicious motifs, making it a notable example for the study of Joseon metal craft.
1123813170000.material: Ink and color on silk; wood chest with metal fittings

1121113180000.description:
This eight-panel folding screen was made by dismantling an astronomical chart painted on paper. It combines the traditional Joseon astronomical chart based on Cheonsang yeolcha bunyajido with Western-style astronomical charts introduced after the 17th century.
It is believed to have been produced in the 1720s or early 1730s. Made by the Office of Astronomy and a unique surviving example in Korea, it reflects the early 18th-century worldview of Joseon scholars.

1121113190000.title_en: Dae Tongnyeok Calendar of the Gyeongjin Year
1121113190000.description:
This is a printed calendar based on the Ming dynasty system of the Dae Tongnyeok, which was used in Korea from the late Goryeo period until the adoption of the Shixian calendar in 1653. The book is composed of 15 leaves, including seasonal tables, monthly calendars, and notes on auspicious and inauspicious activities.
It was made in 1580, likely printed in the previous year for use in the new year. As the only pre-Imjin War calendar printed with type by the Office of Astronomy, it is an important source for the study of Joseon printing and bibliography.

1122213200000.title_en: Beopmun of Repentance for the Amitabha Rite, Volume 7
1122213200000.description:
This Buddhist scripture records the procedures for a repentance rite dedicated to Amitabha Buddha and the hope of rebirth in the Western Pure Land. The volume includes a postface by Bak Myeonta and lists the names of those involved in the publication, including sponsors.
It was printed in 1376, during the reign of King U of Goryeo. The edition is rare and highly valued as a Buddhist textual source.

1121112810700.description: This is one fascicle containing volumes 266–270 of the Korean woodblock-printed edition of the Chinese historical work Zizhi Tongjian. It was compiled in 1434 and completed in 1436, and was printed with early movable metal type at the Jujaso foundry. The extant copy is rare and is valued as an important bibliographic source.

1121112820000.title_en: Choe Yu-ryeon, Meritorious Subject Register of the Founding Merit Order
1121112820000.description: This register was issued in 1395 by the office in charge of meritorious retainers to honor Choe Yu-ryeon for his contributions to the founding of Joseon. It records the recipient’s name and status, the merits, rewards, instructions, and the list of 105 meritorious subjects with their rewards. The document is an important source for the political history of early Joseon and for the study of official documents.

1123612830000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Yongamsaji Temple Site, Wolchulsan Mountain, Yeongam
1123612830000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands on a rock called Tapbong at the Yongamsa temple site in Wolchulsan Mountain. During restoration in 1966, a white porcelain reliquary, a gilt-bronze seated bodhisattva, a celadon bowl, relics, and iron fragments were found from the lower foundation level. The structure is dated to the Goryeo period.

1123412840000.title_en: Five-story Stone Pagoda at Cheongnyangsa Temple Site, Gongju
1123412840000.description: This is one of two stone pagodas remaining at the Cheongnyangsa temple site, which are also called the Sister Pagodas. It rises five stories above a single-tier base and follows the Baekje-style stone pagoda tradition. The pagoda is generally believed to have been made in the mid-Goryeo period.

1123412850000.title_en: Seven-story Stone Pagoda at Cheongnyangsa Temple Site, Gongju
1123412850000.description: This pagoda is one of the two stone pagodas at the Cheongnyangsa temple site, known as the Brother and Sister Pagodas. It has a narrow, tall form with seven stories above a single-tier base and a rectangular niche carved on one side of the first-story body stone. It is thought to have been made in the mid-Goryeo period, showing characteristics of the stone pagoda style that developed from Baekje models.

1121112860000.description: This hanging scroll depicts Avalokitesvara seated on a rock in a half-lotus pose, looking down at Sudhana, as in a scene from the Avatamsaka Sutra. Bamboo stands behind the figure, and a vase with willow branches is placed in front. The painting was restored between 1994 and 1996 and is believed to date to the 14th century.

1122112870000.description: This triad painting places Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva prominently in the center, seated on a rock with a halo around the head. To the left is Domyeong Jozaja holding a long monk’s staff, and to the right is Mudeok Guiwang holding a box containing a Buddhist scripture. The composition is unusual among surviving Goryeo Buddhist paintings, and the work is generally considered to belong to the late Goryeo or early Joseon period.

1123612880000.description: This stele was erected in 1603 to honor Admiral Yi Sun-sin. The inscription explains the name "Tarubi," taken from a Chinese phrase meaning "tear-shedding stele," and records the reason for its erection and the date. The stele has a pedestal, body stone, and capstone, with floral carving on the pedestal and cloud patterns on the capstone.

1122213210000.description: This book was compiled in 1610 by Choi Gi-nam, who served as the docheong of the Hunryeondogam in King Gwanghaegun’s reign. He added a section on Japan to the revised continuation of Muyejebo, and the book is regarded as the only extant copy in Korea and an important source for early 17th-century Korean language studies.

1123613220000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda of Gagok-ri, Gokseong
1123613220000.description: This stone pagoda stands on the site of a former temple on the northern slope of Maebong in Gagok-ri. Built on a two-tier base with five stories of the body, it preserves features associated with Baekje-style pagodas, including broad roofstone corners and the use of separate support stones under each story.

1123113230000.title_en: Lanterns at the Tomb of Gonghyeogong Bak Jung-son, Paju
1123113230000.description: These are the two stone lanterns placed in front of the tombs of Bak Jung-son and his wife. One lantern has unusual openings whose square, round, and crescent shapes are said to symbolize earth, sun, and moon, making the pair a rare example of this type.

1123113240000.description: This rock carving is a slender line-engraved standing Buddhist image on a boulder known as Janggunbawi. It wears a patterned cylindrical crown and a robe covering both shoulders, features that are typical of early Goryeo stone sculpture.

1123513250000.description: This bronze bell was donated and returned in 1999 by a Japanese collector who had inherited it from her family. Although the suspension loop is damaged, the bell is largely complete, and its form and decorative motifs suggest an early Goryeo date, around the 11th century.

1121113260000.title_en: Four Buddha Assembly Hanging Painting of Sangwonsa Temple, Hamchang
1121113260000.description: This Buddhist painting combines four different Buddha assemblies—Bhaisajyaguru, Amitabha, Shakyamuni, and Maitreya—into a single composition. It was made in 1562 by Yi Jong-rin to pray for the repose of his maternal grandfather, Kwon Chan, and other family members, and it preserves detailed inscriptions about its production and patrons.

1121113270000.description: This small stone image depicts Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva seated on a rock-shaped base, wearing a head covering and holding a jewel in the left hand. An inscription on the back of the pedestal records the circumstances of its making, the donors and maker, and the exact date of 1515.

1121113280000.description: This painting records a Giyeonghoe, a gathering of senior scholars and officials aged seventy or older. It shows the banquet in a hall and includes the names, ranks, and literary writings of the participants in the lower register, while also depicting attendants and musicians in lively detail.

1121113290000.title_en: White Porcelain Octagonal Water Dropper with Blue-and-White Eight Views of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers Design
1121113290000.description: This large white porcelain water dropper has an octagonal body. The top is decorated in relief with cloud and dragon motifs, and the eight side panels are painted with the Eight Views of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers, while one panel substitutes a poem for a painted scene.
1121113290000.material: White porcelain with underglaze cobalt blue

1123713300000.title_en: Eight Scenes of the Buddha's Life Hanging Painting, Yecheon Yongmunsa Temple
1123713300000.description: This work is an eight-scene Buddhist painting that depicts the life of the Buddha from conception to nirvana. It is arranged in four panels, with two scenes on each panel, and uses a relatively simple composition with a yellow ground and mainly red and greenish-blue colors.

1123613310000.title_en: Rocana Buddha Hanging Painting, Heungguksa Temple
1123613310000.description: This large hanging painting was used for major Buddhist rites and depicts the principal Buddha alone, filling the entire composition. Rocana Buddha is shown wearing a crown with a small Buddha figure and raising both hands to shoulder height, with pavilion eaves above and pagodas at the lower left and right.

1123613320000.description: This painting depicts Avalokitesvara seated in the center of a pure land setting. Seonjae Dongja stands at the lower right with palms joined, while waves, a vase with bamboo and willow branches, and a bird are shown around the figure.

1123613330000.description: This set originally included a central painting of the Vulture Peak Assembly, but only six panels of arhats remain today. The composition is symmetrical, with the eight chief disciples and other figures arranged on the left and right sides around the central Buddha, and it is notable for the soft use of ink wash and subdued colors.

1122213340100.title_en: Documents Related to the U Baeseon Militia, Hwayeon - Military Merit Register
1122213340100.description: This collection contains documents related to U Baeseon's militia activities during the Imjin War. It includes a military merit register listing the achievements of U Baeseon and 88 of his followers, as well as related edicts, petitions, appointment notices, letters, and other records.

1123113340200.title_en: Documents Related to the U Baeseon Militia, Hwayeon - Royal Edicts
1123113340200.description: This set consists of royal edicts, appointment notices, letters, and related records connected with U Baeseon, a militia commander of the Imjin War. The documents record his appointments and promotions, as well as posthumous honors granted to his parents and other related materials.

1122213350000.description: This book is an excerpted compilation of important passages from the Buddhist canon, Tripitaka, compiled by Chen Shi of the Song dynasty. It was printed in the mid-13th century in Goryeo and is regarded as the oldest extant surviving copy in Korea.

1123213360000.description:
This rainbow-shaped stone bridge links the Daeungjeon area and the Geungnakjeon area of Goseong Beonbongsa Temple. It was first built between 1704 and 1707 during the reign of King Sukjong, and later repaired after flood damage in 1745 and 1749.
The bridge is 14.3 meters long and 3 meters wide, with a central arch made of stone. A commemorative stele records its construction and makes it an important source for the study of arch bridges.

1123213370000.description:
This stone arch bridge stands on the boundary between Haeang-ri and Taphyeon-ri in Ganseong-eup, Goseong-gun. It was repaired in 1746 during the reign of King Yeongjo, and its original construction date is not known.
The bridge makes effective use of the natural terrain, with the eastern side built on exposed bedrock and the western side supported by large stone bases. It is regarded as a well-preserved example of a single-arch stone bridge from the Joseon period.

1123313380000.title_en: East and West Three-Story Stone Pagodas of Yongamsa Temple, Okcheon
1123313380000.description:
These two stone pagodas stand on a low northern ridge with wide views rather than in front of the main hall, which is unusual for a temple layout. They are thought to have been built in the Goryeo period under the influence of the idea of sanch'eon bibo, or supplementing the energy of mountains and streams.
Both pagodas have a two-tiered base and a three-story body, though the eastern pagoda is slightly larger than the western one. The western pagoda has some restored body stones on the second and third stories.

1123413390000.description:
This hanging Buddhist banner shows Śākyamuni Buddha holding a flower branch, with Amitābha Buddha, Medicine Buddha, and the Four Heavenly Kings among the attendants. It is a large altar painting used for major temple rituals.
The composition presents the central Buddha in large scale, with the other figures arranged in groups above and below. Its bright palette, including vermilion, gold, light green, pink, and blue, reflects 18th-century characteristics.

1123613400000.description:
This hanging Buddhist painting depicts Śākyamuni alone in a single standing image. It was painted in 1673 by the court painters Gyeongsim, Gigam, and Neungseong.
The large composition fills the entire screen with the Buddha facing forward. It is valued as an important work that shows new trends in late-17th-century Buddhist painting through its modeling, earthy tones, brushwork, and patterning.

1123613410000.description:
This hanging Buddhist banner is arranged in the form of Śākyamuni Buddha with two attendants, placing the Buddha in the center and bodhisattvas on the left and right. The main Buddha makes the gesture of touching the earth, and the left attendant is Manjusri Bodhisattva.
It was painted in 1683 by the three monk-painters Gyeo-o, Saman, and Singyun. Because it includes a record of its production, it is an especially valuable source for the study of Buddhist painting.

1123613420000.description:
This hanging Buddhist banner places the principal Buddha large in the center of the composition and depicts the Dragon King and Dragon Princess in the lower section. The Buddha’s features are rendered small and the robe decoration reflects patterns seen in paintings from the late 18th century.
It was painted in 1727 by Takhaeng, Seolsim, Hiesim, Imhan, Minhwi, Chuisang, and Myeonghyeon. The work is noted for its large central Buddha and its soft but vivid use of green, red, mung bean green, pink, and ochre tones.

1123613430000.description:
This hanging Buddhist painting shows a standing Śākyamuni triad filling the main part of the screen, with bodhisattvas and tathāgatas painted smaller in the upper section. It was originally enshrined at Bohungsa Temple on Geumsongsan Mountain in Naju.
It was painted in 1745 by the monk-painter Uigyeom and nine other painters. The work is considered important for showing Uigyeom’s later style, in which the fine form, coloring, and brushwork became somewhat less refined.

1123613440000.title_en: Hanging Painting of Buddha at Geumtapsa Temple
1123613440000.description: This hanging painting depicts the Three Buddhas and the main attendant bodhisattvas in a wide horizontal composition. It omits guardian figures such as the Four Heavenly Kings and presents a simplified arrangement centered on the main images. A record indicates that the painting was produced in 1778 by two painters, Bi-hyeon and Gwaeun.

1123613450000.title_en: Hanging Painting of Buddha at Manyeonsa Temple
1123613450000.description: This hanging painting shows the Sakyamuni Triad, with Sakyamuni Buddha in the center and Manjusri and Samantabhadra Bodhisattvas on either side. The composition is decorated with dragon, arabesque, wave, and bead motifs, and the lower garments of the bodhisattvas are painted with blue designs on a white ground. An inscription states that it was made in 1793 by the painters Bi-hyeon, Haeun, and Do-ok.

1123613460000.title_en: Stupa of Soyo Daesa at Baekyangsa Temple, Jangseong
1123613460000.description: This stone stupa is the memorial stupa of Soyo Daesa, who served as head monk of Baekyangsa Temple, and was moved to the temple museum area from the stupa enclosure near the entrance. It is made of granite and consists of a base, body, and finial. The form includes octagonal and bell-shaped elements, and the front is inscribed with 'Soyodang' to identify the deceased monk.

1123613470000.title_en: Stupa of Seosan Daesa at Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1123613470000.description: This octagonal stone stupa stands in the stupa enclosure near the entrance to Daeheungsa Temple and is the memorial stupa of Seosan Daesa. It is 2.7 m high and consists of a base, body, and finial, with the name 'Cheongheodang' carved on the front of the body. Based on a nearby stupa stele dated 1647, it is thought to have been made around that time.

1123613480000.title_en: Reliquary from the West Five-story Stone Pagoda of Hwaeomsa Temple
1123613480000.description: This group of relics was discovered inside the West Five-story Stone Pagoda of Hwaeomsa Temple during dismantling and repair work in 1995. It includes a paper, ink, and Buddhist text of a dharani sutra, a bronze Buddha mold, bronze bells and ornaments, an iron knife, metal fragments, crystal, and other items. These finds provide important evidence for the study of Unified Silla Buddhism, bibliography, and early Korean printing.

1123613490000.title_en: Bronze Bell of Taeansa Temple, Gokseong
1123613490000.description: This bronze bell was made in 1581 after an earlier bell, first cast in 1457, had been damaged. The body is decorated with a dragon-shaped handle, floral and lotus motifs, arabesque patterns, and four rectangular panels with lotus-bud ornaments. The inscription on the bell records its casting history and makes it an important example of a 16th-century temple bell.

1123813500000.title_en: Hanging Painting of Sakyamuni Buddha at Tongdosa Temple
1123813500000.description: This hanging painting depicts Sakyamuni Buddha alone, holding a flowering branch. The figure stands frontally within a large composition framed by Sanskrit characters, with halos and clouds arranged around the upper section. An inscription states that it was produced in 1767 by the patron Taehwal and 14 painter-monks, including Duhun.

1123813510000.title_en: Hanging Painting of Bodhisattva at Tongdosa Temple
1123813510000.description: This hanging painting depicts a standing bodhisattva alone, holding a lotus branch. The central figure wears a jeweled crown that includes seven small Buddhas, and the composition is finished with halos and clouds in the upper section. An inscription states that it was produced in 1792 by the monk Jiyeon and 22 painter-monks.

1123813520000.description: This hanging Buddhist painting from 1811 depicts the "Seven Places and Nine Assemblies" of the Avatamsaka Sutra. It simplifies the complex contents of the 80-fascicle Avatamsaka Sutra into three sections, with heaven shown in the upper part and the earthly realms in the middle and lower parts, and adds newly introduced figures such as Thousand-Armed Avalokiteshvara, Cundi Avalokiteshvara, and the Mirror of Karma.
1123813520000.material: Ink and gold on black ground

1123813530000.title_en: Vulture Peak Assembly Painting of Tongdosa Temple
1123813530000.description: This hanging Buddhist painting depicts the Vulture Peak Assembly, showing Śākyamuni preaching at Mount Grdhrakuta. Śākyamuni sits on a lotus throne atop a high Sumeru pedestal, surrounded by Manjusri, Samantabhadra, the ten great disciples, Indra, Brahma, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the Eight Legions.

1123813540000.title_en: Bronze Incense Burner with Silver Inlay from Tongdosa Temple (2002)
1123813540000.description: This large Goryeo- and Joseon-style high-footed bronze incense burner is the largest surviving example of its type in Korea. An inscription on the back records that it was made in 1674 by Sin Aenam, and the vessel preserves a clear record of its maker and temple dedication.

1121113550000.description: This is a printed Buddhist text that is one of the six treatises of the Sarvāstivāda school and was translated into Chinese by Xuanzang. It is a rare early woodblock-printed edition from the first carving of the Tripiṭaka, valued for its excellent preservation and printing condition.

1121113560000.title_en: Printed Edition of Xianyang Shengjiao Lun, Volume 3
1121113560000.description: This is volume 3 of the Buddhist treatise Xianyang Shengjiao Lun, a 20-volume work by Asaṅga translated into Chinese by Xuanzang. It is an early carved edition of the Tripiṭaka with important differences from the later Haeinsa edition, including format, colophon, and textual variants.

1123613570000.title_en: Relics of Seosan Daisa at Daeheungsa Temple
1123613570000.description: These two items are relics associated with the monk Seosan Daesa (Hyujeong) at Daeheungsa Temple in Haenam. They consist of a 1602 royal document reissuing his appointment as commander of the monk soldiers, and a 1794 inscription composed by King Jeongjo to honor Seosan Daesa's loyalty.

1121113580000.description: This is a handwritten color map of the Korean Peninsula, probably produced by Kim Jeong-ho during the reigns of Cheoljong and Gojong in the 19th century. It is an accordion-fold map in 23 sections and closely follows the structure of Daedongyeojido, with detailed roads, administrative districts, fortresses, relay stations, and other geographic information.

1121113580200.description: This is a handwritten 19th-century map of Joseon, probably made by Kim Jeong-ho in the mid-19th century. It consists of 23 accordion-fold sections and closely matches Daedongyeojido in overall geography, while including many more place names, especially for villages and townships.

1123613770000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Buddha Triad, Yeonggwang Bulgapsa Temple
1123613770000.description: This wooden triad of seated Buddhas is enshrined in Daeungjeon Hall at Bulgapsa Temple. The central Sakyamuni Buddha is flanked by Bhaisajyaguru on the left and Amitabha on the right. An inscription discovered inside the images records that they were made in 1635 by the monk artisan Muyeom and others.

1123813780000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Buddha Triad and Four Standing Bodhisattvas, Hadong Ssanggyesa Temple
1123813780000.description: This set consists of the wooden seated Sakyamuni Buddha and Bhaisajyaguru Buddha, together with four standing bodhisattvas believed to be Suryaprabha, Candraprabha, Avalokitesvara, and Mahasthamaprapta. The figures were made in 1639 by the monk artisan Cheongheon and others, as recorded in an inscription found inside the images. The work is regarded as an important example for studying Buddhist sculpture in the first half of the 17th century.

1123713790000.description: This large Buddhist painting on hemp cloth was made for hanging outdoors during major temple rites and ceremonies. It depicts a standing Buddha filling the center of the composition, with transformed buddhas and bodhisattvas arranged around the halo. An inscription on the lower part records that it was made in 1768 by Monk Jeongil and nine others.

1123313800000.title_en: Royal Certificate of Merit for Sin Gyeong-haeng, and Related Documents
1123313800000.description: This set contains eight kinds of nine documents related to Sin Gyeong-haeng, including his royal certificate of merit, royal orders, documents concerning his posthumous title, and registers of merit office oath gatherings. The materials date from 1604 to 1812 and document his service, his role in suppressing the Lee Mong-hak rebellion, and the process by which he received the posthumous title Chungik. They are valuable sources for the study of Joseon royal documents and merit-ranking records.

1123413810000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Buddha Triad and Reliquary Objects, Yeosan Sudeoksa Temple
1123413810000.description: This set includes the wooden seated triad of Sakyamuni Buddha, associated reliquary objects, lotus pedestal, and sumidan platform enshrined in Daeungjeon Hall at Sudeoksa Temple. An inscription inside the images shows that they were made in 1639 by the monk artisan Suyeon and six others. The sumidan and the relics found inside the images are important materials for the study of Joseon-period Buddhist sculpture, textiles, and ritual objects.

1121113820000.title_en: Celadon Inkstone with Inlaid Chrysanthemum and Peony Design and Inscription 'Sinchuk'
1121113820000.description: This rare celadon inkstone is notable for its fine inlaid decoration and for the inscription naming the date of production, the maker, and the user. The underside bears the inscription "made on the tenth day of the fifth month in the sinchuk year," together with the name Seo Gam-bu. Based on the glaze and inlay style, the sinchuk year is most likely 1181.

1121113830000.title_en: Celadon Iron-painted Floral, Insect, and Bird Vase
1121113830000.description: This is an early example of iron-painted celadon, in which designs are painted with iron-rich slip and then covered with celadon glaze. The vase has a wide mouth, rounded shoulders, and a body that descends in nearly straight lines to the foot, and its surface is decorated with floral scrolls, a large branch design, a bird, butterflies, and a bee. It is considered a representative work of Goryeo iron-painted celadon.

1121113840000.title_en: Celadon Square-shouldered Flask with Inlaid Willow, Heron, Plum, and Bamboo Design
1121113840000.description: This celadon flask is a representative inlaid vessel with a square form and varied decorative motifs. The shoulder is ornamented with carved demon-mask appliqués, and the body is divided into sections containing inlaid willow, birds, bamboo, and plum blossom designs. The glaze is pale grayish, and the vessel shows the refined inlay technique characteristic of late Goryeo celadon.

1121113850000.title_en: Celadon Incised Cloud and Dragon Prunus Vase
1121113850000.description: This prunus vase, made in the mid-Goryeo period, has the standard elegant form of a maebyeong with a large, dignified body. Four dragons are densely arranged on the front, and low, thick cloud designs are incised in the empty spaces on the shoulders and lower body. The vessel is covered with a clear light green celadon glaze and is thought to have been used by the royal court.

1121113860000.description: This prunus vase dates from the late Goryeo to early Joseon period and follows the typical early Joseon maebyeong form, with a flaring mouth, rounded shoulders, a narrow waist, and a wide lower body. It is decorated with inlaid fish-dragon motifs, lotus scrolls, and small mandarin ducks, combining marvelous and everyday subjects in a distinctive composition. The vessel is finished with a clear pale green glaze.

1121113870000.description: This large buncheong jar from the 15th century is decorated with bold black iron-painted designs. A central peony bloom and large leaves fill the body, with simple scroll designs and line work around them. It has a gray clay body with fine sand particles and a thin glaze with an overall subdued sheen.

1121113880000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Sgraffito Lotus Pattern Flat Bottle
1121113880000.description: This flat bottle is a representative 15th-century buncheong ware vessel with a full, rounded form. The lotus design is expressed with an energetic combination of inlay and sgraffito, with the outlines of the lotus and stem drawn boldly while the background is carved away. It is coated with a clear bluish-gray glaze and shows traces of kiln support on the base.

1121113890000.title_en: Celadon Inlaid Poem Inscription Prunus Vase with Plum, Bamboo, and Willow Design
1121113890000.description: This rare celadon prunus vase is decorated with an inlaid poem inscription. Plum, bamboo, and willow designs are placed on the body, and the title of the poem, "Jangjinju," is in black inlay; the poem itself is by Li He of the Tang dynasty. The vessel has a fine clear glaze with a network of crackles over the surface.

1121113900000.title_en: White Porcelain Blue-and-White Landscape Jar with Autumn Moon over Dongting Lake
1121113900000.description: This white porcelain jar, also called a tteokme bottle because of its shape, has a large cylindrical body and a wide mouth. Blue-and-white landscape scenes are painted around the surface, including pavilions on cliffs, a moonlit view with distant peaks, and a river village with boats. It is thought to have been made in the late 18th century, possibly by a royal court painter.
1121113900000.material: White porcelain with cobalt blue underglaze

1123113910000.title_en: White Porcelain Inlaid Openwork Peony Pattern Bottle
1123113910000.description: This early Joseon white porcelain bottle combines openwork and inlay decoration, a rare technique not otherwise known in surviving examples. It has a flaring mouth, a long slender neck, and a broad lower body, matching the typical form of early Joseon porcelain bottles. The openworked outer wall was made separately from the inner bottle that held the contents.

1121113920000.title_en: Yi Am, Flowers, Birds, and Puppies
1121113920000.description: This painting by Yi Am shows three puppies resting in a spring garden with flowering trees in the background. Two birds sit on a curving branch, while butterflies and a bee fly nearby, creating a peaceful scene. The rocks and ground are rendered with short, linear texture strokes typical of the early Joseon period.

1121113590000.title_en: Reliquary from the East Three-Story Stone Pagoda Site of Gameunsa Temple, Gyeongju
1121113590000.description: This set of reliquary objects was discovered in 1996 during dismantling and repair of the eastern three-story stone pagoda at the Gameunsa Temple site in Gyeongju, Gyeongsangbuk-do. It consists of an outer container, an inner reliquary, and a crystal reliquary bottle, and the exterior is decorated with the Four Heavenly Kings, cloud motifs, and face-shaped handles. The set is regarded as an important example of Unified Silla Buddhist craftsmanship.

1123313600000.title_en: Three Seated Buddha Statues of Buried Clay at Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123313600000.description: This group of three seated statues enshrined at Beopjusa Temple consists of Vairocana Buddha in the center, with Amitabha Buddha on the left and Shakyamuni Buddha on the right. The statues were made in 1626, and an inscription indicates that they were re-gilded in 1747. They are considered an important standard work for the study of late Joseon Buddhist sculpture after the Japanese invasions.

1123313610000.title_en: Wooden Seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva of Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123313610000.description: This wooden seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is enshrined at Beopjusa Temple. An inscription found inside the statue shows that it was made in 1655. The work is notable for its voluminous form, restrained style, and the natural flowing drapery of the robe.

1123213620000.title_en: Dry-Lacquer Seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva of Naksansa Temple, Yangyang
1123213620000.description: This dry-lacquer seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is enshrined in the Wontongbojeon Hall of Naksansa Temple, and is also said to have been brought from nearby Yeonghyeolsa Temple. It sits in full lotus posture on an octagonal metal pedestal and is characterized by a high jeweled crown, a rounded face, and fine, elegant modeling. Based on its style, it is considered a work of the early Joseon period influenced by late Goryeo traditions.

1123613630000.title_en: Three Body Buddhas Hanging Scrolls of Daeungjeon Hall, Hwaeomsa Temple
1123613630000.description: This set of three hanging scrolls in Daeungjeon Hall at Hwaeomsa Temple depicts the Three Bodies of the Buddha: Vairocana, Nairatmya/Nosana, and Shakyamuni. The work was painted in 1757 by a group of monks led by Uigyeom, and is notable for its large scale, fine line work, and extensive use of green. It is regarded as one of the representative examples of 18th-century Three Bodies of the Buddha paintings.

1123813640000.title_en: Three Buddhas Hanging Scrolls of Daeungjeon Hall, Ssanggyesa Temple
1123813640000.description: This set of three hanging scrolls in Daeungjeon Hall at Ssanggyesa Temple depicts Shakyamuni Buddha in the center, with Yaksa Buddha on the left and Amitabha Buddha on the right. It was made in 1781 and is an important late-18th-century large-scale Buddhist painting with a well-preserved complete format. The work is also significant for tracing the line of painters from Uigyeom to Seungyun and Pyeongsam.

1123813650000.title_en: Eight Scenes of the Buddha Hanging Scrolls of Pal Sangjeon Hall, Ssanggyesa Temple
1123813650000.description: This set of eight hanging scrolls depicts eight scenes from the life of Shakyamuni Buddha, including his descent from Tusita Heaven, birth at Lumbini, renunciation, ascetic practice, subjugation of Mara, first sermon at Deer Park, and nirvana beneath the twin sala trees. The paintings were made in 1728 by eight monk-painters, as recorded in the inscriptions on the works. They are organized in a simple panel-like format and are important examples of early-18th-century Buddhist painting.

1123613670000.title_en: Seated Sakyamuni Buddha Hanging Scroll and Sixteen Arhats Hanging Scrolls of Eungjindang Hall, Songgwangsa Temple
1123613670000.description: This group of Buddhist paintings in Eungjindang Hall at Songgwangsa Temple consists of a central seated Sakyamuni Buddha hanging scroll, flanked by sixteen Arhats scrolls and images of Indra and Brahma. The central painting was made in 1724, and the set includes inscriptions identifying the figures. The works are important for understanding the iconographic arrangement of Eungjindang Hall and the development of 18th-century Arhat paintings.

1121113930000.description: This painting depicts the scene from Ouyang Xiu’s prose poem "Ode to Autumn Sounds," rendered by Kim Hong-do in 1805. The inscription at the left states that it was painted in the year of Eulchuk, three days after the winter solstice, by Dan-gu.
1121113930000.material: Ink and light color on paper

1121113940000.title_en: Folding Screen of the Gyeonggi Provincial Office
1121113940000.description: This 12-panel folding screen shows the landscape and buildings of the Gyeonggi provincial government office outside Seodaemun, set beneath the ridges of Inwangsan. It includes official buildings, roads, market scenes, and a procession of the Gyeonggi governor, combining landscape, map-like, and genre-painting elements. The work reflects the urban and administrative setting of 19th-century Seoul.

1123613950000.title_en: Stele of Doseon Guksa and Sumiseonsa at Dogapsa Temple, Yeongam
1123613950000.description: This stone stele commemorates the lives of the Unified Silla monk Doseon Guksa and the Joseon monk Sumiseonsa. It has a turtle pedestal, stele body, and capstone, with the inscription stating that it was rebuilt in 1653 after an earlier stele had been damaged. The stele is notable for its large scale and the dragon-and-cloud reliefs on its sides and capstone.

1123613960000.title_en: Historical Stele of Baekryeonsa Temple, Gangjin
1123613960000.description: This stele stands near Daeungjeon Hall at Baengnyeonsa Temple and consists of a turtle pedestal, stele body, and capstone made in different periods. The pedestal is thought to date to the early Goryeo period, while the stele body and capstone were made in 1681. The inscription records the history of the temple and the people involved in its restoration.

1121113970000.title_en: Buddha Preaching the Sermon on Vulture Peak Hanging Scroll, Yeongguksa Temple
1121113970000.description: This hanging scroll places Shakyamuni Buddha at the center, with Manjusri, Samantabhadra, and other bodhisattvas and sacred beings arranged symmetrically around him. The upper area is filled with soft cloud forms, while the figures are painted to become smaller toward the top, creating a sense of depth. The inscription records that it was painted in 1709 by the monk painters Inmun, Mingi, and Sejeong.

1123113980000.description: This Goryeo celadon ewer is formed with a rounded body, a duck head as the spout, and a handle made to resemble folded duck legs. The lid is shaped like a lotus seed pod, and the body is decorated with inlaid and carved feather patterns. Its refined glaze and inventive animal form make it an important example of 12th-century Goryeo celadon.

1123113990000.title_en: Celadon Gourd-shaped Ewer with Relief Floral-line Design
1123113990000.description: This Goryeo celadon ewer has a gourd-shaped body with a high flaring foot and a narrow spout and handle modeled after bamboo shoots and joints. White clay dots are applied along the raised and incised lines of the decoration. The piece is valued as a refined and unusual 12th-century celadon with a clear bluish-green glaze.

1123114000000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Jar with Inlaid Peony and Arabesque Design
1123114000000.description: This buncheong ware jar has a sturdy rectangular form, with wide lips and a broad foot. The body is decorated with inlaid peony-and-arabesque motifs and stamped floral patterns, arranged symmetrically across the front and sides. It is a representative example of 15th-century buncheong ware and an important source for the study of ceramic history.

1122213690000.title_en: Collected Explanations of Translated Sanskrit Terms
1122213690000.description: This Buddhist lexicon, compiled by Song-dynasty monk Fayun, classifies and explains Chinese renderings of Sanskrit terms found in Buddhist scriptures. It is divided into 64 sections and contains about 2,000 terms, with sources and meanings given for each entry. The extant edition is a 14-volume work bound in 8 books and includes a record at the end identifying Fayun as a monk of Jingde Monastery in Suzhou.

1123313700000.title_en: Stupa of Uisang at Gyeongae Temple, Goesan
1123313700000.description: This stone stupa stands on a ridge on the slope of Bogeosan near Gyeongae Temple. It is a typical octagonal, one-story stone stupa with a pedestal, body, and finial, and was reconstructed in 1982 after being found collapsed in 1965. Based on its style and the associated stele, it is thought to have been built in the early Goryeo period.

1123313710000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Banyasa Temple, Yeongdong
1123313710000.description: This stone pagoda stands within the grounds of Banyasa Temple and was moved here in 1950 from Tapbeol in the Seokcheon Valley north of the temple. It is 335 cm high and consists of a single-story stylobate and three stories of body stones, with a largely complete structure despite some replaced pieces. Its form and construction suggest an early Goryeo date and show a mixture of Baekje-line and Silla-line pagoda traditions.

1123613720000.title_en: Stone Bridge over Gomakcheon Stream, Hampyeong
1123613720000.description: This stone bridge spans Gomakcheon Stream on the boundary between Hampyeong and Naju. It is a plank bridge about 20 meters long, 3.5 meters wide, and 2.5 meters high, with a wooden-frame style deck supported by five piers. It is believed to have been built between 1390 and 1495 and preserves an old bridge form at its original location.

1123813730000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Celestial Chart from Tongdosa Temple, Yangsan
1123813730000.description: This gilt-bronze celestial chart shows constellations from the north celestial pole to the equatorial region on the front, with 109 constellations and 481 stars marked. The back is engraved with a landscape of Songak Mountain and a dated inscription stating that it was made by the nun Seonhwaja in 1652. It was designed as a portable instrument for identifying constellations, and its reverse also has artistic value as an engraved image.

1123713740000.title_en: Triad Assembly Hanging Scroll of Yongheungsa Temple
1123713740000.description: This large hanging painting, over 10 meters long, presents three separate Buddha images: Śākyamuni in the center, Bhaiṣajyaguru to the left, and Amitābha to the right. The composition is arranged in three horizontal tiers with attendant bodhisattvas, heavenly kings, disciples, nāga figures, and transformed Buddhas, and shows a highly symmetrical layout typical of the late 17th century. It was made in 1684 and is well preserved.

1123213750000.title_en: Relic Assemblage from the Octagonal Nine-Story Stone Pagoda of Woljeongsa Temple
1123213750000.description: This assemblage was discovered when the leaning octagonal nine-story stone pagoda at Woljeongsa Temple was dismantled and restored in 1970. It consists of 12 objects in 9 types, including a gilt-bronze seated Buddha, silver inner and outer reliquaries, a crystal reliquary bottle, a gilt-bronze square incense container, a bronze mirror, a reliquary scroll, and silk wrapping cloths. The objects are thought to date to the 10th to 11th centuries and were likely placed in the pagoda when it was built.

1123613760000.description: This Tibetan-language edict preserved at Songgwangsa Temple is said to have been brought back by National Preceptor Wongam, who received it from Kublai Khan while returning from Yuan China. The document is now divided into six fragments, but its paper, color, and handwriting indicate that it was originally a single sheet. Its contents can be divided into sections concerning the holder's identity and protection, the request for cooperation from guarantors, and the issuer's certification.

1123314170000.title_en: Stone Standing Hwigyeon Bodhisattva, Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123314170000.description: This unusual Buddhist sculpture shows a bodhisattva standing on a pedestal with a large incense burner balanced on its head. The lower base, body, and burner stand are carved from a single stone, and the figure is associated with offering incense to the Buddha.

1123314180000.title_en: Stele for Monk Hakjo, Bocheonam Hermitage, Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123314180000.description: This tower-shaped monument stands on a hill southeast of Bocheonam Hermitage at Beopjusa Temple. Inscriptions on the monument record the name of Monk Hakjo and state that it was erected in 1514, making it an important early Joseon-period source for dating and identifying the subject.

1123614190000.title_en: Seated Sakyamuni Buddha Hanging Scroll and Associated Relics, Seonamsa Temple
1123614190000.description: This hanging scroll is a single-Buddha composition centered on a standing image of Sakyamuni Buddha, with other buddhas and bodhisattvas placed symmetrically around it. The set also includes the hanging-scroll case and various inner reliquary objects such as a small brass reliquary tube, written prayer texts, and dharani sheets.

1121114200000.title_en: Celadon Ewer and Stand with Inlaid Peony and Willow Design
1121114200000.description: This set consists of a plump ewer and a neatly made stand that fit together harmoniously. The body is decorated with black and white inlay of blooming flowers and willow branches, and the vessel is covered with a soft bluish-green celadon glaze.

1121114210000.title_en: Celadon Ewer and Stand with Dappled Flower Design
1121114210000.description: This complete set includes a ewer, lid, and stand. The floral decoration was applied with the puddled-hua technique using white and brown clay slip, and the vessel is finished with a translucent grayish-blue glaze.

1121114220000.title_en: Buncheong Jar with Inlaid Peony Design
1121114220000.description: This buncheong jar has a strong, sturdy form combined with bold inlaid decoration. Large peonies are rendered in white inlay across the body with little empty space left, creating a lively and forceful overall effect.

1121114230000.title_en: Buncheong Bottle with Stamped Dot Design
1121114230000.description: This buncheong vessel has a horizontally laid cylindrical body with the mouth attached at the top center. Its surface is densely decorated with stamped inlaid dots over the entire body, producing a plain but distinctive appearance.

1121114250000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Iron-spot Plum and Bamboo Design
1121114250000.description: This jar is notable for its refined shape and brushlike decoration that recalls a literati painting. Plum blossoms and bamboo are painted in dark iron pigment, with additional decorative bands around the neck and shoulder, and the vessel is covered with a thin translucent glaze.
1121114250000.material: White porcelain with iron underglaze decoration

1123314090000.description: This is a Goryeo-period printed edition of the commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra, one of the key scriptures of Korean Hwaeom Buddhism. It consists of three volumes from a 120-volume woodblock edition and is considered an important source for studying Buddhism in Goryeo, as well as cultural exchanges with Song China and Japan.

1123714100000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Dragon Head of a Banner Pole
1123714100000.description: This gilt-bronze fitting was placed on top of a Buddhist banner pole and used as part of the device for hanging streamers on a temple banner. A dragon holds a wish-fulfilling jewel in its mouth, and a pulley mechanism for attaching a rope is fitted behind it.

1123714110000.description: This slate inscription has five lines and 74 characters, with the heading "Ipsin" at the beginning. Its text records an oath of loyalty and a promise to study the Confucian classics over three years, making it an important example of early Silla stone inscription and writing practice.

1121114120000.description: This is a gilt-script Buddhist manuscript copied on indigo-dyed paper in 1334, during the restored reign of King Chungsuk of Goryeo. The opening includes a vow text and an illustrated frontispiece, which state that Jeong Deok-man-dal-a commissioned the copying of the Avatamsaka Sutra and the Suramgama Sutra for prayer and dedication.
1121114120000.material: Ink and gold on indigo-dyed paper

1123314130000.title_en: Iron Cauldron of Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123314130000.description: This huge iron cauldron from Beopjusa Temple is said to have been used in temple life and is remarkable for its large size and nearly complete preservation. Although it is traditionally linked to the Silla period, it is thought more likely to date from the Joseon period; no inscription records its maker or exact date.

1123114140000.title_en: Bronze Incense Burner with Inscription from Bongeopsa Temple
1123114140000.description: This large incense burner, said to have been excavated from the site of Bongeopsa Temple in Anseong, has a body, lid, and three-legged stand. An inscription on the lid names it as connected with Bongeopsa Temple and Master Wonjun, and another inscription indicates that 26 geun of copper were used in its casting.

1121114150000.description: This compiled set of letters contains correspondence mainly exchanged among Song Ik-pil, Seong Hon, and Yi I, who were leading Neo-Confucian scholars of the 16th century. The letters are valuable for intellectual history and also preserve important examples of their handwriting, including many letters by Yi I that are otherwise rare.

1123314160000.title_en: Suum Hermitage Monk's Stupa, Beopjusa Temple, Boeun
1123314160000.description: This monk's stupa stands beside the stupa of Hakhjo in the area east of Beopjusa's Bokcheonam Hermitage. An inscription on the stupa body and base records the name "Suum Monk's Stupa" and the date equivalent to 1480, making it an important dated example of an early Joseon stupa that follows the octagonal Buddhist stupa tradition of the Goryeo period.

1123314010000.title_en: Chungju Bonghwang-ri Rock-cut Buddhist Statues Group
1123314010000.description: This group consists of nine Buddha and bodhisattva figures carved in relief on two large rock faces on a mountainside. One seated Buddha is carved on the upper rock face, and eight figures, including a seated Buddha, attendant figures, and half-seated bodhisattvas, are carved on the lower rock face. The group is thought to have been made in the late Three Kingdoms period or the early Unified Silla period and reflects the influence of Goguryeo Buddhist imagery.

1123714020000.description: This shrine within Sosu Seowon served as the memorial hall for ancestral rites, with An Hyang as the principal enshrined figure. The hall also enshrines the spirit tablets of An Chuk, An Bo, and Ju Sebung. It is a three-bay by three-bay gabled building on a low stone platform with a simple traditional timber structure.

1123714030000.description: This hall was used for lecturing and studying at Sosu Seowon. It is a four-bay by three-bay hipped-and-gabled building with double eaves, built on a high stone platform with a surrounding wooden veranda. A plaque inscribed by King Myeongjong reading "Sosu Seowon" hangs inside the main hall.

1121114040000.description: This scroll preserves poems exchanged between the Ming envoy Ni Qian and the Joseon scholars Seong Sammun, Sin Sukju, and Jeong Inji during Ni Qian's mission to Joseon in 1450. It also includes later colophons and many ownership seals, showing the transmission history of the work. The piece is an important record of early Joseon diplomacy and a valuable source for the study of early Joseon calligraphy.

1121114050000.description: This album was compiled in 1442 under Prince Anpyeong's direction from poems based on the Eight Views of Xiaoxiang and related paintings. It contains poems by figures including Kim Jongseo, Seong Sammun, Park Paengnyeon, Sin Sukju, and others, now mounted in album form. It is valued as a rare surviving collection of the calligraphic works of prominent Joseon literati and court scholars.

1123114060000.title_en: Ssamdae Hoe-do and Kim Jonghan Royal Documents
1123114060000.description: This set includes a Joseon-period association painting based on a gathering of 23 officials who had served in the Office of Inspector-General, led by Kim Jonghan. The lower section records the participants' names and ranks, as well as their fathers' offices and names. The five documents are royal appointment documents issued to Kim Jonghan, most of them dating to the reign of King Seongjong.
1123114060000.material: Ink and color on paper; paper

1123314070000.title_en: Brahmajala Sutra Bodhisattva Precepts and Rules for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts
1123314070000.description: This printed book consists of the upper volume of the Bodhisattva precepts section from the Brahmajala Sutra, together with the Chinese Buddhist texts "Rules for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts" and "Etiquette for Receiving the Bodhisattva Precepts." It sets out the ten major precepts, the ten wholesome precepts, and the conduct expected of bodhisattvas. The volume is thought to have been printed in Yuan China and brought to Korea after 1306.

1123314080000.description: This woodblock-printed book is based on Kumarajiva's translation of the Diamond Sutra and includes Huineng's commentary on the text. It was published at Wongeungsa Temple in Cheongju in 1305. As an early printed edition, it is an important source for the history of Korean printing culture.

1123114500000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Inlaid Square Tomb Marker and Buncheong Ware Stamped Square Flask
1123114500000.description: These two Buncheong ware pieces were made at the same time and have identical clay body, glaze condition, forming method, and foot support. The tomb marker is dated to 1448, and the stamped flask is considered an important reference for Buncheong ware research because it was produced together with an item bearing an exact date.

1121114510000.title_en: Celadon Ewer in the Shape of a Bottle with Inlaid Cloud, Crane, and Chrysanthemum Design
1121114510000.description: This Goryeo celadon ewer is representative of bottle-shaped ewers made in inlaid celadon. Its form, inlaid decoration, and glaze all show a high level of refinement, with the inlaid areas neat and evenly executed and the glaze clear and glossy.

1121114520000.title_en: Celadon Maebyeong with Inlaid Lotus, Willow, and Inscription 'Deokcheon'
1121114520000.description: This celadon maebyeong bears the inscription 'Deokcheon' and is notable for its relatively well-preserved form, design, and glaze. It is considered an important example for understanding the transition from Goryeo inlaid celadon to Buncheong ware of the 15th century.

1121114530000.description: This celadon ewer was made in imitation of the form of a bronze ewer from the Goryeo period. It shows the early characteristics of Goryeo celadon in its glaze, clay body, and foot support technique, and is regarded as a particularly well-made example.

1121114540000.title_en: Celadon Octagonal Long-Necked Vase with Incised Lotus Design
1121114540000.description: This octagonal long-necked vase was made by faceting the body and neck into eight planes. The vase is decorated with incised lotus sprays on the body and an embossed lotus-petal band around the foot, and is praised for its slender neck and balanced form.

1121114550000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Inlaid Vase with Wave and Fish Design
1121114550000.description: This early Joseon Buncheong vase has a typical shape and is decorated with bold inlaid designs over the entire surface. The neck has an inlaid bead pattern, the shoulders have stamped chrysanthemum bands, and the body shows large fish swimming over waves in white inlay.

1121114560000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Sgraffito Flat Vase with Taeguk Design
1121114560000.description: This flattened flask has a rounded body compressed to create a stable form. The body is divided into four panels and decorated with sgraffito and carved designs, including a large taeguk motif at the center and peony motifs around it.
