1121114570000.title_en: White Porcelain Square Bowl-Shaped Ritual Vessel
1121114570000.description: This white porcelain ritual vessel is made in a square-bowl form by pressing a broad, deep bowl into four sides. Its surface shows tool-like carving that resembles woodwork, and the feet are attached at four corners with sand used in firing.

1121114580000.title_en: Octagonal Water Dropper with Butterfly Design and the Character “Si,” Blue and Iron-brown Underglaze White Porcelain
1121114580000.description: This octagonal water dropper has a flat top, eight small feet, and a spout attached to one side. A butterfly is painted on the top in cobalt blue and iron-brown glaze, and a seven-character regulated verse is written on the side with alternating blue and iron-brown underglaze decoration. It is finished with a clear, pale bluish glaze and reflects the taste of the scholarly class in the 18th century.

1123114590000.title_en: Miscellaneous Writings of Monk Mubam of the Haedong Jogye Lineage
1123114590000.description: This book is a collection of writings by Chongji (1226–1292), the sixth head monk of Suseonsa at Jogyesan in Goryeo. The extant edition is thought to be a 1447 printing from woodblocks, and it is the only surviving edition that contains only the miscellaneous writings from the monk’s collected works. It is an important source for Buddhist studies and bibliography.

1121114600000.title_en: Bronze Bell Inscribed for Heungcheonsa Temple
1121114600000.description: This bell shows the process by which Chinese bell features adopted in late Goryeo were combined with traditional Korean bell elements and established as an early Joseon form. Made in 1462 as a royal offering, it is also valuable for understanding the production system of the period because the inscription records the organization involved in its casting.

1122114610000.title_en: Jogye Gate of Beomeosa Temple, Busan
1122114610000.description: This temple gate at Beomeosa in Busan is a one-bay main gate with a gabled roof and daipo-style bracket sets above and between the columns. The wooden members are painted in dancheong, and the columns stand on high stone bases with short posts above them. It was repaired in 1781 and is also called Samhaetalmun.

1121114620000.title_en: Site Stele of the Former Villa of King Injo, Seoul
1121114620000.description: This stele was erected in 1695 to commemorate the villa where King Injo stayed before taking the throne through the coup of 1623. The inscription on the front was written by King Sukjong, and the text on the back records Sukjong’s composition written by Yi Hang. The stone base and roof stone show the characteristics of late Joseon stele style.

1122214630000.title_en: Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven, Vols. 8-10
1122214630000.description: This is a 1447 woodblock-printed edition of the first Korean text written in Hunminjeongeum, and it is regarded as a representative work of Joseon court verse literature. The surviving volumes contain volumes 8 to 10 of the original ten-volume set. The typeface, page layout, and printing details suggest it is an early first edition.

1121114630200.title_en: Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven, Vols. 3-4
1121114630200.description: This volume set belongs to the first printed edition of "Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven," a work that recounts the deeds of Joseon ancestors from Mokjo to Taejong and compares them with those of Chinese rulers. It was compiled in 1445 and published in 1447 with commentary added by court scholars. As one of the earliest books written in Hunminjeongeum, it is a valuable source for the history of the Korean language.

1121114630300.title_en: Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven, Vols. 1-2
1121114630300.description: This is a surviving copy of the original 1447 printed edition of "Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven," which records the founding history of the Joseon dynasty and related events. The work was compiled to show that Joseon was established by heaven’s mandate and is an important early book written in Hunminjeongeum. The copy is incomplete, but it remains a valuable source for Joseon-period language and bibliography.

1123114260000.description: This painting is considered a 14th-century Goryeo Buddhist painting, although its exact date and artist are unknown and it shows some signs of damage, repair, and overpainting. Its composition and figure types closely resemble other Water-Moon Avalokiteshvara paintings from the 14th century, and it is valued as a rare and important example of Goryeo Buddhist painting.

1123714270000.title_en: Stone Figures and Stone Pillars at the Royal Tomb of King Wonseong, Gyeongju
1123714270000.description: This set consists of 10 stone pieces placed in pairs at the left and right entrances of the Royal Tomb of King Wonseong in Gyeongju: four civil and military official figures, four lion figures, and two stone pillars. The military figures are notable for showing a Westerner or Western-style appearance, and the whole group is important for the study of Unified Silla sculpture.

1121114280000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Mortuary Jar Inscribed 'Jeongtong 13th Year' and Associated Buncheong Ware
1121114280000.description: This set includes one buncheong ware mortuary jar inscribed with a date corresponding to 1448, the 30th year of King Sejong's reign, and six associated buncheong ware vessels. The mortuary jar carries biographical information about the deceased and family members, making it an important source for understanding early Joseon society and the history of ceramics.

1123714290000.title_en: East and West Three-Story Stone Pagodas at Wongwonsa Temple Site, Gyeongju
1123714290000.description: These twin three-story stone pagodas stand at the site of Wongwonsa Temple in Gyeongju and were restored in 1931 after having collapsed. They are thought to have been made in the mid-8th century, and they are important for their structure, sculptural details, and the early use of twelve zodiac figures on the lower base.

1121114300000.description: This eight-panel folding screen depicts the main events of King Jeongjo's royal visit to Hwaseong in 1795 to celebrate the 60th birthday of Queen Dowager Hyegyeong. It was painted by leading court artists such as Kim Deuk-sin and Yi In-mun, and it is regarded as a major historical record painting of the 18th century.

1121114300200.description: This single panel is one of the eight paintings that make up the Hwaseong Haenghaengdo Folding Screen and depicts the banquet held at Bongsudang for Queen Dowager Hyegyeong's 60th birthday. It is a court event painting from the late 18th to early 19th century and is noted for its composition, coloring, and use of perspective.

1121114310000.title_en: Collection of Gyehoedo Paintings Featuring Jeong Sa-sin
1121114310000.description: This set of six paintings shows literary gatherings that the civil official Jeong Sa-sin attended as a government officer between 1583 and 1587. The works are important because their production dates and participants are known, and they reflect painting styles of the 1580s.

1123714320000.title_en: Jeokcheonsa Hanging Buddha Painting and Supporting Posts
1123714320000.description: This hanging Buddha painting depicts a standing bodhisattva holding a lotus branch, with no other figures or background, and its inscription indicates it was made in 1695. The two stone supporting posts used for hanging the banner were made in 1701, and together they provide valuable evidence for the appearance of hanging banners and their supports in the late 17th century.

1121114630400.description: These two volumes of the first printed edition of Yongbieocheonga are preserved at the Korea University Library (Mansong Collection). They are the 1447 edition and are the same edition as other designated volumes, with some damage to the first volume’s front matter and parts of volume 2. Yongbieocheonga is the earliest extant Korean-language text published after the invention of Hangul.

1122214640000.description: This is the official roster of successful candidates from the civil service examinations held in 1501, the seventh year of King Yeonsan-gun. It records the names of the seonsaeng and jinsa examiners and the examination leaders, and some names were later inked out because those men became criminals. It was printed by the Ministry of Rites in an early movable-type edition.

1122414650200.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the collected works of Yi Sung-in, a scholar of the late Goryeo period, preserves prefaces and postscripts more completely than other surviving editions. It was originally compiled by Byeon Gye-ryang under royal order and first printed in movable type in 1406; this designated copy is a later woodblock reprint. The text is valuable for supplementing the official histories and for providing source material on the history of the Tripitaka and related Buddhist printing.

1122214660000.description: This is the first woodblock edition of the collected works of Seong Gan, a Joseon scholar who served as Left Corrector. It was compiled after his death by his elder brother Seong Im and his younger brother Seong Hyeon, then published in 1467. The volume includes poetry, prose, a preface by Seo Geo-jeong, and a postscript by Lee Seung-so, and it is an important source for early Joseon literature and bibliography.

1123614670000.title_en: Wooden Seated Four Heavenly Kings, Songgwangsa Temple, Suncheon
1123614670000.description: These four clay images of the Four Heavenly Kings stand at the left and right sides of the Cheonwangmun gate at Songgwangsa Temple in Suncheon. They are seated in armor with fierce expressions, and an inscription indicates that they were remade in 1628, likely replacing statues damaged during the Japanese invasions.

1123614680000.title_en: Reliquary Objects from the Wooden Seated Four Heavenly Kings, Songgwangsa Temple, Suncheon
1123614680000.description: These reliquary objects were recovered during dismantling and repair of the wooden seated Four Heavenly Kings at Songgwangsa Temple. The group includes 12 kinds of Buddhist texts in 14 volumes, 428 paper dharani sheets, and four huryeongtong containers. The finds are important for studying Goryeo Buddhist canons and the history of Buddhist printing.

1123614690000.title_en: Grant Certificate for the Merit Subject Ma Cheon-mok
1123614690000.description: This handwritten royal merit certificate was issued in 1401 by the Office for Meritorious Subjects to Ma Cheon-mok, who was rewarded for his role in suppressing the Second Strife of Princes. It is the only surviving example among the certificates issued to the 47 Loyal Meritorious Subjects. The document is valuable for studying the form of early Joseon merit certificates and the organization of the Office for Meritorious Subjects.

1123614700000.title_en: Buddhist Texts from the Relic Deposits of the Seated Sakyamuni Triad and the Sixteen Arhats, Bulgapsa Temple, Yeonggwang
1123614700000.description: These relic deposit texts were found in the Eight Scenes Hall at Bulgapsa Temple in Yeonggwang. They include a few Goryeo-period editions but are mostly early Joseon printings, such as widely circulated Mahayana sutras, texts for Seonjong doctrine, and materials related to water-and-land rites, along with 17 votive inscriptions and Buddhist texts imported from Ming China. They are important sources for studying early Joseon Buddhist belief and the history of Korean Buddhism.

1123814710000.title_en: Three-Story Stone Pagoda of Tongdosa Temple, Yangsan
1123814710000.description: This is a typical Unified Silla stone pagoda built on a two-tiered base with three stories of the main body. It is dated to the late 9th century based on its style, including the recessed reliefs on the lower base and the lively upward turn of the roof stones.

1123814720000.title_en: Amitabha Buddha Preaching Painting of Tongdosa Temple
1123814720000.description: This Buddhist hanging painting shows Amitabha Buddha seated on a jeweled altar in the center, with Avalokitesvara, Mahasthamaprapta, the Eight Great Bodhisattvas, the Four Heavenly Kings, the Ten Disciples, and dragon figures arranged around him. According to the inscription, it was painted by the monk-painter Imhan in 1740. The work is valued as an early painting of Imhan's style, with fine brushwork and a stable composition.

1123714730000.title_en: Old Documents of the Oksan Lineage of the Yeoju Yi Clan
1123714730000.description: This collection preserves documents of the Yeoju Yi clan's Oksan lineage, including materials related to Hwejae Yi Eon-jeok and other generations of the family. The designated group consists of 98 documents from before the reign of King Seonjo, such as royal edicts, warrants, appointment documents, petitions, inheritance records, slave-sale documents, land documents, and letters. They are important sources for studying Joseon-period social and economic history, especially status and slavery.

1123714740100.title_en: Old Documents and Hyangan of the Yangwol Lineage of the Gyeongju Yi Clan
1123714740100.description: This designation includes old documents from the Yangwol lineage and 17 volumes of Gyeongju hyangan, or local register books. The documents include early Joseon appointment records such as josa-cheop and related administrative papers, while the hyangan series, concentrated between 1592 and 1692, preserves materials on local governance, village organizations, and hyangyak. Together they are valuable sources for studying Joseon local society and administration.

1121114740200.title_en: Royal Edict to Yi Jidae from the Old Documents and Hyangan of the Yangwol Lineage of the Gyeongju Yi Clan
1121114740200.description: This royal edict, issued in 1413, is the earliest-dated item among the Yangwol lineage documents. It was granted to Yi Jidae, the founder of the Gyeongju Yi clan's Panyun-gong branch, and is considered highly valuable because related material about him has not been known until now.

1123714750000.title_en: Group of Gilt-bronze Plaque Buddha Images Excavated from Anapji Pond
1123714750000.description: This group consists of 10 plaque Buddha images, including a triad, excavated from Anapji Pond. They show excellent craftsmanship and a strong sense of volume, and stylistically reflect the international Buddhist sculptural trends of the late 7th century in Unified Silla, Tang China, and Japan. The set is thought to have been attached to two small wooden reliquary structures.

1123814760000.title_en: Meritorious Subject Edict for Kim Simin
1123814760000.description: This royal edict was granted to Kim Simin, the magistrate of Jinju, who led the victory at the Battle of Jinju, one of the three great victories of the Imjin War. Issued in 1604 to reward military merit during the war, it records the names of 18 meritorious subjects and details Kim's achievements and rewards. It is regarded as the best-preserved surviving edict of its kind.

1123114770100.title_en: Portrait of Chae Je-gong, Wearing Everyday Court Dress
1123114770100.description: This is a portrait of Chae Je-gong, a key late Joseon official who consistently upheld his political faction’s position on matters such as the restoration of Crown Prince Sado while supporting King Jeongjo’s policy of impartial governance. The 1792 portrait shows him at age 73 seated in full length wearing a pale pink official robe, and it is accompanied by three preparatory sketches, a scented pouch, and a case. A self-written inscription by Chae Je-gong appears on the upper right of the painting.

1122514770200.title_en: Portrait of Chae Je-gong, Wearing Gold Crown and Court Dress
1122514770200.description: This portrait depicts Chae Je-gong at age 65 in formal court dress with a gold crown, and his self-written inscription was added by Yi Jeong-un on the left side. The face is rendered realistically with shading influenced by Western painting techniques, while the ornate costume is expressed with gold leaf, vivid colors, and strong contrasts. The work is attributed to Yi Myeong-gi based on its style.

1123414770300.title_en: Portrait of Chae Je-gong, Wearing Black Danryeong Robe
1123414770300.description: This portrait shows Chae Je-gong seated in full length wearing a black danryeong robe with a double-crane rank badge and an official hat. It was originally enshrined at Dangyeong Hall in Buyeo. The modeling of the face, clothing folds, and floor mat reflects the portrait style associated with Yi Myeong-gi.

1121114780000.title_en: Portrait of the Three Brothers of the Jo Family
1121114780000.description: This work depicts the three brothers Jo Gye, Jo Du, and Jo Gang in a single composition. It shows them as half-length portraits arranged in a triangular format, with the eldest brother at the center, which is unusual in Joseon portrait painting where a single person is usually shown on one canvas. All three wear black hats and pale crimson official robes.

1121114790000.title_en: Portrait of Yu Suk and Related Royal Documents
1121114790000.description: This set includes a portrait of Yu Suk, four preparatory sketches, and three related royal documents, including a decree issued to his wife Chae, which attest that he was a meritorious subject. The portrait shows him seated in full length wearing an official hat and black robe, with a white crane rank badge and a gold belt. The work is believed to have been made in connection with his registration as a meritorious subject in 1613.

1123114800000.description: This portrait shows Sim Hwan-ji seated in full length with both hands hidden inside his sleeves. The inscription at the top identifies him as Chief State Councillor, suggesting that the work was made after 1800, when he held that office. The painting is notable for its realistic facial rendering, strong use of shading, and detailed treatment of the robe and furnishings.

1123114810000.description: This portrait depicts Kim Yu in the standard early-18th-century format of a full-length seated official portrait wearing a round-collared robe. An inscription at the upper right states that it was painted when he was 64 in 1716. The tiger skin draped over the chair, the treatment of the chair handles, and other details reflect the typical style of early Joseon portraiture of the period.

1121114820000.description: This portrait shows Yi Si-bang, a son of Yi Gwi and younger brother of Yi Si-baek, who took part in the 1623 coup that restored King Injo. Among the six portraits preserved by his descendants, the full-length portrait in official dress is regarded as the original meritorious-subject portrait made when he was 30. The monumentality and style are typical of early 17th-century meritorious portraits.

1121114420000.title_en: Sun, Moon, and Peach Tree Folding Screen
1121114420000.description: This pair of large four-panel folding screens is a court decorative painting showing the sun, moon, mountains, water, rocks, and peach trees. The red sun and white moon, along with the symmetrical composition and rich colors, express auspicious meaning similar to that of Ilwol obongdo screens.

1121114430000.title_en: Folding Screen of the Ceremonial Tribute for the Birth of the Crown Prince
1121114430000.description: This court documentary painting records the congratulatory ceremony held at Injeongjeon Hall of Changdeokgung Palace on February 14, 1874, to celebrate the birth of Crown Prince Sunjong. The 10-panel screen depicts the ceremony scene in detail, with officials' names written on the outer panels.

1121114440000.title_en: Iron War Club with Silver Inlay and Demon Face Design
1121114440000.description: This pair of iron war clubs was made for ceremonial use in the 19th century and decorated with silver inlay. The surface is chased and inlaid with thunder patterns, lotus-petal motifs, and demon-face designs symbolizing the repelling of evil and disaster.

1123714450000.title_en: Yecheon Yongmunsa Temple Gwaebultaeng (Votive Buddhist Hanging Scroll of the Vulture Peak Assembly)
1123714450000.description: This 1705 hanging scroll shows a standing triad Buddha composition with Kasyapa and Ananda placed to the left and right of the principal Buddha. It includes a prayer for the royal family's well-being and is notable for its transitional style between the 17th and 18th centuries and for the unusual iconography of the Buddha holding a lotus branch.
1123714450000.material: Ink and color on hemp cloth

1123814460000.title_en: Namhae Yongmunsa Temple Gwaebultaeng (Votive Buddhist Hanging Scroll)
1123814460000.description: This 1769 hanging scroll presents a triad composition with the principal standing Buddha in the center and two attendant bodhisattvas on either side. Its figures and proportions reflect the standard style of Buddhist painting from the mid- to late 18th century, and the lower part of the painting retains an inscription and record of its production.
1123814460000.material: Ink and color on hemp cloth

1121114470000.title_en: Celadon Plaque with Inlaid Floral and Bird Design
1121114470000.description: This small celadon plaque is notable for its highly pictorial inlaid design, one of the few known examples that can be fully reconstructed. Black and white inlay combined with iron painting creates strong color contrast and an effective use of tone and empty space.

1121114480000.title_en: White Porcelain Jar with Underglaze Cobalt Blue and Peony Scroll Design
1121114480000.description: This white porcelain jar has the form characteristic of early Joseon ceramics, with a narrow mouth, broad shoulders, and a body that narrows toward the base before widening slightly at the foot. The lively peony scroll design painted over the body is also typical of early Joseon blue-and-white porcelain.
1121114480000.material: White porcelain with underglaze cobalt blue

1123114490000.description: This celadon water dropper is modeled in the form of a crouching one-horned giraffe, with the water spout made on its back and water issuing through its mouth. It is a fine 12th-century celadon figurine known for its refined carving and stable glaze.

1123614330000.title_en: Five-story Stone Pagoda of Dogapsa Temple, Yeongam
1123614330000.description: This five-story stone pagoda at Dogapsa Temple was originally composed of a single-tier base, a five-story body, and a finial stone, but the lower base was discovered during excavation after 1995 and the pagoda was restored in 2002 as a five-story stone pagoda with a two-tier base. It is thought to date to the early Goryeo period and is notable for its well-preserved parts and balanced proportions.

1123514340000.title_en: Diamond Ordination Platform of Ansimsa Temple, Wanju
1123514340000.description: This stone Buddhist reliquary platform enshrines a tooth relic and robe relic said to have been made after the mid-17th century and before 1759. It consists of a central reliquary stupa, four guardian figures, and a broad stone base, and its lotus and lattice carvings and the detailed treatment of the guardian figures are highly accomplished.

1123114350000.description: This portrait was made to commemorate Yi Won-ik’s appointment as a second-rank meritorious retainer in 1604, and is thought to have been painted a few years later than that event. It depicts him seated in full official dress, with an Osa-mo hat, black danryeong robe, and hands folded in a formal pose.

1123814360000.title_en: Standing Stone Seated Buddha in Nongsan-ri, Geochang
1123814360000.description: This stone standing Buddha follows the typical style of Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture and is made of two stones: a base stone with carved feet and a separate body stone with the halo attached. Although the face is partly damaged, the figure shows the Udyana-style drapery and a refined, relatively large-scale carving.

1121114370000.description: This moon jar has a rounded, spherical body with a stable overall proportion between the mouth and foot. The glaze is thin but well fused to the body, and the rim has been partly repaired; the condition is otherwise very good.

1121114380000.description: This moon jar is large and well proportioned, with a balanced relationship between height, body diameter, mouth, and foot diameter. It has little distortion, a hard glaze with no cracks, and a fine finish on the mouth, foot, and body surface.

1121114390000.description: This large moon jar has a smooth rounded body and relatively small mouth and foot, giving it a calm and orderly appearance. The symmetry is good, the glaze is transparent, and the condition of preservation is excellent.

1123114410000.description: This moon jar has a stable overall proportion, with a body size appropriate to its height and a good ratio between the mouth and foot. The body appears somewhat more angular than rounded, but the symmetry is good and the glaze is glossy and relatively thick.

1121114830000.description: This portrait depicts the late Joseon Neo-Confucian scholar-official Lee Chae (1745–1820) seated in a half-length frontal pose wearing a simui robe and jeongjagwan hat with his hands folded in front. The upper part of the painting includes elegant inscriptions by noted calligraphers of the time. It is regarded as one of the finest late Joseon portraits in informal attire.

1121114840000.description: This portrait shows Nam Gu-man (1629–1711), a Joseon official who later became a leading Soron figure, seated in official robes on a chair. An inscription and a long praise text by Choe Chang-dae indicate that the work was likely made in 1711. The face is rendered frontally with restrained linework and shading, making it an important example of new portrait types and techniques in the early 18th century.

1121114850000.description: This portrait depicts Gang I-o (1788–?), grandson of Gang Se-hwang, as a frontal half-length figure wearing an osa-mo hat and pink civilian robe. The painting includes a title inscription and a praise poem by Kim Jeong-hui, and the artist is identified as Yi Jae-gwan. It is a strong example of early 19th-century portraiture that reflects some Western techniques while maintaining earlier traditions.

1121114860000.description: This portrait of the calligrapher Yi Gwang-sa (1705–1777) records that it was painted in 1775 when he was seventy years old. The inscription identifies Shin Han-pyeong as the painter. It is valued as a rare and refined portrait that successfully conveys both likeness and character.

1121114870000.description: This portrait of Seo Jik-su (1735–?) was made in 1796 when he was sixty-two. The inscription shows that Yi Myeong-gi painted the face and Kim Hong-do painted the body. Unusually for a Joseon portrait, it is a full-length standing figure, and it is regarded as a masterpiece of late Joseon portraiture.

1122414880000.description: This portrait of Sim Deok-gyeong (1673–1710) was completed in 1710 by Yun Du-seo after the sitter’s death. The inscriptions record praise texts by Yi Seo and Yun Du-seo’s posthumous painting. The work combines lifelike portrait features with more generalized figure-painting elements and is an important example of Yun Du-seo’s portrait work.

1123114890000.description: This portrait of Park Yu-myeong (1582–1640) is believed to date to around 1623, when he was rewarded for his role in the Injo Restoration. It shows the characteristic form of 17th-century meritorious subject portraits, with exaggerated rounded shoulders, an official robe, and a tiger rank badge as a military official portrait. A later copy also survives, but only the original is designated.

1121114900000.description: This portrait is thought to be a meritorious subject portrait awarded to Yi Seong-yun (1570–1620) in 1613, when he was recorded as a Wiseong meritorious retainer under Gwanghaegun. It depicts him in official robes seated on a chair with folded hands, in a typical early 17th-century meritorious subject format. The painting is noted for its rich use of gold and silver and its careful, detailed execution.

1121114910000.description: This portrait was made before Yi Geum became king, as shown by the inscription in the upper left stating that it is a portrait from the time when he was first invested as Prince Yeoning. It depicts a full-length seated figure in formal court dress, wearing a saemao hat, a green robe with a white rank badge, a belt, and black shoes. Although about one-third of the painting is missing from fire damage, the face, chest badge, belt, and feet remain intact and make it an important source for studying early Joseon portrait technique.

1121114920000.description: This royal portrait is identified by the inscription in the surviving upper left corner and was made in 1861, the 12th year of King Cheoljong’s reign. The painted version that survives today is the military-uniform portrait, and it is the only known royal portrait showing a king dressed in full military uniform. The work is also important for its vivid coloring, refined shading, and detailed rendering of costume patterns.

1121114930000.description: This portrait is believed to depict O Jae-sun at the age of 65, based on the label attached to the back of the hanging scroll. It shows the sitter in formal scholar-official attire, and the painter carefully rendered the face, drapery, and patterned robes with strong shading and repeated brushwork. The work is regarded as a fine example of late Joseon portrait painting and of the adoption of Western-style techniques within Joseon portraiture.

1123614940000.title_en: Portrait and Photograph of Hwang Hyeon
1123614940000.description: This is a portrait of the late Joseon scholar and patriot Hwang Hyeon, painted by Seokji Chae Yong-sin in 1911 after a photograph taken in 1909. The portrait shows him seated on a woven mat, wearing a jeongjagwan hat, a dark robe, and a cloth belt, while holding a fan and a book. Although based on a photograph, the painting adjusts some details and is noted for its highly realistic depiction and for showing new characteristics of portrait painting around the end of the Korean Empire and the beginning of the modern period.

1123414950000.title_en: Set of Portraits of Yun Jeung and Yeongdanggijeok
1123414950000.description: This designation includes several portraits of Yun Jeung made in 1744, 1788, and 1885, along with the manuscript Yeongdanggijeok recording their production and transmission. The portraits preserve both older and newer portrait styles, and the records describe when the works were copied, how many versions were produced, and how the old and new portraits were enshrined. Together they are important for understanding late Joseon portraiture, copying practices, and the tradition of preserving portrait records.

1121114960000.description: This full-length portrait shows Yun Geup seated half-turned to the right on a tiger-skin-covered chair, wearing a saemao hat, a black official robe, a rank badge with two cranes, and a belt with a white jade ornament. Based on his office and rank insignia, it is thought to have been painted around 1762, when he was about 66 years old. The portrait is important for its careful depiction of facial blemishes and its well-preserved late-18th-century hanging scroll mounting.

1123414970000.description: This portrait shows Kim Si-seup in a half-length seated pose, turned slightly to the left, wearing a straw hat and a light crimson robe with his hands folded. The face and clothing are rendered in restrained tones, and the expression matches literary descriptions of Kim as a thoughtful and troubled figure. It is valued both as a portrait of Kim Si-seup and as an excellent example of Joseon literati portrait painting.

1122114980000.title_en: Portrait of a Late Joseon Literatus
1122114980000.description: This painting depicts an unidentified literatus seated on a tiger skin over a mat, wearing a pink ceremonial robe and shown in a slightly left-turned seated pose. The drapery is modeled with subtle shading, and the figure wears a belt with a gilt central section. It is a fine work that reflects the stylistic features of late-18th-century portrait painting and preserves its original mounting condition well.

1121114990100.title_en: Portraits of Yi Ha-eung (Daewongun) - Black danryeong robe, Court robe with gold crown, Waryonggwan hat and crane-patterned official robe, Black hat and blue robe, and Bokgeon cap and simui robe
1121114990100.description: This set consists of five portraits of Yi Ha-eung, each showing him in a different costume. All five were painted by the late Joseon court painter Lee Han-cheol; the first three were based on a portrait sketch made in 1863 and reworked in 1869, and the last two are portraits made in 1880 when he turned sixty-one. The set also preserves portrait boxes, tassels, scent pouches, inscriptions, and related fittings that document late Joseon royal portrait culture.

1121114990200.title_en: Portrait of Yi Ha-eung - Court robe with gold crown
1121114990200.description: This portrait of Yi Ha-eung in a court robe with a gold crown is closely comparable in size, composition, materials, technique, and style to the gold-crown court-robed portrait in the Seoul Museum of History attributed to Lee Han-cheol and Yu Suk. It is thought to be either a duplicate or another version made by the same artists around the same time.

1121115000000.description: Kim I-an (1722–1791) was a late Joseon scholar-official, and portraits of him survive at Yonsei University Museum and Ewha Womans University Museum. The portrait at Yonsei University Museum is a fine work with a carefully rendered, somewhat idealized face, while the Ewha example is a rare full-length standing portrait. Only the Yonsei University Museum example was designated as a Treasure.

1122115010000.title_en: Portrait of Yi Deok-seong and Related Materials
1122115010000.description: This set includes one portrait of Yi Deok-seong, along with five printed books and 121 documents. The portrait shows him seated on a chair in official robes, with a restrained yet detailed style characteristic of the early eighteenth century. The related documents include appointment materials such as royal edicts, appointment certificates, and examination papers, preserving important biographical and administrative records.

1122215020000.description: This is a portrait of Yun Hyo-jeon (1563–1619), a civil official who passed the civil service examination in 1605 and was later stripped of his post after the Injo Restoration. The figure is shown in a typical early seventeenth-century meritorious-subject portrait format, seated on a chair with formal robes and an official hat. It is thought to have been painted to commemorate his posthumous restoration and promotion.

1121115030000.description: This portrait of Im Jang (1568–1619) shows the typical format of an early seventeenth-century meritorious-subject portrait. He is seated on a chair in official robes with his hands clasped, and the treatment of the face, beard, and robe lines suggests a portrait made from direct observation. Based on the historical records and its iconography, it is believed to be a meritorious-subject portrait made when he was appointed to that rank.

1121115040000.description: This portrait depicts the Joseon scholar-official Yu Eon-ho (1730–1796) at the age of 58. It was painted by court painter Yi Myeong-gi in 1787, as recorded in the inscription on the left side of the painting, and includes a royal appraisal at the top. The figure is shown standing in formal official robes, with careful shading and a strong sense of volume in the face and folds of the clothing.

1122215050000.title_en: Portrait of Samyeongdang Yujeong at Donghwa-sa Temple, Daegu
1122215050000.description: This portrait shows the monk-warrior Samyeongdang Yujeong seated on an elevated chair, facing slightly to the right and holding a fly whisk. The face is rendered in a clean outline style, while the robes and sash are painted in refined gray-white and bright red tones. Based on the inscription, it was made no later than 1796.

1123115150000.title_en: The Śūraṅgama Sūtra, Volume 2 and Volume 10
1123115150000.description: This is a Joseon-period woodblock-printed edition of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, also known as the Surangama Sutra, preserved here in Volume 2 and Volume 10. It was printed at the Gangyeongdogam in 1462, and the text has important value for the study of early Korean language, Chinese characters with Korean readings, and Hangul notation.

1123515160000.title_en: Clay Seated Vairocana Buddha Triad of Guisinsa Temple, Gimje
1123515160000.description: This large clay triad consists of Vairocana Buddha in the center, with the Medicine Buddha on the right and Amitabha Buddha on the left. It is believed to have been made between 1624 and 1633, and shows the influence of Ming-dynasty Buddhist sculpture in its hand gesture, proportions, and style.

1123515170000.title_en: Dry-lacquer Seated Amitabha Buddha with Relics from Seon'guksa Temple, Namwon
1123515170000.description: This seated Amitabha Buddha was made using dry-lacquer technique, a form that was popular from the late Goryeo to early Joseon period. Reliquary contents were discovered inside the statue, and the surviving materials are considered important for the study of Buddhist thought, printing, and bibliography.

1123115180000.title_en: The Great Expansive Perfect Enlightenment Sutra, Volume 1
1123115180000.description: This is a rare woodblock-printed edition of the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra, with a colophon by Yi Saek and a publication note dated the gengshen fourth month. It was printed in 1380 during the reign of King U of Goryeo and is regarded as one of the earliest surviving editions of this text.

1122615180200.title_en: The Great Expansive Perfect Enlightenment Sutra
1122615180200.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra was separately prepared and published in the fourth month of 1380 during the reign of King U of Goryeo. It is the same edition as the registered Volume 1 item and is valued as an early surviving Goryeo printing.

1123115190000.title_en: The Lotus Sutra Samādhi Repentance Ritual, Volume Upper
1123115190000.description: This work was written by the Tiantai monk Sangeung and describes a practice for realizing the principles of suchness and the Middle Way through recitation of the Lotus Sutra. It is believed to have been printed in the late Goryeo period based on its format, line count, and folding style.

1123115200000.description: This is Volume 1 of the Joseon edition of the Śūraṅgama Sūtra printed in 1461 with the Eulhae type, including large, medium, and small metal type and Hangul type. It was produced under royal order for a Korean translation and later served as the model for the 1462 woodblock edition.

1123115210000.description: This is Volume 3 of the Joseon legal code Gyeongguk Daejeon, printed with the first-cast Gapsin type. It is the earliest extant copy of the work and is important for the study of Joseon legal history and bibliography.

1123615060000.title_en: Portrait of Doseon, Seongak Guksa, Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123615060000.description: This portrait depicts Doseon (827–898), a late Silla Seon monk who rebuilt Seonamsa Temple as one of the three "Samam-sa" temples in the southern region. He is shown seated with both feet on a pedestal, holding a staff in his right hand, with the folds of his robes rendered in green and red with distinctive line work. According to the inscription, it was restored in 1805 by the monk Doil together with the portrait of Daegak Guksa at Seonamsa Temple.

1122415070000.title_en: Wooden Seated Amitabha Buddha and Reliquary Objects from Jaunsa Temple, Gwangju
1122415070000.description: This wooden seated Amitabha Buddha image was made before 1388, as a record found among the reliquary objects states that it was repaired and gilt again in that year. The carving is described as natural in technique, graceful in posture, and balanced in proportion, showing a well-rounded form. The reliquary objects include printed books, textiles, and metal and other artifacts from the Goryeo to Joseon periods.

1122315080000.title_en: Letter of Investiture for Yi Seong-yun as Wiseong Meritorious Subject and Related Objects
1122315080000.description: This royal document was issued in 1613 to Yi Seong-yun for merit in escorting King Gwanghaegun during the Japanese invasions of Korea. It preserves the full form of a meritorious-subject investiture letter from Gwanghaegun's reign, and the names of the producer and scribe are written on the back. The related objects include a 1669 certificate of posthumous title, 16 hopae identity tags from the same family, and one ivory court tablet.

1123215090000.description: This is a portrait of the mid-Joseon scholar-official Heo Mok (1595–1682), shown in a half-length seated pose wearing a black scholar's hat, a pale reddish court robe, and a rhinoceros-horn belt. The inscription says that in 1794 King Jeongjo, impressed by Heo Mok's character, had Yi Myeong-gi copy the portrait from an 82-year-old likeness at Eungeodang. The portrait is valued as an example of Joseon literati portraiture and for preserving the style of Yi Myeong-gi.

1123915100000.description: This portrait depicts Choe Ik-hyeon (1833–1906), a leading patriotic activist of the late Joseon period, and is dated to 1905 by the inscriptions on the painting. He is shown wearing a simui robe and a fur hat, which reflect both his Confucian learning and his role as a righteous army leader. The work is one of the early portraits by Chae Yong-shin and preserves the careful, modest style of his early manner.

1123115110000.description: This book records military campaigns conducted from King Sejong's reign to King Jungjong's reign, including expeditions against Tsushima, the Pajok River, Jianzhou Guard, Imajcha, the northwestern Jurchen raiders, and the Sampo Waeran. The text is arranged in chronological, annalistic form, and its wording follows a moral judgment style that calls Joseon actions "conquests" or "punitive campaigns" and enemy forces "bandits" or "rebels." It is known as a rare sole surviving copy and is an important source for early Joseon military history and bibliography.

1123115120000.title_en: Record of the Twenty Meritorious Subjects Ceremony - After the Registration of the Ningguk Meritorious Subjects
1123115120000.description: This hanging scroll records a court oath ceremony held in 1646, after the registration of the Ningguk Meritorious Subjects, bringing together the twenty meritorious subjects from the Founding Meritorious Subjects onward and their descendants. It includes the ceremonial oath text, the register of participants, and a memorial report, along with notes on those absent because of illness, official duty, or mourning. The work is a large, carefully written formal record made for preservation by the royal household or the Office of Meritorious Subjects.

1123115140000.title_en: The Great Buddhist Scripture of Perfect Enlightenment, Volume One, Part One
1123115140000.description: This is a Joseon-period metal type edition of the "Perfect Enlightenment Sutra," printed in 1465 using Eulyu type. The surviving volume in the Kyujanggak collection is incomplete and consists only of the preface and the first part of volume one, with the Korean gugyeol annotations and related passages extracted from the earlier translation text. It is an important source for the study of Joseon-era Korean language and bibliography.

1121115290000.title_en: Old Printing Woodblock Edition of the Samgabhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra, Volume 9
1121115290000.description: This is volume 9 of the early printed edition of the Tripitaka carved at the Daejangdogam in the 11th century. It is a key commentary of the Sarvāstivāda school, translated in the Liu Song period by Saṃghabhadra and others, and is an important source for the study of the Goryeo Tripitaka and Buddhist bibliography.

1121115300000.title_en: Old Printing Woodblock Edition of the Shouyong Sanshui Yaoxingfa
1121115300000.description: This is an 11th-century Goryeo woodblock edition of a work compiled by the Tang monk Yijing, part of the early Tripitaka carved at the Daejangdogam. It explains proper use of water for monks and laypeople, classifying water into three kinds and describing the rules for each.

1121115310000.title_en: Royal Procession Banquet and Conferral Banquet of King Yeongjo Folding Screen
1121115310000.description: This folding screen depicts two court events held in 1765: Yeongjo's visit to the Gyeso, his formal greeting at Yeongsu-gak and presentation of royal wine at Gyeongin-gwan, and the conferral banquet held at Gyeonghyeon-dang in Gyeonghuigung. The screen includes a prefatory text and roster, and it is notable for combining two rare ceremonial scenes in one work.

1123115320000.title_en: Yeoju Royal Tomb Jaesil of King Hyojong, Neungneung
1123115320000.description: This is the auxiliary ritual residence attached to the royal tomb of King Hyojong and Queen Inseon. Jaesil buildings were used for resting ritual officials, preparing offerings, and storing ritual vessels, and this example preserves the basic form and layout of Joseon royal tomb jaesil architecture especially well.

1121115330000.description: This late-17th-century map shows the national system of beacon-fire stations in Joseon. It depicts beacon sites, provincial towns, islands, mountain ranges, and river networks in detail, making the routes of the beacon system easy to follow.

1121115340000.description: This is a monochrome preliminary drawing of Gyeonghuigung, the western palace, showing its full layout. It appears to preserve the palace's pre-reconstruction appearance, and the detailed architectural labels and draft lines make it an important source for studying the old palace and the process of its depiction.

1123115350000.title_en: Map of So-ryeongwon of Lady Choi, Royal Consort Sukbin Choe
1123115350000.description: This set of four paintings shows So-ryeongwon, the burial site of Lady Choi, Royal Consort Sukbin and the mother of King Yeongjo. The set includes a grave-site plan, a burial-ground map with ritual buildings and fields, a firebreak map, and a layout of stone objects, and it is valuable as a visual record of a royal tomb complex.

1123115360000.description: This album of eight paintings shows places in Yeongwol associated with King Danjong's exile and the loyal ministers who remained faithful to him. It includes scenes of Jangneung, Cheongryeongpo, Gwanpungheon, Jagyuru, Changjeolsa, and other sites, and was likely made for court use in the first half of the 19th century.

1121115210200.description: This is a woodblock-printed copy of the first two volumes of the Gyeongguk Daejeon, the fundamental written code of the Joseon dynasty. It is the oldest extant copy of this section, printed with early metal type, and is an important source for the study of Joseon law and institutions.

1122115220000.title_en: Painting of the Assembly on Vulture Peak
1122115220000.description: This Buddhist painting was made in 1565 on a hemp cloth ground joined from seven horizontal strips. The central seated Buddha is identified in the inscription as Shakyamuni preaching at Vulture Peak, with bodhisattvas, the ten great disciples, and the Four Heavenly Kings arranged around him.
1122115220000.material: Ink and color on hemp cloth

1123715230000.title_en: Stone Water Basin of Bulguksa Temple, Gyeongju
1123715230000.description: This stone water basin was made in the Unified Silla period. Its rectangular form, rounded corners, carving on both the inner and outer surfaces, and elaborate lotus motifs on the bottom show the high artistic level of Buddhist art at the time.

1121115240000.title_en: Korean Inscribed Stele of Yi Yuntak, Seoul
1121115240000.description: This tomb stele was erected in 1536 by Yi Mungun for his father Yi Yuntak after the graves of Yi Yuntak and his wife from the Goryeong Sin clan were combined. The Korean warning inscription on the left side is regarded as the earliest tomb stele inscription written in Hangul.

1122115250000.description: This is volumes 1 and 2 of a seven-volume Buddhist text compiled by the Northern Qi monk Doji, focusing on stories about karmic retribution useful for Buddhist teaching. The manuscript preserves a detailed table of contents for the 22 sections, and its printing features suggest it was carved in the late Goryeo period and printed in the early Joseon period.

1122115260000.title_en: Wooden Seated Trinity of Shakyamuni Buddha, Bumeosa Temple, Busan
1122115260000.description: This triad was made in 1661 and installed as the principal image of the Daeungjeon Hall at Bumeosa Temple. The inscription found inside the statue records that it was carved as a triad of Shakyamuni Buddha, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and the Future Buddha of the Lotus Assembly, by the sculptor Hwijang and his group.

1123315270000.title_en: Iron Seated Buddha, Baeunam Hermitage, Chungju
1123315270000.description: This iron Buddha statue was likely moved from the site of a Goryeo-period temple near Baeunam Hermitage. Its posture and drapery preserve features of Unified Silla Buddhist sculpture, but the form also suggests a date from the late Unified Silla to early Goryeo period.

1121115280000.title_en: Early Woodblock Print of the Sutra of Prince Shadougan Jinril
1121115280000.description: This is an early woodblock-printed Buddhist sutra translated by Zhufahu of Western Jin, also known as the Tiger Ears Sutra. It discusses a woman’s attachment and renunciation, the equality of the four castes, and also includes material on astronomy, divination, and the class system of ancient India.

1121115370000.title_en: Map of the Western Northwest Borderlands (2007)
1121115370000.description: This late Joseon military map depicts the northern Korean region and Manchuria together as a border-defense map. Its Manchurian geographic information is based on Seonggyeongji, while the northwestern Korean region reflects information used before Jeong Sang-gi's Dongguk Jido. It is regarded as one of the finest surviving maps of this type from the late Joseon period.

1121115370200.title_en: Map of the Western Northwest Borderlands (2008)
1121115370200.description: This military map shows the northwestern part of Joseon and the Manchurian region of Qing China, and it was made in the mid-18th century. It records routes, forts, checkpoints, and military positions around the Baekdusan and Yalu and Tumen river borderlands. The map is valued for both its historical geography and its high pictorial quality.

1121115380000.description: This large folding map of Joseon covers the Korean peninsula and part of Manchuria. It is made of fine silk joined in three panels, and its careful execution suggests that it was painted by an artist of the Office of Paintings. It is estimated to have been produced between 1755 and 1757 and is considered close to the original line of Jeong Sang-gi's Dongguk Jido.

1121115390000.description: This album gathers poems and prose written in Yang Sa-eon’s own hand, including a copy of Heo Gang’s Seohobyeolgok and his own Chinese and Korean-language poems. It contains more than ten Chinese poems not included in Bongnae Sigjip and is a rare example of Yang Sa-eon’s calligraphy. The work is also an important source for studying sixteenth-century mixed Korean-Chinese writing.

1121115400000.title_en: Celadon Ewer in the Shape of a Gourd
1121115400000.description: This Goryeo celadon ewer from the 12th century is shaped like a gourd. The body, spout, handle, and lid are modeled with decorative forms that evoke gourd vines and leaves, and the base is finished without a separate foot ring. Its refined form and translucent bluish-green glaze make it a representative example of 12th-century celadon.

1121115410000.title_en: Buncheong Bottle with Inlaid Peony and Willow Design
1121115410000.description: This bottle is a typical 15th-century Buncheong ware form decorated with inlaid patterns. Peonies and willow branches are arranged on the body, with white line inlay around the shoulder and lower body. Its balanced form, grayish-green glaze, and bold abstract decoration are characteristic of Buncheong ware aesthetics.

1121115420000.title_en: Map of the Liaodong and Jizhou Border Defenses
1121115420000.description: This military map shows the fortifications, walls, and defensive routes from Liaodong to the Jizhou region near Beijing. It was compiled by Yi Myeong in 1706 and presented to the king, using several Chinese and Korean sources obtained during his diplomatic mission to Qing. Painted on silk as a ten-panel folding screen, it is valued for both map history and pictorial quality.

1123415430100.title_en: Revised and Collated Text of the Ritual of Repentance for the Compassionate Bodhisattva, Vols. 9-10
1123415430100.description: This Buddhist ritual text was printed in Buan in August 1316 through the efforts of the monk Seokyeon of Bohyeonsa Temple. It is a collated and revised edition of the rite known as the Ritual of Repentance for the Compassionate Bodhisattva, and the end of volume 10 records the publication details and participants. The text preserves Goryeo-period taboo-character omissions and is an important source for Buddhist ritual, history, and bibliography.

1123115430200.description: This is Volume 5 of the Buddhist scripture Sanggyojeongbon Jabi Doryang Chambeop, which explains that by participating in repentance rites and receiving the Buddha’s spiritual power, one can cleanse sins, gain blessings, and escape the suffering of rebirth. The Manbulsunwon copy follows the folded-leaf format and appears to be a later printed edition based on an earlier Goryeo woodblock edition, with gugyeol marks preserved throughout the text.

1121115430300.description: This is a three-volume copy of Sanggyojeongbon Jabi Doryang Chambeop, a Buddhist scripture printed from woodblocks in August 1316 under the direction of the monk Seokryeon at Bohyeonsa Temple in Byeonsan. Although parts are worn and repaired, it preserves gugyeol marks and includes volumes not represented in other designated copies, giving it notable documentary value.

1123615440000.title_en: Naju Simhyangsa Dry-Lacquer Seated Amitabha Buddha
1123615440000.description: This statue is a dry-lacquer seated Amitabha Buddha made by the hollow-core dry-lacquer technique, which was especially common in the late Goryeo and early Joseon periods. Its austere foreign-looking face and fine drapery folds are considered characteristic of late Goryeo Buddhist sculpture.

1123615450000.title_en: Naju Bulhoesa Dry-Lacquer Seated Vairocana Buddha
1123615450000.description: This statue is the main image of the Daeungjeon Hall at Bulhoesa Temple and is a dry-lacquer seated Buddha made in the late Goryeo to early Joseon period. It preserves an early example of the Vairocana Buddha’s wisdom-fist mudra, in which the left hand encloses the right fist.

1123615460000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Shrine of Cheoneunsa Temple, Gurye
1123615460000.description: This gilt-bronze shrine, 43.3 cm high, is a small structure made to enshrine Buddhist images and is opened only for worship or rituals. Its front wall contains a Vairocana Buddha triad and ten disciples in relief, with guardian figures on the inner doors and ornate floral and ceiling decoration.

1123615470000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva Seated in Royal Ease, Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1123615470000.description: This is a relatively large gilt-bronze bodhisattva statue seated in royal ease, showing stylistic features inherited from Goryeo sculpture. At the same time, its oval face, pronounced nipples, lack of jeweled adornment across the chest, and stiffly rendered drapery indicate an early Joseon date.

1123615490000.title_en: Wooden Sakyamuni Buddha Triad and Clay Sixteen Arhats, Songgwangsa Temple, Suncheon
1123615490000.description: This group of 26 surviving statues was made in 1624, as recorded on the pedestal of one attendant figure, and includes the Sakyamuni Buddha triad, the two chief disciples, the Sixteen Arhats, Indra, Brahma, guardian figures, and a lion. The Sixteen Arhats are especially important because complete sets from the Goryeo and early Joseon periods rarely survive.

1123615500000.title_en: Wooden Sakyamuni Buddha Triad, Heungguksa Temple, Yeosu
1123615500000.description: This triad, enshrined as the main Buddha image in the Daeungjeon Hall of Heungguksa Temple, was made during the Chongzhen reign period, corresponding to 1628–1644. The central Buddha and attendant bodhisattvas are noted for their balanced proportions, natural poses, and finely rendered drapery and ornaments.

1123115590000.title_en: Avatamsaka Sutra in Silver Ink on Indigo Paper
1123115590000.description: This manuscript was copied in 1336, the 5th year of King Chungsuk’s restored reign, on dark blue paper in silver ink. It consists of selected fascicles from the 60-fascicle Chinese translation by Buddhabhadra and the 80-fascicle translation by Śikṣānanda, for a total of 7 fascicles in 7 booklets.

1121115600000.description: This is a map of Hanyang made in the late 18th century. It depicts the city and its surrounding mountains with pictorial treatment, placing the south at the top in accordance with the king’s perspective, and includes notes on administrative districts, the size of the capital, and road conditions.

1123615610000.title_en: Bronze Bell of Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon (2008-2)
1123615610000.description: This bell was cast in 1657 by Kim Yongam, a leading Joseon bell caster, originally for Buduam Hermitage at Daewonsa Temple in Boseong County. It has a well-balanced form and finely rendered decoration, including a twin-dragon knob, Buddhist Sanskrit inscriptions, lotus bands, deities, and prayer tablets.

1123715620000.title_en: Five-Buddha Gathering Banner Painting of Buseoksa Temple, Yeongju
1123715620000.description: This hanging painting was made in 1745 as a Five-Buddha Gathering composition and was newly created for Buseoksa Temple to replace an older banner from 1684. It arranges the Buddhas in a Three Bodies and Three Ages scheme, with Śākyamuni Buddha at the center, and reflects a mature mid-18th-century Buddhist painting style.

1122215630000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122215630000.description: This main hall of Donghwasa Temple was likely rebuilt between 1727 and 1732 in the late Joseon period. It is a three-bay by three-bay wooden building with a hipped-and-gabled roof, multibracket construction, decorative lattice doors, and unrefined pillar logs that emphasize stability and naturalness.

1123415640000.title_en: King Seonjo’s Investiture Document for Yi Sun-sin as Meritorious Subject (Seonmugongsin Gyoseo)
1123415640000.description: This royal document was issued in 1604 to Yi Sun-sin, honoring his military achievements during the Japanese invasions of Korea. It records his elevation as a first-rank meritorious subject and lists the rewards bestowed on him and his family.

1123415640200.title_en: King Seonjo’s Consolatory and Rewarding Edict for Yi Sun-sin and Others (Seonyuhuangsang Gyoseo)
1123415640200.description: This royal document was issued on September 15, 1596, by King Seonjo to Yi Sun-sin, then Admiral of the Three Provinces and naval commander of the Jeolla Left Naval District, and his troops. It is an edict of encouragement and reward.

1123415640300.title_en: King Seonjo’s Instructional Edict for Yi Sun-sin (Saim Hunyu Gyoseo)
1123415640300.description: This royal document was issued on July 23, 1597, by King Seonjo to Yi Sun-sin, then commander of the Three Provinces’ naval forces. It instructs him to fulfill his mission well.

1123415640400.description: Issued by King Seonjo on February 15, 1591, this royal edict granted Yi Sun-sin, then Jeollajwado Navy Commander, the 29th military seal. It is a royal document connected to Yi Sun-sin.

1123415640500.description: Issued by King Seonjo on July 14, 1594, this royal edict granted Yi Sun-sin, then acting Jeollajwado Navy Commander and commander of the Three Provincial Navies, the 10th military seal. It is a royal document connected to Yi Sun-sin.

1123415640600.description: Issued by King Seonjo on July 23, 1597, this royal edict granted Yi Sun-sin, then Jeollajwado Navy Commander and commander of the Three Provincial Navies of Chungcheong, Jeolla, and Gyeongsang, the 7th military seal. It is a royal document connected to Yi Sun-sin.

1123415640700.title_en: Military Examination Certificate for Yi Sun-sin
1123415640700.description: This certificate records that Yi Sun-sin passed the military service examination in the second degree, placing fourth, in March 1576. It is an official royal document issued during the reign of King Seonjo.

1123415640800.title_en: Royal Appointment Certificate for Mrs. Bang, Wife of Yi Sun-sin (2011-1)
1123415640800.description: Issued on November 26, 1591, this royal appointment document granted Mrs. Bang, wife of Yi Sun-sin, the title of Sukbuin. The title was awarded according to the status of her husband, who then held the office of Jeollajwado Navy Commander.

1123415640900.title_en: Royal Appointment Certificate for Mrs. Bang, Wife of Yi Sun-sin (2011-2)
1123415640900.description: This royal document was issued when Yi Sun-sin was posthumously promoted to Uijeong, and his wife, Lady Bang of Sangju, was elevated to Jeonggyeongbuin. Jeonggyeongbuin was the highest title given to the wives of civil and military officials of the first rank under the Gyeongguk Daejeon system.

1123415641000.title_en: Royal Appointment Certificate for Yi Sun-sin
1123415641000.description: Issued on July 12, 1604, this royal document posthumously reappointed Yi Sun-sin, who had earlier been promoted to Uijeong, as Left State Councillor and Duke of Deokpung, with additional meritorious titles. It is a royal appointment certificate connected to Yi Sun-sin.

1123415641100.title_en: Royal Grant of Slaves to Yi Sun-sin
1123415641100.description: Issued on January 9, 1605, this royal document granted Yi Sun-sin, the deceased first-class meritorious retainer and Duke of Deokpung, government slaves located in Buan, Gosan, Onyang, Jiksan, Cheonan, Jinsan, and Eunjin. It records a royal reward bestowed after his death.

1123415641200.title_en: Royal Edict Bestowing the Posthumous Title on Yi Sun-sin
1123415641200.description: This royal edict, issued by King Injo on March 28, 1643, bestowed the posthumous title "Chungmugong" on Yi Sun-sin. Although Chinese reign titles were usually used in dating royal documents, this edict records the date by the sexagenary cycle instead.

1123415641300.description: Issued on January 21, 1595, this royal instruction was delivered to Yi Sun-sin through Jeong Mo, then a deputy chamberlain. It ordered measures such as opening military farmlands to supplement the shortage of grain for the army during the Japanese invasions.

1123415641400.description: This document records a special grant of land and slaves to Yi Sun-sin, who had passed the military civil service examination in 1576. Because earlier household documents were lost in a fire in 1584, this grant document was rewritten on March 12, 1588, and it also records grants made to his other sons.

1123415641500.title_en: Royal Grant Edict for Yi Sun-sin
1123415641500.description: This edict records the later grant of the remaining five slaves promised to Yi Sun-sin as part of the rewards for his military service. It was issued in 1653 and shows that the slaves assigned to him were those attached to offices such as the Office of Royal Guest Reception, the Office of Finance, and the Office of the Royal Clan.

1123415641600.title_en: Royal Edict of Promotion for Yi Sun-sin
1123415641600.description: Following King Jeongjo's order in 1793, this edict posthumously promoted Yi Sun-sin to the position of Prime Minister. The source notes that the edict was issued on the same day as the rites held for the erection of his stele.

1123415650000.title_en: Clay Seated Triad of Amitabha Buddha, Muryangsa Temple, Buyeo
1123415650000.description: Installed in the Main Hall of Paradise Hall at Muryangsa Temple, this large clay Buddhist sculpture follows the type widely produced at major temples in the 17th century. It depicts the Amitabha triad of Amitabha Buddha, Avalokitesvara, and Mahasthamaprapta, and its votive inscription identifies the sculptor monk Hyeonjin and the date of 1633.

1123615660000.title_en: Wooden Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Triad, Ten Kings, and Related Buddhist Objects, Hungkuksa Temple, Yeosu
1123615660000.description: This set of sculptures, including the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva triad enshrined in Musa Hall at Hunguksa Temple, was made in 1648 by master sculptor monk Ingyun and 11 other sculptors. The group includes the Ten Kings and attendants, and a votive inscription preserves information on the patronage and date of production.

1123115670000.description: This edition is based on a Royal copy first printed in 1474 at Geonseongsa, using funds from the Naesusa office, to pray for Queen Hyeongyeong and Queen Consort Gonghye. Because three woodblocks were missing, it was republished with supplemental carving in 1485; the colophon records the date and the monk Sinhwan, who supervised the reprinting.

1123315510000.title_en: Vulture Peak Assembly Gwaebul Painting, Yeongsusa Temple, Jincheon
1123315510000.description: This hanging Buddhist painting was produced in 1653 by four monk-painters led by Myeongok. It depicts the Vulture Peak assembly from the Lotus Sutra, centered on Sakyamuni Buddha and the gathered audience, including Sariputra seated with his back to the viewer before the Buddha's pedestal. It is an important early example of a Joseon-period gwaebul and is regarded as the earliest known gwaebul to include Sariputra as the listener to the teaching.

1123615520000.title_en: Vulture Peak Assembly Gwaebul Painting, Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1123615520000.description: This gwaebul was created in 1764 under the lead of monk-painter Saekmin. It presents a five-deity composition with Sakyamuni Buddha in the center, Manjushri and Samantabhadra to the left and right, and Avalokiteshvara and Amitabha flanking the Buddha's halo.

1123615530000.title_en: Gamro King Painting, Seobu Buddha Hall Hermitage, Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123615530000.description: This painting was made in 1736 by monk-painter Uigyeom for Seobudojeon, as recorded in the inscription. It shows the upper register with the Seven Buddhas, Avalokiteshvara, Ksitigarbha, and the Leading King Bodhisattva; the middle with a pair of hungry ghosts and an altar; and the lower with scenes of the six realms. The composition emphasizes the Seven Buddhas in the upper register, reflecting the painting's role in a water-and-land rite for guiding departed spirits.

1123615540000.title_en: Thirty-Three Patriarchs Painting, Seonamsa Temple, Suncheon
1123615540000.description: This work depicts the thirty-three patriarchs of the Seon tradition from Kashyapa to Huineng in eleven panels, based on the Joseon-period text Zhutang ji. Only seven of the original eleven panels survive today, and the painting was made in 1753 by five monk-painters including Eungi. The iconography also reflects Chinese illustrated books such as Sancai Tuhui and Hongshi Xianfo Qizong, showing the influence of imported visual sources on late Joseon Buddhist painting.

1123615550000.description: This bell was cast in 1644 under the leadership of metal caster Kim Yongam, a representative artisan of the private foundry tradition in the Joseon period. At 102 cm high, it is relatively large and notable for its balanced proportions, lively four-dragon bell loop, and refined decorative motifs on the body.

1123615560000.description: This large bell was cast in 1665 by Kim Ae-rip, another major figure among Joseon-period bell casters. Standing 121 cm high, it has a narrow upper body that widens toward the base, a double-dragon bell loop, a band of lotus decoration on the crown, and inscriptions and reliefs including bodhisattvas and a tablet praying for the royal family's peace.

1123615570000.description: This bell was made in 1698, the latest known work by Kim Ae-rip, and is considered one of his finest surviving works. Its form resembles the bell at Heungguksa Temple, with a double-dragon loop, four standing bodhisattvas in relief between the sound bands, and a tablet expressing a wish for the safety of the royal household.

1123615580000.description: This large bell, 120 cm high, bears an inscription stating that it was recast in 1700 for the main bell of Seonamsa Temple. The inscription also lists the names of craftsmen associated with Kim Sang-rip's family, making it an important source for understanding the activities of that artisan lineage in the 18th century. Its form and decorative motifs are characteristic of late Joseon bronze bells.

1121115840000.title_en: Map Album of Hwanghae Province (Haeseo Jido)
1121115840000.description: This colored manuscript map album contains county and prefectural maps of Hwanghae Province in the late Joseon period. It consists of three volumes and includes a province-wide map plus 20 local maps; the “Bibyonsa” seal on one map shows that it was kept and used by the State Council Office for Border Defense.

1121115850000.title_en: Map Album of Gyeongsang Province (Yeongnam Jido)
1121115850000.description: This colored manuscript map album contains maps of 71 counties and prefectures in Gyeongsang Province from the late Joseon period. Evidence in the place names suggests it was made between 1745 and 1767, and a later map of Mueuijin was added to the fourth volume.

1121115860000.description: This is a pictorial map of Jeonju, the ancestral home of King Taejo Yi Seong-gye, drawn in a landscape style. It shows Jeonju Fortress, government offices, Gyeonggijeon Shrine, nearby mountains, residences, blossoms, and birds in a detailed bird's-eye view.

1121115870000.description: This colored manuscript map album contains county and prefectural maps of seven provinces, excluding Jeolla Province. The maps are drawn on a uniform grid scale, making this a rare and highly accurate official map album from late Joseon.

1121115880000.title_en: Map Album of Jeolla Province (Honam Jido)
1121115880000.description: This colored manuscript map album contains county and prefectural maps of Jeolla Province from the late Joseon period. The use of the name “Ilshin” for Namwon indicates that it was made between 1739 and 1750, and the album includes a province-wide map and related regional maps.

1121115890000.title_en: Map Album of Chungcheong Province (Hoseo Jido)
1121115890000.description: This colored manuscript map album contains county and prefectural maps of Chungcheong Province from the late Joseon period. It includes provincial and county maps drawn on grid paper, with detailed notes on population, land, transport routes, and other local information.

1121115900000.description: This map depicts East Asia centered on Joseon and China and is thought to have been made in the mid-16th century. It closely follows the general outline of the 1402 Honil gangni yeokdae guktodo, but shows Joseon in greater detail and marks Japan only by location.

1121115910000.description: This colored manuscript map album contains pictorial maps of counties and prefectures throughout Joseon, along with province maps, maps of China and Japan, and maps of major frontier defenses. The contents reflect data from around 1748 to 1750 and show that it was produced in the mid-18th century.

1123715680000.description: Yangjindang in Sangju is said to have been built by Jo Jeong in 1626, and records indicate that it was repaired in 1807. It is a raised-floor house with a square-shaped plan, measuring nine bays across the front and seven bays on the side, and it uses a variety of construction techniques unusual for this type of dwelling. The building is regarded as an important example showing the diversity of Joseon-period residential architecture.

1123415690000.title_en: Eungdodang Hall of Donamseowon Confucian Academy, Nonsan
1123415690000.description: Eungdodang is the lecture hall of Donamseowon, a Joseon-period private Confucian academy founded in 1634 to honor scholars and continue learning. The building originally remained at the old site of the academy and was moved to its present location in 1971 after roof-tile inscriptions confirmed its age. It is a large gabled hall with five bays on the front and three bays on the side.

1123715700000.title_en: Bogwangjeon Hall of Daejeonsa Temple, Cheongsong
1123715700000.description: Bogwangjeon at Daejeonsa Temple was rebuilt in 1672 after the earlier hall was burned during the Japanese invasions of Korea. It stands on a granite foundation with a three-bay front and side, and it has a gabled roof with double eaves only at the front. The hall preserves features of mid-Joseon wooden architecture, including its bracket system, interior dancheong, and wall paintings.

1123715710000.title_en: Wooden Seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva and Reliquaries from Bogwangsa Temple, Andong
1123715710000.description: This wooden seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva is believed to have been made in the first half of the 13th century. The statue shows refined carving, a dignified face, balanced proportions, and detailed ornaments, and it is considered an important example of Goryeo Buddhist sculpture. It was found with 194 reliquary objects of 10 types, including Buddhist scriptures, texts, and a rare Goryeo-period undergarment.

1123415720000.title_en: Reliquaries from the Gilt-bronze Seated Buddha, Munsusa Temple, Seosan
1123415720000.description: These reliquaries came from a gilt-bronze seated Buddha statue that was designated as a provincial cultural property in Chungcheongnam-do, although the statue itself was stolen in 1993. The remains include 17 types of books and documents, textiles, clothing, and other objects, among them printed sutras, manuscript records, and clothing items made in the late Goryeo period. The materials are valuable for the study of Korean language, bibliography, Buddhist history, and textile history.

1123115730000.title_en: Celadon Dish with Relief Lotus-Petal Design
1123115730000.description: This is a graceful celadon dish with a flared rim, curved sides, and a high foot. The exterior is decorated with a carefully carved relief band of lotus petals, and the entire surface is covered with a clear bluish-green celadon glaze. It is thought to have been made at the Sadang-ri kiln site in Gangjin in the late 12th century.

1123715740000.title_en: Geukrakjeon Hall of Bongamsa Temple, Mungyeong
1123715740000.description: Geukrakjeon at Bongamsa Temple is said to have served as a prayer hall for King Gyeongsun during his flight, and it is the oldest surviving building at the temple. Based on its form and location, it is thought to have been built in the mid to late Joseon period, while its foundation stones and base stones may date to Goryeo. The hall preserves the appearance, construction method, and dancheong of a Joseon-period Buddhist building.

1123715750000.title_en: Daeseongjeon Hall and Myeongnyundang Hall of Seongjuhyanggyo Confucian Academy
1123715750000.description: Seongjuhyanggyo follows the usual left-shrine, right-school arrangement when viewed from the front, with Myeongnyundang on the left and Daeseongjeon on the right. Daeseongjeon is a rare example among Korean hyanggyo buildings of a multi-bracket style and preserves features of early Joseon architecture. Myeongnyundang has a typical central-hall flanked by side rooms layout, with older construction details still visible in the doors, windows, and roof form.

1123715760000.description: Daeungjeon at Jikjisa Temple in Gimcheon is a Buddhist worship hall arranged within a two-pagoda courtyard layout, with two three-story stone pagodas standing in front of the main hall. The present structure reflects architectural features of the late Joseon period and the rebuilding of Buddhist halls after the Imjin War. Wall paintings and the altar remain, giving it historical, artistic, and scholarly value.

1123115770000.description: This is a Joseon-period medical text compiled in the 15th century from two Chinese emergency prescription manuals: Iggabibuseusinbiyo Gagamsipsam-bang and Gyeongheom Gupgubang. It contains prescriptions for conditions such as colds, flu, and abdominal pain, along with an appendix on making a health pillow. The book is valued as an important source for the history of Korean medicine and printing, and is a rare surviving edition.

1123515780000.description: Gyeonggijeon was built to enshrine the portrait of King Taejo, founder of the Joseon dynasty, and the present main hall was rebuilt in 1614 after the site burned during the Jeongyu Jaeran in 1597. Jeongjeon is a dignified wooden building with a multi-bracket structure, double-eaved gabled roof, and a formal arrangement with the Bae Ryecheong hall in front. Its precise joinery, structural stability, and elaborate interior ornamentation are cited as reasons for its heritage value.

1123115790000.title_en: Early Woodblock Edition of the Seongjise Dharani Sutra
1123115790000.description: This Buddhist scripture was translated by the Indian monk Shihu and belongs to the first carved edition of the Tripitaka Koreana. It teaches that reciting and upholding the dharani can remove grave sins and fulfill wishes. The end of the volume preserves records of the translation process, making it an important source for the study of Buddhist scripture translation in the period.

1121115800000.title_en: Seoul Sukguksa Wooden Seated Amitabha Buddha and Buddhist Relics from the Womb Deposit
1121115800000.description: Sukguksa was founded in 1459 as a royal temple near the tomb of Prince Uigyeong, later posthumously honored as King Deokjong. The wooden seated Amitabha Buddha has no dated inscription, but its heavy face, robust body, layered robe folds, and restrained treatment of details are stylistically close to Buddhist statues of the late 13th to early 14th century. The collection includes the statue and 36 kinds of reliquary objects, 84 pieces in total.

1121115810000.description: These are 11 surviving woodblocks used to produce Daedong yeojido, one of the largest and most scientifically advanced maps of Joseon Korea. The blocks are made of linden wood and are carved on both sides, with each face showing geographic information for a separate area. They are an important source for the history of Korean cartography and science.

1121115820000.description: This large map shows Joseon’s frontier defenses and maritime defenses at a glance and also includes Manchuria and Japan. Its place names suggest it was made after 1776, and its Korean portion follows the Dongguk jido tradition associated with Jeong Sang-gi. The map is well preserved and is considered an especially good example of its type.

1121115830000.description: This is a five-volume atlas of local maps for Hamgyeong Province in late Joseon Korea, drawn in color by hand. It is thought to have been produced by the Board of National Defense during the reign of King Yeongjo and is drawn on gridded paper. The atlas records fortresses, storehouses, beacon towers, roads by sea, and administrative and military information, showing that it was made for governmental and military use.

1121115920000.description: This is a colored manuscript atlas made in the late Joseon period and consisting of three volumes.
