The portrait shows him seated in full ceremonial dress, with the title "Portrait of an Old Man of Geumwon at Fifty-Two" written at the upper right. It carefully records his facial features and official attire, including the rank badge and gold belt of a second-rank official.

1123717250000.title_en: Old Documents of the Kim Jong-jik Family Clan
1123717250000.description: These documents are related to Kim Jong-jik, the leading scholar of the Yeongnam Sarim faction, and to his descendants. They include royal appointment documents, passing certificates, official notices, land and property division records, sale documents, and letters. They are valuable sources for studying Joseon-period examinations, bureaucracy, property distribution, sales practices, and everyday life.

1123717500000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Triad, Gyeongheungsa Temple, Gyeongsan
1123717500000.description: This wooden triad of Sakyamuni, found at Gyeongheungsa Temple in Gyeongsan, preserves an inscription and votive text that identify its exact date of creation, 1644, and the people involved in its production. It is an important reference for 17th-century Buddhist sculpture and is associated with the sculptor Cheongheo, who was active widely across Korea in the early to mid-17th century.

1123417510000.title_en: Wooden Seated Amitabha Triad, Bongseosa Temple, Seocheon
1123417510000.description: This Amitabha triad consists of Amitabha Buddha with Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta as attendant bodhisattvas. A votive inscription records its exact creation date, 1619, as well as the patrons and other details, making it an important source for the study of early Joseon-period Buddhist sculpture.

1123417520000.title_en: Clay Seated Vairocana Triad, Seonunsa Temple, Gochang
1123417520000.description: This large clay triad of Vairocana Buddha shows a broad, imposing form and reflects major 17th-century trends in large-scale clay Buddhist sculpture. An inscription on the base records the date of creation as 1633 and identifies the sculptor Mueom and his disciples, making it a key work for the study of Vairocana triads.

1123517530000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Incense Burner from Mireuksa Temple Site, Iksan
1123517530000.description: This gilt-bronze incense burner was excavated from the Mireuksa Temple Site and is considered the first known Unified Silla gilt-bronze animal-shaped incense burner in Korea. Its form reflects Chinese Tang-period animal-shaped incense burners, while also combining elements that were adapted in a Korean way in the early Unified Silla period.

1123117540000.title_en: Printing Blocks for the Buddha Speaks of the Great Repayment of Parents' Kindness Sutra
1123117540000.description: This set consists of 73 printing blocks: 42 woodblocks, 7 copper-iron plates, and 24 stone blocks. They were made between 1796 and 1799 by royal order and later sent to Yongjusa Temple, and they are valuable as late-18th-century materials for Korean language history and printing history.

1121117550000.description: This is an early Korean woodblock edition of a Chinese mathematics book by Yang Hui, made before 1433 and probably copied from a Chinese printed edition. It was used as a basic text in Joseon mathematics education and is an important source for the history of mathematics, scientific education, and bibliography.

1121117560000.title_en: King's Grant of Meritorious Service to Kim Eung-nam and Related Documents
1121117560000.description: This royal charter was granted to Kim Eung-nam in 1604 for his service in escorting King Seonjo and the crown prince during the Imjin War. The set also includes a later document granting him the posthumous honorific title "Chungjeong" in 1753, and it is an important source for the history of the war and for the study of Joseon official documents.

1123817570000.title_en: Mural Paintings of Daeungjeon Hall, Sinheungsa Temple, Yangsan
1123817570000.description: These mural paintings cover the interior and exterior walls of Daeungjeon Hall, with major scenes including the Medicine Buddha triad, Amitabha triad, the Eight Scenes, the Four Heavenly Kings, and other Buddhist images. The hall was originally built in 1657, and the murals are generally understood to date from the late 17th century, though some areas were repainted during later repairs.

1121117680000.title_en: Myoji and Stone Case of Heungnyeong Budaebuin, White Porcelain with Underglaze Cobalt Blue Design
1121117680000.description: This grave inscription and stone case were discovered in 2001 at the Yun clan burial ground in Danghari, Paju, where six white porcelain inscription tablets were found inside a rectangular stone case. The inscription records the death and burial of Incheon Yi Clan, the mother of Queen Jeonghui and mother-in-law of King Sejo, and is dated to 1456. It is regarded as an early and important example for the study of underglaze cobalt-blue porcelain in Joseon.

1121117690000.description: Juhamnu Pavilion is a two-story building in the rear garden of Changdeokgung Palace, built in 1776 to store royal writings and calligraphy of King Jeongjo. The surrounding layout includes a garden, flower terraces, and Eosumun Gate, which was given a symbolic meaning linking the king and his officials. The building has a well-preserved original form and is valued for its historical and architectural significance.

1121117700000.description: Yeongyeongdang Hall is a residential complex in the rear garden of Changdeokgung Palace, built around 1827–1828 by Crown Prince Hyomyeong for King Sunjo and Queen Sunwon. Its layout separates the men's and women's quarters while linking them through a connected plan, and it includes auxiliary structures such as Seonhyangjae and Nongsujeong. The building is an important example for the study of palace architecture and Joseon upper-class house planning.

1122117710000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Jangansa Temple, Gijang
1122117710000.description: Daeungjeon Hall is the main Buddha hall of Jangansa Temple, a temple said to have been founded in 673 during the Unified Silla period. The present building was rebuilt in 1657, repaired in 1744, and partially restored in the 20th century. It is a three-bay by three-bay building with a paljak roof and a bracket system extending both above and between the columns.

1122217720000.title_en: Samjang Bodhisattva Painting, Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122217720000.description: This Buddhist painting was produced in 1728 for a ritual to guide the souls of the dead, and depicts the three Samjang Bodhisattvas with their attendants on a single horizontal scroll. The inscription identifies Uigyun as the leading monk-painter, and the work helps show the production network of Buddhist painters active around Palgongsan in the early 18th century. It is also important for the history of Joseon Buddhist painting because early examples of this iconography are rare.

1122217730000.title_en: Ksitigarbha and the Ten Kings Painting, Donghwasa Temple, Daegu
1122217730000.description: This Buddhist painting was made in 1728 for the middle register of a triad set enshrined at Donghwasa Temple, together with the Samjang Bodhisattva Painting. It depicts Ksitigarbha, the Ten Kings, and attendant figures in a strictly symmetrical group composition, and the record names the monk-painters who participated. The work is important for studying early 18th-century Ksitigarbha and Ten Kings paintings and the style of painters active in inland Gyeongbuk.

1121117740000.description: This set consists of four surviving volumes of the Joseon edition of Zhu Xi's abridged historical work Jachitonggam Gangmok, printed in 1493 with the metal type Gyesukja. The text and commentary include punctuation marked in white circles, and some volumes preserve stamps and correction notes, showing that this copy functioned as a corrected working text. It is a rare early Joseon metal-type edition valuable for the study of history, bibliography, and printing technology.

1121117750000.description: Jinsiljup is a three-volume, one-book collection compiled in the Song dynasty from selected Zen-related writings such as songs, inscriptions, verses, and prose by various masters. The Joseon edition was first carved in 1462 and reprinted in 1472, with Kim Su-on's postscript added in type. This copy is valuable for studying early Joseon woodblock printing and the royal family's Buddhist devotion.

1121117590000.description: Sajeongjeon Hall is a subsidiary hall of Gyeongbokgung Palace where the king stayed in ordinary times and handled state affairs. It was first built in 1395, rebuilt after fires and war, and the present structure was reconstructed in 1867.

1121117600000.description: Sujeongjeon Hall stands west of Geunjeongjeon Hall in Gyeongbokgung Palace and was used as a royal office and later as the seat of government offices. The present building was reconstructed in 1867, and it is the only surviving building from the palace inner administrative quarters in that area.

1121117610000.description: Hyangwonjeong Pavilion is a hexagonal pavilion on an island in Hyangwonji Pond in the rear garden of Gyeongbokgung Palace. The pond and pavilion were created in the late Joseon period, and the wooden bridge to the island was restored in 2021.

1121117620000.description: Geumcheon Bridge crosses the palace stream between Donhwamun Gate and Jinseonmun Gate of Changdeokgung Palace. Built in 1411, it is the oldest stone bridge remaining inside a palace in Seoul and preserves its original form.

1121117630000.description: Buyongjeong Pavilion stands on the south side of Buyongji Pond in the rear garden of Changdeokgung Palace. The pavilion is recorded as first built in 1707 and later repaired and renamed during King Jeongjo's reign.

1121117640000.description: Nakseonjae is a palace residential complex at the boundary of Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung Palaces. Built in 1847 for the royal family, it later served as a work place for King Gojong and as a residence for Prince Yi Un and Lady Bangja.

1123417650000.title_en: Five Directional Deities and Four Messenger Paintings, Gaesimsa Temple
1123417650000.description: This set of ritual Buddhist paintings consists of five panels of the Five Directional Deities and four panels of the Four Messenger paintings. Dated to 1676, they were made by the monk-painter Iho as ritual paintings for a Buddhist altar and preserve an inscription with the date and production details.
1123417650000.material: Ink and color on silk and hemp

1123417660000.title_en: Indra and Brahma, the Eight Vajra Warriors, and the Four Bodhisattvas Paintings, Gaesimsa Temple
1123417660000.description: This set of ritual Buddhist paintings was made in 1772 and consists of paintings of Indra, Brahma, the Eight Vajra Warriors, and the Four Bodhisattvas. The inscription states that these works were produced together with the large hanging scroll painting for use in Buddhist rituals such as Yeongsanjae.

1123117940000.description: This is volume 9 of the Korean vernacular translation of the Shurangama Sutra, whose translation work began in 1449 under King Sejong and was completed in 1461 under King Sejo. The extant volume is a proofed printed edition from the Sejo period, using metal type, and it is an important source for early Joseon linguistics and bibliography.

1121117950000.title_en: Manuscripts from the Inner Storage of the Dry-lacquer Seated Amitabha Buddha, Cheongwon-sa Temple, Anseong
1121117950000.description: These inner-storage manuscripts were found inside the dry-lacquer seated Amitabha Buddha at Cheongwon-sa Temple, Anseong. They include three fascicles of the Avatamsaka Sutra and one fascicle of the Avatamsaka Sutra in the Jingyuan recension, all copied in the Goryeo period and valuable for the study of Goryeo Buddhist manuscripts.

1123100001796.title_en: Album of Landscapes of the Eight Scenic Views of Haeak and Eight Worthies of the Song Dynasty by Jeong Seon
1123100001796.description: This album consists of eight true-view landscape paintings of Geumgangsan and eight figure paintings of the Eight Worthies of the Song Dynasty. Based on the painting style and the seals used, it is thought to have been made in the late 1740s, when Jeong Seon was in his seventies.

1123717970000.title_en: Yeongsanhoesang Painting and Four Heavenly Kings Murals, Bulguksa Temple, Gyeongju
1123717970000.description: This Buddhist set was made in 1769 through donations by Princess Hwaan and Court Lady Kim. It consists of one Yeongsanhoesang painting and two Four Heavenly Kings murals, and the works are thought to have been produced together in the same year by the same group of monk-painters.
1123717970000.material: Ink and color on silk and wall painting

1123117980000.title_en: Set of Clay Seated Sakyamuni Triad and Sixteen Arhats, Heungguk-sa Temple, Namyangju
1123117980000.description: This set includes a clay seated Sakyamuni triad and sixteen arhats. Although no original dedicatory inscription has been found, a record of the third repair in 1650 shows that the sculptures were made earlier, and they preserve stylistic features transitional between early Joseon Buddhist sculpture and later developments.

1123817990000.title_en: Ksitigarbha and the Ten Kings Painting, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123817990000.description: This hanging scroll was created in 1739 for the Gwaneumjeon Hall at the request of the donor Cheokok, with the monk-painter Hye-sik and five other painters taking part. The composition densely arranges Ksitigarbha, the Ten Kings, officials, underworld messengers, attendant boys and girls, and jailers, and it is an early surviving example of a Joseon-period underworld painting.

1123618000000.title_en: Set of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Painting and Ten Kings Paintings, Daewon-sa Temple, Boseong
1123618000000.description: This set of Buddhist paintings was made in 1766 for enshrinement in the underworld hall, with the leading painter Seokmin participating. It is notable for preserving a rare combination of Ksitigarbha, the Ten Kings, and attendant-messenger paintings together in a single surviving set, along with inscriptions recording the production details.

1122218010000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Triad and Reliquaries, Boseong Seonwon, Daegu
1122218010000.description: This set includes a wooden seated Sakyamuni triad and related reliquaries, including the original dedicatory text and sarira container, preserving the original form of the production context. The inscription records the exact date of 1647, the temple of enshrinement, the patrons, and the makers, making it an important benchmark for seventeenth-century Buddhist sculpture.

1122118100000.title_en: Bronze Drum with Inscription of Hwangnri-hyeon
1122118100000.description: This bronze drum was made in 1085, Goryeo Seonjong 2, by officials of Hwangri-hyeon, now in Yeoju, Gyeonggi-do. It has raised concentric circles on the front, with a lotus-decorated striking boss in the center and cloud designs around it, and an inscription incised on the side. It is considered the fourth-oldest known bronze drum and an important source for the study of Goryeo local administration and related terminology.

1123218110000.title_en: Wood Seated Manjushri Bodhisattva, Samhwasa Temple, Pyeongchang, and Relics from the Statue's Inner Belly
1123218110000.description: This is a seated wooden Manjushri Bodhisattva made in 1661, along with inner-belly relics including a sutra container and nine dedicatory texts in twelve pieces. The dedicatory inscriptions record the production date, the participation of sculptor monks including Hoegam, and details of the statue's making. It is noted for its rare iconography, refined carving, and importance as a representative late-17th-century Buddhist sculpture.

1123218120000.title_en: Inner-Belly Buddhist Texts from the Wood Seated Manjushri Bodhisattva, Samhwasa Temple, Pyeongchang
1123218120000.description: These are two texts found inside the seated wooden Manjushri Bodhisattva at Samhwasa Temple: a manuscript of the Diamond Sutra written in ink on paper, and volume 6 of the Lotus Sutra. The Diamond Sutra appears to date to the 14th century, while the Lotus Sutra volume is a rare late-Goryeo-or-early-Joseon printed edition based on a 1240 woodblock text. They are valuable materials for studying Buddhist manuscripts, printing, and bibliography.

1122218130000.title_en: Wood Seated Amitabha Triad and Relics, Yongyeonsa Temple, Daegu
1122218130000.description: This wooden Amitabha triad was made in 1655 and retains relic containers, dedicatory inscriptions, and other inner-belly materials from the time of production. The inscriptions identify the date, the temple of enshrinement, the patrons, and the maker, making it a key reference work for 17th-century Buddhist sculpture. A later repair and gilding record from 1762 is also preserved, providing evidence for the study of restoration and gilding practices.

1122218140000.title_en: Wood Seated Amitabha Triad, Unheungsa Temple, Daegu
1122218140000.description: This wooden Amitabha triad was made in 1653 and preserves a relic container and a dedicatory inscription from the time of production. The inscription records the date, temple, patrons, and maker, and also describes the full production process from felling the tree to completing the statue. It is regarded as the earliest known work by the sculptor monk Dou and an important source for the study of 17th-century Buddhist sculpture.

1123418150000.title_en: Royal Certificate of Merit for Hong Gashin, Pacification of Rebellion Merit Subject, and Related Documents
1123418150000.description: This group of documents centers on the royal certificate awarding Hong Gashin first-rank merit for suppressing rebellion, together with related registers of posthumous promotions for him and his parents. It also includes earlier documents reflecting his career, such as the office appointment document issued to his wife and documents bestowing honors on his father. The set is an important primary source for the study of the Imyo-ran rebellion, Joseon documentary history, and local elite families in the Hoseo region.

1123818160000.title_en: Mural of Avalokiteśvara, Daeungjeon Hall, Guryongsa Temple, Changnyeong
1123818160000.description: This mural depicts Avalokiteśvara preaching on Mount Potaraka, with Sudhana visiting to request instruction, and fills the entire wall with the bodhisattva figure. Although it has been repainted several times, it preserves features typical of 18th-century Joseon Buddhist painting, including the wide crown and ornaments, pale ink depiction of rocks and bamboo, a vase with willow branches, and the bodhisattva seated in a relaxed pose. It also includes distinctive features such as the strong shading on the face and the presentation of Sudhana and Potaraka Mountain.

1123718170000.title_en: Mural of Avalokiteśvara and Bodhidharma, Daeungbojeon Hall, Unmunsa Temple, Cheongdo
1123718170000.description: This mural shows Avalokiteśvara and Bodhidharma together on one large earthen wall, set against steep rocky mountains. It is considered the only known example of a mural that presents these two figures side by side, and it reflects the character of Unmunsa Temple as a Seon monastery that inherits the Gaji Sanmun tradition. Its style is close to late-17th-century to early-18th-century Buddhist painting, including the treatment of Avalokiteśvara's crown and the clothing of Sudhana.

1121117760000.description: This printed Buddhist text is an edition of the "Jeungdoga," a song attributed to Jingak Daesa of the Tang dynasty, together with several commentaries. It is estimated to have been printed with Eulhaeja metal type between 1455 and 1494, during the reigns of King Sejo to King Seongjong, and preserves the original cover binding and title slip in very good condition.

1123817780000.title_en: Buddhist Texts Enshrined in the Wooden Seated Vairocana Buddha Statue at Beopbojeon Hall, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123817780000.description: These are the enshrined scriptures and related texts found inside the wooden seated Vairocana Buddha statue at Beopbojeon Hall, Haeinsa Temple. The group includes rare Goryeo-period Buddhist books such as the Heart Sutra and a fragment of the Avatamsaka Sutra, and dates mainly to the 12th and 13th centuries.

1123817800000.title_en: Buddhist Texts Enshrined in the Wooden Seated Vairocana Buddha Statue at Daejeokgwangjeon Hall, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123817800000.description: These are the enshrined scriptures and related texts discovered inside the wooden seated Vairocana Buddha statue at Daejeokgwangjeon Hall, Haeinsa Temple. The collection includes several rare Goryeo Buddhist texts, such as fragments of the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Golden Light Sutra, and the Heart Sutra, most of which date to the 12th and 13th centuries.

1123117810000.title_en: Bronze Bell with Inscription of Daehwawon Temple
1123117810000.description: This bronze bell was cast in 1223, as recorded in the inscription on its body. Its form follows the general tradition of Silla bells, while features such as the floral band and ornamentation reflect characteristics of late Goryeo bells.

1123617820000.title_en: Celadon Toad-shaped Inkstone with Slipped Floral Design
1123617820000.description: This celadon inkstone was excavated from the Taean Daeseom shipwreck together with other ceramics and a wooden tag, indicating that it had been made in Gangjin and was being transported to Gyeongju. It is notable as a rare Goryeo-period celadon inkstone with iron-painted and slipped decoration, and its excavation context is relatively secure.

1123617830000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Inlaid Chrysanthemum, Peony, Willow, Reeds, and Bamboo Design and Wooden Tag
1123617830000.description: This celadon meiping vase and wooden tag were excavated from the Goryeo-period Mado No. 2 shipwreck off Taean, and are estimated to date to the late 12th to early 13th century. The vase has inlaid floral and plant designs, while the wooden tag records the vessel name and contents, showing that the jar was used to carry sesame oil.

1123617840000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Incised Lotus and Branch Design and Wooden Tag
1123617840000.description: This celadon meiping vase and wooden tag were excavated from the Goryeo-period Mado No. 2 shipwreck off Taean, and are estimated to date to the late 12th to early 13th century. The vase uses incised lotus decoration, and the wooden tag records the vessel name and contents, indicating that it was used to carry honey.

1122317850000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Triad, Jeondeungsa Temple, Ganghwa
1122317850000.description: This set of three wooden seated Buddha statues was made in 1623, with the monk-sculptor Suyeon serving as the chief sculptor. The triad is arranged with Sakyamuni Buddha at the center and Amitabha and Bhaisajyaguru as attendants, reflecting a form of the Three Buddhas image popular in the Joseon period.

1121118180000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Bodhisattva Seated in Royal Ease, Botasa Temple, Seoul
1121118180000.description: This gilt-bronze Bodhisattva is seated in royal ease, with the left leg lowered to rest on the ground and the right knee raised. Its full cheeks, half-open eyes, and small lips give the face a feminine expression, and its large scale suggests it was made by or for the royal family or the ruling elite in the early Joseon period.

1121118190000.title_en: Wooden Seated Triad of Shakyamuni Buddha, Bongeunsa Temple, Seoul
1121118190000.description: This triad of seated Buddhas was made in 1651 by the monk-sculptor Seungil, who led nine assistant sculptors. A later gilt-painting dedication text records that the principal Shakyamuni image was newly made after the original was destroyed by fire in 1689.

1121118200000.title_en: Rock-carved Seated Bodhisattva, Okgwiam Hermitage, Seoul
1121118200000.description: This large rock-carved image is more than 5 meters high, and its front was traditionally coated with white pigment, so it was commonly called Bodaegak Baekbul or Baekui Gwaneum. A record in Seong Hyeon's Yongjaechonghwa confirms the image and its local reputation, and its realistic features and flowing drapery show the style of late Goryeo Buddhist sculpture.

1121118210000.title_en: Stone Seated Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Triad and the Ten Kings, Cheongnyongsa Temple, Seoul
1121118210000.description: This group centers on a seated Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva triad and also preserves ten Kings, two ghost kings, two judges, two messengers, one attendant boy, and two guardian generals. It was made in 1660 by the monk-sculptor Seungil and is an important example for understanding the composition of a late Joseon underworld hall.

1121118220000.title_en: Wooden Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Triad and the Ten Kings, Hwagyesa Temple, Seoul
1121118220000.description: This set consists of a Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva triad, the Ten Kings, judges, messengers, attendant boys, and guardian figures, for a total of 25 images. It was made in 1649 and shows the style of the Seuyan line of sculptors, with records preserving information on the date, the sculptors, and the temples involved in its enshrinement and relocation.

1121118230000.description: This bronze object, thought to be a ritual vessel, is engraved on one side with a man plowing a field and a woman catching birds, and on the other side with a bird perched on a tree branch. Although the lower part is missing, it is valued for vividly showing aspects of life and belief in its time, including agricultural rites and a pole or sacred-rod belief.

1122118240000.title_en: Stone Seated Shakyamuni Buddha Triad, Jangansa Temple, Gijang
1122118240000.description: This triad was made by the chief sculptor Nokwon in the mid-17th century and is carved in steatite, like other early examples such as the 1655 triad at Songnimsa Temple and the 1648 seated Buddha at Wonhyosa Temple. The triad is centered on Shakyamuni Buddha with Bhaisajyaguru Buddha and Amitabha Buddha on either side, and its dated construction makes it an important benchmark for the study of steatite Buddhist sculpture.

1123718250000.description: Manchuidang was built by Kim Sa-won, a disciple of Toegye Yi Hwang, as a place for study and for training younger scholars. Construction began in 1582 and was completed in 1584, and later additions in 1711, 1727, and 1764 formed the present T-shaped layout.

1122218020000.title_en: Reliquary Books from the Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Triad, Boseong Seonwon, Daegu
1122218020000.description: This record comprises four Buddhist books placed as reliquary objects inside the wooden seated Sakyamuni triad at Boseong Seonwon in Daegu. The items include the fifth volume of the Korean vernacular commentary on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, a woodblock edition of the Diamond Sutra, Inmun angmok printed in 1395, and the lower volume of the Commentary on the Essentials of the Four Teachings of Tiantai, printed in 1464.

1123118030000.title_en: Stele for King Taejo's Geonwonneung Tomb, Guri
1123118030000.description: This stele was erected in 1409 to honor King Taejo Yi Seong-gye, founder of the Joseon dynasty, and to record his life and achievements. The stele body, tortoise pedestal, and dragon-head finial are well preserved, making it an important example for the study of early Joseon tomb steles.

1121118040000.title_en: Stele for King Taejong's Heolleung Tomb, Seoul
1121118040000.description: This tomb stele was erected in 1422 to commemorate King Taejong Yi Bang-won, the third king of Joseon. The stele inscription was written by Byeon Gye-ryang, and the engraved head inscription was written by Gwon Hong; the original tortoise pedestal was damaged during the Imjin War, but the finial remains well preserved.

1121118050000.title_en: Stele for King Sejong's Yeongneung Tomb, Seoul
1121118050000.description: This stele was erected in 1452 to honor King Sejong and his achievements. The inscription was composed by Jeong In-ji and written by Prince Anpyeong Yi Yong, and although much of the surface is eroded, the stele remains an important example of early Joseon tomb steles.

1123818060000.title_en: Woodblock for Volume 490 of Naejeon suham eumso, Haeinsa Temple, Hapcheon
1123818060000.description: This woodblock was carved in 1245 at the Tripitaka Hall Office (Daejanggam) during the Goryeo period. It contains the explanatory notes on the sound and meaning of a text on the six pāramitās, and its colophon records that it was carved under royal order in the year of Eulsa.

1123618070000.title_en: Cheonbuljeon Hall of Daeheungsa Temple, Haenam
1123618070000.description: Cheonbuljeon Hall is the main hall of the southern precinct of Daeheungsa Temple in Haenam. The present building was reconstructed in 1813, and its plan, bracket system, and decorative details show a restrained but elaborate style suited to enshrining one thousand Buddhas.

1123118080000.title_en: Octagonal Five-Story Stone Pagoda of Sujongsa Temple, Namyangju
1123118080000.description: This stone pagoda, handed down at Sujongsa Temple on the slope of Ungilsan in Namyangju, is a Joseon-period pagoda that continues the tradition of Goryeo octagonal pagodas in a smaller and more decorative form. Relic deposits and inscriptions show that it was erected by 1493 at the latest and repaired in 1628.

1122118090000.title_en: Auspicious Longevity Banquet for Seven Ladies
1122118090000.description: This painting records a longevity banquet held in 1691 for seven officials who were caring for their mothers aged seventy or older. The work is a later copy made before 1745, and it is notable for its horizontal handscroll format and for preserving writing by Gye Se-hwang.

1123618340000.title_en: Wooden Seated Sakyamuni Triad and Clay Seated Sixteen Arhats, Dabo-sa Temple, Naju
1123618340000.description: This set consists of the Sakyamuni triad and sixteen arhats made in 1625 by the sculptor Suyeon and his group, representing a major current in early 17th-century Buddhist sculpture. The recorded votive inscriptions preserve detailed information on the date of production, purpose, makers, and patrons, making the group an important source for the study of Joseon Buddhist sculpture.

1123718350000.title_en: Certificate of Meritorious Service for Jeong Jong and Related Documents
1123718350000.description: The certificate of meritorious service issued to Jeong Jong in 1467 records his contributions in suppressing the I Sae rebellion and provides valuable evidence on the registration of meritorious subjects. The set also includes a military service certificate issued to Jeong Jong in 1442, an early example from the period when the format of royal documents changed from wangji to gyoji.

1121118360000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Buljeong Chiseung Dharani Sutra
1121118360000.description: This sutra was translated into Chinese by the Tang monk Dipoheluo, and explains that reciting the dharani every day removes all suffering and leads to rebirth in a pure Buddhist land and nirvana. The surviving copy is believed to be an early 12th-century printing based on the Song dynasty Kaibao canon, and it is the only extant example.

1121118370000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Bulseol Munsu Sari Ilbaek Palmyeong Beomchan
1121118370000.description: This short Buddhist text praises Manjusri through 108 names and was translated by the Song monk Fatian around 990. The surviving copy is believed to be an early 12th-century printing from the Early Tripitaka, and it preserves evidence about the translators and assistants involved in its production.

1121118380000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of Fayuan Zhulin, Volume 82
1121118380000.description: Fayuan Zhulin is a large Buddhist encyclopedia compiled by Dao Shi of the Tang dynasty, and this copy corresponds to volume 82, which includes material on the virtues of keeping the precepts and endurance. It is a re-engraved copy added to the Early Tripitaka after the main carving was completed, and it is important for understanding the history of the canon's compilation.

1121118390000.title_en: Early Printed Edition of the Sutra of the Supreme Secret Dharmas of All Tathagatas, Vajra Three Karmas, Volume 4
1121118390000.description: This esoteric Buddhist scripture, translated by the Song monk Shihu, consists of seven volumes and explains the powers of the three secrets: body, speech, and mind. The surviving copy is a rare re-engraved edition of the Early Tripitaka, based on a printed version offered in 1002 and later incorporated into the canon after 1087.

1123718400000.title_en: Geungnakjeon Hall of Bogwang-sa Temple, Cheongsong
1123718400000.description: Geungnakjeon Hall at Bogwang-sa Temple is believed to have been built in 1615, based on an inscription found during recent repairs. It is a Joseon-period Buddhist hall with a gable roof and dapo-style bracket complexes, showing structural features characteristic of the mid-Joseon period.

1123618410000.title_en: Bronze Seated Bodhisattva, Goseong-sa Temple, Gangjin
1123618410000.description: This 13th-century Goryeo bodhisattva sits in the royal-relaxed pose and is notable for its elegant smile and foreign-looking face. It is one of the largest known Korean examples of this pose, and its finely cast drapery and lively treatment of the hands and feet show highly accomplished metalworking.

1122218500000.title_en: Wontongjeon Hall of Pagyesa Temple, Daegu
1122218500000.description: Pagyesa Temple is said to have been founded in 804, and its main hall, Wontongjeon, was begun in 1605 and completed in 1606. The building has a typical mountain temple layout and preserves an old bracket structure and other architectural features, as well as relics that indicate it was a royal family temple.

1123418510000.title_en: Clay-Seated Shakyamuni Buddha Triad of Ssanggyesa Temple, Nonsan
1123418510000.description: This triad of clay statues was made in 1605 by the sculptor monk Won-o, with four assistant sculptor monks. It is considered an outstanding work that continues the tradition of late Goryeo and early Joseon Buddhist sculpture and shows Won-o’s distinctive style.

1123518520000.title_en: Wood Seated Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Triad and Clay Ten Kings Figures of Seonwonsa Temple, Namwon
1123518520000.description: This set of Buddhist sculptures was produced in two phases, in 1610 and 1646. The main Ksitigarbha triad was made under the direction of the sculptor monk Won-o in 1610, and additional figures including kings and attendants were added in 1646 by other sculptor monks.

1123518530000.title_en: Wood Seated Amitabha Buddha Triad of Jeongsusa Temple, Wanju
1123518530000.description: According to an inscription, this triad was made in 1652 by the sculptor monk Muyeom, who led six assistant sculptor monks. It is regarded as one of Muyeom’s representative works because of its large scale and accomplished form.

1123718540000.title_en: Amitabha Buddha Preaching Painting of Gobangsa Temple, Gimcheon
1123718540000.description: This hanging scroll was painted in 1688 by the painter monk Minwon, together with three other monk painters, as the rear Buddha painting for Gobangsa Temple. It depicts Amitabha Buddha with attendant bodhisattvas and other heavenly figures, and shows characteristic late-17th-century Buddhist painting style.

1123218550000.title_en: Painting of the Three Bodhisattvas of the Water-Land Ritual, Guryongsa Temple, Wonju
1123218550000.description: This painting was made in 1727 by the monk painters Baekgi and Yeonghwi and enshrined at Guryongsa Temple. It depicts the assembly of the three bodhisattvas associated with water-land ritual practice, and the painting box with reliquary materials is also preserved.

1122218560000.title_en: Ksitigarbha and the Ten Kings Painting of Seobongsa Temple, Daegu
1122218560000.description: This painting was made in 1741 by the painter monk Seogwan and his team, and the inscription records that it was originally enshrined at Muryangsujeon Hall of Namjangsa Temple. It is an important work for understanding the artist’s style and the original context of a Jigeumjeonsik painting, also called a painting of the Underworld Assembly.

1123718570000.title_en: Painting of the Easy Path to Rebirth through Nianfo of Eunhaesa Temple, Yeongcheon
1123718570000.description: This painting depicts Amitabha’s Pure Land and the scene in which Avalokitesvara and Mahasthamaprapta lead beings on a prajna boat to rebirth there. An inscription once showed that it was made in 1750, and it is considered the earliest surviving Joseon-period painting of this theme.

1123318580000.description: This bronze temple bell was cast in 1636. It follows the traditional Korean bell form, with a dragon-shaped suspension loop, a tubular pipe, lotus panels, and decorative motifs including Buddhist figures and bodhisattvas.

1123718590000.title_en: Gimcheon Jikjisa Temple Daeungjeon Sumeru Altar
1123718590000.description: This wooden altar table was made in 1651, as confirmed by an inscription, and was produced together with the reconstruction of Daeungjeon Hall. It is an important example of mid-17th-century Buddhist altar furniture and a valuable work for studying Joseon-period interior decoration of Buddhist halls.

1123418600000.description: These three plaques were made in 1654 by Cheolhak, Cheonseung, and Dogyun, and the inscription says they were prepared for the peace and well-being of the royal family. They are notable for their dragon carving, gold and red polychromy, and stepped pedestal, making them representative works of 17th-century Buddhist woodcraft.

1123618610000.title_en: Boseong Daewonsa Temple Geukrakjeon Hall Avalokitesvara and Bodhidharma Murals
1123618610000.description: These two murals were painted on the east and west interior walls of Geukrakjeon Hall, with Avalokitesvara on one side and Bodhidharma on the other in a symmetrical arrangement. They are thought to have been painted around 1766–1767 and show the stylistic influence of the Uigyeom school.

1123618620000.title_en: Yeosu Heungguksa Temple Daeungjeon Hall Avalokitesvara Mural
1123618620000.description: This mural is a paper-mounted wall painting, attached to the wall rather than painted directly on it. It depicts Avalokitesvara and Sudhana against a sea and lotus setting, and is considered a distinctive example of late Joseon Buddhist mural painting.

1123618630000.title_en: Haenam Daeheungsa Temple Seokgareuryeosambul Sitting Statues
1123618630000.description: These three wooden seated Buddha statues were made in 1612, six years after the relics of the monk Seosan were enshrined there. The inscription inside the statues records the date of production, the ten sculptors involved, the donors, and more than 380 lay and monastic participants.

1123818640000.title_en: The Eight Views of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers
1123818640000.description: This set of eight landscape paintings is done in ink on paper and arranged in paired compositions. It is a complete version of the Eight Views of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers theme and reflects the style of the An Gyeon school in the early Joseon period.

1123818650000.description: This is volume 72 of the revised eighty-fascicle Buddhist scripture translated by Śikṣānanda in the Tang dynasty. It is a rare surviving printed copy and is considered an important source for studying Buddhist scriptures, bibliography, and Goryeo woodblock printing culture.

1123518420000.title_en: Wooden Standing Bodhisattva, Gwanumsa Temple, Iksan
1123518420000.description: This wooden bodhisattva statue was made in 1605, in the 38th year of King Seonjo of Joseon. The dedication inscription found inside the statue records the rebuilding of the temple after the Japanese invasions of 1592 and 1597, providing valuable evidence for Buddhist reconstruction efforts after the wars. It is also important for understanding the sculptural lineage associated with the sculptor Won'o.

1123618430000.title_en: Seated Triad of Shakyamuni Buddha, Jeungsusa Temple, Gangjin
1123618430000.description: This group consists of three seated Buddha statues and three pedestals. Inscriptions on the wooden pedestals show that the left clay Buddha was made in 1561, and the central and right wooden Buddhas were made in 1648 and later repaired. The mixed dates reflect temple reconstruction and Buddhist image production after the Japanese invasions, and the set is considered an important reference for Joseon Buddhist sculpture.

1123718440000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Wick Scissors from Wolji Pond, Gyeongju
1123718440000.description: This object was excavated from Wolji Pond, adjacent to the royal palace area in Gyeongju. It is a specialized wick-cutting scissors rather than an ordinary pair of scissors, and its delicate fish-scale ornament suggests a production date in the 8th century, during the height of Unified Silla. Its findspot and craftsmanship make it an important source for studying Unified Silla metalwork and court culture.

1123418450000.description: This stele was made to commemorate Sataek Jijeok, a Baekje official who retired and built a temple. It is the only known stele produced by a Baekje hand, and it provides important evidence for Baekje aristocratic life, official ranks, and religious thought. Its refined text and calligraphy also reflect the high cultural level of late Baekje.

1121118460000.description: This is the eighth volume of the Tang-dynasty translation of the Avataṃsaka Sutra, specifically the "Entry into the Realm of Inconceivable Liberation and the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra" chapter. It is a rare edition with 26 lines and 17 characters per line, and it is thought to be either a woodblock edition carved at Hyeonhwasa Temple in 1021 or at Jingwansa Temple in 1051. The volume is an important source for the study of Buddhist texts, bibliography, and Goryeo woodblock printing.

1121118470000.description: This is the thirty-fourth volume of the 80-fascicle Chinese translation of the Avataṃsaka Sutra by Śikṣānanda. It is believed to be the model used for the printed edition at Haeinsa Temple and is a surviving domestic copy of the 1098 edition that was used as a source for the Tripitaka Koreana. The volume is rare and includes marked dots and punctuation in the margins, making it valuable for the study of old reading marks and Goryeo printing culture.

1121118480000.description: This woodblock printed edition is based on the teachings of the Goryeo monk Jinul's "Susimgyeol". It was published in 1467 by the Gangyeongdogam, after King Sejo had the text read aloud and translated by the monk Sinmi. The volume also includes four related Buddhist sermons, and it is an important source for studying the Gangyeongdogam and the history of Hunminjeongeum.

1123818490000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Yongmunsa Temple, Namhae
1123818490000.description: This Buddhist main hall was built in 1666 during the reign of King Hyeonjong and was repaired in 1773. It is a three-bay-by-three-bay building with a multi-bracket system and hip-and-gable roof, and its bracket sets and decorative members show the elaborate style of 18th-century temple architecture. The ceiling and interior carvings, including sea creatures such as turtles, crabs, fish, and seaweed, reflect the building's coastal location.

1123718670000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Changnimsa Temple Site, Gyeongju
1123718670000.description: This three-story stone pagoda stands at the Changnimsa Temple Site in Gyeongju, a site excavated to reveal separate enclosed spaces typical of Unified Silla temple layouts. Its construction is estimated to date to around 855, based on the relic inscription found inside one of the nearby pagodas. The pagoda is notable for its two-tiered base and the relief carvings of the Eight Guardian Deities on the upper base.

1123718680000.title_en: Jeokgwangjeon Hall of Bogyeongsa Temple, Pohang
1123718680000.description: Jeokgwangjeon is the main hall of Bogyeongsa Temple and is a three-bay by two-bay pavilion built with a gabled roof and multi-bracket system. The building uses old structural members believed to have been reused from an earlier period, including stone foundations and a carved lintel beam with a lion figure. It shows architectural features associated with the late 17th century and the middle period of the Joseon dynasty.

1121118690000.title_en: Celadon Meiping Vase with Cloud and Crane Inlay
1121118690000.description: This Goryeo celadon meiping vase is a highly refined inlaid celadon made in the middle period of the Goryeo dynasty. The vase is decorated with bands of cloud and crane motifs in white inlay, with some black inlay added, creating a spacious and restrained design. It is also noted for its excellent firing condition and well-preserved state.

1123718700000.title_en: Relic Inscription for the Gilt-bronze Pillar of the Nine-story Wooden Pagoda at Hwangnyongsa Temple Site, Gyeongju
1123718700000.description: This gilt-bronze inscription records the rebuilding of the nine-story wooden pagoda at Hwangnyongsa Temple during the reign of King Gyeongmun of Unified Silla. It is an important contemporaneous source for the construction and restoration of the pagoda, and it can be compared with later historical texts such as the Samguk sagi and Samguk yusa. The inscription also provides valuable evidence for Buddhist relic containers and the script style of the ninth century.

1123218710000.title_en: Copper Inscription for Monk Yeomgeo's Stupa
1123218710000.description: This stupa inscription was engraved on a thin copper plate and records the funeral inscription for the Unified Silla Seon monk Yeomgeo, who died in 844. The text is executed in a clerical-style script using the double-hook engraving technique. It is an important source for studying ninth-century calligraphy, metalcraft, and the dating of Yeomgeo's stupa.

1123218720000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Seated Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva from Jangyeon-ri, Hweyang
1123218720000.description: This gilt-bronze seated Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva statue is said to have been excavated in Jangyeon-ri, Hweyang, near Mount Geumgang. Although some gilt surfaces have flaked away and there are traces of corrosion, the statue is generally well preserved. Its refined treatment of ornaments, jewelry, and facial features reflects Buddhist sculpture influenced by Yuan-period Tibetan Buddhist art and is considered important for understanding late Goryeo and early Joseon sculpture.

1123218730000.title_en: Iron Seated Medicine Buddha from Hakseong-dong, Wonju
1123218730000.description: This iron Buddha statue was one of five iron images left in a field in Hakseong-dong, Wonju, until the Japanese colonial period, and it is now displayed at the National Chuncheon Museum. The statue is close to life-size and has a round, naturally sloping shoulder line with balanced proportions. It is an important work for understanding late Unified Silla to early Goryeo iron Buddha casting and the iconography of Medicine Buddha.

1122418740000.title_en: Bronze Buddhist Shrine and Gilt-bronze Seated Amitabha Triad from the Stone Pagoda at Maeok-dong, Suncheon
1122418740000.description: This set consists of a bronze Buddhist shrine and a gilt-bronze seated Amitabha triad, accompanied by votive inscriptions. The inscriptions identify the production date as 1468, and the figures show characteristics of fifteenth-century early Joseon Buddhist sculpture, including the form of the attendant bodhisattvas. The shrine is an unusual pavilion-shaped type and is also significant for its fit with the statues it contains.

1121118820200.title_en: Painting of the Sixteen Arhats (No. 15, Abeolda Honored One)
1121118820200.description: This Goryeo painting depicts the Fifteenth Arhat, Abeolda Honored One, with two attendants. The composition emphasizes open space, fine and fluent linework, realistic figures, and a strong contrast of white, red, and dark ink; the painter’s name, Hyegan (or Hyehan), is also recorded, which is rare among surviving Goryeo arhat paintings.

1121118830000.title_en: Painting of the Five Hundred Arhats
1121118830000.description: This group comprises six surviving Goryeo paintings of the Five Hundred Arhats, each showing an arhat in a distinct pose or act of practice. They were made in 1235–1236 and preserve inscriptions naming the arhat and the patron, making them important sources for the study of Goryeo Buddhist painting.

1121118840000.title_en: Register of the Civil and Military Service Examination, Third Month of the Sinmyo Year
1121118840000.description: This printed register lists the successful candidates in the special civil and military service examination held in the third month of 1471. It is the earliest known surviving example of this kind of document and includes a postscript written by Jo Bin, who passed the examination.

1121118850000.description: This woodblock-printed edition of the Surangama Sutra was published in 1309 during the reign of King Chungseon of Goryeo. It is thought to be an early impression made soon after carving, and it preserves phonetic glosses throughout, making it an important source for the study of Korean language history before Hunminjeongeum.

1121118860000.title_en: Recarved Edition of the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra, Volume 20
1121118860000.description: This scroll is the twentieth volume of the Korean re-engraved Tripitaka edition of the Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra, carved in 1246 at the Daejanggam Office. Although the first leaf is missing and the second and third leaves are damaged, it is valuable for the study of Korean language history because it preserves reading glosses in ink along the margins.

1121118870000.title_en: Painting of Amitāyus Tathāgata and the Nine Assemblies, and Painting of King Taejo of Goryeo Worshipping Danmugal Bodhisattva
1121118870000.description: This double-sided Goryeo Buddhist painting was made by the painter Noryeong in 1307 on a black-lacquered wooden board with gold linework. One side depicts Amitāyus Buddha with eight attendant bodhisattvas, and the reverse shows King Taejo of Goryeo worshipping Danmugal Bodhisattva at Baejae in Geumgangsan.

1123618880000.title_en: Three Assemblies Bodhisattva Painting, Cheoneunsa Temple, Gurye
1123618880000.description: This Three Assemblies Bodhisattva painting was made in 1776 for enshrinement in the main hall of Cheoneunsa Temple. It depicts the bodhisattvas of the upper, middle, and lower rites of a water-and-land ritual, with their retinues named individually in the inscription, making it an important reference for the iconography of Three Assemblies Bodhisattva paintings.

1123618890000.title_en: Wooden Seated Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva and Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva, Cheoneunsa Temple, Gurye
1123618890000.description: These two wooden seated bodhisattva images were made in June 1614 by the sculptor Uigena and four other sculptors, as confirmed by the dedicatory inscription found inside the Avalokiteshvara image. They were created as attendant figures for the main Buddha in the Amitabha Hall of Cheoneunsa Temple and are considered important early works of the sculptor Hyeonjin.

1123818260000.description: Yeongsanjeon is the main hall of the lower compound at Tongdosa Temple, facing south, with Geungnakjeon Hall and Yaksajeon Hall placed to its left and right in front. The hall was rebuilt in 1714 after a fire in 1713, and the inscription on the roof tiles supports this date. It is a three-bay by three-bay dapo-style building with a gabled roof, and its interior murals include a unique painting of Dabotap Pagoda illustrating the "Appearance of the Stupa" chapter of the Lotus Sutra.

1123818270000.description: Daegwangmyeongjeon is the main Buddha hall of the middle compound at Tongdosa Temple, located northwest of Daeungjeon Hall. After a fire in 1756, it was rebuilt in 1758 and its dancheong painting was completed in 1759, as recorded in a hanging board inscription. It is a five-bay by three-bay dapo-style hall with a hipped-and-gabled roof and carved decorative details such as dragon heads and tails.

1121118280000.title_en: Mazae Balsaja Sittingsang of Botasa Temple, Seoul
1121118280000.description: This relief carving is on the rock wall behind the main hall of Botasa Temple, an hermitage of Gaeunsa Temple in Seoul. The bodhisattva wears a crown and draped heavenly robes, with the left hand lowered and the right hand raised to shoulder height. The form, together with the inscription on the left side, suggests a late Goryeo to early Joseon date.

1122518290000.title_en: Wood Seated Vairocana Buddha of Biraesa Temple, Daejeon
1122518290000.description: This seated Buddha image is slightly smaller than life-size and shows a calm, restrained style. The bottom inscription records the exact date of 1651 and the sculptor Mueom, making it an important reference for 17th-century Buddhist sculpture. The figure sits in the vajra-bound mudra and has well-balanced proportions with delicately carved robes.

1123118300000.title_en: Buncheong Ware Inlaid Tomb Inscription for Kim Myeong-ri with Inscription Dated Jeongtong 4th Year
1123118300000.description: This is the tomb inscription of Kim Myeong-ri (1368–1438), who served as vice magistrate of Seongcheon. The ceramic is a rare bell-shaped tomb inscription, and the text was written by Yu Uiseon. Based on the record, the object was likely made after late October 1439.

1123718310000.description: Daeungjeon is the main Buddha hall of Daegoksa Temple and was rebuilt in 1687. It is a three-bay by two-bay dapo-style hall, and the arrangement of the altar, the use of double-window openings on the rear side, and traces of an exterior floor on the front reflect architectural features of the late 17th century. These details make it an important example for studying the development of Buddhist temple architecture in the Uiseong area.

1123218320000.title_en: Five-Story Stone Pagoda of Bongjeongam Hermitage, Inje
1123218320000.description: This stone pagoda stands within Bongjeongam Hermitage at an altitude of 1,244 meters below Socheongbong Peak in Seoraksan Mountain. Tradition says that seven relics of the Buddha brought from Tang China by the monk Jajang were enshrined in this pagoda. Its simplified structure and the form of the roof stones indicate characteristics of late Goryeo stone pagodas.

1123518330000.title_en: Wood Seated Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva of Cheongnyongsa Temple, Gimje
1123518330000.description: This seated Avalokitesvara image was made for enshrinement in Hyangnojeon Hall at Bongseosa Temple in Wanju. The work bears a precise date of 1655, the name of the sculptor Jo Neung, and a dedicatory inscription, making it an important reference for mid-17th-century Buddhist sculpture. It reflects the restrained and approachable aesthetic of the late Joseon period.

1123518900000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Miniature Shrine and Gilt-bronze Amitabha Triad with Seven Figures from Simgoksa Temple Five-Story Stone Pagoda, Iksan
1123518900000.description: This gilt-bronze miniature shrine and seven gilt-bronze Buddhist images were found in 2012 during dismantling repair of the five-story stone pagoda at Simgoksa Temple, Iksan, in a square cavity on top of the foundation stone. The shrine includes depictions of Amitabha preaching on the back wall in repoussé, while the doors are decorated with Vajrapani figures. The seven images consist of Amitabha, Avalokitesvara, Mahasthamaprapta, and four other Buddha and bodhisattva figures, showing styles influenced by Yuan- and Ming-dynasty Lama Buddhism.

1121118910000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Thousand-Armed Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva Seated Statue, Heungcheonsa Temple, Seoul
1121118910000.description: This is a rare surviving 42-armed Thousand-Armed Avalokitesvara statue in Korea, and records show it was enshrined at Heungcheonsa Temple by at least the 19th century. Its facial features, proportions, ornaments, and narrow waist suggest it was made sometime between the Goryeo period and the early Joseon period. It is an important example for studying Avalokitesvara iconography and the history of belief in Thousand-Armed Avalokitesvara.

1122218920000.description: This is a printed edition of volumes 6–7 of the collected works of Ikjae Yi Je-hyeon (1287–1367), a leading late Goryeo statesman and scholar. The work was first published in 1363, but that edition no longer survives; the designated copy is part of a later Joseon reprint issued in 1432 under King Sejong's order. Its continued use of Goryeo-style orthographic practices and punctuation makes it an important source for early Joseon literary, publishing, and bibliography studies.

1122218930000.description: This is a four-volume, one-volume printed edition of a critical collection by the late Goryeo scholar and statesman Ikjae Yi Je-hyeon (1287–1367). The first edition was printed in 1363, but it is no longer extant; the designated copy was printed from woodblocks carved in 1432 at Wonju under King Sejong's order. It preserves Goryeo-style textual conventions and is a valuable source for the study of early Joseon literary criticism and bibliography.

1122218940000.title_en: Collected Works of Toegye Yi Hwang
1122218940000.description: This is the first printed edition of the collected works of Toegye Yi Hwang (1501–1570), a major scholar of Joseon and the leading figure of the Yeongnam school. The work is significant not only for its rich contents and large scale, but also because the methods used in its editing and printing became a model for later Joseon collected works. The designated copy is valuable for studying the publication process and provenance of literary collections in Joseon.

1123718950000.title_en: Printing Woodblocks for the Collected Works of Toegye Yi Hwang
1123718950000.description: These woodblocks were used to print the first edition of the Collected Works of Toegye Yi Hwang in 1600. The original complete set of the edition no longer survives, so the exact original number of blocks cannot be confirmed. They are important sources for the study of Joseon-period bibliography, printing culture, and Neo-Confucian scholarship.

1122118960000.title_en: Daeungjeon Hall of Unsusa Temple, Busan
1122118960000.description: This Buddhist hall was confirmed by inscriptions discovered during dismantling repairs in 2013 to have been begun in 1647 and completed in 1655. It is a three-bay by three-bay gable-roofed hall with a modest jusimpo bracket system, and it preserves structural features and later repairs that help trace changes in mid-Joseon Buddhist architecture. The hall is notable as the oldest surviving wooden building in Busan.

1123118970000.title_en: Portrait of Seo Gyeong-u and Portrait Case
1123118970000.description: This is a full-length seated portrait of Seo Gyeong-u (1573–1645), shown in an official cap and black robe with a crane rank badge. The painting preserves the original appearance well and shows the refined portrait style of the early 17th century, including careful line work, subtle coloring, and detailed rendering of costume and facial features. The accompanying portrait case is also preserved and shares the historical value of the portrait.

1121118750000.title_en: Album of Mount Geumgang Landscapes Painted by Jeong Seon
1121118750000.description: This is the earliest known work by Jeong Seon, dated to 1711. It is regarded as an important example for understanding the formation of his true-view landscape painting. As an early work, it shows some less mature features, but the paintings in the album are filled with the vitality and enthusiasm of the artist’s early career.

1123518760000.description: This folding-screen style pictorial map, made in Joseon society after 1875, is the only known example with an attached explanatory text panel. It places Jeonju and its surroundings in an unusual arrangement, with the south shown on the right side, and depicts the fortress, government buildings, royal shrines, and houses in detail. The map and its texts together present Jeonju as the spiritual center of Joseon political authority and as the former capital of Later Baekje.

1121118770000.title_en: Stele for Monk Nanggong at Taejasa Temple, Bonghwa
1121118770000.description: This is the funerary stele of Nanggong Daesa Haejeok, a renowned Buddhist monk of the late Silla and early Goryeo periods. It was erected in 954 by Buddhist monks including Danmok, with the inscription composed by Choe In-yeon and Seok Sun-baek, and the calligraphy assembled from the running-script writing of Kim Saeng. The stele preserves detailed information about Nanggong Daesa’s life and about the people involved in its composition and erection, making it an important historical source.

1121118780000.title_en: Bronze Bowl Inscribed with the Name of King Gwanggaeto, Excavated from Ho-ujeong Tomb, Gyeongju
1121118780000.description: This bronze bowl was excavated from Ho-ujeong Tomb in Gyeongju in 1946 and is now in the collection of the National Museum of Korea. An inscription on the base records the year Eulmyo and the words referring to King Gwanggaeto, showing that a Goguryeo vessel was placed in a Silla royal tomb. The object is valued as a rare Goguryeo bronze vessel and as an important source for studying relations between Goguryeo and Silla.

1121118790000.description: This is a dated pledge-meeting painting made after a group of five men who passed the civil and military state examinations in 1546 met again at Hikyeongnu Pavilion in Gwangju in 1567. It is one of only two surviving 16th-century banghoe paintings and is an early example among such works. The painting, the list of participants, and the colophon are all preserved, and the figures and pavilion are rendered with lively and unforced brushwork.

1123318800000.title_en: Goryeo Ink Inscribed "Dansan O-ok," Excavated from Myeongam-dong, Cheongju
1123318800000.description: This is the oldest surviving Goryeo-period ink and was excavated from a wooden-chamber tomb in Myeongam-dong, Cheongju. The surviving fragment bears the inscription "Dansan O-ok," referring to the famous ink produced in Danyang. The object is important evidence for the study of traditional ink and the history of ink production in Korea.

1121118810000.description: Changuimun Gate is one of the four small gates of the walls of Hanyang. It was built during the construction of the capital walls in 1396, closed in 1416, and reopened in 1506. The gate was also the scene of the forces of the Injo Restoration entering the palace in 1623, and the present gatehouse was rebuilt in 1742 after being burned during the Japanese invasions.

1122118820100.title_en: Goryeo Painting of the Sixteen Arhats (No. 7, Karika-zhonja)
1122118820100.description: This painting depicts the seventh of the Sixteen Arhats, Karika-zhonja, seated in quiet contemplation. It was painted in 1236 with prayers for peace in the realm and long life for the king, and its brushwork, color, and composition are closely related to other Goryeo arhat paintings of 1235–1236. It is one of the few surviving Goryeo Sixteen Arhats paintings and a rare example of a 13th-century Buddhist painting.
1122118820100.material: Ink and light color on silk

1122119010600.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-6)
1122119010600.description: This volume consists of two royal protocol books recording court rites and state ceremonies of the late Joseon period. The contents cover the investiture of the Crown Prince Uiwang in 1900 and the posthumous elevation of Heonui Daewonwang, Sunmok Daewonbi, Wanhyohyeonwang, and Uiwangbi in 1907. It is a handwritten court record prepared for royal viewing.

1121119010700.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-7)
1121119010700.description: This entry preserves one royal protocol book from the late Joseon period. It is the illustrated record of the Hwaseong Fortress construction project, compiled in 1801 and intended for distribution. The volume is a printed edition in nine fascicles bound into nine books.

1121119010800.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-8)
1121119010800.description: This entry consists of one late Joseon royal protocol book recording the construction of the Jogyu Temple site for Juknyeongmyo, Gyeongneung, and Yeongneung. It was compiled in 1901 as a distributed copy and survives as a complete manuscript volume. The record documents the related royal works and ceremonies.

1123219010900.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-9)
1123219010900.description: This item is a two-volume royal protocol book from the late Joseon period. It records the posthumous investiture of Heonui Daewonwang, Sunmok Daewonbi, Wanhyohyeonwang, and Uiwangbi, and was made in 1907 as a distributed copy. The surviving work is a complete manuscript edition.

1121119011000.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-10)
1121119011000.description: This is a single late Joseon royal protocol volume recording the posthumous investiture of Heonui Daewonwang, Sunmok Daewonbi, Wanhyohyeonwang, and Uiwangbi. It was made in 1907 as a royal-viewing copy and survives as a complete manuscript volume. The entry identifies the version preserved by the Seoul Museum of History.

1123319011100.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-11)
1123319011100.description: This volume is a royal protocol book for the elevation of royal titles involving King Gojong, Queen Myeongseong, Queen Sinjeong, Queen Hyojeong, and Queen Cheorin. It was compiled in 1877 as a distributed copy and survives as a complete manuscript volume. The record is held by Ewha Womans University.

1121119011200.title_en: Royal Protocols of the Joseon Dynasty (2016-12)
1121119011200.description: This item is a single royal protocol volume for the construction-related rites of King Yeongjo's saritdung and railings at the royal tomb precinct. It was compiled in 1729 and is described as a distributed copy. The volume survives as a complete manuscript.

1125019020000.description: Daeseongjeon is the main hall of Jeju Hyanggyo, a Confucian school originally founded in 1394 and moved several times before settling at its present site in 1827. The building is a five-bay by four-bay hall with a hipped-and-gabled roof, and it retains local architectural features characteristic of Jeju. Its design includes a distinctive structural system and details adapted to Jeju's windy and rainy climate.

1123118980000.title_en: Portrait of Seo Mun-jung and Case
1123118980000.description: This is a full-length seated portrait of Seo Mun-jung (1634–1709), a Joseon-period civil official who rose to the posts of Left and Right State Councillor and later Chief State Councillor. The portrait shows him in official dress with a black cap, peach-colored robe, and a ceremonial chair covered with leopard skin, and the case is also designated together with the painting because it shares its historical significance.

1121118990000.title_en: Gilt Silver Flower-shaped Cup and Stand
1121118990000.description: This silver cup and matching stand are gilded over the surface and both are made in a six-petal flower shape. The footed stand is decorated with raised floral designs, and the cup bears engraved peony scroll motifs, showing refined metalworking techniques of Goryeo. It is considered one of the finest surviving examples of a Goryeo silver cup-and-stand set.

1121119000000.description: This is a 1441 printing in early movable metal type of a book based on the Daoist text Zhouyi Cantongqi by Wei Boyang of the Later Han. It was printed from a model text that combined Yu Yan’s Zhouyi Cantongqi Fahui and Zhouyi Cantongqi Shiyi, and it is regarded as the only known surviving copy of this early edition. It is also an important source for studying early Joseon Daoist thought and funeral customs.

1121119010100.description: Uigwe are illustrated court records that document major state and royal ceremonies in the Joseon Dynasty. This designated group consists of 1,373 items in 2,203 volumes preserved at the Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies, including both royal-review copies and distributed copies, as well as unique and non-unique volumes. The records cover events such as royal marriages, investitures, funerals, banquets, palace construction, and state processions.

1123119010200.description: Uigwe are illustrated court records that document major state and royal ceremonies in the Joseon Dynasty. This designated group consists of 291 items in 384 volumes preserved at the Kyujanggak Institute for Korean Studies, including royal-review copies and distributed copies, as well as unique and non-unique volumes. The records cover events such as royal marriages, investitures, funerals, banquets, palace construction, and state processions.

1121119010300.description: Uigwe are illustrated court records that document major state and royal ceremonies in the Joseon Dynasty. This designated group consists of 80 items in 133 volumes preserved at the Academy of Korean Studies Jangseogak Archives, including royal-review copies and distributed copies, as well as unique and non-unique volumes. The records cover events such as royal marriages, investitures, funerals, banquets, palace construction, and state processions.

1123819010400.description: Uigwe are illustrated court records that document major state and royal ceremonies in the Joseon Dynasty. This designated group consists of three volumes held by Sacheon City Hall: Sejong Daewang Taesilsukgangan Sugeo Uigwe, Sejong Daewang and Danjong Daewang Taesil Sugeo Uigwe, and Sejong Daewang and Danjong Daewang Taesil Pyoseok Geonlipsi Uigwe. The items were made in 1601, 1730, and 1734 respectively, and the 1601 volume is noted as the earliest surviving Joseon Uigwe.

1121119010500.description: Uigwe are illustrated court records that document major state and royal ceremonies in the Joseon Dynasty. This designated group consists of two titles in three volumes preserved at the National Library of Korea, both copies of the 1901 Yeonggeoncheong Uigwe for Jongmyo-related royal tomb and shrine construction projects. The records are important examples of late Joseon court documentation and one copy is incomplete.

1121119030000.description: This Buddhist painting illustrates the chapter of the Flower Garland Sutra in which Sudhana visits Avalokiteshvara during his pilgrimage in search of enlightenment. The composition places Avalokiteshvara large at the center and Sudhana small at the lower right, showing a strong sense of space and the typical iconography of late Goryeo Water-Moon Avalokiteshvara paintings.

1122219040000.title_en: Reliquaries Excavated from the East and West Three-Story Stone Pagodas of Galahangsa Temple Site, Gimcheon
1122219040000.description: These reliquary objects were discovered in 1916 while the east and west three-story stone pagodas at the Galahangsa temple site were being moved to Gyeongbokgung Palace. They were enshrined in the relic cavities beneath both pagodas, along with a bronze bottle and a sutra dharani, and are important reference materials for the study of Unified Silla reliquaries.

1121119050000.title_en: White Porcelain Jars Excavated from Cheongjin-dong, Seoul
1121119050000.description: These three plain white porcelain jars were excavated together in 2009 from the Pimatgol area of Cheongjin-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul. They are fine-quality early Joseon court-kiln ware, and their clearly documented excavation context makes them especially valuable for understanding early Joseon urban life and ceramics.

1121119070000.title_en: Bronze Drum with Inscription of the Sixth Year of Xiantong
1121119070000.description: This bronze drum is a ritual Buddhist instrument used to produce sound during temple ceremonies, together with the bell. It bears an inscription dating its manufacture to the sixth year of Xiantong, corresponding to 865, and is considered an important standard example of Unified Silla metalwork.

1122319080000.description: These woodblocks at Jeondeungsa Temple were made in 1543 by copying an edition of the Lotus Sutra associated with the calligraphic style of Seong Dalseaeng. Although one block is missing and some blocks show insect damage, most of the set is well preserved, and the inscriptions provide valuable evidence for the temple's publication history and donors.

1123619090000.title_en: Woodblocks of the Commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra
1123619090000.description: These woodblocks at Songgwangsa Temple preserve a 120-fascicle edition of the commentary compiled by Song-dynasty monk Jingyuan. They are the largest surviving set of Buddhist text woodblocks in Korea apart from the Tripitaka, and the colophons record that the full edition was carved and printed at Songgwangsa in 1634-1635.

1123619100000.description: These woodblocks at Songgwangsa Temple preserve the vernacular Korean annotated edition of Gyecho Simhak Inmun, along with related texts such as Balsim Susengjang and several Dharma talks. The carving record indicates that the blocks were made in June 1577, and they are considered the oldest surviving woodblocks of an eonhae edition.

1123619110000.description: These woodblocks at Songgwangsa Temple preserve the 1529 edition of Incheon Anmok and survive as the only extant original woodblocks for that work. The colophons show that the book was printed at Songgwangsa in the summer of 1529, and the blocks are an important source for the history of early Joseon Buddhism and printing.

1123719280000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Mitansa Temple Site, Gyeongju
1123719280000.description: This stone pagoda stands at the Mitansa Temple Site, a temple site formed within the Silla royal capital during Unified Silla. Excavation recovered a roof tile inscribed “Mi-tan,” confirming the site mentioned in the Samguk yusa, and the pagoda was restored in 1980 using surviving and newly carved stones. It is the only surviving stone pagoda in the Silla royal capital and is an important source for studying Silla pagoda foundations and construction methods.

1122119290000.title_en: Yengnam Travel Album by Kim Yun-gyeom
1122119290000.description: This album consists of 14 landscape paintings depicting scenic places mainly in the Busan and Gyeongnam area. Kim Yun-gyeom (1711–1775) was a late Joseon literati painter known for highly simplified brushwork and pale color washes, and the album shows the travel culture and painting practices of Joseon literati. It is an important record of regional landscape painting and literary-artistic exchange in late Joseon.
1122119290000.material: Ink and light color on paper

1121119300000.title_en: Goryeo Celadon Ewer in Bottle-Gourd Shape with Sgraffito Floral Design and Stand
1121119300000.description: This celadon set consists of a bottle-gourd-shaped ewer with lid and a stand, decorated with a freehand floral design made using the sgraffito technique. The black-and-white decorative effects and the complete matching set show the high level of workmanship. It is regarded as an outstanding example of Goryeo celadon from the 12th to 13th century.

1121119310000.title_en: Goryeo Celadon Ewer in Bamboo Shoot Shape
1121119310000.description: This celadon ewer is shaped like a bamboo shoot and belongs to the category of animal, plant, or object-shaped celadon. It is notable for its refined form, excellent glaze color, and nearly flawless surface with very little crazing. The work is considered a top-tier example of shaped Goryeo celadon from the 12th century.

1121119320000.title_en: Goryeo Celadon Brush Holder with Openwork Lotus and Scroll Design
1121119320000.description: This is a brush holder used to keep writing brushes upright. The rectangular body, dragon-head ornament, and openwork lotus-scroll decoration are combined in a dense and refined composition, with especially fine blue glaze color. It is a rare and high-quality example of Goryeo celadon from the 12th century.

1123719330000.title_en: Painting of the Three Bodhisattvas at Bulguksa Temple, Gyeongju
1123719330000.description: This Buddhist painting bears an inscription stating that it was made in 1739 by Milgwi, Chaewon, and Seojeung at Ojuam Hermitage of Geodongsa Temple in Gyeongju and later enshrined at Bulyeongsa Temple. The composition places the three figures side by side on the same horizontal line, and the painting uses strong red, green, and yellow tones with careful line work. It is an important source for studying 18th-century Three Bodhisattvas iconography and Buddhist painting style.

1123619340000.title_en: Amitabha Buddha Preaching to the Assembly at Dorimsa Temple, Gokseong
1123619340000.description: This Buddhist painting was made in 1730 as a hanging painting for the main hall of Dorimsa Temple, under the supervision of Gyeongmae, with the chief painters Chaein, Jinhaeng, Jeuksim, Gakcheon, and Chaekhwal. Its composition, drawing style, and color scheme generally follow the style associated with the painter-monk Eungam, and it is important for studying the transmission of 18th-century Buddhist painting traditions. The painting presents Amitabha Buddha with the attendant bodhisattvas in a carefully balanced symmetrical composition.

1123719350000.title_en: Three-story Stone Pagoda at Site 3 of Yongjanggye Valley, Namsan Mountain, Gyeongju
1123719350000.description: This pagoda was reconstructed in 2002 after excavation surveys in 2000 and 2001, using surviving original stones where possible. Although no documentary record identifies the exact date of construction, excavated roof tiles and other remains suggest that the temple site was established in the late 9th century of Unified Silla. The pagoda is a rare masonry-style stone pagoda in Gyeongju and is an important example of the local tradition of brick-like stone pagodas.

1123519200000.title_en: Wooden Seated Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva and Ten Kings from Munsusa Temple, Gochang
1123519200000.description: This set consists of a seated Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva in monk’s robes and ten Kings of the Underworld depicted in kingly dress. According to an inscription on one of the figures, the set was made in 1654 by a group of sculptor-monks led by Hae-sim, following the sculptural tradition of Myeonyam Gakseong and his circle. Some attendant figures are now missing because of theft and loss over time.

1122119210000.title_en: Artifacts Excavated from Geumjo Tomb, Yangsan
1122119210000.description: This group of artifacts was excavated from Geumjo Tomb in Yangsan and is important for studying the spread and lineage of Silla tomb culture beyond the Gyeongju area. Based on stylistic comparisons with finds from Gyeongju, the objects are estimated to date to the 6th century during the Three Kingdoms period. The assemblage includes gold and silver ornaments, a bronze vessel, and other items that are significant for the study of ancient metal craft.

1123819220000.title_en: Gilt-bronze Crown Excavated from Bokcheon-dong, Busan
1123819220000.description: This gilt-bronze crown was excavated from Tomb No. 11 at the Bokcheon-dong burial complex in Dongnae, Busan. Unlike the familiar 5th- to 6th-century Silla crown forms, it has a plain, archaic shape with tree-branch-like uprights attached to a circular band. It is an important archaeological source for understanding the lineage of Silla and Gaya crowns and the metalworking techniques of the Three Kingdoms period.

1121119230000.description: This album contains royal letters sent by King Jeongjo to Sim Hwan-gi between 1796 and 1800. The letters deal mostly with state affairs and are an important source for understanding the political situation of the time.
